records.name: Animated Feature List
records.description: A feature list template where items animate into view one at a time. Perfect for product pages and pitch content with multiple points to cover clearly.
records.move: header lines rise, feature cards slide in one by one, checks draw
records.how: A two-column layout: a soft blue radial glow drifting slowly across the frame (x/y sine.inOut over the full 5s), a header with eyebrow, three-line title and subtitle, and four glassy list items each with a coloured icon tile, a checkmark path and two lines of copy. In the first 20% the eyebrow fades up, the title lines rise from yPercent 110 with expo.out and 0.08s stagger, and the subtitle fades in. From 10% the items enter one at a time every 0.38s: each slides in from x 80 with scale .96 and opacity 0 (expo.out), its icon pops from scale 0 with back.out(2.2), the check draws with DrawSVG from 0% to 100% (power2.inOut) and the text nudges in from x 14. At 87% the items sweep up and fade (y -30, power2.in, 0.06s stagger) followed by the header, so the frame ends empty.
records.adapt: Replace the eyebrow, three title lines, subtitle and the four item titles/descriptions; swap the four icon tile colours and the glow colour to the brand palette; item count can change (the 0.38s per-item cadence and the 1.5s intro still work up to ~5 items). Keep the expo.out entries and the back.out icon pop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the .glow, .head and .list markup inside el from shot.items; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the same tweens placed at fractions of D (title 0.03D, items from 0.1D with 0.076D stagger, exit at 0.87D), all selectors scoped via el.querySelectorAll. DrawSVGPlugin must be registered; the fallback is animating stroke-dashoffset.
caveats: from() tweens on a paused timeline need immediateRender handled if the timeline is built after mount
backdrop-filter on the items is mildly expensive
does not loop: ends on an empty frame

records.name: Animated Repeater
records.description: An animated repeater that multiplies and sequences elements into a rhythmic motion pattern. Great for abstract backgrounds and branded motion graphics.
records.move: grid of rounded dots pulses in radial waves, colours rotate around centre
records.how: A 20x11 grid of 36px rounded yellow squares fills the frame with a large white 'Northwind' wordmark on top in mix-blend-mode difference. Nothing is on a GSAP timeline: a seek(t) function computes, for each dot, two sine waves travelling outward from the centre (one keyed on distance, one on distance plus angle), and writes transform scale (0.15 to 1), rotate (plus or minus 45deg) and opacity (0.35 to 1) each frame. The dot colour cycles through four palette swatches by angular sector, advancing one full turn per loop. The phase runs exactly 2pi over the 5s duration so the last frame equals the first and the loop is seamless.
records.adapt: Change the wordmark string, the four palette colours, the dot size and radius, and the COLS/ROWS density; the wave frequencies (0.55 and 0.25 per cell distance) set the look and are worth keeping. gsap is loaded but not used.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the grid of .dot cells inside el and stores the per-cell distance/angle list; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline holding a single tween on a proxy object {p:0 to 1, duration D, ease none} whose onUpdate runs the same per-dot math with ph = p*2pi and writes styles directly. Scope the grid to el rather than document.getElementById.
caveats: 220 DOM style writes per frame; fine at 30fps but heavier than a tween
the fx.register seek loop must become an onUpdate tween on the returned timeline

records.name: Animated Text Messages
records.description: An animated chat template where text message bubbles appear in a conversation sequence. Great for messaging app UI mockups and social content that tells a story through dialogue.
records.move: chat bubbles pop in sequentially with typing dots between replies
records.how: A portrait phone mockup on a diagonal gradient with a status bar, contact header, message list and compose bar. Seven rows carry data-t timestamps: at each one the row expands from height 0 (power3.out, 0.45s) while its bubble scales from .5 and opacity 0 with back.out(1.8), anchored at the bubble's bottom corner (left for 'them', right for 'me'). Two typing-indicator rows show three grey dots bobbing y -10 in a yoyo sine loop, then shrink out (scale .6, power2.in) and collapse their row just before the next real message lands. The phone drifts y 8 / rotation -0.6deg in a sine yoyo across the 10s; at 93% all rows fade out with a 0.05s stagger so the loop restarts on an empty thread.
records.adapt: Edit the row texts, the data-t / data-end timings, who is 'me' vs 'them', the header name/avatar, bubble colours and the background gradient; add or remove rows freely. Keep the 0.45s height reveal plus back.out bubble pop and the typing-dot cadence (0.3s, 0.1s stagger).
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone and rows from shot.messages (text, side, t, typingUntil); animate(el, shot, D) loops rows and returns one gsap.timeline placing each row's from() at t/10*D. Timestamps become fractions of D; the typing repeat count is derived from the gap. Selectors must use el.querySelectorAll('.row'), not document.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920, not 16:9
the .stage backgroundPosition tween is a no-op
from() height tweens rely on layout; set immediateRender:false if built after first paint

records.name: Appear
records.description: A minimal reveal animation template from Antinomy where elements appear with a quiet clean entrance. Works for subtle UI transitions and text reveals where you don't want the animation to steal focus.
records.move: card and lines fade up from blur, breathe, leave the same way
records.how: A single white card on a warm off-white ground containing a pill tag, a two-line headline, a paragraph and a dark button. The card fades in rising y 10 with power2.out over the first 45%; its four children follow from y 10, opacity 0 and filter blur(6px) with power2.out and a 0.11s stagger starting at 6%. At 50% the card lifts y -2 with sine.inOut as a barely visible breath. At 78% the children move up y -6 to opacity 0 with blur(4px) and a 0.04s stagger (power2.in), and the card fades out by 100% so the last frame is the empty ground.
records.adapt: Replace the tag, headline, paragraph and button label; change card width, radius and the background/ink colours. Keep the 10px travel, 6px blur and power2 eases; they are the quiet character of the piece.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders the .card with .el children from shot.tag/title/body/cta; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the same five tweens at 0, 0.06D, 0.5D, 0.78D and 0.85D, durations scaled by D/2, selectors scoped to el.
caveats: filter: blur on text costs a little per frame but the elements are small
from() tweens need immediateRender:false if the timeline is built lazily

records.name: Blend Modes: Color And Text
records.description: A template where text interacts with colored layers through blend modes creating a printed quality. Good for editorial motion design with a graphic tactile aesthetic.
records.move: multiply ink plates slam in, letters stamp up, cyan ghost misregisters
records.how: On a paper-coloured ground three large multiply-blended discs (pink, cyan, yellow) plus two stacked uppercase words 'PRESS RUN' in dark ink with a second cyan copy of the same words underneath as a misregistered ghost plate; a fractalNoise SVG-filter grain layer sits on top at 35% opacity. In the first 30% the discs slide in with expo.out from left, right and top (x -900, x 900, y -700), then drift a few dozen pixels with sine.inOut until 83%. From 12% the letters rise from yPercent 110 with expo.out and a 0.05s stagger, the ghost plate 0.07s later, then the ghost slides from x 14 / y -8 to x -10 / y 8 so the registration wanders. The grain layer creeps x 40 / y -30 linearly. From 82% the letters shoot up to yPercent -120 (expo.in) and the discs exit the way they came, ending on bare paper.
records.adapt: Change the two words (letters are individual spans, so split any string), the three plate colours and the paper tint, and the two small caption strings. Keep the expo.out plate entries, the 0.05s letter stagger and the ghost offset amounts; reduce grain opacity for cleaner output.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the discs, the .k and .ghost word stacks split into .l spans, captions, the inline SVG filter and the .grain div; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the same tweens at fractions of D (plates 0-0.3D, letters 0.12D, exit 0.82D). Give the SVG filter id a per-instance suffix so two shots do not collide; selectors scoped to el.
caveats: feTurbulence grain over the full frame plus multiply blending is slow to render
mix-blend-mode needs isolation on the container to match the lab

records.name: Blend Modes: Mode Showcase
records.description: A template showing multiple blend modes applied to overlapping elements.
records.move: six tiles pop in, shapes orbit inside each with different blend modes
records.how: A 3x2 grid of rounded tiles, alternating dark and light, each holding a pink disc, a cyan disc and a yellow rounded square; the cyan and yellow shapes use the tile's own mix-blend-mode (screen, multiply, difference, overlay, exclusion, hard-light) and a label pill names it. Tiles scale from .85 / y 30 / opacity 0 with expo.out and a grid stagger of 0.08s in the first 20%, labels rise in just after. A proxy tween (ease none, full 4s) drives an onUpdate that sets x/y on every shape: the pink and cyan discs orbit an ellipse (55 by 32px) on opposite sides with a per-tile phase offset, the yellow square weaves on a figure-eight and rotates 360deg. One full revolution per loop so the orbit seams, but at 86% the tiles shrink and fade out (power2.in), so the frame ends empty.
records.adapt: Change the three shape colours, the tile backgrounds, which six blend modes are shown and their labels; the grid can be 2x2 or 4x2. Keep the elliptical orbit radii and the per-tile phase offset of pi/3 so tiles read as related but not identical.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders .grid with tiles from shot.modes and sets --m per tile; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline containing the entrance/exit tweens and one proxy tween {p:1, duration:D, ease:'none'} whose onUpdate applies the orbit math with gsap.set. Replace document.querySelectorAll('.tile') with el.querySelectorAll.
caveats: 18 gsap.set calls per frame from onUpdate
orbit is seamless but the tile exit means the loop does not close visually

records.name: Blend Modes: Overlay Poster
records.description: A poster template using overlay blend mode effects to layer color and content. Good for editorial motion graphics and promotional content with a graphic quality.
records.move: overlay panels wipe over photo, poster type rises, badge spins, ticker crawls
records.how: A portrait poster: an ocean photo doing a slow Ken Burns (scale 1.12 to 1.02, y -20 to 20, linear over the whole 4s) under three mix-blend-mode overlay panels: an orange full-bleed sheet that wipes in via scaleX from the left (expo.out, first 20%), a blue lower block that grows via scaleY from the bottom, and a white inset card that slides up from yPercent 110. Three headline lines 'Open / Water / Fest' rise out of clipped rows from yPercent 105 with expo.out and 0.1s stagger from 11%; a round 'Live Sept 12' badge pops from scale 0 with back.out(1.8) and then rotates 360deg linearly across the loop; a white ticker strip scales open and its track crawls x -880 linearly. From 84% the panels collapse back (expo.in), the headline shoots up, and badge, ticker and footer fade so the loop restarts on the bare photo.
records.adapt: Swap the background image, the three headline words, badge text, ticker string and footer meta; recolour the orange/blue panels. Keep the scaleX/scaleY wipes with expo.out and the 0.1s line stagger; the ticker distance (-880) must equal one repeat of the string width.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .img (from shot.image), the three .panel divs, badge, headline rows, strip and meta inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns one gsap.timeline with the same tweens at fractions of D (wipes 0-0.2D, type 0.11D, exit 0.84D), with the Ken Burns, badge rotation and ticker as full-D linear tweens. Selectors scoped to el; the image URL becomes a shot parameter.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920
four overlay-blended layers over a full-frame photo are slow to composite
from() tweens need immediateRender:false if built after paint

records.name: Blend Modes: Type Blend
records.description: A typography template that uses blend modes to layer text over imagery in an interesting way. Good for editorial motion design and brand films where type and visuals need to work together.
records.move: three blend-mode type rows glide opposite ways over slow-zooming imagery
records.how: An aurora photo zooms slightly (scale 1.06 to 1.12, x 20 to -20, linear across 4s) under three rows of huge uppercase type, each row doubled so it can drift: row one white in difference, row two yellow in overlay, row three white in exclusion, plus a red screen-blended bar behind the middle row. The rows glide horizontally at constant speed in alternating directions for the full loop (x 0 to -820, -900 to -100, -120 to -760). In the first 20% the rows rise from yPercent 60 and opacity 0 with expo.out and 0.12s stagger, the bar scales open from the left (expo.out) and two small tags fade in. From 82% the rows lift out to yPercent -60 (expo.in, 0.08s stagger), the bar collapses to the right and the tags fade, ending on the plain photo.
records.adapt: Change the background image, the three row strings (keep each row duplicated so the drift never shows an edge), the accent colours of row two and the bar, and the two tag strings. Keep the alternating drift directions and the expo.out entry.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates .img, .bar, three .row elements with duplicated spans and the tags from shot; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with three full-D linear drift tweens plus the entry at 0-0.2D and the exit at 0.82D. Drift distances depend on the rendered text width, so measure row width in mount and drift by half of it. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: difference/exclusion/overlay over a full-frame photo costs per frame
drift distances are hardcoded for these strings

records.name: Blur: Text Scroller
records.description: A text animation template where words scroll past with a blur effect, giving a sense of speed and momentum. Good for editorial intros and title sequences.
records.move: word column steps up with directional motion blur, dims from centre
records.how: A dark frame with a hairline rule at the centre and a column of six large uppercase words (each 200px tall, with a small index label), repeated three times so the column can be scrolled through the middle copy. Every 1.5s (six holds over 9s) the column jumps up one word: y tweens by -200px with expo.inOut over 0.55s while an SVG feGaussianBlur on the column ramps its vertical stdDeviation 0 to 26 (power2.in) and back to 0 (power2.out), giving a smear in the direction of travel. A linear proxy tween drives an onUpdate that sets each row's opacity (1 down to 0.22) and scale (1 down to 0.82) by distance from the centre line, and a top/bottom gradient fade frames the window. After six steps the column has advanced exactly one copy, so frame 270 matches frame 0 and the loop is seamless.
records.adapt: Change the word list (any count; the duration becomes N * HOLD), the hold length, the font size / STEP height together, and the colours. Keep the 0.55s expo.inOut step with the blur peaking mid-move; that is the whole feel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the inline SVG filter with a unique id, the .win with the tripled word column and the fade overlay; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline whose per-word step tweens sit at (i*HOLD+0.85)/total*D, the blur attr tweens alongside, and one full-D linear proxy tween with onUpdate for the dimming. Replace getElementById with el.querySelector; STEP must match the rendered row height.
caveats: animating an SVG filter attribute on a full-width column is moderately slow
duration is derived from word count (N*1.5s), not a free parameter

records.name: Blurry Text Spin
records.description: A blurred, rotating text reveal template inspired by spatial audio and music app promos. Great for feature announcements and any brand introducing something new.
records.move: headline swings in from blurred 3D rotation, snaps sharp, spins out
records.how: Three huge blurred colour orbs (pink, blue, mint, filter blur(70px)) drift slowly on sine.inOut for the whole 2s behind a centred stack of headline, subline and a glass pill. The headline enters over the first 42% from rotationY -100, rotationX 25, z -300, scale 1.35, opacity 0 and filter blur(28px) to flat and sharp with expo.out; the subline follows at 9% from rotationY 80 / z -200 / blur(18px), and the pill fades up from y 20 / blur(10px) with power3.out at 19%. During the hold the whole wrap sways rotationY 6 / rotationX -3 with sine.inOut. From 77% the headline spins away to rotationY 90 with z -250 and blur(24px) (expo.in), the subline counter-rotates to -70 and the pill blurs out, leaving the drifting orbs.
records.adapt: Replace the headline, subline and pill strings and the three orb colours; adjust font size to the headline length. Keep the entry values (rotationY -100, blur 28px, expo.out over ~0.85s) and the exit to the opposite side; they give the spin its snap.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders the three .orb divs and the .wrap stack, with perspective set on el; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the orb drifts as full-D sine tweens and the text tweens at 0, 0.09D, 0.19D, 0.4D and 0.77D. Selectors scoped to el.
caveats: three 500px orbs with filter blur(70px) plus blur on text are slow to render
backdrop-filter on the pill adds cost

records.name: Bold Text Snap
records.description: A stacked text template where headline lines collide and settle into place over moving imagery. Great for product drops and any brand pairing bold animated typography with dynamic visuals.
records.move: lines collide from opposite sides, squash on landing, snap out
records.how: A sunset photo drifts under a dark gradient (scale 1.08 to 1.14, xPercent -1.5 to 1.5, linear across the 2s) behind three stacked uppercase lines in clipped rows. Line one slides in from xPercent -140 (expo.out, 0.55s) at 2.5%, line two from xPercent 140 at 9%, line three rises from yPercent 120 at 16%. At 31% the middle line takes the collision shock: scaleX 1.12 / scaleY 0.86 relaxing to 1 with elastic.out(1,0.45). From 77% the lines snap out in reverse order with expo.in over 0.3s each, line three up, line two left, line one right, so the loop ends on the moving photo.
records.adapt: Change the three words, the accent colour on the middle line and the background photo. Keep the 0.55s expo.out entries at 0.13s spacing and the elastic squash; shorten only the hold if the copy is longer.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates .bg from shot.image plus the three .row/.line pairs; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the same tweens at 0.025D, 0.09D, 0.16D, 0.31D and the exit from 0.77D. Scope '.line.a' etc. to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false if built after first paint

records.name: Bouncy Period
records.description: An animated period character that bounces with a springy motion. A small typographic detail that works well as a loading indicator or punctuation accent.
records.move: period drops from above, bounces with squash, hops twice, springs away
records.how: The word 'Loading' in large type with an orange circular period and a soft elliptical shadow beneath it, on a cream ground. The word rises in from yPercent 40 / opacity 0 with expo.out in the first 17%. From 5% the period falls from y -420 over 1.4s on a CustomBounce ease ('drop', strength .62, squash 3) while a paired 'drop-squash' ease drives scaleX 1.5 / scaleY .55 on each impact and the shadow scales from .3 and fades in on the same bounce ease. At 47% and 69% it hops: y -150 with power2.out over 0.32s, then back down on the bounce ease, with a stretch (scaleX .82 / scaleY 1.18) on the way up and a squash on landing while the shadow shrinks and returns. At 91% the word lifts out and the period shoots back up off-frame.
records.adapt: Change the word, the period colour and size (scale the -420 drop and -150 hop with the font size), and the caption. Keep the CustomBounce strength .62 with squash 3; it is the character of the bounce.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders the .line with word, .dot and .shadow and the caption; animate(el, shot, D) registers CustomEase/CustomBounce once (create the 'drop' eases at module load), then returns a gsap.timeline with the drop at 0.05D, hops at 0.475D and 0.69D, exit at 0.91D. Selectors scoped to el.
caveats: needs the CustomBounce and CustomEase plugins loaded before animate runs
the two eases must be created only once or CustomBounce will warn on redefinition

records.name: Cascading Text
records.description: A text animation template where lines of text fall into place in a staggered sequence. Good for feature highlights and announcement content where you want each line to land separately.
records.move: lines drop in one by one, squash on impact, spring back, exit
records.how: An aurora photo at 35% opacity zooms out slightly (scale 1.1 to 1.02, linear over 5s) behind a left-aligned stack of four headline lines in clipped rows, the third in mint, with a small numbered index on the right. Each line falls from yPercent -110 / opacity 0 with power3.in over 0.55s, starting at 3% and every 0.42s after; on landing it squashes to scaleY .86 (power2.out, 0.09s, origin at the baseline) and recovers to 1 with elastic.out(1,.4) over 0.5s. The index fades in from x 20 at 24%. From 85% the lines drop out through the bottom (yPercent 110, power3.in, 0.07s stagger) in the same order and the index fades, ending on the photo.
records.adapt: Change the line strings and count, which line is highlighted, the accent colour, the index labels and the background image. Keep the power3.in fall plus the squash-and-elastic recovery and the 0.42s cadence.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .bg, the .stack of .row/.ln pairs from shot.lines and the .num index; animate(el, shot, D) loops the lines and returns a gsap.timeline with each fall at (0.15+i*0.42)/5*D, the squash 0.5s later, the exit at 0.85D. Scope gsap.utils.toArray to el.
caveats: from() on .num needs immediateRender:false if built lazily

records.name: Countdown: Bold
records.description: A countdown template with large animated numbers. Perfect for event announcements and social teasers where building anticipation is the point.
records.move: digits punch in from blur, ring draws each beat, GO pops
records.how: A dark radial-gradient ground, a 560px SVG circle ring at centre, four stacked numerals (3, 2, 1 and a yellow GO) and a small caption. Each second for the first 75%, one digit lands: from scale 2.6, opacity 0 and filter blur(30px) to sharp at 1 with expo.out over 0.45s, a slow settle to scale .92 over 0.35s, then a collapse to scale .6 with blur(14px) and expo.in over 0.22s; simultaneously the ring draws 0% to 100% with DrawSVG (power1.inOut, 0.95s) and the background pulses scale 1.03. At 75% GO pops from scale .3 / rotation -8 with back.out(2.5) while a full-frame white flash decays from opacity .9 (power2.out) and the ring turns yellow and redraws with expo.out; at 94% GO blows out to scale 1.6 with blur and the ring and caption fade, ending on the empty ground.
records.adapt: Change the count (any digits; one beat per second), the GO word and its accent colour, the caption and ring stroke. Keep the 0.45s expo.out landing from blur, the 0.35s settle and the flash on the last beat; a longer count means a longer D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .bg, the ring SVG (unique id), one .n per step from shot.steps and the .sub; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline placing beat i at i/steps*D with the same relative durations, the GO/flash at (steps-1)/steps*D. DrawSVGPlugin must be registered; scope '#ring' etc. to el via querySelector.
caveats: filter: blur on 520px text costs per frame
the flash tween uses immediateRender:false and must keep it
duration is tied to step count

records.name: Counter: 1,000 Figma Plugin Installs
records.description: An animated counter template celebrating a milestone number. Good for product growth announcements and community milestone posts.
records.move: number counts up with expo ease, pops on landing, confetti bursts
records.how: A square dark card with a violet radial glow, a three-bar Figma-style logo, a 300px tabular numeral, a label and a violet 'Thank you' pill. The logo bars pop in from scale 0 / x -20 with back.out(2) and 0.08s stagger in the first 17%; the numeral fades up from scale .9 and a proxy value tweens 0 to 1000 with expo.inOut over 53% of the duration, written each frame as a locale-formatted string. At 60% the number pops to scale 1.1 (0.12s) and relaxes with elastic.out(1,.35), the pill springs in with back.out(2), the glow expands scale .8 to 1.2 with expo.out, and 60 seeded confetti rectangles fly out radially 260 to 640px with random rotation, fading over 0.9 to 1.3s (power2.out). At 90% everything lifts and fades (y -20, power2.in) to the glow alone.
records.adapt: Change the target number, the label, pill text, brand mark and the confetti/glow palette; format via toLocaleString or a custom formatter. Keep the expo.inOut count with the pop-and-elastic landing and the confetti burst timed to the landing.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders glow, logo, .num, label, pill and an empty confetti container; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the count tween (onUpdate writing textContent) from 0.07D for 0.53D, landing at 0.6D, and the 60 confetti fromTo tweens generated with a seeded rng so renders are deterministic. Replace getElementById with el.querySelector.
caveats: square 1080x1080
60 confetti elements are tweened individually; fine, but generate with a seeded rng
from() tweens need immediateRender:false if built lazily

records.name: CRT Effect
records.description: A CRT screen effect that adds scanlines, noise, and a retro monitor look to your animations. Perfect for vintage-inspired motion graphics and title sequences.
records.move: CRT powers on, text scrambles in, scanlines flicker and tear, powers off
records.how: A rounded 'tube' with an inset shadow holds green glowing text (two headline words and a monospace status line with a block cursor) under a stack of overlays: a fractalNoise SVG filter noise layer, repeating-gradient scanlines in multiply, a rolling bright band, a black flicker layer, a vignette and a glass highlight. Power-on: the content scales from scaleY .01 / scaleX 1.3 to full with expo.out over the first 12%. From 10% the two words scramble in with ScrambleTextPlugin (chars '01#$%&/', 0.6s each) and the status line scrambles over 1.2s from 27%. A linear proxy tween drives, every frame, the noise seed (advances per frame), flicker opacity from a seeded random table (up to .12), the roll band's translateY sweeping the tube twice per loop, and an feDisplacementMap scale that jumps to 22 on random frames for horizontal tears; two short x-jitter yoyo bursts hit at 47% and 77%. Power-off from 89%: collapse to a bright line (scaleY .01, expo.in) then to nothing.
records.adapt: Change the two headline words, the status string, the phosphor colour (text, shadow and the feColorMatrix tint) and the tube inset. Keep the power-on/off scale choreography and the per-frame noise-seed/flicker driver; reduce tear probability (.93 threshold) for a calmer look.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the inline SVG filters with per-instance ids, the .tube with .content and the overlay layers; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the power-on at 0, scrambles at 0.1D/0.175D/0.27D, one full-D linear proxy tween whose onUpdate does the seed/flicker/roll/tear writes (using a seeded rng table built in mount), jitter bursts at 0.47D and 0.77D and the power-off at 0.89D. Replace document.querySelector calls with el.querySelector and register ScrambleTextPlugin.
caveats: the fromTo text:'' start values need TextPlugin, which is not loaded; gsap ignores them and scrambleText still works
two SVG filters (noise seed changed every frame, displacement map) plus blend layers are slow to render
setAttribute on the noise seed each frame forces a filter re-render

records.name: Design: Negative Mask Effect
records.description: A mask template that reveals content through inverted shapes. Works for editorial motion work and creative reveal sequences.
records.move: white difference-blend shapes sweep across type, inverting whatever they cover
records.how: On a white ground the words 'Negative' (grotesk caps) and 'space' (italic serif) sit centred in black, with two small footer captions. Four white shapes in mix-blend-mode difference (a 520px circle, a 360px circle, a tilted 260x900 bar and a 300px rounded square) start off-frame and traverse the stage: the big circle crosses left to right growing from scale .6 to 1.1 with power2.inOut over 80% of the duration, the small circle drops 800px with power1.inOut, the bar whips across with expo.inOut, and the square travels diagonally up-left rotating 90deg. Where a shape overlaps the black type it renders white on black, so the letters appear cut out of the shapes. The type rises in from yPercent 40 (expo.out, 0.12s stagger) in the first 20% and lifts out at 87% (expo.in), ending on white.
records.adapt: Change the two words and their typefaces, the caption strings and the shape sizes/paths; on a coloured ground difference yields colour inversions instead of black/white. Keep the long overlapping inOut sweeps so shapes cross the type at different moments.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders the .type stack, footers and the four .neg shapes with isolation on el; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the type entry at 0, the sweeps starting at 0.05D, 0.15D, 0.25D and 0.275D with durations of 0.8D, 0.75D, 0.55D and 0.65D, and the exit at 0.875D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: mix-blend-mode difference over large shapes is moderately expensive
requires isolation:isolate on the container so the blend does not leak into the page

records.name: Elastic Text
records.description: A bold, playful stretch-and-snap text animation template. Great for mood-driven social posts and any brand with a casual, punchy voice.
records.move: letters yank in tall and thin, snap elastic, tug wide, rip out
records.how: An orange ground with a yellow 520px blob breathing behind seven uppercase letter spans and a small caption. The blob scales .9 to 1.08 and rotates 25deg with sine.inOut yoyo over the 2s. Letters arrive from scaleY 3.4 / scaleX .35 / yPercent -90 / opacity 0 with power2.in over 0.12s and a 0.05s stagger from 2.5%, then relax to natural shape with elastic.out(1.15, 0.38) over 0.85s. At 55% a second tug stretches every letter to scaleX 1.55 / scaleY .72 with power3.in staggered from the centre, snapping back with elastic.out(1.2, 0.35). At 84% the letters are yanked up as tall thin ribbons (scaleY 3, scaleX .3, yPercent -120, power3.in) and the caption fades, leaving the blob.
records.adapt: Change the word (split into .ch spans), the ground/blob/ink colours and the caption. Keep the elastic.out parameters and the two-phase stretch; adjust font size for word length.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders the .blob, the .word split into .ch spans and .sub; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the entry at 0.025D, elastic settle at 0.085D, the tug at 0.55D and the exit at 0.84D, with the blob yoyo as a D/2 tween repeated once. Use el.querySelectorAll('.ch').
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false if built after paint

records.name: Feature List [Apple Event]
records.description: A feature list template with the measured pacing of an Apple event presentation. Good for product launches and keynote-style content where each feature deserves its own moment.
records.move: each feature blurs in large at hero, then recedes small into stack
records.how: Black keynote frame with a violet blurred glow drifting sine.inOut across the 4s, a grey kicker, three feature lines (violet dot, white lead, grey tail), a hairline rule that draws via scaleX with expo.out and a footer. Every 1.1s from 9%, one feature resolves at the hero position: opacity 0 to 1, filter blur(18px) to 0 and x 40 to 0 with power3.out over 0.7s, no bounce. When the next arrives, the previous one recedes: y moves up to its slot in a stack and scale drops to .42 with power3.inOut over 0.75s while its lead colour dims to grey. The last feature joins the stack at 81%; at 90% every line, kicker and footer blur out (blur(10px), power2.in, 0.03s stagger) and the rule retracts from the right.
records.adapt: Change the kicker, the lead/tail pairs (three to five), the accent colour and the footer; LIST_Y slots must be regenerated for the item count and the hero y from the font size. Keep the 1.1s beat, the 0.7s power3.out blur-in and the scale .42 recede.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders glow, kicker, .item lines from shot.features, rule and foot, and applies the initial gsap.set state; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with item i at (0.35+i*1.1)/4*D, recedes at at+beat-0.1, and the exit at 0.9D. Scope '#i1'-style ids to el classes.
caveats: filter blur(40px) on the 1100px glow plus text blur is slow to render
the initial gsap.set must run in mount before the timeline is built

records.name: Glide
records.description: A smooth animation template from Antinomy with fluid elegant motion. Works for product showcases and abstract visual content where subtlety is the goal.
records.move: blurred colour blobs, serif letters and hairlines all sway on sines, seamless
records.how: Three large blurred radial blobs (blue, pink, mint, screen-blended, blur(70px)), a static SVG fractalNoise grain at 18%, a thin 560px ring, two gradient hairlines above and below, an italic serif title split into letter spans, and a spaced caption. There is no timeline: seek(t) maps t to a phase p over 2pi and sets every property as a sine of p: blobs drift 120 to 160px and breathe 8 to 12% in scale, each letter bobs y 22 / x 6 / rotate 1.5deg with a 0.55 rad phase offset per letter and opacity .86 to 1, the hairlines slide x 220 in opposite directions while scaleX breathes .55 to 1.05, the ring spins 360 per loop with a 3deg skew wobble, and the caption's letter-spacing and opacity pulse. Because every value is periodic in D, frame 0 equals frame 90 and the loop is seamless.
records.adapt: Change the title word (split into spans), the three blob colours, the caption and the serif face; the amplitudes (22px letter bob, 140px blob drift) can be scaled to taste. Keep everything as pure sines of the phase so it stays seamless.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates blobs, grain SVG (unique filter id), ring, lines, title spans and caption; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline holding one proxy tween {p: 0 to 1, duration D, ease 'none'} whose onUpdate runs the same gsap.set calls with phase p*2pi, targets resolved once from el in mount.
caveats: three 500-700px elements with filter blur(70px) are slow to render
the fx.register seek loop must become an onUpdate proxy tween on the returned timeline

records.name: Glitch 01: Text Reveal
records.description: A text reveal template with digital glitch distortion effects. Good for tech brand intros and motion design with a more edgy aesthetic.
records.move: canvas text wipes in under RGB-split slice tears, settles, tears out again
records.how: A full-frame 2D canvas redrawn every frame from an offscreen text mask ('SYSTEM ONLINE' plus a mint spaced subline). A reveal value wipes the mask in from the left with expo.out over the first 30%, holds fully visible until 78%, then wipes back out with expo.in. A glitch intensity envelope is hard during the reveal (decaying 1 to 0), near zero while settled with occasional sine-timed hiccups, and ramps back to 1 for the exit. Each frame, with a per-frame seeded rng, the frame is cut into 6 to 28 horizontal slices that shift up to 140px, some rows dropped, each slice drawn as red and cyan tinted copies offset by up to 18px in 'lighter' blend under the clean copy; up to 30 mint/white noise chips scatter, faint scanlines step every 4px, and a soft mint scan bar sweeps top to bottom once per loop. The canvas ends empty with the bar back at the top, so it loops visually.
records.adapt: Change the two strings, the font, the accent colour used for chips/subline/bar, and the ink/paper colours; the intensity envelope breakpoints (0.9s, 2.1s, 2.35s) scale with D. Keep the per-frame seeded rng so renders are deterministic and the slice/split amplitudes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends a canvas sized to the shot and two offscreen canvases, preloads the font via document.fonts.load, and pre-renders the text mask; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with one proxy tween {t: 0 to D, ease 'none'} whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) drawing code. gsap.parseEase is used for the reveal curves; no document-level selectors beyond the canvas, but W/H must come from the canvas, not constants.
caveats: fx.register canvas seek loop must become an onUpdate tween on the returned timeline
redraws the full 1280x720 canvas up to 3 times per slice each frame; moderately slow
the canvas is a fixed 1280x720 backing store scaled by CSS
needs the font loaded before the first frame or the mask is drawn in a fallback face

records.name: Glitch 02: Text Reveal
records.description: A second glitch text reveal template with different distortion characteristics. Works alongside the first glitch template for variety within the same aesthetic.
records.move: type warps in through displacement, RGB ghosts lock, twitches, warps out
records.how: A dark frame with a hairline border, a grain SVG layer, the headline 'Break Through' inside a wrap filtered by an feTurbulence-driven feDisplacementMap, red and cyan screen-blended ghost copies of the headline behind it, a red monospace subline and two thin white difference-blend tear bars. A state object tweens the displacement scale from 260 to 0 with expo.out over the first 27% (seed and frequency also sliding) while the headline flickers in with steps(6) and the ghosts slide in from x -70 / 70 to 0 fading out with expo.out; the subline resolves via ScrambleTextPlugin over 1.2s from 7%. At 47% and 67% short hits: displacement spikes to 90 / 60 for 0.08s, the ghosts flash apart yoyo, the wrap jolts x 24 / -16, and a tear bar sweeps vertically. At 86% the displacement ramps to 320 with expo.in, ghosts fly apart to x -90 / 90, and the text cuts out in steps(5), ending on the empty frame.
records.adapt: Change the headline (two lines), the subline string, the tag, the ghost colours and the accent red; keep the displacement envelope (260 in, spikes, 320 out) and the stepped opacity eases, which are what makes it read as signal loss rather than a fade.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the two inline SVG filters with per-instance ids, the grain, frame, tag, both ghosts, .wrap and the bars; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline containing the state-object tweens (onUpdate writing the filter attributes) at 0, 0.475D, 0.675D and 0.86D plus the DOM tweens at the same fractions. Register ScrambleTextPlugin; replace getElementById with el.querySelector.
caveats: feDisplacementMap over the whole wrap plus the grain filter is slow to render
the stray .to('.wrap', {x:0, duration:0.01}) is a no-op

records.name: Glitchy Text Reveal
records.description: An animated text template inspired by sportswear branding. Great for community events and any brand driving RSVPs.
records.move: lines slam in stepped, clip-path slices tear lime and pink, stepped exit
records.how: A square dark frame with a tilted lime stripe drifting xPercent -8 to 8 linearly across the 2s, a small top caption, three stacked uppercase lines (the middle one knocked out dark on the stripe) and a lime meta row. Each line carries two absolutely-positioned coloured copies (lime and pink, screen-blended). Lines slam in alternately from xPercent -60 / 60 with steps(5) over 0.3s starting at 4% and every 0.16s; for six 0.055s ticks after each landing the copies are set to random horizontal clip-path inset bands shifted up to 45px either way, then hidden, so slices of colour tear off and snap back. At 57% a single twitch repeats one slice on every line with an 8px jolt. From 83% the lines exit the opposite way with steps(4) and the meta and caption cut out in steps(2), ending on the drifting stripe.
records.adapt: Change the three line strings (each needs its two .s copies), the caption and meta words, and the lime/pink pair; the stripe colour and angle. Keep the steps() eases and the 0.055s slice cadence; regenerate slice bands from a seeded rng so the render is deterministic.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds stripe, top, the .line stack with .s.a/.s.b copies from shot.lines and the .meta row; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with each line at (0.08+i*0.16)/2*D, its six set() ticks, the twitch at 0.575D and the exit at 0.83D, using fx-style seeded rng for the clip bands. Scope gsap.utils.toArray('.line') to el.
caveats: square 1080x1080
uses many timeline set() calls; fine, but they must be placed at absolute times not chained

records.name: Gradients: Animated List
records.description: A list template where each item has its own animated gradient treatment. Ideal for feature lists and visual menus where color adds hierarchy.
records.move: gradient rows scale in from left, gradients drift, sheens cross, reverse exit
records.how: A dark frame with a small uppercase header and four full-width rounded rows, each filled with its own four-stop diagonal gradient at 300% background-size, containing an index number, a title and a description, plus a skewed white sheen strip. Every row's gradient drifts backgroundPosition 0% to 100% linearly on a repeat -1 loop with a different period (6s divided by 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75). Rows enter from xPercent -8, scaleX .6 and opacity 0 with expo.out over 0.9s, one every 0.16s from 4%, and their text rises from y 24 with power3.out and 0.06s stagger. From 27% a sheen crosses each row (x -260 to 1300, power2.inOut, 1.1s) at 0.35s intervals, while the list breathes y -6 with sine.inOut yoyo. From 89% the rows collapse back (xPercent 6, scaleX .7, power3.in) in reverse order and the header fades, ending on the dark frame.
records.adapt: Change the header, the row count and their number/title/description strings, and each row's gradient stops. Keep the expo.out entry with scaleX from .6, the 0.16s cadence and the sheen sweep; each row's gradient period should still differ so they never sync.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the .head and .list of .row elements (with .g gradient and .sheen children) from shot.items; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the per-row gradient drifts (repeat -1 for D/(1+i*0.25)), entries at (0.25+i*0.16)/6*D, sheens at (1.6+i*0.35)/6*D and the exit at 0.89D. Scope gsap.utils.toArray('.row') to el.
caveats: animating background-position on four 300%-size gradients is fine but not free
repeat:-1 gradient tweens make tl.duration() infinite: use a finite repeat count in the port
from() text tweens need immediateRender:false if built lazily

records.name: Gradients: Logo Reveal
records.description: A logo reveal template where shifting gradient layers surface the mark. Good for brand intros where color is part of the identity.
records.move: blurred gradient sheets sweep in, ring draws on, mark rises, name reveals
records.how: Four oversized blurred gradient layers in screen blend (pink radial, blue radial, amber radial and a violet-cyan conic) plus a centred SVG mark (a gradient-stroked ring and a white triangle under a clip), a letter-spaced wordmark split into spans, a tag line and a dark veil. The veil fades out over the first 24% with power2.out while the layers sweep in from off-frame with power2.inOut over 52%: pink from lower-left rotating -20 to 10, blue from upper-right, amber rising from below scaling .7 to 1.1, the conic spinning to 140deg while fading up to .45. At 18% the ring draws with DrawSVG 0 to 100% with expo.inOut over 1.3s while the mark scales from .7 and rotate -30 with expo.out; the triangle rises from y 120 at 30%. Letters rise from yPercent 110 (expo.out, 0.07s stagger) at 38% and the tag settles its letter-spacing from .6em. The layers keep drifting through the hold, then at 86% they blow out (scale 1.3, opacity 0), the mark shrinks to 0 rotating 60deg, and name and tag lift away, ending on the dark ground.
records.adapt: Replace the SVG mark (keep a stroke path for the draw-on), the wordmark letters, the tag and the four layer gradient colours; the gradient id must be unique per instance. Keep the 2.6s power2.inOut sweep and the expo.inOut ring draw.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the four .layer divs, the .mark SVG with suffixed gradient/clip ids, .name spans, .tag and .veil; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline placing the sweeps at 0-0.03D, veil at 0, ring draw at 0.18D, triangle 0.3D, name 0.38D, drift 0.52D and exit at 0.86D. Register DrawSVGPlugin; the gsap.set('#ring', drawSVG 0) belongs in mount, scoped via el.querySelector.
caveats: four 180%-size layers with filter blur(30px) in screen blend are slow to render
SVG gradient and clipPath ids collide if two instances share a document

records.name: Morph: Dots To Text
records.description: An animation template where dots gradually rearrange themselves to spell out text. A distinctive way to open a reel or introduce a brand name without a standard text reveal.
records.move: dots drift on arcs into a word, rearrange into second word, scatter
records.how: A canvas with 900 small dots. In mount, two words ('ACME', 'STUDIO') are rasterised at 300px and each sampled into 900 points by seeded rejection sampling. seek(t) interpolates every dot between states with power3.inOut, each dot delayed by its own random fraction of a spread window, and adds a sideways sine arc so dots swing rather than fly straight: from 2% to 36% a random cloud gathers into the first word (1.2s spread), holds until 47%, rearranges into the second word by 76%, holds, then disperses back toward the cloud from 87% to 100%. Settled dots grow slightly and shift hue from blue toward pink (hsl 200 to 360) while every dot breathes 1.6px on sines so the word never freezes. The end cloud is the same seeded start cloud, so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Change the two words (or use one), the font, dot count N, dot colour range and the background; the segment boundaries (3.2, 4.2, 6.8, 7.8) scale with D. Keep the per-dot delay spread and the arc so the transition reads as rearranging.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas, waits for the font, samples the words once with a seeded rng and stores cloud/A/B/delay/size arrays; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with one proxy tween {t: 0 to D, ease 'none'} whose onUpdate runs the mix-and-draw code. Sampling in the first seek must move to mount; W/H come from the canvas.
caveats: fx.register canvas seek loop must become an onUpdate tween on the returned timeline
sampling uses getImageData on a 1280x720 canvas: do it once in mount, not per frame
900 arc fills per frame is fine, but a fixed 1280x720 backing store is assumed

records.name: Morph: Inflating Text
records.description: A text animation template where letters swell and inflate with a soft morphing effect. Works for playful headlines and expressive brand animations.
records.move: letters pop in, strokes inflate so glyphs balloon and fuse through goo
records.how: An SVG with the word 'PUFFY' as five text elements (stroke same colour as fill, paint-order stroke) inside a group filtered by a gooey feGaussianBlur plus alpha-boost feColorMatrix, on a cream ground with a small caption. Letters pop from scale 0 with back.out(2.5) and 0.06s stagger in the first 27%. From 17% the stroke-width attribute swells 0 to 16 and the glyph scales to 1.12 / 1.06 with elastic.out(1.1, 0.5), so the letters puff up and merge where they touch. At 57% they exhale: stroke to 6 and scaleY .96 with power2.inOut staggered from the end. At 80% they over-inflate (stroke 22, scale 1.25, power3.in) and at 92% collapse to scale 0, ending on the empty ground.
records.adapt: Change the word (letters are laid out at 150px pitch from centre, so adjust pitch for width), the ink colour (fill and stroke must match) and the caption; the goo blur/alpha values set how much letters fuse. Keep the elastic inflate and the exhale/over-inflate rhythm.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the SVG with a per-instance filter id and one text element per letter, setting transformOrigin; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the pop at 0.025D, inflate 0.175D, exhale 0.575D, over-inflate 0.8D and collapse 0.925D. Use el.querySelector for the group; the viewBox is 1280x720 so it scales with el.
caveats: the goo filter (blur plus colour matrix) on large text is moderately slow
from() scale tween needs immediateRender:false if built lazily

records.name: Morph: Lines To Text
records.description: An animation template where lines rearrange and resolve into readable text. Works for abstract intros and data-driven motion graphics.
records.move: horizontal rules fly into the scanline runs of a word, fly back
records.how: A canvas: in mount, the word 'DATA' is rasterised at 280px and scanned every 7px row into horizontal runs, giving a few hundred short line segments that together form the glyphs. Each segment is assigned a start state on one of 14 long horizontal rules spread over the frame, with a random x, a random length 40 to 540px and a random delay up to 0.25s. seek(t) interpolates each segment's x0, x1 and y from its rule to its glyph position with expo.inOut: assembling over the first 55% (each over 0.3s after its delay), holding until 72%, then flying back over 0.16s. Colour shifts from blue (hsl 205) toward white as p approaches 1, so the word turns solid white when it locks. The frame ends with segments returning to the rules, close to the first frame.
records.adapt: Change the word and font (longer words need a smaller size), the STEP row pitch (thicker or thinner lines), the number of origin rules and the background/line colours. The whole thing is 1s; scale the 0.55/0.72 boundaries with D and keep expo.inOut.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas, waits for the font, builds the segment list once with a seeded rng; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with one proxy tween {t: 0 to D, ease 'none'} whose onUpdate clears and strokes every segment at its interpolated position. Move build() out of the first seek into mount; W/H from the canvas.
caveats: fx.register canvas seek loop must become an onUpdate tween on the returned timeline
loop nearly closes: segments with the largest delay are still returning at the last frame
getImageData scan must run once in mount, not in seek
fixed 1280x720 canvas backing store

records.name: Morph: Shape To Text
records.description: A morphing animation template where an abstract shape gradually transforms into readable text. Good for concept-driven openers and creative intros.
records.move: gooey blob stretches into a bar, letters bud out, collapse back
records.how: An SVG on near-black with a yellow blob path and five yellow text letters (stroke same as fill) sharing a gooey filter (feGaussianBlur 10 plus alpha-boost colour matrix) so touching shapes fuse. The blob morphs with MorphSVG to a second wobbly shape over the first 22% (sine.inOut), then to a long horizontal bar by 47% (expo.inOut). From 40% the letters scale up from 0 to 1.15 with back.out(1.8) staggered from the centre while their stroke-width grows to 14, budding out of the bar; the bar flattens to scaleY .05 and the letters settle to scale 1 with stroke 4 by 82%. At 81% the letters collapse to scale 0 (stroke 20, power3.in, from the edges) as the bar re-inflates to full scale, and a set() at the very end snaps the path back to the original blob so the loop restarts on the shape.
records.adapt: Change the word (150px letter pitch from centre), the ink colour (fill and stroke together), the blob path pair and the caption. Keep the goo filter values and the blob-to-bar expo.inOut, which is what makes the letters read as emerging from the shape.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the SVG with a per-instance filter id, the blob path and one text element per letter with scale 0 set; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the morphs at 0 and 0.225D, letter pop 0.4D, bar flatten 0.475D, settle 0.65D, collapse 0.81D and the reset set() at D. Register MorphSVGPlugin; scope '#blob' to el.querySelector.
caveats: the return morph targets '#blob' (its own current data) so it is a no-op; the original shape is restored by a hard set() at the last frame, not tweened
letters do not morph from the shape, they pop out of the bar: an approximation of the description
goo filter on large glyphs is moderately slow

records.name: Motion Blur
records.description: A blur-in text template inspired by fintech and app marketing. Great for app promos and any brand delivering a clean, confident message.
records.move: headline lines rush in from right with blur streak, resolve sharp
records.how: A navy frame with a mint radial glow drifting sine.inOut over the 2s, a small logo top-right, three stacked 112px lines (the third in mint) filtered by an SVG feGaussianBlur, and a glassy transaction pill filtered by a second blur. From 2.5% each line arrives from x 520, opacity 0 and scaleX 1.25 with expo.out over 0.7s, 0.14s apart, while the horizontal stdDeviation of the text blur ramps 48 to 0 with expo.out so the streak sharpens as the lines land. At 27% the pill rises from y 90 with a vertical blur 30 to 0 (expo.out) and the logo fades in from x 30. At 75% the lines exit to x -520 with scaleX 1.25 and the blur returning to 48 (expo.in, 0.05s stagger), the pill drops out with vertical blur, and the logo fades, ending on the glow.
records.adapt: Change the three lines, the accent colour, the pill contents and the logo text. Keep the 0.7s expo.out entry paired with the 48px horizontal blur decay; the blur must always track the direction of travel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the two inline SVG filters with per-instance ids, glow, logo, .stack rows and the .pill; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the line tweens at (0.05+i*0.14)/2*D, the blur proxy tweens (onUpdate writing stdDeviation) alongside, the pill at 0.275D and the exit at 0.75D. Replace getElementById with el.querySelector.
caveats: animating an SVG blur filter on three 112px lines each frame is moderately slow
from() on .logo needs immediateRender:false if built lazily

records.name: Motion Design: Looped Text
records.description: A text template that scrolls in a continuous loop without a visible seam. Good for marquee effects and compositions that need ongoing typographic motion.
records.move: three type bands marquee in alternating directions, seamless one-unit seam
records.how: A saturated blue frame with three 150px uppercase bands: solid white words with yellow dot separators on the top and bottom rows, outlined (text-stroke) words on the middle row. Each band's track repeats the four-word unit three times. seek(t) measures the unit width once, then sets x linearly: the outer bands move left by exactly one unit width over the 1s duration, the middle band moves right by the same amount, so frame D equals frame 0 and the marquee is seamless. No eases, no entry or exit.
records.adapt: Change the word list, colours, which band is outlined, band count and font size; duration sets the speed (one unit per D). Keep the linear motion and measured unit width so the seam stays invisible.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the bands and fills each track with the unit repeated three times, measuring unit width after layout; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with three fromTo x tweens of duration D and ease 'none' (or one proxy tween with onUpdate). Scope gsap.utils.toArray('.track') to el; widths depend on el being laid out before measuring.
caveats: unit width is measured with getBoundingClientRect, so measure after the font has loaded and el is in the document
no entry or exit; it is a pure marquee

records.name: Multiply
records.description: A blend mode template from Antinomy using multiply effects to create layered color interactions between elements. Works for editorial motion graphics and experimental visual work.
records.move: multiply-blended discs, bars and serif word drift through each other on sines
records.how: On a paper ground, three large multiply-blended discs (red, blue, yellow), a teal horizontal bar and a pink vertical bar, plus two copies of the serif word 'Multiply', one upright in near-black and one italic in blue, both multiply-blended. No timeline: seek(t) maps t to a phase over 2pi and sets every transform as a sine or cosine of it: the discs drift 200 to 300px in x and 60 to 120px in y while breathing 10 to 15% in scale, the bars slide 220 to 240px and rotate plus or minus 14 to 18deg with a scaleX/scaleY breath, and the two words counter-drift x 40 / y 12 in opposite phase. Where shapes overlap, the multiply blend stacks their colours like ink. Every value is periodic in the 8s so the last frame returns to the first.
records.adapt: Change the word (and whether it is doubled), the five shape colours, sizes and starting positions, the paper tint and the captions; amplitudes can scale with the frame. Keep everything as sines of the phase so the loop stays seamless.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the five .s shapes, the two .t words and captions inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline holding one proxy tween {p: 0 to 1, duration D, ease 'none'} whose onUpdate runs the gsap.set calls with phase p*2pi on targets resolved once from el.
caveats: seven multiply-blended layers over most of the frame are moderately expensive to composite
the fx.register seek loop must become an onUpdate proxy tween on the returned timeline
no entry or exit: it is a pure ambient loop

records.name: Save The Date
records.description: An animated save-the-date template with a clean elegant reveal. Great for event invitations and launch announcements where you want the first impression to feel considered.
records.move: frame draws edge by edge, words rise under masks, rings breathe
records.how: A square cream card: a hairline frame inset 64px whose four edges are each hidden by a cover strip, two concentric ornament rings, a red centre dot, and a centred column of eyebrow, vertical rule, a three-word serif title (middle word italic) in clipped spans, a spaced date and an italic venue line. Over the first 34% the four covers scale to 0 with expo.inOut in sequence (top, right, bottom, left, 0.4s apart) so the frame appears to draw itself. The rings scale up from .6/.5 and fade in with expo.out, then breathe 5% on a sine yoyo through the hold. From 9% the eyebrow tightens its letter-spacing from .9em to .48em with power3.out, the rule grows scaleY 0 to 1 with expo.inOut at 16%, the title words rise from yPercent 110 with expo.out and 0.16s stagger at 21%, the date characters fade up with 0.09s stagger at 34% and the venue at 41%; the column drifts y 6 to -6 during the hold. From 84% the words lift out (expo.in), copy fades, the rule retracts, the rings blow out, and the covers scale back so the frame is hidden again for the loop.
records.adapt: Change the eyebrow, three title words, date parts, venue and the ink/paper/accent colours and typefaces. Keep the sequential expo.inOut frame draw (1.1s per edge, 0.4s apart) and the 0.16s word stagger; it is meant to feel unhurried.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the .frame with its four cover strips (applying the gsap.set positions), the rings, the dot and the .col from shot fields; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the covers at 0.014D to 0.19D, copy from 0.086D to 0.41D, drift 0.36D, exit 0.84D. Replace '#fa'-style ids with classes scoped to el.
caveats: square 1080x1080
from() on letterSpacing and yPercent needs immediateRender:false if built lazily

records.name: Sliding Text Reveal
records.description: A text reveal template where words slide in from behind a mask. Great for title sequences and section headers where you want the text to feel deliberate.
records.move: colour bar wipes across each row, retracts, words slide in behind it
records.how: A cream frame with a greyscale photo at 35% in multiply drifting xPercent -2 to 2 linearly, a left-aligned stack of three rows (two uppercase grotesk headlines and a smaller italic serif row in rust), a short rule and a meta line. Each row is clipped and holds a solid mask block: from 3% and every 0.22s, the mask scales open from the left (scaleX 0 to 1, expo.inOut, 0.45s), flips its origin to the right and retracts (scaleX to 0, expo.inOut, 0.5s) while the row's words slide in from fully left of their slot (x -(offsetLeft+width+40), expo.out, 0.07s stagger) so they appear to be dragged in behind the retreating bar. The rule grows from scaleX 0 at 30% and the meta line rises from yPercent 120. From 78% the words slide out to the right under the mask edge (expo.in, 0.08s per row), the rule retracts to the right and the meta lifts out, ending on the paper and photo.
records.adapt: Change the row strings (each word is a .w span), the mask colours (ink and accent), the typefaces and the photo; row count can grow with the 0.22s cadence. Keep the wipe-open then retract-with-origin-flip pattern and the expo eases.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders .grain, the .stack rows with .words and .mask, the rule and meta; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with each row at (0.1+i*0.22)/3*D, the rule at 0.3D and exit at 0.78D. The from() x values are computed from offsetLeft/offsetWidth, so el must be laid out before animate runs; scope gsap.utils.toArray('.row') to el.
caveats: slide distances read offsetLeft/offsetWidth at build time, so the timeline must be built after layout and fonts
from() tweens need immediateRender:false if built lazily
multiply-blended photo with grayscale/contrast filter over the full frame adds cost

records.name: Sliding Title Reveal [Apple Event]
records.description: A title reveal template inspired by Apple keynote presentation design. Good for premium product announcements and polished presentation openers.
records.move: glow blooms, title words rise through mask, blur clears, keynote cut left
records.how: A black stage with a blurred violet-pink radial glow, a small rounded logo tile, a kicker line, three gradient-filled title words and a subline, each in an overflow-hidden row, plus a dateline at the bottom. The glow scales 0.6 to 1 with opacity over the first 40% (power2.out) then drifts to scale 1.15 and xPercent 6 (sine.inOut); the logo scales in (expo.out), the kicker span rises yPercent 120 to 0, and the title words rise yPercent 115 to 0 while filter blur(14px) clears, staggered 0.12s, 12% to 40% of the duration (expo.out); the subline and dateline follow. From 82% everything exits: words slide xPercent -40 and fade with a 0.05 stagger (expo.in), kicker and sub fly up yPercent -120, logo and dateline fade, the glow shrinks and fades, so the last frame is black like the first.
records.adapt: Replace the kicker, title words, subline and dateline strings, the two glow colours, the title gradient and the logo tile; add or remove title words (the stagger scales with count). Keep the expo.out 1.1s word rise, the blur clear, and the fast expo.in exit at 82%.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the glow, logo, kicker, title words, sub and dateline from shot text; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same GSAP timeline with all positions scaled as fractions of D (glow 0 to 0.4D, words 0.125D, exit at 0.825D). All selectors must be scoped with el.querySelectorAll; nothing else blocks a direct port.
caveats: filter: blur(40px) on an 1100x520 glow plus animated blur on gradient-clipped text is heavy to render
from() tweens rely on immediateRender to hide elements before their start time

records.name: Snappy Text Stretch
records.description: A snappy text template inspired by film festival announcements. Great for animated event promos and any brand making a bold opening statement.
records.move: lines shoot up stretched tall, snap, punch wide, squash flat on exit
records.how: Two huge uppercase lines (the second an outlined knockout) on an acid-yellow stage, a circular badge top-right and a small tag bottom-left. Each line starts yPercent 110 with scaleY 3.2 and scaleX 0.7 and snaps to 0/1/1 in 0.55s (expo.out) starting at 2.5% and 10% of the duration. At 40% both lines punch to scaleX 1.25 scaleY 0.85 (power2.in, 0.12s) and rebound with elastic.out(1,0.5) over 0.45s, staggered 0.06s; the badge scales from 0 with rotate -90 (back.out(2)) then rotates linearly to 30deg; the tag rises through its mask. At 80% the lines squash to scaleY 0.05 and drop yPercent 60 (expo.in), the badge scales to 0 and the tag flies up, so the stage is empty at both ends.
records.adapt: Change the two words, the badge text, the tag, the stage colour and the text colours; keep the 3.2 tall-stretch entry, the 0.12s wide punch with its elastic rebound at 40%, and the squash-drop exit at 80%.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the two overflow-hidden rows, badge and tag; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with positions at 0.025D, 0.1D, 0.4D, 0.46D and 0.8D. Selectors must be scoped to el; otherwise a direct port.
caveats: the squashed lines (scaleY 0.05, yPercent 60) may leave a hairline visible at the row edge on the last frame

records.name: Squeeze
records.description: An animation template from Antinomy where elements compress and snap back with an elastic physical quality. Works for expressive UI transitions and motion design that wants to feel less digital.
records.move: press compresses card flat and wide, elastic release, dots ripple the shock
records.how: A white card with a title and orange button on a warm off-white stage, four dots beneath it and a translucent finger circle. At 5% the finger appears and the card compresses to scaleY 0.62 scaleX 1.18 (power3.in, 0.18s) from its bottom edge, the title to 0.7/1.25 and the button to 0.5/1.4 slightly later. At 25% the finger fades and grows while the card, title and button release back to 1/1 over 0.7s with elastic.out(1.2,0.35) at slightly offset starts. The dots squash to scaleY 0.4 scaleX 1.5 with a 0.04s stagger and rebound with elastic.out(1,0.35), so the stage returns to its rest pose by the end.
records.adapt: Swap the card content, colours, radius and button label, and the number of dots; keep the 0.18s power3.in press and the 0.7s elastic release ratios.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card, dots and finger; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with press at 0.05D, release at 0.25D and dot ripple at 0.23D and 0.31D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.

records.name: Stretch
records.description: An animation template from Antinomy where elements stretch and snap back with an elastic quality. Works for expressive UI transitions and motion design that wants to feel a bit more physical.
records.move: pills stretch in anticipation, fly across track, elastic snap-back at stop
records.how: Three coloured pills on a dark stage sit at the left end of a thin track with three stop dots. For each hop the pill first stretches away from its travel direction to scaleX 1.6 scaleY 0.8 with transformOrigin on the trailing edge (power2.in, 0.25s), then translates x across the track over 0.5s (expo.out) while its origin flips to the leading edge, and finally settles to scale 1/1 over 0.9s with elastic.out(1.1,0.35). Hops go right at 3%, 12% and 20% of the duration and back left at 53%, 62% and 70%, so the pills end near their starting positions.
records.adapt: Change the pill labels and colours, the count of pills and the track width (dist is derived from the stage width); keep the 0.25s anticipation, 0.5s expo.out flight and 0.9s elastic settle.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the track, stops and pills and computes dist from el.clientWidth; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with hop() positions as fractions of D. The transformOrigin sets are already on the timeline; scope selectors to el.
caveats: the last two return hops finish their elastic settle after the timeline ends (~0.3s over), so the final frame is slightly mid-wobble

records.name: Stretched Type Repeater
records.description: A stretched type animation combined with a repeater for bold, rhythmic typographic motion. Ideal for titles, social content, and brand animations.
records.move: repeated rows rise from centre line, stretch-waves ripple down, collapse flat
records.how: Nine rows of alternating red and white uppercase words are built into a centred column on a near-black stage. Phase 1 (0 to 15%): each row scales from scaleY 0.05 scaleX 2.2 and opacity 0 to 1/1/1 (expo.out, 0.9s), ordered by distance from the middle row. Phase 2 (20% to 75%): three beats 1.5s apart run a wave down the stack, each row stretching to scaleY 3.4 scaleX 0.72 (power3.in, 0.22s) then rebounding with elastic.out(1,0.45) over 0.7s with 0.09s per-row lag, while the rows drift alternately xPercent +/-6 per beat (expo.inOut). Phase 3 (from 89%): rows flatten to scaleY 0.04 scaleX 3 and fade from the outside in (expo.in) as the drift returns to 0, leaving the stage empty.
records.adapt: Change the words array (odd count keeps a middle row), the two text colours and the corner labels; keep the 0.22s stretch / 0.7s elastic wave timing and the three-beat rhythm.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the rows from shot words; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with beats at 0.2D + k*0.1875D and the collapse at 0.89D. Scope gsap.utils.toArray to el.
caveats: nine rows each with three stretch/rebound pairs plus drifts is a dense timeline; keep row count modest

records.name: Text Extrusion
records.description: A text extrusion effect that adds depth and dimension to animated typography. Perfect for titles, logos, and 3D-style motion graphics.
records.move: flat word grows a 48-layer extrusion while the rig tumbles in 3D
records.how: A yellow front word sits in a perspective rig with 48 darker copies inserted behind it (colour stepping toward deep violet), a radial floor shadow and a caption. The front face fades and scales in (expo.out, first 17%). From 8% each layer moves to z = -(i+1)*4px with a tiny 0.008s stagger (expo.out, 1s) so the depth appears to extrude out of the face, while the rig rotates to rotateY -38 rotateX 14 (power3.inOut, 40%), swings to rotateY 34 rotateX -10 (48% to 88%) and returns to 0. From 83% the layers collapse back to z 0 from the last layer inward (expo.in) and the caption fades.
records.adapt: Change the word, the front colour and the HSL range of the layers, N and STEP for depth; keep the two power3.inOut swings and the 1s extrusion.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the rig and inserts the N layer spans; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with positions at 0.08D, 0.48D, 0.85D. The stage needs perspective on el; scope selectors to el.
caveats: 48 text layers in preserve-3d is heavy
the front face is hidden at t=0 (from opacity 0) but fully visible on the last frame, so the loop pops

records.name: Text Mirror Effect
records.description: A template where text is mirrored into a symmetrical composition. Work great for artistic title sequences and editorial motion design.
records.move: letters fold up from mirror line, reflection lags a beat, halves breathe
records.how: A dimmed aurora background, a horizontal axis line and a word split per character into a top half and a scaleY(-1) bottom half fading through a mask. Top letters come from yPercent 105 rotateX -70 opacity 0 with origin at the baseline, staggered 0.06s from the centre (expo.out, 1s, at 2.5%); the reflection does the mirror move at 5.5%. The axis draws scaleX 0 to 1 (expo.inOut). From 30% to 65% letter-spacing opens to 0.12em and the halves drift +/-22px apart (sine.inOut) while the background scales 1 to 1.08 over the whole clip. At 84% the letters fold back into the axis from the edges (expo.in), the axis retracts and side labels fade.
records.adapt: Change the word, the serif font, the side labels and the background image; keep the 0.06s centre-out stagger, the 0.12s reflection lag and the sine.inOut breathe.
records.port: mount(el, shot) splits the word into .ch spans in both halves; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entries at 0.025D and 0.055D, breathe 0.3D to 0.65D, exit at 0.84D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: the background zoom ends at scale 1.08 and jumps back to 1 on loop
letterSpacing tweened on em values relayouts every frame

records.name: Text Scramble
records.description: An animated text template inspired by streaming platform teasers. Great for entertainment drops and any brand building anticipation for a release.
records.move: kicker tracks in, scrambled glyphs resolve to the title, flicker lock, scramble-out
records.how: A contrasty sunset background with vignette and scanlines, a red kicker, a huge uppercase title and a date line. The kicker fades in from letter-spacing 1em (expo.out, first 30%). ScrambleTextPlugin resolves the title from random uppercase glyphs to the final string over 50% of the duration (revealDelay 0.15, ease none) and the date line from digit/slash noise to its text from 25% to 70%; a red progress bar scales x to full. At 57% the title flickers opacity 0.3 four times, then at 82% scrambles out to an empty string while the kicker, date and bar fade; the background scales 1 to 1.06 throughout.
records.adapt: Change the kicker, title and date strings, the accent red and the background image; keep the 1s scramble with revealDelay, the 4x flicker at 57% and the 0.35s scramble-out.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the layers with placeholder scramble text; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with scrambleText tweens at 0.05D and 0.25D, flicker at 0.575D and exit 0.825D. Needs ScrambleTextPlugin registered; scope selectors to el.
caveats: the title starts visible with placeholder glyphs at frame 0 and empty at the last frame
background scale jumps from 1.06 back to 1 on loop

records.name: The Crust: Animated Menu
records.description: An animated menu template inspired by bakery and café signage. Great for daily specials, new menu launches, and any restaurant highlighting menu items.
records.move: menu board scales in, items slide in with leaders, sweep out
records.how: A cream bordered board on a 1080 square with a headline and italic accent, a day pill, six menu items (name, optional tag, dotted leader, serif price), a footer and a decorative croissant shape. The board scales 0.92 to 1 with opacity (expo.out), the headline rises through its mask and the day pill slides in from xPercent 120. From 10% each item enters 0.32s apart: the name slides from xPercent -110, the dotted leader grows scaleX 0 to 1 from the left, the price rises yPercent 120 to 0 (all expo.out) and any tag pops scaleX with back.out(2). The footer rises and the croissant scales in with rotation (back.out(1.6)) then rocks slowly; at 55% the prices pulse scale 1.12 in sequence. From 87% items sweep out xPercent 110 with a 0.06 stagger (expo.in), the heading and footer fly up and the board fades.
records.adapt: Replace the heading, day, item names, prices and tags (any count; entries are 0.32s apart), the palette and the decorative shape; keep the name/leader/price 0.12s and 0.3s offsets and the expo.in sweep.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders the board and items from shot data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with item i at (0.1 + i*0.04)D and the sweep at 0.875D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.
caveats: borderBottomWidth is tweened on the header, which relayouts

records.name: The Crust: Lunch Time
records.description: A bold, oversized typography template inspired by bakery signage and packaging design. Great for product launches and any restaurant or food brand that wants a punchy title moment.
records.move: giant words slam together from top and bottom, elastic punch, beat bounce
records.how: An orange 1080 square with faint diagonal stripes, a top and bottom caption, a small clock and two 270px uppercase words, the second as an outlined knockout, plus an italic ribbon. The first word rises from yPercent 110 with scaleY 1.8 and the second drops from yPercent -110 (expo.out, 0.7s, at 1% and 4%); at 15% both punch to scaleX 1.08 scaleY 0.9 and rebound with elastic.out(1,0.4). The ribbon pops from scale 0 rotate 20 (back.out(2.2)), the clock scales in and its hands sweep for the rest of the clip, the stripes slide xPercent -8 to 8 linearly. From 44% the words bounce yPercent +/-4 four times and the ribbon rocks; at 88% the words slide out xPercent -120 and 120 (expo.in), the ribbon shrinks and captions fade.
records.adapt: Change the two words, ribbon text, captions, brand colours and the knockout stroke; keep the 0.7s tall-stretch entries, the 0.1s punch with elastic rebound at 15% and the opposite-direction exit.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the rows, ribbon, clock and captions; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entries at 0.01D/0.04D, punch at 0.15D, bounces at 0.44D and exit at 0.88D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: the stripe drift ends at xPercent 8 and jumps back to -8 on loop

records.name: The Crust: Slideshow
records.description: An animated close-up slideshow template inspired by pastry photography. Great for product showcases, seasonal menu drops, and any food brand highlighting their ingredients.
records.move: close-up slides push in, focus ring pulses, colour wipe closes loop
records.how: Three stacked full-bleed slides on a 1080 square, each with a sepia-filtered image, a bottom gradient shade, a centred ring and a caption pair, plus a brand label, a counter and a full-frame amber wipe layer. Each slide owns a third of the duration: its image pushes from scale 1.35 with xPercent +/-4 to 1.05/0 (power2.out) while the ring expands scale 0 to 1.6 and fades (expo.out, 0.9s) and the name and description rise through a mask (expo.out). Slides 2 and 3 reveal with clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to 0 (expo.inOut, 0.55s) and the counter text updates. At 90% the amber wipe scales up from the bottom (expo.in), then at 99% its origin flips to the top and it snaps away, handing back to slide one.
records.adapt: Swap the three images, captions, filters and the wipe colour; add slides by extending per = D/n. Keep the push-in, ring pulse and 0.55s expo.inOut clip reveal.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the slides from shot images; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with per = D/slides and the wipe at 0.9D. The textContent set calls port as-is; scope selectors to el.
