caveats: the wipe retracts in the final 0.04s, so the last frame briefly shows slide three instead of slide one
full-frame images with sepia/saturate filters are heavy

records.name: The Crust: Tagline
records.description: A tagline template inspired by bakery photography. Great for brand statements, "freshly baked" promos, and any food brand pairing a strong message with product imagery.
records.move: circular photo irises open, lines rise through masks, stamp spins in
records.how: A cream 1080 square with a large circular photo (clip-path circle), two uppercase lines and an italic pill line stacked over it, a round stamp and a brand footer. The photo opens from clip-path circle(0%) to circle(50%) (expo.inOut, first 20%) while its image zooms 1.25 to 1 with a small rotate over the whole clip. Lines rise yPercent 110 to 0 (expo.out, 0.8s) at 10%, 13% and 17%, the pill also un-rotating from 6deg; the stamp scales from 0 with rotate -120 (back.out(1.8)) then turns slowly; the pill pulses scale 1.04 four times from 40%. At 84% the lines fly up staggered (expo.in), the stamp shrinks, the photo irises closed and the footer fades.
records.adapt: Replace the photo, the three lines, stamp text and palette; keep the 1s expo.inOut iris and 0.15s line offsets.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the photo, lines, stamp and footer; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with iris 0 to 0.2D, lines at 0.1D, exit at 0.84D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: animated clip-path circle over a filtered image is moderately heavy

records.name: The Crust: Tagline and Menu
records.description: A animated menu template inspired by bakery and sandwich shop boards. Great for menu rollouts, seasonal lineups, and any food brand or restaurant showcasing multiple items at once.
records.move: tagline rises then flies up, six menu cards pop in, prices pulse
records.how: Act one on a dark 1080 square: three big lines (one italic amber) rise yPercent 110 to 0 through masks (expo.out, 0.8s) at 1%, 4% and 6% and fly out yPercent -120 at 31% (expo.in). Act two from 36%: a grid with a header, an italic subtitle and six coloured cards is revealed via autoAlpha; the header text rises, then the cards enter from scale 0.6 with alternating rotate +/-6 and opacity 0 (back.out(1.6), 0.7s) in grid order with a 0.12s stagger, and the footer fades in. At 66% the prices pop scale 1.2 in sequence. At 89% the cards shrink and fade from the last one back (expo.in), the header slides up and the footer fades.
records.adapt: Change the three lines, the six card names, descriptions, prices and colours (grid stagger uses [3,2]); keep the back.out(1.6) card pop and the 0.12s stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the tagline stack and the grid from shot items; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the act change at 0.36D and the exit at 0.89D. The autoAlpha set at 0 then 0.001 should become a single gsap.set in mount; scope selectors to el.
caveats: frame 0 flashes the full menu grid because the grid is set autoAlpha 1 at 0 and only hidden at 0.001s
the header underline (border-bottom) stays visible on the last frame while everything else is gone, so the loop does not close cleanly

records.name: The Edit: Instagram Story
records.description: A story edit template with smooth cuts and a layout built for the Instagram format. Drop in your own content and it's ready to go.
records.move: three story cuts via clip-path, bars tick, sticker pops, white flash-cut
records.how: A 1080x1920 story: three full-bleed image frames, a header with avatar, three segment progress bars, two big uppercase words, an italic pill line, a yellow round sticker, a CTA and a white cutbar. Cut one: the first image drifts scale 1.15 to 1 with yPercent 3 to -3 (linear), the header drops in and the two words rise through masks (expo.out). At 30% the second frame reveals from clip-path inset(0 0 0 100%) (expo.inOut, 0.45s) while the words slide out xPercent -110 and the italic pill rises un-rotating; the sticker pops from scale 0 rotate -40 (back.out(2)) and rocks. At 65% the third frame reveals from the bottom, the CTA rises and bobs. Each progress bar fills scaleX over its third of the duration. At 93% the white cutbar wipes across from the left (expo.in), flips origin and snaps away.
records.adapt: Swap the three images, handle, words, pill text, sticker and CTA; keep the thirds structure, the 0.45s expo.inOut clip reveals and the flash-cut at 93%.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds frames, bars and text from shot; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with cuts at 0.3D and 0.65D, bars at D/3 each, cutbar at 0.93D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: the cutbar retracts in the final 0.03s so the last frame shows frame three under a sliver of white
the filled progress bars and the third image scale jump back on loop, hidden only by the flash

records.name: The Edit: Product Launch
records.description: A product launch template with bold cuts and a pace that builds toward the reveal. Perfect for new product announcements and e-commerce campaigns where the buildup matters.
records.move: accelerating single-word hard cuts, white flash, product spins in, copy staggers
records.how: Four full-frame colour cuts each holding one 190px word, then a light reveal panel with a product tile and a copy stack, a flash layer and a corner date. Cuts run 1.0s, 0.7s, 0.5s and 0.35s (17%, 12%, 8%, 6% of the duration), toggled with autoAlpha sets; each word enters yPercent 110 or xPercent -110 to 0 (expo.out) and creeps to scale 1.06 for the length of the cut. At 42% the reveal appears under a white flash fading over 0.5s: the product scales 0.3 to 1 un-rotating from -25 (expo.out, 0.9s) then rocks, the copy lines rise yPercent 130 with opacity, 0.09s apart (expo.out). At 92% the product shrinks away rotating +25 and the copy flies up (expo.in), the panel fades to the dark base.
records.adapt: Change the four cut words and colours, the product tile art, the kicker/headline/sub/button strings; keep the shrinking cut lengths, the 0.5s flash and the 0.09s copy stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the cuts and reveal; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with cut lengths scaled by D/6. The autoAlpha sets use immediateRender:false and must keep it; scope selectors to el.
caveats: relies on immediateRender:false on set() calls to avoid hiding cuts at build time

records.name: The Edit: Tagline [Dark]
records.description: A dark-themed tagline template with bold typography and a clean reveal motion. Works for brand campaign videos and product launches with a dark aesthetic.
records.move: dot punches in, stretches into rule, lines rise, kerning tightens, retract
records.how: A near-black 1080 square with an SVG turbulence grain overlay, a small header row, three 150px uppercase lines (the middle one lime) in masked rows, a thin rule and two footer lines. A lime dot scales in from 0 (expo.out, first 12%) and fades as the rule grows scaleX 0 to 1 from the left (expo.out, 0.7s, at 17%); the lines rise yPercent 110 to 0 with a 0.09s stagger (expo.out, 0.8s, at 18%), then the footer lines and header fade in. From 43% to 83% letter-spacing tightens from -0.045em to -0.06em (sine.inOut). At 78% the lines exit yPercent -110 staggered (expo.in), the footer follows, the rule retracts to the right and the header fades.
records.adapt: Change the three lines, the accent colour, the header and footer strings; keep the dot-to-rule handoff at 17% and the 0.09s stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid of rows and the SVG grain; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the rule at 0.17D, lines at 0.18D, exit at 0.78D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.
caveats: full-frame feTurbulence grain is expensive to composite every frame
letterSpacing tween relayouts text each frame

records.name: The Edit: Tagline [White]
records.description: A white-themed tagline template with bold type and clean motion. Ideal for brand campaign videos and product presentations with a light aesthetic.
records.move: black bar wipes across, thins away, type rises, bar returns to wipe
records.how: A warm white 1080 square with a 14px black bar across the middle, four corner labels, a kicker, two 132px lines (one italic serif word) and three sub items in masks. The bar grows scaleX 0 to 1 from the left (expo.inOut, first 16%) then collapses scaleY to 0 (expo.inOut) as the kicker and lines rise yPercent 110 to 0 with a 0.12s stagger (expo.out, 0.9s, from 19%), then the sub items and corners fade in. The whole block eases from x 24 to 0 over 2.2s and the italic skews to -6 and back (sine.inOut). At 83% the lines fly up (expo.in), the kicker and subs follow, corners fade, and the bar returns from the right at full height (expo.inOut) then snaps to scaleX 0 from the left in the last 2%.
records.adapt: Change the two lines (keep one italic word), kicker, sub items and corners, the bar colour and thickness; keep the bar-in/thin/bar-return structure at 0%, 17% and 89%.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the bar, rows and labels; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the bar at 0, 0.17D and 0.89D, lines at 0.19D. Scope selectors to el.

records.name: The Harvest: Banana Spin
records.description: A typographic animation where a banana spins through bold serif lettering. Great for food and drink promos and playful brand moments.
records.move: serif letters bounce in, banana spins through and parks, letters shove aside
records.how: A yellow stage with a large faint ring, the word RIPE split into serif characters, an SVG banana and two masked tags. Letters drop from yPercent -160 with random tilt (bounce.out, 0.9s, 0.1s stagger) and the ring scales in. At 9% the banana flies from x -1100 rotating -540 to the centre (expo.out, 1.4s); at 15% the letters shove xPercent +/-34 from the centre (expo.out) and settle to +/-26 with elastic.out(1,0.5). From 23% to 87% the banana turns 720deg (power1.inOut) while bobbing y -22 (sine.inOut yoyo) and the ring turns 180. At 89% the banana flicks out to x 1200 with an extra spin (expo.in), the letters close back and drop yPercent 160 (power3.in), tags fly up and the ring fades. Timeline duration is 10s.
records.adapt: Change the word (letters shove by index relative to the middle), the SVG fruit, colours and tags; keep the bounce.out drop, the 1.4s fly-in and the elastic shove.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the ring, letters, fruit SVG and tags; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with fly-in at 0.09D, shove 0.155D, spin 0.23D to 0.87D, exit 0.89D. fx.rng(7) becomes a seeded rng in mount; scope selectors to el.
caveats: the letters exit by yPercent 160 without a mask, so they simply drop below the frame
catalog says 11s; the timeline is 10s

records.name: The Harvest: Fruit Bounce
records.description: A logo animation with fruit bouncing into a serif wordmark. Ideal for brand intros and food and drink identities.
records.move: fruit drops with CustomBounce squash, wordmark letters flinch on impact
records.how: A dark green stage with a thin floor line, a serif wordmark split into letters resting on it, four SVG fruits above and a masked subline. The floor draws scaleX 0 to 1 (expo.out). Each fruit falls from y -220 to the floor over 1.3s with a CustomBounce ease (strength 0.6) while a paired squash tween drives scaleX 1.35 scaleY 0.65 from the bottom origin, starting 0.18s apart from 2.5%. Letters rise yPercent 120 to 0 (expo.out, 0.05 stagger) then at 21% flinch yPercent -10 scaleY 0.92 from the edges and settle with elastic.out(1,0.4). The fruit rolls +/-8deg (sine.inOut yoyo) during the hold; at 82% fruit launches up with back.in(2), letters drop yPercent 120, the subline flies up and the floor retracts.
records.adapt: Change the wordmark, the fruit SVGs (any count, 0.18s apart) and colours; keep the CustomBounce strength 0.6 with squash 3 and the 1.3s drop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the letters and fruit; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with drops at (0.025 + i*0.045)D and the exit at 0.82D. landY depends on the 720 stage height and must be derived from el; CustomBounce.create should run once in mount.
caveats: the wordmark has no overflow mask so at yPercent 120 the lower part of the letters stays visible below the baseline on the first and last frames
landY is hard-coded for a 720px stage

records.name: The Harvest: Orange Float
records.description: A vibrant animation where an orange floats between a stacked serif headline. Perfect for beverage ads and fresh, colorful campaigns by food and drink brands.
records.move: stacked headline rises, orange floats up between lines, middle word yields
records.how: An orange 1080 square with four faint bubbles, two corner badges, three masked serif rows (the middle one behind the fruit) and an SVG orange with a leaf. Rows rise yPercent 110 to 0 with a 0.12s stagger (expo.out, 0.9s); the orange rises from y 700 rotating -40 scale 0.8 to rest (expo.out, 1.3s, at 7%) and the middle word slides x -250 to make room (expo.out). From 27% the orange bobs y -28 three times and tilts to 14deg and back (sine.inOut) while drifting x 90 and the middle word drifts further; the leaf wags. Bubbles rise from y 120 to -320 over the whole clip. At 88% the orange drops through y 800 rotating 60 (power3.in), rows fly up and badges fade.
records.adapt: Change the three words, badges, footer and fruit SVG, the brand colours; keep the 1.3s expo.out rise, the sine.inOut bob and the power3.in drop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds rows, fruit and bubbles; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with rise at 0.075D, float 0.27D onward, exit 0.88D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: bubbles end at y -320 and jump back to y 120 on loop

records.name: The Harvest: Peach Plunge
records.description: A typographic poster perfect for food and drink campaigns and editorial-style promos.
records.move: pool rises, poster type lands, peach plunges with elastic splash
records.how: A 1080x1920 poster: kicker row, three 250px serif lines (one italic) in masked rows, body copy, two stacked orange pools with a scrolling SVG wave, a peach SVG, six splash droplets and a ripple ring. The pools rise yPercent 100 to 0 (expo.out, first 15%), the wave scrolls x -300 linearly for the whole clip, and kicker, lines (0.14 stagger) and body rise through masks (expo.out). At 24% the peach falls from y -400 accelerating (power3.in, 1.1s) and continues to y 2200 while fading; at 37% the water bulges scaleY 1.06 and the wave scaleY 2.2 then both settle with elastic.out, the ring expands scale 0.2 to 1.8 and fades, six droplets fly out on seeded arcs (power2.out) then fall (power2.in), and the headline shudders y 14 with an elastic settle. From 89% the lines fly up, the pools sink yPercent 110 and the footer fades.
records.adapt: Change the three lines, kicker, body, fruit SVG and pool colours; keep the 1.1s power3.in plunge, the elastic water rebound and the seeded droplet arcs.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the poster, pools, wave, fruit and droplets with a seeded rng; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with plunge at 0.24D, impact 0.37D, exit 0.89D. The 1920 fall distances should scale with el height; scope selectors to el.
caveats: fall distances (y 1150, 2200) assume a 1920px-tall stage

records.name: The Harvest: Pulp
records.description: An animated juice label that reveals cold-pressed ingredient details line by line. Perfect for beverage promos and product storytelling.
records.move: label settles in, ingredient lines and bars reveal in turn, fold up
records.how: A 1080x1920 cream label card with a serif brand, a subline, a rule, four ingredient rows (name, percentage, and a bar), two juice blobs, a round stamp and a footer. The card comes from scale 0.92 y 60 opacity 0 (expo.out, 0.9s); brand rows and subline rise through masks, the rule grows scaleX from the left, the blobs scale in (expo.out / back.out) and the stamp spins in with back.out(1.6). From 12% each row enters 0.55s apart: its text rises yPercent 120, the divider colour fades in and the bar grows scaleX 0 to 1 to its data width (expo.out, 1s). During the hold the stamp turns 360 and the blobs breathe (sine.inOut yoyo). From 84% the rows and bars fold up and retract to the right (expo.in, 0.08 stagger), the rule and brand follow and the card drops y 120 and fades.
records.adapt: Change the brand, subline, ingredient names and data-w percentages (any count, 0.55s apart), colours and stamp text; keep the expo.out 1s bar fill and the expo.in fold.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the label and rows; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with rows at (0.12 + i*0.061)D and the exit at 0.84D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.
caveats: width and scaleX are tweened together on the bars, which relayouts each frame

records.name: The Harvest: Raspberry Check
records.description: A typographic animation where raspberries drift inside a bold blue checkerboard frame. Perfect for playful promos and graphic food and drink reveals.
records.move: checkerboard ticks on from edges, panel opens, berries drift, board inverts
records.how: A 12x12 grid of white cells on a blue 1080 square with alternating opacity forms a checkerboard border around an inner blue panel holding two italic serif rows, seven seeded SVG raspberries and two captions. The cells scale from 0 with back.out(2) in a grid stagger from the edges (first 8%), the panel scales 0 to 1 (expo.out) and the rows and captions rise through masks. Berries pop in from scale 0 with back.out(1.7) 0.09s apart and each glides along its own x/y/rotation path over 70% of the clip (sine.inOut). At 50% the cells invert their opacity from the centre outward. From 87% berries shrink with back.in(2), rows fly up, the panel scales to 0 and the cells scale out from the centre.
records.adapt: Change the two words, captions, berry SVG, the blue and the grid size; keep the from-edges grid stagger and the sine.inOut drift.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the 144 cells and seeded berries; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the panel at 0.06D, inversion at 0.5D, exit at 0.87D. Grid stagger options carry over; scope selectors to el.
caveats: 144 grid cells with two staggered tweens each is a large tween count

records.name: The Harvest: Raspberry Glide
records.description: A typographic animation with layered lettering on a dark, slow motion background. Great for product promos and premium food and drink content.
records.move: four layered word copies glide in from four sides, parallax over video
records.how: A dark 1080 square with a muted background video scrubbed at quarter speed, a vignette, four overlaid copies of the word (outline, screen-blend red, italic cream, faint outline), a berry SVG and small captions. The copies slide in from x -700, x 700, y 300 and y -300 with opacity 0 (expo.out, 1.4s) at 0%, 2%, 5% and 7% of the clip and land slightly offset from one another; from 28% they glide a few px in opposing directions over 3s (sine.inOut) for a parallax feel, while the berry crosses behind the italic layer from x -700 to 700 turning 70deg. Captions rise through masks. At 86% each copy leaves the way it came (expo.in, 0.06s apart) and the captions fly up.
records.adapt: Change the word, the four layer treatments (stroke, blend, italic), the video and captions; keep the 1.4s expo.out entries with 0.12s offsets and the 3s sine.inOut glide.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the layers, berry and video, waiting for loadeddata; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline; the video-scrub tween is already an onUpdate tween setting currentTime and ports directly. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: background video currentTime is set from a tween and needs the video decoded before the first frame (fx.wait)
the video scrub and its scale 1.06 zoom do not return to frame 0 on loop
mix-blend-mode screen on a 190px text layer over video

records.name: The Prompt: Text To Image
records.description: An animated UI template showing a text-to-image AI interface from prompt to output. Great for generative AI product demos where showing the moment of creation is the most convincing argument.
records.move: prompt types out, generate press, noise diffuses into an image
records.how: A dark app frame with a prompt field, option chips, a gradient button, and an output pane holding a canvas, a step counter, a progress bar and a done badge. The caret blinks (steps(1) yoyo) while TextPlugin types the prompt over 26% of the clip; a chip toggles on; at 41% the button presses scale 0.96 and rebounds with elastic.out(1,0.4) with a white flash, and the label changes. From 44% a state object tweens p 0 to 1 over 3.4s (power2.inOut) with an onUpdate that redraws the canvas: a procedural sunset scene drawn pixelated (block size 48 to 1) and blurred (14px to 0) with a fading seeded noise overlay, while the progress bar fills, the step counter counts to 30 and the grid fades. At 79% the done badge pops with back.out(2) and the canvas zooms 1.06; at 95% the output pane fades, the prompt clears and the placeholder returns. Timeline is 10s.
records.adapt: Change the prompt string, app name, chips, step count and the procedural scene (or draw a supplied image into the offscreen canvas); keep the 2.6s type, 3.4s power2.inOut resolve and the button press.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the UI and the offscreen scene canvas; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline; the canvas is already driven by an onUpdate tween on a state object, so it ports directly with draw() closed over el. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: the output pane is faded to opacity 0 at the end but never restored, so the loop does not return to the empty-state first frame
per-frame pixel noise loop (fillRect per 4px cell) and canvas filter blur are slow
catalog says 11s; the timeline is 10s

records.name: The Route: Cities
records.description: A route map template that draws an animated path between city destinations. Perfect for travel apps and location-based content where the journey is part of the story.
records.move: dashed guide draws ahead, route follows with plane, pins pop, labels rise
records.how: A 1080 map square with a grid, two land shapes, a dashed guide path and a solid red path over it, four pin groups, four city labels in masks, a headline, meta text and a distance card. The headline and card rise (expo.out), the land fades in. From 5% the dashed path draws via DrawSVG 0 to 100% over 1.6s (power2.inOut); from 13% the solid path draws over 3.2s (power1.inOut) while the plane rides it with MotionPathPlugin (autoRotate 90) and a proxy tween counts the km readout. Pins pop scale 0 with back.out(3) at the arrival times, each emitting a radius-30 fading ring, and the city name and code rise through masks. At 87% both paths erase from the start (drawSVG 100% 100%), the plane flies off up-right fading, pins shrink with back.in(2), labels drop and the headline and card leave.
records.adapt: Change the path d, pin positions and city labels (arrival times must match path progress), the km total and colours; keep the guide-then-solid draw and the 3.2s plane ride.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the SVG map and labels; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with draws at 0.05D and 0.13D and the exit at 0.87D. MotionPath aligns to a path inside el; the km onUpdate ports as-is; scope selectors to el.
caveats: the land shapes fade in from 0 at the start but stay visible at the end, so the loop pops
the plane sits visibly at the top-left corner until its motionPath tween starts at 0.8s

records.name: The Route: Departures Board
records.description: An animated departures board template with flip-style text revealing destination information. Good for travel product showcases and transport app demos where authenticity matters.
records.move: split-flap cells cycle characters row by row, clock ticks, top row departs
records.how: A dark board with a header and clock, column labels and five rows of flap cells (time, destination, flight, gate) plus a status pill. The board rises in (expo.out), the header text and rows fade in. From 8% each flap runs a proxy tween of 6 to 13 steps at 0.07s per step whose onUpdate writes the next character from a seeded alphabet, landing on its target, while a paired scaleY 0.6 to 1 pulse repeats per step; rows start 0.28s apart and columns cascade 0.03s per flap. Status labels rise through masks 0.28s apart. A proxy tween drives the clock seconds for the whole clip; at 58% one status slides up, swaps to BOARDING with a colour change and slides back. At 81% the top row slides out x -60 fading (power3.in), the others shuffle up y -72 (expo.inOut) and the board fades.
records.adapt: Change DATA rows (widths per column are fixed in cell()), the alphabet, colours and brand footer; keep the 0.07s step cadence and the 0.28s row cascade.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the rows and flap cells and returns the flap list; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline; the character cycling already runs from onUpdate proxy tweens so it ports directly. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: around 130 flaps each with two tweens; heavy timeline
not a true 3D flap flip: the .n/.t/.b markup is unused and the flip is a scaleY pulse

records.name: The Route: Logo Reveal
records.description: A template where an animated route path draws itself across the frame and arrives at a logo. Good for travel brand intros and any identity where telling a small story before the reveal makes sense.
records.move: route draws with plane, erases into last stop, stop blooms into logo
records.how: A navy stage with a dense dot grid, a curved route path with a blurred glow twin, five stop circles, a plane icon and a centred logo (ring, arrow mark, name and tag in masks). Dots fade in with a tiny stagger; stops pop scale 0 with back.out(3) 0.45s apart; from 4% the path and glow draw with DrawSVG 0 to 100% over 2.2s (power2.inOut) while the plane rides the path with MotionPathPlugin. At 46% the line erases from its tail (drawSVG 100% 100%, power3.in), the plane shrinks, the other stops collapse and the last stop tweens its cx/cy/r attributes to the centre at radius 38 (expo.inOut). It fades as the logo ring draws itself (DrawSVG), the arrow spins in with back.out(2), and the name and tag rise through masks. At 92% the logo lifts y -40 and fades and the dots go out.
records.adapt: Change the path d and stop coordinates, the mark SVG, name and tag, colours; keep the 2.2s draw, the tail erase at 46% and the stop-to-ring handoff.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the SVG, dot grid and logo and measures the mark centre from el (not the document) in stage coordinates; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with draw at 0.04D, handoff 0.46D to 0.62D, exit 0.92D. The getBoundingClientRect measurement assumes the stage is unscaled at 1280x720; convert to viewBox units in mount.
caveats: uses getBoundingClientRect of the mark at build time, so it assumes an unscaled 1280x720 stage
the plane is visible at the top-left corner until its motionPath tween starts at 0.2s
attr tween on cx/cy/r plus a blurred glow stroke

records.name: The Vault: Card Features
records.description: An animated card UI template that reveals features in a structured layered layout. Great for fintech product demos and subscription plan presentations.
records.move: card tilts up from flat, sheen sweeps, feature rows stack, fold back
records.how: A dark 1080 square with a perspective stage, a heading in a mask, a card (chip, brand, number, name, expiry, two circles, a diagonal sheen) and three feature rows with icon, text and value. The heading rises; the card comes from rotationX 70, y 180, scale 0.9, opacity 0 to rest (expo.out, 1s, at 2.5%); the sheen sweeps xPercent -60 to 60 (power2.inOut); card details fade up. From 20% the features drop in from y -40 scaleY 0.6 opacity 0 with a 0.14s stagger (expo.out), their text rises through masks, values slide in and icons pop with back.out(3). During the hold the card rocks rotationY -14 rotationX 6 and back (sine.inOut) while a proxy tween counts the cashback value to 248. At 80% the features fold back up from the last (power3.in), the card flips away rotationX -70 y -120 and the heading exits.
records.adapt: Change the card art and strings, the three features and values, the accent colours; keep the 1s expo.out tilt-in and the 0.14s feature stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and feature rows; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with card at 0.025D, features 0.2D, hold rock 0.3D, exit 0.8D. The counter onUpdate ports as-is; el needs perspective; scope selectors to el.

records.name: The Vault: Feature List
records.description: An animated feature list template in the Vault fintech style. Good for banking and payments product content that needs to communicate value clearly and confidently.
records.move: rows slide in, each checked: circle fills, tick draws, underline runs
records.how: A dark stage with a dot grid, a left column (eyebrow, two-line title, description in masks) and a right list of five items each with a check circle, a masked label, an index and a bottom underline, plus a counter. Left text rises through masks (expo.out) and items slide in from x 60 with opacity (expo.out, 0.1 stagger). From 16% each item is checked 0.9s apart: the green fill scales in with back.out(2.5), the border recolours, the tick path draws 0 to 100% via DrawSVG (power2.out), the row flashes a green background and nudges x 8 with an elastic settle, the underline grows scaleX (expo.out) and the counter increments. At 66% the fills pulse scale 1.15 in a chase. At 90% items slide out from the last (power3.in), the left text flies up and the counter fades. Timeline duration is 10s.
records.adapt: Change the eyebrow, title, description and the item labels (any count, 0.9s apart), accent green; keep the fill/tick/underline 0.12s offsets and the elastic nudge.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the columns and items; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with checks at (0.16 + i*0.09)D and exit at 0.9D. The counter uses onStart/onReverseComplete and should become an onUpdate on a proxy tween; scope selectors to el.
caveats: the counter text is set from onStart/onReverseComplete callbacks, which are not seek-safe when scrubbing
the dot grid fades in from 0 but stays visible at the end
catalog says 20s; the timeline is 10s

records.name: Tilted Text Snap
records.description: A snappy animated text template where each line rotates in at a slight tilt and settles into place. Great for editorial promos and any brand delivering a punchy, high-energy message.
records.move: lines rotate up tilted on left baseline, overshoot flat, elastic snap
records.how: A red stage with four corner labels and three 170px uppercase lines (the middle one white) in overflow-hidden rows, each with transform-origin at its left baseline. Corners fade in. Each line comes from yPercent 120 rotation 12 to 0/0 (expo.out, 0.55s) starting 0.14s apart from 2.5%, then overshoots to rotation -2.5 (power2.out, 0.12s) and settles to 0 with elastic.out(1,0.4). At 72% the lines tilt to rotation -10 and fly up yPercent -120 (power3.in) 0.08s apart and the corners fade.
records.adapt: Change the three lines and corner labels, the colours and which line is highlighted; keep the 12deg tilt, 0.55s expo.out entry and the -2.5 overshoot with elastic settle.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the rows and corners; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with line i at (0.025 + i*0.07)D and exit at 0.725D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.

records.name: Type Trail
records.description: A typographic trail effect that leaves a motion blur behind animated text. Perfect for kinetic typography and high-energy motion graphics.
records.move: words rush in skewed, six lagging ghost copies smear a motion trail
records.how: A dark stage with a drifting grid and three words, each built from a lead span plus six ghost spans that carry a directional feGaussianBlur (22 1) and decreasing opacity. Every move is applied to the lead and then to each ghost 0.035s later, which draws the smear. KINETIC rushes from xPercent -170 to 0 (expo.out, 0.75s, at 1%) with skewX -28 easing to 0; at 29% it shoots up yPercent -320 (expo.in) and TYPE drops in from yPercent 320 with a scaleY 1.25 settle; at 56% TYPE exits left and TRAIL enters from the right with skewX 26; at 85% TRAIL leaves to the right with skewX 18. The grid translates -80px on both axes over the clip, matching its 80px period, so the loop is seamless.
records.adapt: Change the three words and their colours, GHOSTS count and lag, blur strength in the filter; keep the 0.035s ghost lag, the expo.out in / expo.in out pairing and the skew as velocity.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the layer spans per word and the SVG filter def; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with moves at 0.01D, 0.29D, 0.56D, 0.85D. The fromTo tweens need immediateRender:false plus the gsap.set start positions in mount; scope selectors to el.
caveats: fromTo tweens rely on immediateRender:false and initial gsap.set positions
six SVG-blurred 230px text copies per word is heavy to composite

records.name: Video Title Slide
records.description: A clean animated title slide template for video openers. Great for YouTube intros and presentation title cards.
records.move: rule draws, label and title lines rise through masks, all retract upward
records.how: A cream stage with an orange blob top-right and a faint dark blob bottom-left that breathe (sine.inOut yoyo) for the whole clip, a frame with a top rule, a dotted label, two 132px title lines (accent word), a subline, a footer rule and footer items, all in overflow masks. The rule grows scaleX 0 to 1 (expo.inOut, first 22%), the dot pops with back.out(2), label spans rise yPercent 110 to 0 (expo.out, 0.08 stagger), title lines rise with a 0.12 stagger (expo.out, 0.9s, at 11%), then the subline, the footer rule and footer items. From 79% the lines exit yPercent -110 (expo.in, 0.08 stagger), the subline, label and footer follow, the dot shrinks, and both rules retract (expo.inOut), leaving the blobs as at the start.
records.adapt: Change the episode label, two title lines (keep one accent word), subline, footer strings and date, the blob colours; keep the expo.inOut rule draw and the 0.12s title stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the frame and masked rows; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with title at 0.11D and exit at 0.79D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.

records.name: Wow: Rotate and Scale
records.description: An animation template that combines rotation and scaling for a strong entrance effect. Good for hero elements and title reveals where the first impression needs to do some work.
records.move: word screws in rotation-first, letters late-spin, sparks burst, blows past camera
records.how: A violet radial stage with a dashed ring and a thin ring turning full opposite turns over the clip, a pink halo breathing scale 0.9 to 1.1, a 300px three-letter word, a masked subline and six sparks. The word comes from scale 0 rotation -540 to 1/0 (expo.out, 1.3s, at 2%) with a second scale tween from 0 with back.out(2.2) overriding it for the overshoot; at 15% each letter spins from rotation 180 scale 0.6 to rest with back.out(1.8) 0.09s apart; the subline rises. At 23% six sparks fly from the centre along fixed angles to 380x280px, growing scale 1.4 and fading (expo.out). At 81% the word blows to scale 4 rotation 90 and opacity 0 (expo.in) and the subline exits.
records.adapt: Change the word (any short string, letters spin individually), the accent letter colour, subline, ring and halo colours; keep the -540 rotation lead, back.out(2.2) scale overshoot and the scale-4 exit.
records.port: mount(el, shot) splits the word into spans and creates the rings, halo and sparks; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entry at 0.02D, letter spins 0.15D, sparks 0.23D, exit 0.81D. Scope selectors to el; direct port.
caveats: two overlapping fromTo scale tweens on the same element; the later back.out one wins the overshoot

records.name: Zero Gravity: Bouncy Words
records.description: A text animation template from Rico where words float and bounce with a weightless physical feel. Great for playful title cards and social content where you want the type itself to be entertaining.
records.move: pill words drift weightless, each squashes, springs and bounces once
records.how: Five pill-shaped words and four faint dots sit on a lavender square. Every word drifts on a seeded sine in x, y and rotation (fromTo with yoyo, half the duration each way, sine.inOut) so the field is always slowly turning and returns to its start at D. Staggered 0.5s apart from 0.05D, each word gets a tap: scaleX 1.25 / scaleY 0.75 over 0.12s (power2.in), then elastic.out(1.1,0.35) back to 1 over 0.9s while y jumps -70 (power2.out, 0.28s) and drops back with bounce.out over 0.5s. Dots bob on the same sine yoyo.
records.adapt: Change the five word strings, pill colours and positions, and the seed passed to fx.rng; keep the 0.12s squash / 0.9s elastic / 0.5s bounce timings and the 0.5s stagger, which read as the weightless tap.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends the .word pills and .dot divs with the shot's strings and colours; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with drifts as D/2 yoyo tweens and taps at 0.05D + i*0.17D. Scope querySelectorAll('.word') to el; the relative y '-=70' / '+=70' tweens must stay after the drift tween in build order.
caveats: relative y tweens (-=70/+=70) stack on the sine drift tween on the same property; scrubbing backwards can leave words offset
last word's elastic settle ends at 3.17s, past D=3, so the loop closes only approximately
positions are absolute pixels for a 1080x1080 stage

records.name: Gradient Background Loop
records.description: A procedural gradient background animated through smooth color transitions. Ideal for looping backgrounds and branded motion graphics.
records.move: five blurred colour blobs orbit Lissajous paths, hue rotates once per loop
records.how: A 2D canvas paints a deep purple ground, then five additive (lighter) radial gradients under ctx.filter blur(40px), each moving on a closed Lissajous path (integer fx/fy multiples of the loop phase) with a hue that turns a full 360 degrees over D so t=D is pixel-identical to t=0. A multiply vignette keeps the corners dark and a static seeded film-grain canvas sits over it at 7% overlay. A small white circle-and-wordmark lockup sits bottom-left and does not move.
records.adapt: Change the ground colour, the base hues and radii in the blobs array, the lockup text, and drop or keep the grain; keep the integer Lissajous frequencies and the 360-degree hue turn per loop or the loop will no longer close.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the two canvases and the lockup inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with a single tween on {u:0->1, ease:none, duration:D} whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) paint (the fx.register loop). Canvas is fixed 1280x720; scale via CSS or read el size.
caveats: ctx.filter blur(40px) on five large radial fills per frame is slow to render
the grain canvas fills 1280x720 ImageData once at mount

records.name: Gradients: Perspective Tunnel
records.description: A gradient tunnel template with a deep vanishing point that creates a sense of traveling through color. Perfect for atmospheric backgrounds and ambient loop sequences.
records.move: glowing gradient rounded rings rush toward camera from a drifting vanishing point
records.how: A canvas draws 18 rounded-rectangle rings stacked in depth; each frame their z advances by three ring-spacings per loop (integer, so t=D equals t=0) and they re-enter at the back, scaled by a steep depth^2.6 perspective around a vanishing point that drifts on a small circle. Stroke width, glow (shadowBlur) and alpha grow with depth, and each ring's linear-gradient hue turns 360 degrees per loop. Over the canvas a GSAP timeline spins the logo's rounded-diamond outline 45 to 405 degrees (ease none), pulses the centre dot 0.8 to 1.2 and the glow disc 0.9 to 1.15 with sine.inOut yoyo. Dark radial fog hides the vanishing point.
records.adapt: Replace the mark and wordmark, set the ring hue offset and the background colour; keep N=18 rings, the 3-rings-per-loop speed and the full logo turn so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas, glow and logo inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the logo timeline plus a {u:0->1, duration:D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate paints the rings (replacing the fx.register seek that also called tl.seek). Scope '.mark i', '.mark b', '.glow' to el.
caveats: shadowBlur up to 62px on 18 strokes per frame is expensive
canvas is hard-coded 1280x720

records.name: Kaleidoscope: Intro Slide
records.description: A kaleidoscope pattern template that unfolds into an intro slide. Good for vibrant openers and title sequences where the reveal should feel like an event.
records.move: full-frame kaleidoscope irises to a disc, slide text rises, bursts back
records.how: An offscreen 1400px tile of 220 seeded circles, triangles and bars drifts on sines; it is mirrored into 12 clipped wedges on a full-frame canvas and again, smaller, inside a 230px disc. A GSAP timeline spins the pattern two wedges per loop (ease none) and breathes zoom 1.2 to 0.85 with sine.inOut yoyo. At 0.3D the full canvas irises shut via clip-path circle(120%) to circle(0%) over 1.1s (expo.inOut); the disc scales in from 0 with rotation -90 (back.out(1.6)), and kicker, two title lines, a scaleX bar and a footer rise from yPercent 110 with expo.out staggers. At 0.84D everything leaves upward (expo.in) and the clip-path reopens over 0.5s (expo.out) so the loop restarts on the full kaleidoscope.
records.adapt: Swap the kicker/title/footer strings, the six shape colours, the tile background and the seed; keep the 12-segment mirror, the two-wedge spin per loop, and the 1.5s / 4.2s iris in/out beats.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds both canvases and the .slide copy in el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with an extra {u:0->1, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate redraws the source tile and both kaleidoscopes from the st.spin/st.zoom values (the fx.register seek). Scope '#k', '.disc', '.kick', '.title', '.bar', '.foot' to el and give the canvases unique ids.
caveats: from() tweens on .kick/.title/.bar/.foot need immediateRender:false when ported
redraws a 1400px source and 24 clipped drawImage wedges every frame
the reopen ends at 5.05s, 0.05s past D, so the last frame is a hair short of the first

records.name: Collage Art Promo
records.description: A cut-paper collage opener: one shot is torn away to a newsprint wall and paper cutouts, hands and labels pop in one by one with stop-motion jitter. After NixMotion's Collage Art Promo for After Effects (Motion Array).
records.move: a torn-paper hole rips one collage shot away to a newsprint wall, then cutouts pop in one by one with 12fps stop-motion jitter
records.how: Two full-frame layers: shot A (teal paper, a gilded frame, torn text strips) underneath, shot B (a canvas-painted newsprint wall with mirrored headlines, body columns and white-out washes, plus an feTurbulence grain) on top, hidden by a CSS clip-path polygon. A 28-point jagged polygon grows from r=0 at 0.45s to past the frame by 1.45s on steps() eases, biased toward the bottom-left so it reads as paper peeled from a corner; a second white layer with the same polygon at 1.08x gives the torn white edge. Every cutout (sofa, statue-head figure with popcorn and ticket, cactus with sunflowers, two grey hands, phone, teacup, five paper labels) is an SVG or a text block wrapped in a filter that dilates its alpha by 7px, roughens it with feDisplacementMap and fills it white, so anything dropped in gets the cut-paper rim. Each cutout pops from scale 0 with a rotation and offset on steps(6) at its own time between 0.75s and 2.7s; the hands then pull back out. A jitter function, seeded per 12fps frame index and per element with fx.rng, offsets every cutout plus or minus 3px and 0.8deg, which is the stop-motion feel. Authored at 1920x1080 and scaled to the 1280x720 stage. Reference: NixMotion's Collage Art Promo (Motion Array), one 3.9s shot.
records.adapt: Swap any .cut's inner SVG for an of a real cutout (transparent PNG); the #cutout filter draws the white torn rim around whatever is inside, so photographic cutouts are the intended content. Change the label copy, colours and the newsprint headline list; reorder the pop schedule in the pop() calls. Keep the steps() eases and the frame-indexed jitter, or it stops being stop-motion. Drop shot A and start with the hole already open for a mid-film shot.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the two layers and the cutouts into el (unique the filter ids) and paints the newsprint canvas with ShotKit.rng; animate(el, shot, D) returns the gsap.timeline built here, with jitter(t) run from a single linear {u:0->1} tween's onUpdate over D instead of the seek hook. Scale the 1920x1080 root to the film stage (1x at 1920x1080).
caveats: feMorphology plus feDisplacementMap on every cutout is expensive; twelve cutouts at 1080p renders slowly and can stutter in live preview
clip-path polygons in percent are per layer; the torn edge is the white layer, not a stroke
the cutouts are vector stand-ins for the photographic collage elements of the reference

records.name: Morph: Animated Face
records.description: A face animation template that morphs between different expressions. Good for character animation and expressive brand mascot content.
records.move: flat face morphs eyes, mouth and head through happy, surprised, wink, neutral
records.how: A black circle head with yellow eyes, brows and mouth on a yellow square. At 0.05D, 0.3D, 0.55D and 0.8D the eye, mouth and head paths morphSVG to the next expression over 0.32s (power3.inOut; head with back.out(2)), brows translate and rotate, blush fades in or out, and the caption drops out (yPercent 120, 0.14s power2.in), swaps text in a callback, and falls in from -120 (expo.out). The face bobs y 0 to -10 and the eyes look side to side on 0.75s sine yoyos, and the surprise state adds a jump: y -40 in 0.18s then bounce.out back. The last state returns to neutral so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Replace the head/eye/mouth colours and the four labels; add or reorder expressions in the EYE/MOUTH/HEAD dictionaries; keep the 0.32s morph, the 0.75s state spacing and the bob yoyo.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the inline SVG and .label into el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with state times at 0.05D/0.3D/0.55D/0.8D. Scope '#eyeL' etc. to el (use el.querySelector) since ids are document-level.
caveats: label text is swapped in tl.add callbacks, so a backwards scrub does not restore the previous word
requires the MorphSVG plugin

records.name: Morph: Animated Icon
records.description: An icon animation template where an icon morphs fluidly from one form into another. Good for UI demonstrations and icon system showcases.
records.move: white icon morphs play, pause, heart, alert, star; blob background recolours
records.how: A dark card holds an SVG with a coloured blob and a white icon path, a name label under it and five pager dots. Every 0.2D (from 0.11D) the icon morphSVGs to the next shape over 0.55s (power3.inOut) while spinning 180 degrees and squeezing to scale 0.7 (power2.in) then back with back.out(3); the blob morphs to a new outline and fill colour over 0.6s, the name drops out (yPercent -110, power2.in), swaps in a callback and rises from 110 (expo.out), and the active dot moves. The blob rotates a full 360 over D (ease none). Five icons in 5s bring it back to Play.
records.adapt: Replace the ICONS paths, names and colours and the BG blob outlines; keep 0.55s morph, the 180-degree spin and the back.out(3) release; step = D / icon count.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card, SVG and dots; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with at = i*(D/n) + 0.11D. Scope '#icon', '#bg', '#nm', '.dots i' to el.
caveats: name and dot changes happen in callbacks and do not reverse on backward scrub
the last transition ends ~5.2s, past D=5, so the loop point cuts the final morph short
fromTo tweens use immediateRender:false and must keep it

records.name: Morph: Line to Radar Chart
records.description: A morphing animation template that transitions from a simple line into a full radar chart. Good for data visualization presentations where you want the chart to feel earned rather than just appearing.
records.move: line draws, bends into hexagon, grid spokes draw, data blooms, folds back
records.how: On a dark frame a white stroke draws itself left to right (drawSVG 0 to 100%, 1.2s expo.inOut at 0.02D), then morphSVGs into the outer hexagon over 1.4s (power3.inOut). Six spokes and two inner rings draw from the centre with staggered drawSVG (expo.out / expo.inOut), labels fade in, then two data polygons morph from a collapsed centre point to their values with back.out(1.4/1.6), dots scale in with back.out(3), and a score counts 0 to 76 (power2.out). At 0.66D the primary polygon re-flows to a second dataset with elastic.out(1,0.6) and the score runs to 84. From 0.84D everything collapses: dots, polygons to zero, grid drawSVG back to 0, copy leaves upward, and the hexagon morphs back to the line which erases (drawSVG 100% 100%).
records.adapt: Change the six axis labels, the A1/A2/B value arrays, colours and the side copy; keep the draw 1.2s, morph 1.4s, bloom back.out and the 8.4s fold-back that closes the loop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG and .side copy and builds the dot circles from the data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with beats as fractions (0.02, 0.17, 0.3, 0.41, 0.66, 0.84 of D). Scope all id selectors to el and the score onUpdate to el.querySelector('#num').
caveats: from() tweens on .kick/h1/.legend/.score need immediateRender:false
gsap.set drawSVG 0% on rings and spokes must run in mount before the timeline
needs both MorphSVG and DrawSVG plugins

records.name: Morph: Running Character
records.description: An animation template where an illustrated character morphs through a running loop. Good for fitness app mascots and playful brand character animations.
records.move: stick-figure limbs morph through a four-pose run cycle with body bob
records.how: A black blob-bodied runner on orange: four limb paths (front/back leg and arm) morphSVG through four stride poses, one per quarter of D with power1.inOut, the back limbs offset by two poses and arms counter to legs. The body group bobs y 384 to 358 twice per stride (sine.inOut yoyo), the lean group rocks 10 to 14 degrees, the shadow ellipse scales 1 to 0.8, the head lags by 0.04s, and three speed lines stream left 300px twice per loop (ease none).
records.adapt: Change body and background colours, the tag string, and the pose point arrays for a different gait; keep one stride per D and the half-stride offset of the back limbs.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with STEP = D/4. Scope '#legF' etc. via el.querySelector and call gsap.set on initial pose d attrs in mount.
caveats: speed lines tween x 0 to -300 with repeat 1 and no yoyo, so at t=D they sit at -300 while at t=0 they sit at 0; the loop is seamless for the runner but the lines jump
D=1 is very short; the catalog says 1s

records.name: Morph: Video Mask
records.description: A template where video is revealed through a shape that morphs as it opens. Works for cinematic openers and creative video transitions.
records.move: video window morphs dot, blob, flower, full frame, folds back to dot
records.how: A muted video is clipped by an SVG clipPath whose 8-segment cubic ring path starts as a 70px dot; a white stroke copy follows 0.06s behind. At 0.04D the path morphSVGs to a lumpy blob (back.out(1.5), 0.8s), at 0.24D to an 8-petal flower (power3.inOut), at 0.44D to a shape larger than the frame (expo.inOut, 1s) so the video fills the screen, while the mask rotates 0 to 40 degrees (sine.inOut). Title and subtitle rise from yPercent 110 (expo.out) at 0.54D, leave at 0.82D (expo.in), then the mask morphs back to blob and dot and the rotation returns to 0 by D. Video currentTime is set on every seek.
records.adapt: Swap the video src, the title/subtitle strings and the stroke colour; change the ring() radius functions for other shapes but keep 8 segments so morphs stay clean; keep the 0.2/1.2/2.2/4.25/4.65 beat structure scaled to D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the video, the clipPath SVG (unique id) and the title in el and returns once loadeddata fires; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline plus a {t:0->D} tween whose onUpdate sets video.currentTime (replaces the __fx.seek override). Scope '#mp', '#edge', '.t', '.s' to el.
caveats: clip-path: url(#m) is a document-level id, so multiple instances need unique ids
video seeking per frame needs the asset preloaded (fx.wait) and is not frame-exact on all browsers
from() tweens on .t/.s need immediateRender:false

records.name: Morph: Weather Icons
records.description: A template where weather icons morph smoothly between states. Good for weather app UI demos and forecast feature showcases.
records.move: sun morphs to cloud, rain, snow, storm; card colour and temperature follow
records.how: A blue card holds an SVG with a white body path (sun), eight ray lines, precipitation lines/circles, a bolt, a temperature and a label. Every D/5 (from 0.12D) the body morphSVGs SUN to CLOUD to CLOUD_LOW (power3.inOut, 0.7s), the rays scale/fade out (power2.in) or in (back.out(2), staggered), the card backgroundColor crossfades over 0.8s, the temperature counts (power2.out), and the label drops out and rises in via a callback swap. During rain, drops fall y -6 to 16 on repeating 0.45s power1.in tweens; snow flakes drift down with sideways x on sine; storm pops the bolt in with back.out(3) and flickers it. Rays rotate 90 degrees per loop (symmetric, seamless) and the body drifts x 0 to 4 on sine yoyo.
records.adapt: Change STATES (label, degrees, background colour, body path), the city string and the H/L/Wind row; keep 0.7s morphs and the step = D / states.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the card and builds rays/drops/flakes; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with STEP = D / states.length. Scope '#body', '#rays', '#lab', '#deg', '#card', '#bolt' to el.
caveats: the last state's morph and label swap run to ~7.25s, past D=7, so the loop cuts the return to Sunny slightly
label text changes in a callback and does not reverse on backward scrub
repeat-based rain/snow tweens use immediateRender:false and must keep it

records.name: Blur: Article Gallery [iOS]
records.description: An iOS-inspired article gallery template with blurred card backgrounds and a frosted glass feel. Good for editorial app UI demos and news app showcases.
records.move: frosted cards rise blurred, page sideways three times, fling home, fade
records.how: Portrait iOS feed: a blurred aurora wall drifts xPercent -3 to 3 and rotates 2 degrees over the whole loop, four 760px cards with blurred colour-blob art and backdrop-filter glass panels rise from y 260 / blur(30px) / scale 0.94 with a 0.09s stagger (expo.out, 0.9s), plus header and tab bar. At 0.21D, 0.41D and 0.61D the track slides -796px (expo.out, 0.85s); the leaving card blurs to 14px and scales 0.96, the arriving one sharpens, and the pager pill widens 14 to 44px. At 0.81D the track flings back to 0 (expo.inOut) with the same blur swap, and the last 0.3s fades header, cards and tab to opacity 0 so the entrance can replay.
records.adapt: Replace the four card titles, tags, blurbs, bylines and blob colours, the header date and tab labels; keep STEP = card width + gap, the three 1.6s page beats and the 0.85s expo.out slide.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the wall, header, .track cards, dots and tab; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with beats at 0.21D/0.41D/0.61D/0.81D and the fade at 0.96D. Scope '.wall', '.track', '.card', '.dots i', '.tab' to el.
caveats: animated filter: blur() on 760x1000 cards plus backdrop-filter glass and a full-frame blur(60px) wall is slow to render
from() tweens on .head/.card/.tab need immediateRender:false
the wall drift does not yoyo, so the background jumps slightly at the loop point
layout is absolute for a 1080x1920 stage

records.name: Blur: Bubbles
records.description: A template with soft blurred bubble shapes floating in a looping composition. Works as an ambient background for UI content and visual overlays that need a gentle layered feel.
records.move: eight blurred colour bubbles orbit and breathe behind a frosted card
records.how: Inside a filter: blur(38px) field, eight radial-gradient discs (260 to 560px, screen blend) move on seeded ellipses with integer cycle counts per loop and scale 0.85 to 1.1 on their own sine, all written as transform strings from a seek(t) function so t=D matches t=0. A fractal-noise grain sits over the field at 7%, and a centred backdrop-filter glass card with kicker, headline and a white button floats up and down 8px on one sine per loop.
records.adapt: Change the eight bubble colours, the card copy and the seed; keep integer kx/ky/ks cycle counts so the loop closes, and keep blur(38px) for the soft look.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends the .field with generated bubbles, .grain and .ui; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap timeline holding one {u:0->1, duration:D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate sets each bubble transform and the card translateY (the fx.register seek). Replace document.querySelector('.ui') with el.querySelector.
caveats: filter: blur(38px) over a full-frame field of eight large discs plus backdrop-filter is heavy per frame
no GSAP in the original; the port must add the timeline wrapper

records.name: Blur: Bubbles & Carousel
records.description: A template combining softly blurred bubble shapes in the background with a content carousel in the foreground. Works for lifestyle brand content and UI showcases that need a layered feel.
records.move: product cards slide left five times over drifting blurred bubbles
records.how: Cream stage with six blurred (46px) pastel discs orbiting on integer-cycle ellipses, driven directly from t. A track of five glass cards (backdrop-filter blur 20px) is duplicated so five steps of 428px land on an identical frame. Every 0.18D from 0.09D the track slides -428px more (expo.inOut, 0.9s); the passing card shrinks to 0.9, blurs 10px and dims to 0.6 (power2.in, 0.45s), the arriving card lifts y -18 (expo.out) and settles (power2.inOut), and the pager pill moves. Brand and title text are static.
records.adapt: Replace the items array (name, note, price, gradient pair), the brand and title, and the bubble colours; keep STEP = card width + gap, N steps at D/N spacing and the 0.9s expo.inOut slide.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the field bubbles, the doubled track and pager; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with steps at 0.09D + i*0.18D plus a {u:0->1, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate moves the bubbles (the __fx.seek override). Scope '.track', '.card', '.pager i' to el.
caveats: the track ends at -5*STEP, not 0; the loop only closes because the card set is duplicated
animated filter blur on cards plus backdrop-filter and a blur(46px) field is heavy
catalog lists 14s but the file renders D=10

records.name: Blur: Logo Switcher
records.description: A logo switcher template that transitions between marks with a blur. Ideal for brand family presentations and logo evolution showcases.
records.move: logos resolve from heavy blur, dissolve back into blur, glow recolours
records.how: Four logo lockups (SVG mark + wordmark) are stacked at centre on near-black. Each takes a 2.5s segment: it enters from opacity 0, blur(40px), scale 1.18 and loose letterSpacing to sharp, scale 1, -0.05em over 0.9s (expo.out) while its mark rotates in from -40 degrees; in the last 0.55s of the segment it dissolves out to blur(36px), scale 0.86, opacity 0 (power3.in). A 900px blur(120px) glow disc behind crossfades backgroundColor to each logo's colour (0.8s power2.inOut), rotates 360 and shifts xPercent -8 to 8 over the loop, and a pager dot brightens and scales 1.4 per logo.
records.adapt: Replace the SVG marks, names, taglines and --c colours; SEG = D / logo count; keep the 0.9s expo.out resolve and 0.55s power3.in dissolve.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends .glow, the .logo lockups and .idx dots; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with SEG = D/n. Scope '.logo', '#glow', '.idx i' to el and read --c from each logo.
caveats: filter: blur(120px) on a 900px disc plus blur(40px) on animating text is slow to render
the glow xPercent -8 to 8 does not return, so the background jumps a little at the loop
from() on the svg rotation needs immediateRender:false

records.name: Blur: News Stack [iOS]
records.description: An iOS-style news card stack template with blurred card backgrounds. Good for editorial and news app UI demos where you want the design to feel considered.
records.move: top news card swipes off up-left blurring, stack springs forward one step
records.how: A phone mock-up over a blurred ocean wall shows four frosted news cards stacked with depth: each deeper card is translated 22px down, scaled 0.07 smaller, blurred 4px more and darkened. Every D/4 the top card flies translate(-340,-180), rotates -14 degrees, shrinks 0.9 and blurs 18px over the first 32% of the segment (quartic ease-out) while fading, then re-enters at the back rising with opacity; the remaining cards move up one depth with a damped-cosine spring over 45% of the segment. The phone wallpaper and the wall drift on one full circle per loop. All state is computed from t in a seek function.
records.adapt: Replace the stories array (source, tag, headline, blurb, three blob colours), the header and side copy; keep SEG = D / cards, the 0.32 swipe fraction and the spring constants.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the wall, phone and .stack cards; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) placement. Replace document.querySelector('.wallpaper'/'.wall') with el.querySelector.
caveats: per-frame filter: blur() on four cards plus backdrop-filter glass and two full-frame blurred images is heavy
no GSAP in the original; the port must wrap the seek function in a tween

records.name: Blur: Swirl
records.description: A swirling blur effect template that distorts content in a circular motion. Works as an atmospheric transition or abstract background element.
records.move: rainbow band gradient and wordmark twist in a pixel swirl that breathes
records.how: A 480x270 offscreen canvas draws a rotating five-colour band gradient (one full turn per loop) with the word SWIRL punched in dark; every frame a per-pixel loop remaps that buffer through a swirl whose angle grows toward a centre that drifts on a small Lissajous, with strength 4.5*sin(2*pi*t/D) so it twists one way, unwinds, twists the other way and is zero at both ends. The result is upscaled to 1280x720 through ctx.filter blur that breathes 6 to 16px with the swirl, then saturate/contrast via CSS. A small caption sits at the bottom.
records.adapt: Change the gradient stops, the word drawn in drawContent, the swirl radius R and strength; keep strength on sin(2*pi*u) and the full gradient turn so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the output canvas and caption in el; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {u:0->1, duration:D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek paint. Canvas sizes are fixed constants; the source font must be loaded before drawing text.
caveats: a JavaScript per-pixel loop over 129,600 pixels plus getImageData every frame is CPU heavy
catalog lists 22s but the file renders D=10
canvas text uses the Sharp Grotesk font, which must be loaded

records.name: Counter: Blur
records.description: A counting animation that sharpens numbers from a soft blur. Great for loading screens and suspenseful reveals.
records.move: blurred percentage sharpens as it counts to 100, snaps, dissolves back
records.how: A 300px three-digit percentage on black with a blue halo and a thin progress bar. A state value tweens 0 to 100 over 3.1s (power3.out) from 0.07D and is written into the digits each seek; the whole number starts at blur(28px), scale 1.12, opacity 0.6 and resolves to sharp over 3.2s (power2.out), the label fades in with an 8px blur, and the halo scales 0.6 to 1.2. The changing units digit gets a tiny 6px re-blur that decays until its next change. At 0.85D the number pops to 1.04 and settles with elastic.out(1,0.5); at 0.93D the whole block blurs to 24px and fades to 0.
records.adapt: Change the label, the target value, the accent halo colour and the digit font; keep the 3.1s power3.out count and the 3.2s blur resolve that make it feel like focus pulling.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends .halo, .num digits, .lbl and .bar; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline plus an onUpdate on the state tween that writes digit text, per-digit blur and bar width (the __fx.seek override). Scope '#d0..d2', '#bar', '.num', '.wrap' to el.
caveats: ends faded to opacity 0 while it starts at opacity 0.6 blurred, so the loop point is a soft cut, not identical
animated filter: blur() on 300px text is slow to render
from() on .lbl needs immediateRender:false

records.name: Counter: Bold Poster
records.description: An oversized counting number in a poster-style layout. Perfect for event promos and bold, graphic animations.
records.move: giant two-digit count-up stamps down on a grid poster, page shakes once
records.how: Orange 1080 square with a faint grid, a top rule that draws in via scaleX (expo.out), header labels, a 760px two-digit number, a rotating black circular badge and bottom headline/blurb. The number rises from yPercent 30 / opacity 0 (expo.out), then a state value tweens 0 to 48 over 2.3s with power4.out; the units digit flickers opacity 0.75 to 1 as it changes. The badge pops in with back.out(2) from scale 0 rotation -90 and then turns 360 (ease none). At 0.69D the number scales 1.06 (power3.out, 0.12s) and settles with elastic.out(1,0.4) while the stage shakes y 10px three times. At 0.93D everything fades and lifts y -40 (power3.in).
records.adapt: Change TARGET, the header, badge and bottom copy, and the two poster colours; keep the 2.3s power4.out count and the stamp-and-shake at ~0.69D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the poster elements; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the digit-writing onUpdate attached to the state tween (the __fx.seek override). The shake tween targets .stage and must target el instead; scope '.big', '.badge', '.top', '.bottom', '.rule' to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
digit roll is a plain opacity flicker, not a slot-machine slide

records.name: Counter: Dotted Circle
records.description: A bold counter framed by an animated dotted circle. Great for vibrant stat reveals and playful countdowns.
records.move: dotted ring lights up clockwise to 87%, number pops, confetti bursts
records.how: A 520px SVG ring of 48 dots (dash pattern) with a grey track and a pink inner dotted orbit, a 200px percentage at centre. The ring scales in from 0.6, rotation -60 (expo.out) and the centre from 0.7 with back.out(2). A state value tweens 0 to 87 over 2.2s (power3.inOut) from 0.12D; each seek writes the number and sets stroke-dashoffset on a mask circle so the yellow dots reveal clockwise. The dot ring ticks in discrete steps and the inner orbit spins -360 over the loop. At 0.68D the number pops to 1.12 and settles with elastic.out(1,0.4) while 26 seeded confetti squares fly out radially (expo.out) and fall away; at 0.93D ring and centre fade to 0 and scale 0.9.
records.adapt: Change TARGET, the label, the dot count N and colours; keep the 2.2s power3.inOut fill and the 0.68D pop-plus-confetti beat.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG (with a unique mask id) and the confetti pieces; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with an onUpdate on the state tween that writes the number, the mask dashoffset and the ring rotations (the __fx.seek override). Scope every getElementById to el.
caveats: SVG mask id is document-level; multiple instances need unique ids
from() tweens need immediateRender:false
ring rotation is quantised in the seek so the dots step rather than glide

records.name: Counter: Frosted Glass
records.description: A frosted glass clock animation. Perfect for sleek countdowns, timers, and premium motion graphics.
records.move: frosted glass countdown, seconds digits flip up with a blur each tick
records.how: A backdrop-filter glass panel (blur 34px) over an aurora image and two blur(40px) orbs shows HH:MM:SS at 150px. Each digit cell holds two stacked spans; in the last 28% of every second the changing digit translates up 100% with a quartic ease while blurring 6px and the next digit rises from below. The colons blink with steps(1) every 0.5s, a diagonal sheen sweeps xPercent -120 to 120 over 1.6s (power2.inOut) at 0.24D, the background image drifts xPercent -2 to 2 and scales 1.05 to 1.1, the orbs bob 50px on sine yoyo and the panel floats 6px.
records.adapt: Change the START time array, the kicker and column labels, the orb colours and the background image; keep the 0.72 flip threshold and the 0.28s quartic flip.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the glass panel and digit cells; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline plus a {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate computes the remaining seconds and sets each digit's transforms (the __fx.seek override). Scope '.bg', '.orb', '.shine', '.colon', '.glass' to el.
caveats: the clock keeps counting, so the last frame (14:54) does not match the first (14:59); it is a clip, not a loop
the background drift does not yoyo and jumps at the loop point
backdrop-filter plus two blur(40px) orbs and a full-frame image is heavy to render

records.name: Counter: Glitch
records.description: A glitchy digital timer with a flickering, high-tech feel. Ideal for futuristic intros and countdown sequences.
records.move: monospace T-minus timer counts down with seeded RGB-split slice glitches
records.how: On a dark HUD grid a 210px monospace timer counts 00:10.00 down to zero over D (2.5x speed) with corner labels, a frame counter and a progress bar. A deterministic burst schedule from fx.rng marks 2 to 6 frame glitch windows every 8 to 30 frames; during a burst the red and cyan copies (mix-blend screen) offset horizontally by 8 to 34px with clip-path insets, the base layer gets a horizontal polygon slice tear, translateX and skewX, the timer may invert, the label flips to ##ERR_SYNC and the stage jitters 6px. Between bursts a faint frame-keyed opacity flicker remains, and scanlines roll 1440px per loop (an integer number of 4px periods).
records.adapt: Change the start time and speed, the four HUD strings and the accent colours; keep the burst schedule seed and lengths, and the 2.5x count rate scaled to D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the HUD, timer layers and bar; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) glitch/text logic. The jitter writes transform on .stage; target el instead, and scope all querySelectors to el.
caveats: the timer ends at 00:00.00 and starts at 00:10.00, so it does not loop
no GSAP in the original; the port wraps the seek in a tween
shakes the whole stage element, which must be the shot root in the port

records.name: Counter: Halftone Poster
records.description: A large halftone counter styled like a print event poster. Ideal for editorial layouts and graphic countdown designs.
records.move: huge halftone-screened number wipes in top-down and counts up on cream poster
records.how: Cream 1080 square with serif header, a rule that draws in via scaleX, uppercase headline, blurb and a circular stamp that pops in with back.out(2) and slowly turns 20 degrees. Each seek draws the two-digit value (0 to 21, power3.out over 2.4s from 0.1D) crisp to an offscreen canvas at 720px, then samples it on a 15-degree rotated dot grid whose cell tightens 60 to 22px (power2.out) as the number resolves, drawing dots sized by coverage; a top-down wipe (reveal 0 to 1, expo.out) grows the dots in. At 0.71D the number scales 1.06 and settles with elastic.out(1,0.4); at 0.93D the reveal runs back to 0 and the copy fades.
records.adapt: Change TARGET, the header, headline, blurb and stamp strings, ink and paper colours; keep the cell 60 to 22 tightening and the 2.4s power3.out count.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and the copy; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with an onUpdate on the state tweens that runs the halftone paint (the __fx.seek override). Scope '.rule', '.top', '.bot', '.stamp' to el; canvas is fixed 1080x1080.
caveats: per-frame getImageData on a 1080x1080 buffer plus thousands of sampled arcs is CPU heavy
canvas text uses Sharp Grotesk which must be loaded
from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: Counter: Pixel
records.description: A pixelated counter rendered on an animated halftone dot grid. Great for retro-style motion graphics and bold poster animations.
records.move: blocky pixel number counts to 256 over a rippling dot grid
records.how: A 64x36 offscreen canvas renders the three-digit value in Sharp Grotesk so it pixelates honestly; each frame every 20px cell that is lit becomes a yellow square and every other cell a white dot whose radius and alpha follow a two-axis sine wave (integer cycles per loop) scaled by an amplitude that tweens 1 to 0.25 over 2.8s (power2.out) as the number climbs 0 to 256 (power3.out, 2.6s from 0.075D). At 0.72D a pop value enlarges the glyphs 8% for 0.15s and settles with elastic.out(1,0.4); at 0.91D the amplitude ramps back to 1 (power2.in). A monospace caption and HUD score sit at the bottom.
records.adapt: Change TARGET, CELL size, the two colours and the caption strings; keep the amp 1 to 0.25 calming and the 2.6s power3.out count.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and captions; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with an onUpdate on the state tweens that runs the grid paint (the __fx.seek override). Canvas is fixed 1280x720 with COLS/ROWS derived from CELL.
caveats: ends on 256 and starts on 000, so the number does not loop even though the grid wave does
2304 cells drawn per frame with arcs; acceptable but not free
canvas font must be loaded before the first frame

records.name: Counter: Progress Ring
records.description: A circular progress counter that fills a ring as the percentage climbs. Perfect for loading indicators and stat reveals.
records.move: ring arc fills to 100 with a hesitation at 70, turns green
records.how: Light stage with a 420px SVG ring (grey track, blurred glow arc, blue arc via stroke-dashoffset, white tip dot) and a white sync card with three thin bars. Ring scales in from 0.85 (expo.out), card slides from x 60 (expo.out). Progress tweens 0 to 68 over 1.3s (power2.out) from 0.1D, creeps to 74 (power1.inOut) then runs to 100 (power3.inOut, 0.8s); each seek sets both arcs' dashoffset, moves the tip along the circle, writes the number, swaps the subtitle (Uploading / Almost there / Complete) and scales the card bars. At 0.75D the number pops 1.1 and settles with elastic.out(1,0.45) while arc, glow and bars recolour to green over 0.4s; at 0.93D ring and card fade and lift 20px.
records.adapt: Change the card title, folder names and bar ratios, the accent and completion colours, and the three-stage progress values; keep the hesitation beat and the 0.8s power3.inOut run to 100.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the ring SVG and card; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with an onUpdate on the state tweens that sets dashoffsets, tip position, number, subtitle and bar widths (the __fx.seek override). Scope '#arc', '#glowarc', '#tip', '#v', '#sub', '.f' to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
the glow arc uses an inline style filter: blur(10px) on an SVG stroke

records.name: Blend Modes: Circle Stack
records.description: A template with circles stacked and layered using blend mode effects. Creates an abstract visual that works well for experimental motion design and brand content.
records.move: five multiply-blend circles orbit on ellipses and breathe, stacking order flips
records.how: Five 420px flat-colour circles with mix-blend-mode multiply on cream, each on its own ellipse (radii 180 to 260 by 90 to 150) at one orbit per loop, alternating direction, phased a fifth apart, with scale 1 plus 0.18*sin at two pulses per loop and a zIndex that follows the orbit depth so the stacking order rolls. Everything is computed from t in a seek function via gsap.set, so t=D equals t=0. A small label and ring mark are static.
records.adapt: Change the five circle colours (multiply wants saturated primaries on a light ground), the circle size, the label; keep integer orbit and pulse counts per loop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends the .c circles and label; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) gsap.set calls. Scope querySelectorAll('.c') to el.

records.name: Blend Modes: Collage Shuffle
records.description: A template where a collage of images shuffles through blend mode transitions. Good for editorial motion graphics and dynamic portfolio presentations.
records.move: six tinted photo tiles swap grid slots, each pass a new blend
records.how: A 3x2 grid of 352x274 image tiles, each with a colour-blend tint overlay, over a drifting aurora paper. Every 0.25D a permutation of order four moves each tile to its next slot over 0.9s (expo.inOut) with a 0.06s stagger per column; during the move the tile scales to 1.12 and tilts 3 degrees (power2.out) then settles, and its mix-blend-mode is switched to difference, screen, exclusion or lighten for that pass so overlapping tiles flash inverted or bleached colours mid-flight, then back to normal. An index counter updates each pass; four passes return every tile home.
records.adapt: Replace the six background images and --tint colours, the caption; keep the perm array (a 4-cycle plus a 2-cycle) or pick another permutation whose order divides the pass count so it returns home.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .paper and the six .tile divs with the shot's images; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with passes at i*0.25D. Scope '.tile', '.idx', '.paper' to el.
caveats: the paper drift (scale 1.05 to 1.1, xPercent -1 to 1) does not return, so the background jumps slightly at the loop
blend-mode switches are tl.set calls and are scrub-safe, but mid-flight blends depend on image content
needs image assets from ../../../assets/backgrounds

records.name: Blend Modes: Color Blocks
records.description: A blend mode animation template with layered color blocks that interact to create rich visual depth. Great for abstract backgrounds and brand-forward motion graphics.
records.move: multiply colour rectangles fly in from edges, drift over each other, exit
records.how: Five flat rectangles (cyan, magenta, yellow, blue, green) with mix-blend-mode multiply on off-white enter from four edges with slight rotation over 1s (expo.out), staggered 0.07s from 0. From 0.22D they slide 100 to 220px across each other for 2.8s (sine.inOut) so the overlap colours keep changing.
