The headline pops in at 0.15D with back.out(1.8) in overlay blend and snaps out (power3.in) at 0.77D; from 0.82D the blocks leave the way they came, staggered 0.07s (expo.in, 0.55s), so t=D matches t=0.
records.adapt: Change the block colours, sizes and positions, the headline and footer strings; keep the enter/exit symmetry, the 1s expo.out entrance and the 2.8s sine drift.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends the .b blocks, .word and .foot; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entrances at i*0.014D, drift at 0.22D, exits from 0.82D. Scope '.b1..b5' and '.word' to el.

records.name: Blend Modes: Double Exposure
records.description: A double exposure animation template created through layered blend modes. Good for editorial motion graphics and visual storytelling that needs a more cinematic quality.
records.move: three lighten-blend photos drift and breathe inside a dark silhouette
records.how: A black SVG head-and-shoulders silhouette on white, covered by three full-frame images with mix-blend-mode lighten and heavy contrast filters; over white lighten is white, over the dark silhouette the image shows, giving the double exposure. Each layer moves x/y 12 to 50px, scales 1.04 to 1.15 and breathes opacity on sines of the loop phase (every term a whole cycle), and the silhouette bobs 6px and scales 1%. All values are set from t in a seek function via gsap.set.
records.adapt: Replace the silhouette path and the three images (high-contrast landscapes work best), the caption and tag; keep whole-cycle sine terms so the 2s loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the silhouette SVG and the .ex image layers; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) gsap.set calls. Scope '.ex1..3' and '.silhouette' to el.
caveats: three full-frame images with filter contrast/saturate and mix-blend-mode are costly to composite
needs image assets from ../../../assets/backgrounds

records.name: Blend Modes: Gradient Orbs
records.description: A template with glowing gradient orbs that interact through blend modes in a looping animation. Good for atmospheric brand backgrounds and ambient visual content.
records.move: five blurred screen-blend gradient orbs weave on Lissajous curves and pulse
records.how: Five 520px radial-gradient orbs with mix-blend-mode screen and filter blur(28px) on near-black, each following a Lissajous curve with integer frequencies 1 to 3 and radii 260 to 320 by 150 to 230, scaling 0.9 to 1.3 on a two-pulse sine, all set from t via gsap.set so t=D equals t=0. A fractal-noise SVG grain overlay at 14% and a static caption sit on top.
records.adapt: Change the five gradient colour pairs, the orb size and the caption; keep integer Lissajous frequencies so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends the .o orbs, the grain SVG (unique filter id) and caption; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) gsap.set calls. Scope querySelectorAll('.o') to el.
caveats: filter: blur(28px) on five 520px orbs with screen blend plus a feTurbulence overlay is heavy
SVG filter id #g is document-level

records.name: Gradients: Bento
records.description: A bento grid template where each cell has its own animated gradient. Ideal for colorful product showcases and social media content where you want color to do some of the heavy lifting.
records.move: bento cells run separate gradient loops: conics spin, linears scroll, radials breathe
records.how: A 4x2 bento grid with wide and tall cells, each holding a 1400px gradient layer larger than the cell. Two conic gradients rotate 360 and -360 over D (ease none), two linear gradients scroll backgroundPosition one tile (700px) in x or y, two radial gradients slide 240px and 160px while scaling 0.55 to 0.8 and 0.45 to 0.7 with sine.inOut yoyo. Every cell also breathes scale 1 to 0.97 on one sine yoyo per loop. Stat numbers and labels are static text over the colour.
records.adapt: Change the six gradient definitions, the stat and label strings and the grid spans; keep full turns and one-tile scrolls per D so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the .grid cells; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with durations D and D/2. Scope '.g.conic' etc. and '.cell' to el.
caveats: six 1400px gradient layers with rotation are large to rasterise
linear scroll relies on background-size 50%/100% of a 1400px layer equalling 700px

records.name: Gradients: Diagonal Sweep
records.description: A gradient animation template with a diagonal sweep that moves across the frame in a loop. Works well as an animated background for brand content and social media.
records.move: two blurred diagonal light bands sweep purple ground, one period per loop
records.how: A 2600px square rotated -35 degrees holds two repeating-linear-gradient bands (warm pink-orange-yellow, cooler blue-violet) with screen blend and blur 6 to 10px over a dark purple base. The warm band translates x -1300 to 0 and the cool band -650 to 650, each exactly one gradient period, over D with power1.inOut so the sweep pushes and settles yet stays seamless; a centred wordmark breathes scale 0.98 to 1.02 on sine yoyo, and a radial darkening keeps edges deep.
records.adapt: Change the gradient stop colours, the band angle and the wordmark; keep the translate distance equal to the repeating period (1300px) so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends .base, .band with .i/.j, .soft, .title, .sub; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with duration D. Scope '.band .i', '.band .j', '.title' to el.
caveats: 2600px rotated layers with blur and screen blend are expensive to composite
power1.inOut on a seamless period makes the sweep visibly slow down at the loop point

records.name: Gradients: Geometric Morph
records.description: A template with gradient-filled geometric shapes that shift and morph between forms. Good for abstract motion graphics and modern brand content.
records.move: three glowing gradient shapes cycle circle, square, triangle, hexagon while spinning
records.how: Three SVG paths filled with linear gradients sit at thirds of the width, each with a blurred (feGaussianBlur 18) glow copy behind at 55% opacity. Every D/4 each shape morphSVGs to the next form in the ring circle, square, triangle, hexagon over 0.75s (expo.inOut) from a different starting form so the fourth morph lands on its first; all rotate 360 over D (ease none) and the main shapes pulse scale 1 to 1.12 on a sine yoyo eight times per loop.
records.adapt: Change the three gradient pairs, the radius R, the caption and the forms list; keep the ring walk so each shape returns to its start after N morphs.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG with unique gradient and filter ids; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with step = D/N. Scope '#sa'..'#sc2' to el.
caveats: SVG feGaussianBlur on three glow copies re-rasterises every frame
gradient and filter ids are document-level

records.name: Gradients: Haze
records.description: A gradient animation template that shifts slowly between colors with a hazy atmospheric quality. Works as a background for brand visuals that need mood without too much movement.
records.move: five heavily blurred colour blobs circle slowly under drifting fog and grain
records.how: Inside a wrapper with filter blur(70px) saturate(1.2), five 760px radial-gradient blobs circle once per loop on ellipses (radii 300 to 380 by 160 to 260), alternating direction, and breathe scale 1 to 1.25 on one sine; the wrapper rocks 4 degrees. An SVG feTurbulence fog rect in soft-light blend drifts on a 60px circle, a fine-noise grain sits over it at 12% overlay, and an italic serif caption sits at the bottom. All values come from t via gsap.set.
records.adapt: Change the five blob colours, the ground colour and the caption; keep single-cycle sines so the 7s loop closes, and keep blur(70px) for the haze.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends .wrap with blobs, the fog and grain SVGs (unique filter ids) and caption; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) gsap.set calls. Scope '.blob', '#fogRect', '.wrap' to el.
caveats: filter blur(70px) over a 130% wrapper plus two feTurbulence full-frame filters is very slow to render
SVG filter ids #f and #g are document-level

records.name: Gradients: Kaleidoscope
records.description: A kaleidoscope gradient template with rotating patterns that shift in a loop. Good for vibrant backgrounds and experimental motion design.
records.move: twelve mirrored wedges of drifting gradient discs turn as a kaleidoscope
records.how: A 520px offscreen canvas draws four additive radial-gradient discs moving on sines (one and two cycles per loop). The main canvas clips 12 wedges around centre, mirrors every other one, rotates the whole pattern two wedges per loop, and inside each wedge counter-rotates the source a full turn and slides it one tile (520px) per loop before filling with a repeating pattern of the source, so t=D is identical to t=0. A radial vignette darkens the edges and a static caption sits bottom-left.
records.adapt: Change the four disc colour pairs, the source background and N wedges; keep the two-wedge spin, the full counter-rotation and the one-tile slide so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and caption; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek paint. Canvas is fixed 1280x720.
caveats: createPattern and 12 clipped 7x-tile fills per frame are moderate cost
catalog says rotating patterns; the pattern is mirrored wedges of a canvas, not CSS gradients

records.name: Gradients: Morphing Shapes
records.description: A template with gradient-filled shapes that slowly morph between forms in a continuous loop. Works as an abstract background or a statement visual element.
records.move: three gradient blobs morph through four forms, drift, rotate, multiply-blend
records.how: Three SVG paths filled with linear gradients (orange-pink, violet-cyan, green-yellow) sit on cream with mix-blend-mode multiply so overlaps go dark and rich. Each path is a seeded 8-spoke blob; MorphSVG tweens it through four seeded forms and back to the first, one form per D/4 with sine.inOut, so the silhouettes swell and dent continuously. On top, each blob turns a full 360 (alternating direction) linearly over D, sways x by ±40px over one sine yoyo cycle and bobs y ±25px over two, so the last frame equals the first. A serif italic word sits top-right and a caption bottom-left, static.
records.adapt: Swap the three gradient stop colours and the background, the wordmark and caption text; change blob count, base radius and seeds for a different silhouette. Keep the four-form morph at D/4 each and the whole-cycle drift/rotation so the loop still closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG with gradient defs and three paths, builds the blob path strings with a seeded rng and gsap.set positions; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with morph steps at k*D/4, rotation over D and yoyo drifts, selecting paths via el.querySelector. Needs MorphSVGPlugin registered; blob centres are absolute 1280x720 coordinates, so scale them to the shot size.
caveats: mix-blend-mode multiply on three gradient paths is fill-rate heavy at full frame
blob positions are hard-coded for a 1280x720 viewBox

records.name: Gradients: Petals
records.description: A looping gradient animation template with soft organic shapes drifting and blending into each other. Works well as a background for brand content or social media posts that need a bit of visual warmth.
records.move: six blurred gradient petals orbit an ellipse, rotate and squash, multiply-blending
records.how: Six rounded-blob divs, each a warm linear gradient (pink, peach, lilac, gold, rose, mint) with mix-blend-mode multiply, live inside a field blurred by filter blur(22px) on a pale peach background. A seek function places each petal on an ellipse (rx 260-340, ry 130-160) at phase i/6, using x/y = cos/sin of one full revolution per D, spins it a full turn (alternating direction) and breathes scaleX 1±0.15 / scaleY 1∓0.1 at twice the orbit rate. Everything is a whole number of cycles per D so the last frame matches the first. A small dark dot at top and a serif italic caption at the bottom stay still.
records.adapt: Change the six petal gradients and the background, the caption line, and the petal size or count; the ellipse radii can grow for a wider frame. Keep one orbit and one rotation per D and the 2x breathing so it still loops.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the blurred field and six petal divs plus the caption; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear tween of a progress object (0 to 1 over D) whose onUpdate runs the seek maths and gsap.sets each petal, because the original drives it with fx.register rather than a timeline. Scope querySelectorAll(".p") to el.
caveats: filter: blur(22px) on a full-frame container with six multiply-blended layers is slow to render
motion is a seek function, not tweens; port it as a progress tween with onUpdate

records.name: Gradients: Vertical Sweep
records.description: A gradient animation template with a vertical sweep that moves through the frame in a loop. Works well as an animated background for brand and social content.
records.move: two blurred colour bands sweep vertically past each other, screen-blended
records.how: On a navy base gradient, two 2880px-tall repeating-linear-gradient bands (green-cyan-yellow, and violet-pink at 55% opacity) are blurred 8-14px and screen-blended over the frame. Band A slides y from -1440 to 0 (exactly one repeat period) and band B slides from 720 to -720 over the full D, both with power1.inOut, so the sweep pushes through the frame and settles at the loop point with identical pixels. A large centred wordmark bobs y 6 to -6 and back with one sine yoyo cycle; a radial vignette and a small uppercase subline stay still.
records.adapt: Replace the two band colour stops and the navy base with the product palette, and the title and subline text. Keep the one-period travel distances so the band tiles seamlessly; ease can become none for a constant conveyor feel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) adds the base, two band divs, vignette and title inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the two band tweens over D and the title yoyo. The band heights assume a 720px frame; scale the 1440px period with the shot height.
caveats: power1.inOut means velocity dips to zero at the loop boundary, a visible breath rather than a constant sweep
blur(8px)/blur(14px) on 2880px-tall screen-blended layers is expensive

records.name: Animated Stripes
records.description: A template with animated stripes flowing across the composition in a continuous loop. Good for energetic backgrounds and motion graphics with a sporty feel.
records.move: tilted colour stripes conveyor one way, thin dark stripes race the other
records.how: A 2400px square sheet rotated -24deg holds two layers: wide 64px bands on a 96px pitch cycling orange, cream and yellow, and thin 10px near-black stripes on a 48px pitch. Layer one translates y by -8 pitches and layer two by +20 pitches over D with ease none, so both tile seamlessly and appear to flow in opposite directions. The whole sheet leans from -24 to -18deg and scales 1 to 1.08 in one sine yoyo cycle, and the wide bands pulse scaleY 1 to 0.72 in a staggered wave (0.035s each) down the sheet. A radial vignette darkens the corners.
records.adapt: Change the three band colours and the background, the tilt angle and band pitch; fewer, fatter bands read as more graphic. Keep the integer-pitch travel distances so the scroll loops.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the rotated sheet and appends the band divs for both layers; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline: two linear y tweens over D, the yoyo lean/scale and the staggered scaleY pulse, with selectors scoped to el. The 2400px sheet assumes a 1280x720 frame; size it to cover the rotated shot.
caveats: the staggered scaleY pulse starts up to 1.1s late for the last bands so they are still mid-cycle at D; the loop does not close cleanly on band thickness
about 85 animated band elements

records.name: Big Waves
records.description: A template with large wave shapes sweeping across the frame in a continuous loop. Good for bold background compositions and fluid visual atmospheres.
records.move: three layered gradient waves sweep sideways and heave up and down
records.how: Three SVG paths, each a cubic-approximated sine wave three wavelengths wide with a vertical blue gradient (deep blue back, mid blue, pale cyan front), are stacked with baselines at 300, 420 and 540px. Each path translates x by an integer number of wavelengths over D with ease none (back layers 1-2 cycles leftward, front layer 3 cycles rightward) so the seam is invisible. Each also heaves y up 30-54px and back with sine.inOut yoyo, one cycle for the back layer and up to three for the front. The stage is a navy vertical gradient.
records.adapt: Change the three gradient pairs and the background, the amplitudes and baselines, and the number of layers. Keep the integer-wavelength travel per D and integer heave cycles so the loop stays seamless.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG with gradient defs and generates the wave paths from the layer table; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline of x sweeps over D and y yoyos, selecting paths within el. Path geometry assumes a 1280x720 viewBox with preserveAspectRatio none, so it stretches to any shot size.

records.name: Chevrons Moving Down
records.description: A template with downward-pointing chevrons flowing continuously in a loop. Perfect for directional backgrounds and motion graphics.
records.move: five columns of stacked chevrons stream downward, centre column fastest
records.how: An SVG holds five columns of rounded-stroke polyline chevrons pointing down, cycling orange, white and amber, with the centre column widest and most opaque and the outer ones smaller and dimmer. Each column group translates y by pitch times speed (3, 4, 5, 4, 3 pitches) over D with ease none, so the centre streams fastest and every column tiles seamlessly. The whole SVG sways x from -14 to 14px and back with one sine.inOut yoyo cycle, and a vertical fade masks the top and bottom 22% into the near-black background.
records.adapt: Change the three stroke colours and background, the column widths and stroke weights, or the number of columns. Keep integer pitches per D for each column so the stream loops; D is 10s here although the catalog lists 15.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the SVG, builds the column groups of polylines and adds the fade overlay; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with one linear y tween per column over D plus the SVG sway. Column centres are absolute 1280-wide coordinates; scale them to the shot width.
caveats: duration is 10s, not the 15s listed in the catalog

records.name: Chevrons Moving Up
records.description: A template with upward-pointing chevrons flowing continuously in a loop. Good for motion graphics and backgrounds where upward movement carries meaning.
records.move: five columns of stacked chevrons stream upward, centre column fastest
records.how: An SVG holds five columns of rounded-stroke polyline chevrons pointing up, cycling mint, pale mint and green on a dark green background, with the centre column widest and most opaque and the outer ones smaller and dimmer. Each column group translates y by minus pitch times speed (3, 4, 5, 4, 3 pitches) over D with ease none, so the centre rises fastest and every column tiles seamlessly. The whole SVG sways x from -14 to 14px and back with one sine.inOut yoyo cycle, and a vertical fade masks the top and bottom 22% into the background.
records.adapt: Change the three stroke colours and background, the column widths and stroke weights, or the number of columns. Keep integer pitches per D for each column so the stream loops; D is 10s here although the catalog lists 15.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the SVG, builds the column groups of polylines and adds the fade overlay; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with one linear negative y tween per column over D plus the SVG sway. Column centres are absolute 1280-wide coordinates; scale them to the shot width.
caveats: duration is 10s, not the 15s listed in the catalog

records.name: Circle Cascade
records.description: A template where circles cascade into view in a staggered sequence. Works for animated intros and abstract visual sequences with a satisfying rhythm.
records.move: grid of dots pops in along the diagonal, then shrinks away
records.how: A 10x6 CSS grid of 92px circles, mostly near-black with seeded orange, blue and yellow accents, sits on cream. Each dot scales 0 to 1 and fades in with back.out(2.2) over 0.55s, delayed by (row+col)*0.045s so the cascade sweeps from top-left to bottom-right, finishing by 0.6 D. From 0.62 D each dot shrinks to 0 with power3.in over 0.3s along the same diagonal at 60% of the in-delay, so the frame is empty at both ends of the 2s loop.
records.adapt: Change the dot colours and accent ratio, grid dimensions and dot size, or start the cascade from another corner by changing the delay formula. Keep the 0.045s diagonal stagger and the back.out in / power3.in out for the same rhythm.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid of cells and dots with a seeded rng for colours; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with fromTo pops at (r+c)*0.045 and the shrink-outs at 0.62 D, scaled as fractions of D. Nothing is viewport-dependent beyond the grid filling el.

records.name: Dancing Dots
records.description: A looping animation template where dots bounce in a playful rhythmic pattern. Good for loading states and animated backgrounds.
records.move: coloured balls bounce in a travelling wave with squash and stretch
records.how: Nine 84px balls in orange, yellow, mint and blue sit on a faint floor line with a blurred dark shadow ellipse under each. A seek function gives every ball a bounce phase once per second offset by 0.11 per ball, so the bounce runs down the line: 16% of each cycle is floor contact with scaleX up to 1.32 and scaleY down to 0.62, the rest is a parabola into the air with a slight stretch. Jump height swells between 100 and 280px with one sine cycle per D, and each shadow shrinks and fades as its ball rises. Four bounces per 4s loop, so the last frame equals the first.
records.adapt: Change the ball colours and count, the floor position and the bounce period; a single ball works as a loader. Keep the 0.11 phase offset per ball and an integer number of bounces per D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the floor, shadows and balls; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with a single linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate runs the bounce maths and gsap.sets y/scaleX/scaleY per ball and scale/opacity per shadow. The x layout is centred on 640px; compute from the shot width.
caveats: motion is a seek function with a custom bounce curve, not tweens; port as a progress tween with onUpdate

records.name: Fluted Glass Background [iOS]
records.description: A fluted glass iPhone background effect that distorts visuals with a refractive, ribbed texture. Ideal for modern UI animations and product reveals.
records.move: iPhone lock screen behind sliding fluted glass ribs, colours refract
records.how: A phone frame with Dynamic Island, clock, a glass notification and controls holds a 340x700 canvas. Each frame the canvas draws four coloured radial blobs orbiting on ellipses (1 or 2 cycles per D) into a source canvas, then redraws it column by column through a 22px sawtooth lens so every rib stretches and offsets the picture, adds a specular highlight and shadow edge per rib, and slides the rib pattern one full rib per D so it loops. A paused GSAP timeline turns the phone rotationY -14 to 14 and rotationX 4 to -4 in one sine yoyo cycle, and a notification drops in with expo.out at 0.16 D and lifts out with power3.in at 0.78 D. A violet halo glows behind.
records.adapt: Change the four blob colours and the base tint, the lock-screen time and date, the notification brand and message; rib width RIB controls the flute pitch. Keep the one-rib slide per D and integer blob orbits.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone DOM and both canvases; animate(el, shot, D) returns the phone/notification timeline with an added linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate redraws the source and the per-column refraction. The seek override that chains the DOM timeline onto fx.register is replaced by that single timeline; canvas size is fixed at 340x700 regardless of shot size.
caveats: per-column drawImage (340 calls) plus per-rib gradients every frame; fine at this size, slow if the canvas grows
backdrop-filter blur on the notification and controls
DOM motion and canvas motion are combined by overriding window.__fx.seek

records.name: Gradient Background
records.description: A simple animated gradient background template that shifts through colors in a slow continuous loop. Works as a versatile backdrop for almost any composition.
records.move: four huge blurred colour blobs drift while the hue wheel turns
records.how: Four 900px circles in pink, orange, blue and teal, blurred 90px at 0.9 opacity, sit in an oversized field on deep violet with a faint scanline overlay. Each blob sweeps x by 2rx and back with sine.inOut yoyo (one or two cycles per D) and y between -ry and ry offset by a quarter cycle, so they slide past each other; a separate lead-in tween eases y from -ry to 0 over the first quarter. The whole field runs filter hue-rotate 0 to 360deg linearly over D, so the palette walks the colour wheel once. D is 10s.
records.adapt: Change the four blob colours (hue-rotate moves them together, so pick the starting relationship), the background, blob size and blur radius. Keep integer orbit cycles per D and the full hue turn.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the field and four blob divs plus the grain overlay; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline of x/y yoyos and the hue-rotate tween, selectors scoped to el. Blob offsets are pixel values tuned for 1280x720.
caveats: the y lead-in tween ends at 0 while the yoyo orbit starts at -ry, so y jumps at D/4 and the y position at D differs from t=0; the loop does not close cleanly on blob position
filter: blur(90px) on four 900px layers plus hue-rotate on the parent is slow to render
duration is 10s, not the 15s listed in the catalog

records.name: Gradient Noisy Blur
records.description: A gradient background template with a noisy blur texture that adds grain and warmth. Good for lo-fi brand aesthetics and atmospheric visuals.
records.move: warm blurred blobs breathe and swap places under live film grain
records.how: Four 820px circles in orange, hot pink, gold and plum, blurred 110px, sit on deep brown; two full-frame SVG feTurbulence layers (fine grain soft-light, coarse grain overlay) and a radial vignette lie on top. Each blob slides on a short diagonal and back (b1 +220/+120, b2 -260/+140) or scales 1 to 1.25 / 1 to 0.85 with sine.inOut yoyo over one cycle per D. Every frame the fine noise seed advances (30 per second, cycling 120) and the coarse seed steps 6 per second, so the grain crawls like film; both seeds return to their start at D.
records.adapt: Change the four blob colours and the background tint, blob size and blur, and the grain strength via the two layer opacities. Keep the yoyo cycles whole per D and the seed cycle lengths so grain and blobs both loop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) adds the blobs, the two filter SVGs with unique filter ids and the vignette; animate(el, shot, D) returns the blob timeline plus a linear progress tween whose onUpdate sets the two feTurbulence seed attributes from the current time, replacing the window.__fx.seek override. Filter ids must be unique per instance.
caveats: filter: blur(110px) on four large layers plus two full-frame feTurbulence filters is slow to render
grain seeding is done by patching window.__fx.seek, not on the timeline

records.name: Halftone Effect
records.description: A halftone effect that breaks your visuals into a pattern of animated dots. Great for retro-inspired motion graphics and print-style animations.
records.move: rotated halftone dot screen renders a sun and word, screen angle breathes
records.how: A canvas draws a low-res source each frame: a vertical white-to-grey gradient, a shaded sun disc that swings across and up on a cosine arc once per D, and the word RETRO along the bottom. The output samples that source on a rotated lattice of 14px cells and fills a dark dot per cell whose radius grows with darkness, on a cream background. The screen angle drifts 0.26 rad plus or minus 0.06 and the dot gain 1 plus or minus 0.12, each one sine cycle per D, so the print screen seems to breathe; every quantity is periodic so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Replace drawSource with the product image or logo (same-origin so getImageData works), change the word, the paper and ink colours, and CELL for coarser or finer dots. Keep the angle and gain breathing to avoid a static screen.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the output canvas and offscreen source canvas; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate draws the source and rasterises the dots, replacing fx.register. Wait for the font before the first frame. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused in the original.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it
per-frame getImageData plus roughly 6000 arcs; acceptable at 1280x720
the source picture is procedural, not an uploaded image

records.name: Luma Dot Background
records.description: A luminance-based dot background that reacts to the brightness of your image. Perfect for abstract motion graphics and looping backgrounds.
records.move: dot grid sized by brightness of drifting aurora and roaming light
records.how: A canvas paints a low-res source each frame: three coloured aurora ribbons (mint, periwinkle, pink) whose vertical position and thickness ripple with sine waves that travel across the frame 1 or 2 cycles per D, plus a white radial light that roams on a Lissajous path (cos once, sin twice per D). The output is a 16px grid of dots on near-black, each dot radius rising with source luminance to the 1.3 power and coloured slightly brighter than the source pixel, so bright regions bloom into large dots and dark sky vanishes. All motion is periodic in D.
records.adapt: Replace drawSource with the product image or brand gradient (same-origin), change the ribbon colours, CELL size and the luminance exponent for contrast. Keep the roaming light for life across a still image.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the output and offscreen canvases; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate draws the source and the dot grid, replacing fx.register. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it
per-frame getImageData and about 3600 arcs; fine at this size

records.name: Moving Dots
records.description: A template with a field of dots drifting in a continuous loop. Ideal for subtle animated backgrounds and ambient visual textures that add depth without drawing too much attention.
records.move: two dot lattices drift diagonally at parallax speeds, breathing in waves
records.how: A canvas on off-white draws two dot fields: a fine 56px lattice of 3px dots at 35% and a coarser 112px lattice of 6px dots at 70%, offset from each other. Each frame both lattices shift one full pitch diagonally over D (the coarse one moves twice as far in pixels so it reads nearer), and every dot radius breathes between 0.65x and 1.35x on a diagonal sine wave that crosses the field once per D. A radial fade softens the edges into the background. D is 2s.
records.adapt: Change the dot colour and background, the two pitches and radii, or the drift direction; fewer layers reads calmer. Keep whole-pitch travel per D so the loop is seamless.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and fade overlay; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate redraws both lattices, replacing fx.register. Draw loops use the canvas size, so it adapts to any shot. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it

records.name: Moving Lines
records.description: A template with parallel lines moving continuously across the frame in a loop. Good for kinetic backgrounds and striped visual patterns.
records.move: tilted parallel lines march sideways while a compression wave bunches them
records.how: A canvas on navy draws a fan of vertical lines tilted -0.35 rad about the centre, spaced 36px. Each frame the lines scroll six pitches across D so the march is seamless, while a sine compression wave (two cycles across the span, travelling the opposite way once per D) displaces each line by up to a third of the pitch, thickens it from 2 to 7px and brightens it from dim blue to near-white cyan where the wave crests. The result reads as light pulsing through a striped field.
records.adapt: Change the background and line colour ramp, the pitch, the tilt, and the wave count; a vertical tilt of 0 gives a pure barcode. Keep the integer-pitch scroll and one wave cycle per D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate redraws the line fan, replacing fx.register. The span is computed from the canvas diagonal so it works at any size. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it

records.name: Rotating Crosses
records.description: A template with cross shapes rotating in a looping animation. Good for geometric pattern backgrounds and abstract visual compositions.
records.move: grid of plus signs quarter-turn in a checkerboard with a diagonal ripple
records.how: A 10x6 grid of 64px plus-shaped crosses, near-black with every fourth diagonal in orange, on warm off-white. Each cross rotates 0 to 90deg with expo.inOut over 0.55s, neighbours turning opposite ways, delayed up to 0.35s by diagonal distance so the turn ripples from top-left; because a cross is fourfold symmetric the end state equals the start. During the turn each cross dips scale 1 to 0.8 and back with sine.inOut yoyo. The full cycle is 1s.
records.adapt: Change the ink and accent colours and background, the grid size, the cross arm thickness, or replace the cross with any fourfold-symmetric glyph. Keep the 90deg turn and the diagonal delay so the loop stays clean.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid and cross elements; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline of rotation and scale tweens with delays as fractions of D. Nothing depends on viewport size beyond the grid filling el.

records.name: Rotating Squares
records.description: A template with squares rotating in place in a looping animation. Great for geometric backgrounds and abstract motion design.
records.move: grid of rounded squares spins twice with a rotation ripple outward
records.how: A 12x7 grid of 58px rounded squares, coloured in four concentric rings (periwinkle, mint, gold, pink) by distance from the centre, on deep navy. A seek function rotates every square 720deg per D minus 40deg per unit of distance, so the spin reads as a ripple spreading outward, and breathes scale between 0.72 and 1 on a sine wave with two cycles per D phased by the same distance. All terms are periodic so the 10s loop closes.
records.adapt: Change the four ring colours and background, grid density and square size or corner radius; a single colour with the ripple still reads well. Keep the whole turns per D and distance-phased rotation; D is 10s though the catalog lists 15.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid and squares recording each distance; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate gsap.sets rotation and scale per square, replacing fx.register.
caveats: motion is a seek function, not tweens; port as a progress tween with onUpdate
duration is 10s, not the 15s listed in the catalog

records.name: Small Waves
records.description: A subtle looping wave animation template. Works as a calm background element for brand content and ambient visuals.
records.move: fourteen thin sine lines slide left and right with a faint swell
records.how: Fourteen SVG stroke paths, each a cubic-approximated sine wave (wavelength 320-590px, amplitude 8-16px) stacked every 30px from y=250, in teal at 25-45% opacity on a pale aqua gradient. Each line translates x by 1-3 whole wavelengths over D with ease none, alternating direction per line, so the stack shears calmly; each also lifts y by 10px plus its amplitude and returns with one sine.inOut yoyo cycle. D is 10s.
records.adapt: Change the stroke colour and background, the line count, spacing and amplitudes; thicker strokes and fewer lines make it bolder. Keep the whole-wavelength travel per D so each line loops seamlessly.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG and generates the wave paths; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline of x sweeps and y yoyos with paths selected within el. Path widths assume a 1280 viewBox; the SVG scales to the shot.

records.name: Themes: Animated Gallery
records.description: An animated gallery template that moves through multiple visual themes in sequence. Good for design system presentations and theme picker UI demos.
records.move: dashboard cycles four colour themes via CSS variables, bars re-pop each switch
records.how: A mock analytics app (sidebar with four theme rows, stat tiles, a bar chart) is styled entirely from CSS custom properties on the stage. At 0.15, 0.4, 0.65 and 0.9 D a selection pill slides to the next theme row with expo.out, all eight custom properties tween to the new palette over 0.6s with power2.inOut (Daylight, Midnight, Lagoon, Ember, back to Daylight), a ring pulses out from the swatch, the theme label swaps with a small y fade and the bars and tile numbers re-enter with staggered expo.out. Between switches the bars breathe scaleY 0.85 to 1 with a slow sine yoyo so nothing is still.
records.adapt: Replace the four theme palettes and names, the brand name, tile numbers and bar heights with the product; the switch cadence of 1.5s per theme can stretch with D. Keep the 0.6s variable tween and the bar re-pop so each switch has a beat.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the app markup and sets the initial custom properties on el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with switches at 0.15 D + j*0.25 D, tweening the custom properties on el rather than .stage, and the label text set via a direction-safe onUpdate rather than the window.__fx.seek patch. Ring positions come from getBoundingClientRect so measure after mount.
caveats: .from(".tile b") lacks immediateRender:false, so the tile numbers most likely sit hidden until the first switch at 1.1s and the loop start does not match its end
the last switch bar and tile tweens run about 0.4s past D; boundary state is close but not identical
theme label text is corrected by patching window.__fx.seek

records.name: Vector Animation
records.description: A template with an animated vector illustration with moving paths and shapes. Good for illustrated explainer content and brand character animations.
records.move: flat landscape illustration: morphing hills and tree, plane loops, birds flap
records.how: A flat vector scene (sky gradient, sun with rays, clouds, two hills, road, tree, balloon, paper plane, two birds). Over one 4s cycle the tree crown and both hills MorphSVG to a second shape and back with sine.inOut yoyo, the sun rays rotate 45deg linearly (eightfold symmetric, so it closes), the sun scales 1.06, clouds and balloon drift and return, the plane rides a closed MotionPath loop with autoRotate over the full D while its dashed trail DrawSVGs on in the first half and off in the second, the road dashes scroll four periods, and the birds flap by morphing their wing path 16 times while bobbing.
records.adapt: Replace the SVG artwork with the brand illustration keeping ids for the parts you want to move, change the sky and hill colours; drop the parts you do not have. Keep whole-cycle yoyos and the full-loop motion path so it still loops.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with durations expressed as D/2 and D, selectors scoped to el (ids must be unique per instance). Requires MorphSVG, MotionPath and DrawSVG plugins registered.
caveats: bird 2 tweens start 0.12-0.3s late and run past D, a small wing mismatch at the loop point
duplicate ids if mounted twice on a page

records.name: 3D Rotation
records.description: A 3D rotation effect that spins and tilts your visuals. Ideal for product showcases, logo reveals, and dynamic motion graphics.
records.move: CSS 3D product box spins a full turn, tilts, with lambert-shaded faces
records.how: A six-face CSS box (gradient front and back with brand copy, plain sides and caps) sits in a 1400px perspective world over a soft glow and a floor shadow. A seek function sets rotationY to one full 360 per D, rotationX swinging -18 plus or minus 22deg once, rotationZ plus or minus 6deg twice, and a 14px float; the shadow scales and fades with the float and the glow pulses. Each face carries a black shade overlay whose opacity is computed from the face normal against a fixed light after the rotation, so the box appears lit from upper left as it turns. Loop closes since every term is periodic.
records.adapt: Replace the front and back face gradients and text with the product, resize the box and caps to the product proportions, change the glow colour. Keep one full spin per D and the computed shading.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the world, box faces, glow and shadow; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate applies the rotation, float and per-face shade opacities, replacing fx.register.
caveats: motion is a seek function with computed shading, not tweens; port as a progress tween with onUpdate
backface-visibility and preserve-3d must survive any parent transform in the host

records.name: Card Flip
records.description: A smooth card flip animation that reveals content with a 3D rotation effect. Perfect for product showcases, app UI animations, and interactive mockups.
records.move: product card lifts, flips 180 to specs, rows slide in, flips back
records.how: A 400x520 card with a front (gradient hero, name, price, button) and a dark back (spec rows, CTA) in a 1600px perspective scene over a rotating blurred conic blob. The card floats y -8 with a slight rotationX in one sine yoyo cycle; at 0.175 D it rotates Y to 180 with expo.inOut over 0.9s while scaling to 1.08 and back, the spec rows slide in from x 24 with staggered expo.out and the CTA rises; at 0.675 D it rotates on to 360 with the same lift and the front body items re-enter with a stagger. A hint label pulses opacity. rotationY 360 equals 0 so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Replace the hero gradient, product name, price, spec rows and CTA text, the card size and corner radius, the blob colours. Keep the 0.9s expo.inOut flip with the scale lift and the stagger after each flip.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the scene, card faces and hint; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with flips at 0.175 D and 0.675 D and durations as fractions of D. The from() tweens need immediateRender:false as in the original; selectors scoped to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
filter: blur(60px) on the 900px conic blob is slow to render
backdrop-filter on the hero shape

records.name: Color Keying Effect
records.description: A color keying effect that isolates and replaces a specific color in your footage. Ideal for compositing and green screen-style animations.
records.move: green-screen key: tolerance slider rises, split wipe reveals keyed composite
records.how: A canvas paints a green (#00B140) screen with a subtle lighting gradient, a bobbing phone mockup and five orbiting coloured dots as the source; a per-pixel chroma key with spill suppression removes the green at the current tolerance and composites the subject over a drifting aurora image. A GSAP timeline tweens tolerance 0 to 1 with power2.inOut from 0.08 to 0.32 D, a split line wipes from left to right with expo.inOut from 0.1 to 0.38 D showing raw source on its right and keyed result on its left, then wipes back at 0.68 D and tolerance returns to 0 by 0.96 D. A panel shows the key colour and a live tolerance percentage and knob.
records.adapt: Feed the product footage or render into the source canvas (same-origin), change the key colour and the background image, the panel labels; the subject animation is only a placeholder. Keep the tolerance rise before the wipe so the key is visibly earned.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the output, source and keyed canvases, loads the background image and builds the panel and split line; animate(el, shot, D) returns the state timeline with an onUpdate on a progress tween that draws the source, keys it, composites and positions the split and panel, replacing the window.__fx.seek patch. Loads a file image; wait for decode before the first frame.
caveats: subject bob, orbiting dots and background drift use raw t (sin(t*1.2), t*0.9) so they are not periodic in D; the loop does not close
per-pixel key over 1280x720 every frame is slow
the source is procedural; real footage must be same-origin to avoid canvas taint

records.name: Dithering Effect
records.description: A dithering effect that renders your visuals with an animated noise pattern. Great for retro-style motion graphics and textured video content.
records.move: ordered Bayer dither to four colours, matrix crawls, lit sphere orbits
records.how: A 320x180 canvas upscaled with image-rendering pixelated draws a scene each frame: a diagonal violet gradient whose midpoint sweeps, a large sphere whose specular highlight circles it once per D while the sphere sways, six small orbs orbiting it, and the word DITHER. The frame is then quantised through a 4x4 Bayer matrix to a four-colour palette (near-black, purple, coral, cream); the matrix offset steps by frame index so the dither pattern crawls like animated noise. All scene motion is periodic in D and the crawl returns to zero at 120 frames.
records.adapt: Replace drawScene with the product image or logo drawn at low res, change the four palette entries and the word; raise the canvas size for finer dots. Keep the frame-indexed matrix crawl so the pattern feels alive.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the low-res canvas and offscreen scene canvas; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate draws the scene and applies the dither, replacing fx.register. No GSAP is loaded in the original.
caveats: does not load gsap; the port adds it for the progress tween
per-pixel loop is small at 320x180 but grows quadratically with resolution

records.name: Gooey Effect
records.description: A fluid gooey effect that blends and morphs shapes with a liquid-like animation. Perfect for playful transitions and organic motion graphics.
records.move: satellites blob out of a core and back through goo filter
records.how: An SVG group filtered by feGaussianBlur (18) plus an alpha-contrast feColorMatrix, the classic goo filter, holds a central circle, six satellites and a drop. A seek function moves each satellite out to 200-280px along its own angle and back on a sine over D with phase i/6, spinning around the core and swelling radius up to 1.2x when fully out, so blobs stretch, neck and snap free of the core then rejoin. The core wobbles scaleX/scaleY plus or minus 0.12 three times per D, a drop falls from the top twice per D and dissolves into the core, and the group fill hue drifts plus or minus 40deg. Everything is periodic so the 8s loop closes.
records.adapt: Change the fill colour and background, satellite count and radii, and the caption word; the goo filter values (blur 18, alpha 28/-12) set how sticky the merge looks. Keep the phase-offset orbits so blobs leave one at a time.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG with a uniquely-id filter and circles; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate sets cx, cy, r and the fill, replacing fx.register. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused in the original.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it
full-group feGaussianBlur filter is slow at large sizes

records.name: Grainy Color Clamp
records.description: A grainy color clamp effect that maps your footage to a limited color palette. Perfect for editorial and retro-style motion graphics.
records.move: footage posterised to editorial palettes, hard cuts with grain surges
records.how: A 640x360 canvas paints procedural footage (sunset sky, sun, three parallax ridges, shimmering sea, a walking figure) with a slow pan on a sine over D. Each frame the pixels are mapped by luminance plus seeded grain to one of three five-colour palettes (rust, blue, violet); the loop is cut into thirds, and at each cut the palette hard-switches, grain surges (exponential spikes either side of the cut) and the level count re-opens from 2 to 5 colours over the first 70% of the segment. Five swatches at bottom right show the active palette and which levels are open; a serif caption reads as a magazine issue.
records.adapt: Feed the product footage into the source canvas (same-origin), replace the three palettes with brand colour sets, the caption text and swatch styling. Keep the grain surge on each cut and the 2 to 5 level opening, which is the editorial rhythm.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the low-res canvas and swatches; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate paints the footage, clamps it and updates the swatches, replacing fx.register. The seeded per-frame rng must use frame index, not Math.random.
caveats: sea shimmer and figure legs use raw t so they are not periodic, but the loop boundary is one of the hard palette cuts so the mismatch is hidden
per-pixel loop at 640x360 every frame

records.name: Highlight Effect
records.description: An animated highlight effect that draws attention with a sweeping light motion. Perfect for social media and ads..
records.move: light sweeps across headline, button and stat card; marker underline draws
records.how: A dark hero layout: headline with one word wrapped in a yellow marker stroke, body copy, a white button and a stat card. A full-frame overlay gradient sweeps xPercent -110 to 110 with power2.inOut over 0.35 D, twice per loop; skewed sheen bands follow it across the headline, then the button, then the card, each 0.7-0.9s with the same ease. The marker path DrawSVGs in behind the key word at 0.175 D with power3.out and wipes away at 0.83 D with power3.in; the card ring flashes on with expo.out and the stat number pops scale 1.08 with back.out(3) twice.
records.adapt: Replace headline, highlighted word, body, button and stat text, the marker colour and stroke width; add or remove sheen targets. Keep the sweep-then-local-sheen order and the draw-then-wipe on the marker so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the layout with sheen divs and the marker SVG; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with sweep times at 0.025 D and 0.575 D and sheens following, selectors scoped to el. DrawSVGPlugin must be registered.
caveats: mix-blend-mode screen and overlay layers over text

records.name: Holographic Logo
records.description: A holographic logo animation that renders your brand mark with a shimmering, iridescent foil effect. Perfect for premium product reveals and high-end brand animations.
records.move: foil-masked logo and wordmark: conic rainbow turns, specular band sweeps, tilts
records.how: A hexagonal mark is a div whose background is a conic rainbow gradient plus a white specular band, masked by an inline SVG data-URI, and the wordmark uses the same gradients with background-clip text. A seek function rotates the conic angle a full 360 per D (opposite direction on the word), and sweeps the specular band across twice per D via background-position with a smoothstep, offset between mark and word so the flash travels. The mark tilts rotationY plus or minus 22 and rotationX plus or minus 12 once per D like a foil card in hand, breathes scale 1.03, a violet glow pulses behind it, and a low-opacity feTurbulence grain shifts by frame.
records.adapt: Swap the mask data-URI for the brand logo path (any black silhouette SVG), change the wordmark text, and edit the six conic stops for a different foil. Keep the full conic turn and the two offset sweeps per D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the scene, logo, foil div with mask and the wordmark; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate sets the --a and --px custom properties, the tilt and the glow, replacing fx.register. Custom properties must be set on the instance elements, not document-wide.
caveats: animating a conic-gradient angle through a custom property repaints the gradient every frame
background-clip text plus filter on the same element

records.name: Image Stretch Transition
records.description: An image stretch transition that warps and pulls your visuals into the next scene. Great for dynamic video editing and social media reels.
records.move: outgoing image smears left, incoming stretches in from right, hot seam
records.how: A canvas cycles three landscape images (aurora, ocean, sunset), each held about 1.57s with a slow push-in then transitioned in 1.1s, three times in 8s so the loop closes. During a transition, drawn column by column, the outgoing image is redrawn into a shrinking left region with a power-curve resample so its trailing edge stretches into a long smear (pull up to 8 at mid-transition on a sine), while the incoming image fills the right region with the mirrored curve; a white gradient seam glows at the boundary, peaking mid-wipe. The caption is pulled with the image: slides and stretches out left, then in from the right with the next name and index.
records.adapt: Replace the three images and names, change the count (the slot maths uses count times hold plus transition equals D), the smear strength 7 and seam colour. Keep the sine-shaped pull so the smear builds and releases.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and caption and loads the images; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate runs frame() and positions the caption, replacing fx.register. Wait for image decode before the first frame.
caveats: about 1280 drawImage calls per frame during transitions
images must be reachable from the host; no getImageData so taint is not an issue

records.name: Inward Echo Loop
records.description: An inward echo animation that layers repeating shapes into a hypnotic looping effect. Perfect for abstract motion graphics and animated backgrounds.
records.move: fourteen rounded rings rush inward, shrinking, rotating and colour-cycling
records.how: Fourteen rounded-square outlines sit centred on near-black with a glowing white core and a vignette. A seek function gives each ring phase (p + i/14) mod 1: it is born at scale 4.2 beyond the frame, rushes inward with an ease-out to scale 0.12 at the core, turns 90deg in transit plus a full 360 field spin per D, fades in fast and out with a cubic, thickens from 2 to 8px, cycles hue by 220deg along the trip plus a full turn per D, and sinks in z. The core pulses scale 1.18 once per ring birth and rotates once per D. Everything is periodic so the 6s loop closes.
records.adapt: Change the ring shape (border-radius), count N, stroke colours (fix the hue or use the brand palette) and the core mark. Keep the phase-offset pipeline and the power-2.2 inward ease so rings bunch near the centre.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the ring divs and core; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate gsap.sets scale, rotation, opacity, borderColor, borderWidth and z per ring, replacing fx.register. Ring size 360px is fixed; scale to the shot.
caveats: motion is a seek function, not tweens; port as a progress tween with onUpdate
rotation ph*90 relies on the fourfold symmetry of the rounded square

records.name: Pixel Dissolve Transition
records.description: A pixel dissolve transition that fragments your visuals into an animated pixel grid. Ideal for product reveals, stylized transitions, and social media content.
records.move: two title scenes swap through a pixel grid popping cell by cell
records.how: Two offscreen canvases each draw a landscape image with a slow sine zoom, a dark wash and a centred title and subline (Before / After). The output holds scene A for 0.15 D, dissolves to B over 0.35 D, holds B, then dissolves back. Each 40px cell has a seeded threshold biased along a top-left to bottom-right diagonal; when the eased progress passes a cell threshold the incoming cell pops in from its centre with a cubic ease over a 12% window, flashed white as it lands, so the wipe travels while staying speckled.
records.adapt: Replace the two images, titles and sublines, cell size CW/CH, and the diagonal bias to change the wipe direction. Keep the 12% per-cell pop window and the white flash for the pixel feel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the output and two scene canvases, loads images and builds the threshold table; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate draws both scenes and the cell dissolve, replacing fx.register. Wait for image decode and fonts before the first frame.
caveats: scene zoom uses raw sin(t), about 2% scale mismatch at the loop boundary
canvas text depends on the fonts being loaded; the original only relies on document.fonts.ready

records.name: Pixelated Mask
records.description: A pixelated mask effect that reveals or hides your content through an animated pixel grid. Great for stylized transitions and retro motion graphics.
records.move: grid of tiles shrinks away to reveal a card, then closes
records.how: A 32x18 grid of 40px tile divs in alternating off-white shades covers an editorial card (photo, eyebrow, headline, copy, buttons). From 0.025 D each tile scales to 0 with expo.in over 0.42s, ordered by distance from a point near the photo plus jitter (spread over 1.5s), so the card is uncovered in a speckled radial pixel wipe; from 0.65 D tiles scale back to 1 with expo.out from the opposite corner, and once closed the tiles breathe 0.92 briefly. Under the mask the photo pans, the headline, copy and row slide up on reveal, and the card drifts up 20px before it is hidden.
records.adapt: Replace the card content and photo, the tile colours (match the stage background) and the reveal and hide origin points; cell size sets the pixel scale. Keep the 0.42s expo tile pops and the 1.5s spread so the wipe travels.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and appends the 576 tile divs with seeded orders; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with reveal at 0.025 D + ord*0.25 D and hide at 0.65 D + ord*0.25 D, from() tweens keeping immediateRender:false, selectors scoped to el. The grid is fixed at 1280x720; derive columns and rows from the shot size.
caveats: 1728 tweens on 576 DOM elements; heavy timeline
the closing breathe tweens run slightly past D
from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: Pixelated Slideshow
records.description: A pixelated slideshow transition that dissolves between images through an animated pixel effect. Great for presentations and social media content.
records.move: slides pixelate to 64px blocks, swap at peak, resolve back sharp
records.how: A canvas shows three landscape images in equal slots with a slow push-in and drift; the last second of each slot is the transition. Block size rises 1 to 64px on a sine bell shaped by power 1.6 and quantised to steps of 4, drawn by downscaling to a tiny canvas and upscaling with smoothing off, so the image chunks into mosaic and resolves; the next image swaps in at the peak. A title with a small label pops up and fades in on each swap, three dots mark the active slide, and a thin progress bar runs across the full D.
records.adapt: Replace the three images and names and the label, change slot count (D divides into equal slots), the peak block size 64 and the quantise step 4. Keep the sine bell so pixelation builds and releases symmetrically around the swap.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas, tiny canvas, title, dots and bar and loads images; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate computes the block size, draws, and updates the UI, replacing fx.register. Wait for image decode before the first frame.
caveats: resizing the tiny canvas every frame is cheap but image-rendering: pixelated must be on the output canvas
images must be reachable from the host

records.name: Ring Scale: Animated Loop
records.description: A looping ring scale animation that pulses and scales in perfect rhythm. Great for intros, badges, and attention-grabbing motion graphics.
records.move: rings expand and fade on the beat, badge hits and settles
records.how: A purple gradient badge sits centre on a dark stage with a blurred halo behind it, four concentric ring outlines and twelve small white ticks orbiting at 300px radius. Each ring is born on its own beat (one per second of a 4s loop) and lives a full loop: scale runs 1 to 3.6 with an expo-out curve while opacity falls quadratically from 0.9 to 0 and borderWidth thins 4px to 1px. The badge scale takes a damped-cosine hit (exp(-9b)*cos(22b)*0.12) at every beat, an elastic snap that settles in about a third of a beat, plus a slow 2% sine breath; the halo scale and opacity spike on the beat and decay exponentially. The ticks rotate one full turn per loop and each brightens and grows (scale 0.6 to 2.2) as a lit pulse passes around the circle three per second. Everything is phase-based on t so frame 0 and frame D are identical.
records.adapt: Change the badge text ('Live' / 'Now on air'), the purple accent, and the badge size; ring count N and tick count can grow or shrink. Keep the one-ring-per-beat cadence, the expo-out expansion and the damped-cosine badge hit — that beat feel is the effect.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the halo, N ring divs, the badge and 12 tick divs inside el. The effect is a fx.register seek loop, so animate returns gsap.timeline().to({}, {duration: D, ease:'none', onUpdate}) where onUpdate reads tl.time() and applies the same per-ring/badge/tick gsap.set calls with BEAT = D/N. All selectors must be scoped to el; the 300px tick radius should scale with el height.
caveats: seek-loop effect: motion is computed from t, not a GSAP tween list
tick pulse rate (t*3) is tied to absolute seconds, so it only loops cleanly when D*3 is an integer

records.name: Ripple Effect
records.description: A ripple effect that sends animated waves across your visuals. Great for fluid transitions, water simulations, and dynamic motion graphics.
records.move: radial water ripples warp painted footage from four drop points
records.how: A 640x360 canvas is repainted every frame with a procedural sunset (sky gradient, sun, three parallax ridges, shimmering sea, a walking silhouette) plus the word RIPPLE and a brand line drawn into it. Four drop points are born at 0, 1.7, 3.4 and 4.6s of the 6s loop; each drop's wavefront expands at 120px/s and, in a 140px band behind the front, per-pixel displacement (sin(d*0.16) times an exponential envelope, up to 14px) samples the source image while cos(d*0.16) adds a highlight so the ridge of each wave catches light. Drops fade over 3.2s and ages wrap modulo D, so a drop born at 4.6s is still expanding at t=0.2 and the loop closes. The canvas is upscaled to fill the 1280x720 stage.
records.adapt: Replace the footage() painter with drawImage of a product image or video frame (must be same-origin so getImageData works), change the RIPPLE / brand strings and the drop positions and birth times. Keep SPEED 120, wavelength K 0.16, the 3.2s drop life and the 140px band width for the same water feel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the display canvas and an offscreen source canvas scaled to el. animate returns a timeline with a single D-long no-op tween whose onUpdate repaints the source, computes the displacement pass per pixel and putImageData — the fx.register seek(t) body verbatim with t = tl.time(). Nothing is document-level; only the canvas width/height assumption (640x360 half-res) needs to derive from el.
caveats: per-pixel JS displacement over 230k pixels per frame, slow but deterministic
footage is painted procedurally because file:// images taint the canvas; real images need same-origin serving
text inside the canvas uses Sharp Grotesk / Atlas Grotesk and falls back silently if fonts are missing

records.name: Threshold Effect
records.description: A high-contrast threshold effect that converts your visuals into monochrome. Ideal for bold, graphic animations.
records.move: threshold level sweeps footage between ink and paper, accent band rides the edge
records.how: A 640x360 canvas repaints a procedural sunset each frame (panning 60px on a sine over the loop) then every pixel's luminance is compared to a threshold level that sweeps 0.18 to 0.82 on a full sine over the 4s loop; pixels resolve to near-black ink or warm paper through a soft edge whose width tightens (0.02 to 0.08) at the extremes, so the picture breathes from mostly-ink to mostly-paper and back. A thin luminance band just above the level is painted orange-red, giving a sweeping accent contour. Over the canvas, a 'Threshold 50%' readout with a bar (width = level) updates in DOM, and a large 'Bold graphic' word in mix-blend-mode difference inverts against whatever passes beneath. Sine-driven so the last frame equals the first.
records.adapt: Swap the painted footage for a same-origin product image, change ink/paper/accent triplets and the 'Bold graphic' word. Keep the full-sine level sweep and the accent band offset (+0.18 to +0.26 above level) — that is the two-tone graphic look.
records.port: mount(el, shot) adds the canvas, the readout div and the headline inside el. animate returns a timeline with one D-long tween whose onUpdate runs the seek body: repaint footage, per-pixel threshold with lvl = 0.5 + 0.32*sin(2πp), update bar width and percentage text. Scope the #v / #bar lookups to el.
caveats: per-pixel canvas pass every frame, slow to render
mix-blend-mode: difference on the DOM text over a canvas relies on compositing, check in the renderer
procedural footage stands in for real imagery

records.name: Animated Emoji Button
records.description: A button animation template where an emoji reacts and pops on press. Adds a bit of personality to app UI demos and social media content.
records.move: cursor presses pill button, emoji squashes then elastic pops with particle burst
records.how: A dark pill button holds an emoji, a label and a counter, with a pink radial glow behind. A cursor flies in with power3.out over the first 22% of the 4s loop and the button lifts 4% on hover. At 1.1s (28%) the press: cursor, button and emoji all shrink with power2.in over 0.12s (emoji to 0.7 with -12deg rotation). Release at 1.24s (31%): button springs to 1.06 with elastic.out(1,0.4), emoji overshoots to 1.55 and +14deg with elastic.out(1.2,0.35) then eases back with back.out(2), a pink ring scales 0.9 to 1.35 fading out, the counter rolls 128 to 129 with yPercent ±110 power3.inOut, the glow swells, and 14 heart/star glyphs fly upward on seeded random arcs fading over about a second. Cursor exits at 2.6s, button relaxes, and the counter rolls back to 128 in the last 10% so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Change the emoji, the label, the two counter values, the accent pink and the glyph list; particle count 14 is a tunable. Keep the press-at-28% / release-at-31% timing and the elastic eases — that is the tactile pop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates glow, button (ring, emoji, label, counter c1/c2, burst container with 14 particles seeded by fx.rng) and the cursor svg. animate builds the same timeline with times scaled as fractions of D (press at 0.275D, release at 0.31D, exit at 0.65D, counter reset at 0.9D) and returns it. All '.cursor', '.btn' etc. selectors must be scoped to el; the cursor start offsets (300,260) assume a centred stage.
caveats: counter rollback in the last 0.4s is visible as a reset rather than a natural loop
glow opacity tweened to 1.5 relies on clamping

records.name: Animated Slider
records.description: An animated slider template with an interactive feel. Good for survey UI demos and feedback collection feature presentations.
records.move: cursor drags slider thumb across, faces swap with elastic pops, settles back
records.how: A white card holds a question, a large emoji face, a gradient track with a fill, thumb, tooltip and a cursor pinned to the thumb. The cursor arrives with power3.out in the first 18% of the 4s loop; the thumb grows 1.25x with back.out(3) and the tooltip fades in. From 0.85s to 1.85s a proxy value tweens 0.12 to 0.92 with power2.inOut, driving translateX of the thumb group and the fill width via onUpdate, then overshoots back to 0.86 with elastic.out(1,0.5). As the value crosses 0.3, 0.55 and 0.8 the current face drops away (yPercent -60, scale 0.7, power2.in, 0.18s) and the next rises in with rotation -15 to 0 and elastic.out(1,0.5) while the tooltip text swaps Meh / Okay / Good / Amazing. Cursor leaves at 2.7s, tooltip hides, and the value glides back to 0.12 with power3.inOut in the last 12% while the first face returns with back.out(2).
records.adapt: Change the question, the four faces and labels, the gradient colours and the crossing thresholds; the track width W is derived from the card width. Keep the 1s drag with power2.inOut and the elastic overshoot back.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card, faces, track/fill/pos/thumb/tip and the cursor inside el. animate returns the same timeline with a proxy object tween ({v}) whose onUpdate writes transform and width on scoped elements; time constants become fractions of D (drag 0.21D to 0.46D, exit 0.68D, reset 0.875D). The crossT() mapping from threshold to time must use the same fractions.
caveats: the face-swap times are computed by inverting power2.inOut analytically and only match if the drag ease stays power2.inOut
tooltip text is changed with .set(textContent) which does not scrub backwards cleanly

records.name: Back / Next Buttons
records.description: An animated back and next button template with clear interaction states. Good for UI demos and prototype walkthroughs where navigation is part of what you're showing.
records.move: cursor clicks Next, step slides left; clicks Back, slides home
records.how: An onboarding card shows four progress dashes, a step viewport and a grey Back and blue Next button. Cursor enters with power3.out in the first 15% of the 4s loop and hovers Next: an overlay fades in, the button lifts 3px and scales 1.03, its arrow nudges 5px right. Press at 0.8s (20%) scales 0.95 with power2.in for 0.1s, release rebounds to 1.03 with back.out(3). At 0.9s step 1 slides out with xPercent -110 and step 2 slides in from 110% with expo.inOut over 0.55s while the second progress dash fills with scaleX 0 to 1 power3.out and Back brightens from 0.45 to full opacity. The cursor then travels to Back (power3.inOut, 0.7s), repeats the hover/press at 2.2 to 2.67s, the steps slide back and the dash empties from the right, Back dims, and the cursor exits by 3.9s so the first frame returns.
records.adapt: Replace the step copy, dash count, button labels and the blue accent; the cursor target coordinates nx/ny are computed from the card layout constants and must be recomputed if the card size changes. Keep expo.inOut 0.55s slides and the back.out(3) release.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card with dots, two steps, two buttons and a cursor inside el. animate returns the timeline with the same sequence at fractions of D (Next press 0.2D, slide 0.225D, Back press 0.64D, return slide 0.66D, exit 0.825D). Scope all selectors to el and derive nx/ny from the card element's layout rather than hard-coded numbers.
caveats: cursor positions are hard-coded from card layout math
only two of four steps exist; dashes 3 and 4 never fill

records.name: Floating Action Menu
records.description: An animated floating action button template that expands to reveal a menu of options. Good for mobile UI demos and app navigation presentations.
records.move: FAB press morphs to X, options stagger up with back ease, close reverses
records.how: A phone mock with a list, a blurred scrim, a blue FAB and three hidden option rows (label plus icon) above it. Cursor arrives with power3.out over the first 15% of the 4s loop. Press at 0.6s: FAB scales 0.88 with power2.in, then at 0.72s rebounds to 1.08 with elastic.out(1,0.5) while its borderRadius rounds from 24px to 34px and the plus icon rotates 135deg with back.out(2). The scrim fades in over 0.4s and the three options rise from y 30 / scale 0.6 to rest with back.out(2.2), staggered 0.08s from the end (nearest the FAB first). The cursor drifts to hover the middle option, which nudges 6px left and back. At 3.0s (75%) the cursor re-presses the FAB: options drop away with power3.in staggered 0.05, the icon spins back, radius returns to 24px, scrim fades, and the cursor exits by 3.9s.
records.adapt: Change the three option labels and icons, the blue accent, the list placeholder contents and the phone frame. Keep the press/rebound timing and the from-end stagger so the menu appears to grow out of the FAB.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone, list, scrim, menu options, FAB and cursor inside el. animate returns the same timeline at fractions of D (open press 0.15D, options 0.195D, hover 0.4D to 0.625D, close 0.75D, exit 0.85D). Scope '.opt', '.fab', '.scrim', '.cursor' to el; fx0/fy0 are derived from the 340x680 phone size and should come from the FAB's offset instead.
caveats: backdrop-filter: blur(6px) on the scrim
borderRadius tweened as a string value

records.name: Glass Button
records.description: A button animation template with a frosted glass texture and a subtle shimmer. Good for glassmorphism-style UI demos and modern design presentations.
records.move: frosted pill floats over drifting blobs, shine sweeps, cursor press springs
records.how: An aurora background image and three 520px blurred colour blobs (pink, blue, teal) drift on yoyo sine tweens across the full 6s loop while a frosted-glass pill button with backdrop-filter blur floats up and down 6px. A skewed white gradient shine strip sweeps across the button from x 0 to 640 with power2.inOut over 1.3s starting at 0.4s and again at 3.9s. At 1.6s the cursor flies in with power3.out, the button scales to 1.05 and its star icon rotates 72deg with back.out(2); at 2.8s (47%) the press shrinks it to 0.96 with a white press overlay, and at 2.94s it springs back to 1.05 with elastic.out(1,0.45). The button eases back to 1 and the icon unwinds with power2.inOut at 3.8s while the cursor leaves. The yoyo repeat:1 on 3s tweens makes the blob drift return exactly to its start at 6s.
records.adapt: Replace the background image and blob colours, the label 'Get started' and the icon; keep the 22px backdrop blur and grain for the frosted look. Keep the two shine sweeps and the press at ~47% of the loop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds bg, three blobs, the glass button (hi, grain svg, shine, press overlay, icon, label) and the cursor inside el. animate returns the timeline with blob yoyo tweens of duration D/2, shine sweeps at 0.067D and 0.65D, press at 0.467D. The shine travel of 640px and cursor offsets should scale with the button width; scope selectors to el.
caveats: backdrop-filter: blur(22px) plus three filter: blur(40px) blobs and a feTurbulence grain, heavy to render
loads assets/backgrounds/aurora.png via a relative path

records.name: Glow Button
records.description: A button animation template with a soft ambient glow that pulses around it. Great for CTA highlights in product videos and UI demos.
records.move: conic aura spins, halo breathes, cursor press sends double ring out
records.how: A dark pill button 'Start free trial' sits over a large blurred purple-to-cyan halo and a conic-gradient aura clipped to a pill and blurred 12px. Across the 8s loop the halo yoyos scale 0.9 to 1.15 and opacity 0.55 to 1 eight times (one breath per second, sine.inOut), the aura opacity and scale breathe in step, the aura rotates a full 360 with ease none, the small dot inside the button pulses 0.8 to 1.3, and the whole wrap floats up 8px and back. At 2.4s (30%) the cursor arrives with power3.out; hover scales the wrap 1.05 and swells the halo to 1.4 and brighter. Press at 3.8s (47.5%) scales 0.96 with power2.in, release at 3.94s springs to 1.05 with elastic.out(1,0.45) and fires two white rings outward (scale 1 to 1.5 and 1 to 1.8, fading, power2.out). Everything settles to rest and the cursor exits by 5.8s, leaving the ambient breath to carry the loop home.
records.adapt: Change the label, the purple/cyan/pink aura stops and the pill size; the breath count (repeat 7 on 1s tweens) should stay an integer multiple of D so the loop closes. Keep the press at ~47% and the double ring.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates vig, wrap (halo, auraWrap/aura, btn, ring) and cursor inside el. animate returns the timeline: breath tweens of duration D/8 with repeat 7 yoyo, aura rotation over D, float D/2 yoyo, visit at 0.3D to 0.725D. Selectors scoped to el; the 700px halo and aura sizes should scale with el.
caveats: filter: blur(30px) on a 700x420 halo and blur(12px) on the aura, slow to render
halo opacity tweened to 1.6 relies on clamping

records.name: Interactive Button: Glow

Press at 2.5s (42%) squashes to 0.95 with power2.in; a white ripple circle inside the button scales 0.2 to 14 fading out over 0.9s, the wrap springs to 1.08 with elastic.out(1,0.45) and the glow flares to 1.6 scale then settles. records.name: Interactive Button: Trace
records.description: A button template with an outline that draws itself around the edges on press. Good for UI demos and CTA animations that want a hand-drawn quality.
records.move: press draws a wobbly ink outline around the button, tick checks, line retracts
records.how: A white hard-shadow button 'Sign me up' in italic serif floats on paper-textured cream. From 1.5s the red path draws 0% to 100% with power2.inOut over 1.1s and the black path follows 0.2s behind; at 2.5s a red check mark draws in 0.4s and pops from scale 0.6 / -10deg with back.out(3).
