caveats: needs DrawSVGPlugin
feDisplacementMap wobble filter on the stroke svg and an feTurbulence paper layer
boxShadow tweened as a string

records.name: Liquid Glass Menu: Horizontal
records.description: A horizontal navigation menu template with a liquid glass aesthetic. Perfect for iOS 26-inspired UI demos and modern horizontal navigation showcases.
records.move: glass pill stretches between nav items, squashes, elastic settles, cycles around
records.how: A frosted pill nav bar (backdrop blur 26px) with four items floats over a sunset image and two blurred colour orbs that drift on 3s yoyo sine tweens. A translucent highlight pill sits under Home. On each hop (at 1.0, 2.2, 3.4 and 4.7s of the 6s loop) the pill's x and width tween to the target item with expo.out over 0.55s while it is stretched to scaleX 1.45 / scaleY 0.82 in 0.18s and released with elastic.out(1,0.45), so it reads as a liquid blob snapping into place. The outgoing item fades to 70% white, the target darkens to near-black, hops 6px up with power2.out and settles with elastic.out(1,0.4), and its icon swings in from -14deg times direction with back.out(3). The cursor travels ahead of each hop with power2.inOut, dips scale 0.85 as it clicks. The final hop returns to Home so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Change the four labels and icons, the background image and orb colours; the pill geometry is measured from the items via offsetLeft/offsetWidth so labels can be any length. Keep the 0.55s expo.out slide and the stretch-then-elastic release.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds bg, orbs, the nav with pill, items and cursor inside el, then measures geo from the items (needs layout, so measure after append). animate returns the timeline with hops at 0.167D, 0.367D, 0.567D and 0.783D and orb drift of D/2 yoyo. caveats: backdrop-filter: blur(26px) and two blur(30px) orbs
geometry measured at build time from offsetLeft, so the nav must be laid out before animate runs

records.name: Liquid Glass Menu: Vertical

height tween on the container triggers layout every frame

records.name: Liquid Glass Toggle
records.description: A toggle template with a liquid glass aesthetic and a fluid state change animation. Good for iOS 26-inspired UI demos and modern interface presentations.
records.move: gooey knob stretches across toggle, tail lags and merges, elastic settle
records.how: A frosted glass row 'Focus mode' with a 180x96 glass toggle floats over an aurora image and two drifting blurred orbs (4s yoyo sine over the 8s loop). fromTo tweens rely on immediateRender:false

records.name: Black Social Handle
records.description: A dark-themed lower-third template for displaying a social media handle over video. Simple and easy to adapt to any brand.

A black 76px pill scales in with back.out(2) at 0.1s and an Instagram glyph pops in from scale 0 / rotation -90 with back.out(2). At 0.55s the pill width expands to 450px with expo.out over 0.7s while the handle '@northwind.studio' slides in from xPercent -110 inside a clipped mask. A red notification dot pops with back.out(3) at 1.3s and pulses 1 to 1.3 on a 4-cycle yoyo. From 3.1s (78%) the text slides back out with expo.in, the pill collapses to 76px with expo.inOut, the dot vanishes and the icon spins away (rotation +90, back.in(2)) as the pill scales to 0, so the lower-third is gone by 4s.
records.adapt: Change the handle string and W (icon 76 + padding 34 + text width), swap the glyph, and the black/red for a brand pair; the background image is optional. Keep the 0.7s expo.out stretch and the 0.1s text lag.

records.name: Button: Hover Effect

The cursor glides to the button's left edge with power3.inOut, and at 1.15s (29%) a 40px white circle positioned at that edge scales 0 to 12 with power3.out, flooding the button white; the label tweens to black, an arrow slot widens 0 to 34px with back.out(2) as the arrow slides in, the button lifts 4px at scale 1.04 and a soft glow appears. The cursor tracks across the button for 1.2s; at 2.55s the fill circle jumps to the right edge and collapses to scale 0 with power3.in, the label returns to white, the arrow folds, glow fades and the cursor retreats. records.adapt: Change the headline, label and the white/black inversion colours; the fill entry and exit points are measured from the button's bounding rect so any button width works. Keep the 0.6s power3.out flood and the arrow's back.out(2) unfold.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds headline, glow, button (fill circle, label, arrow slot) and cursor inside el, then reads the button rect relative to el. animate returns the timeline with flood at 0.2875D, glide 0.325D to 0.625D, retreat 0.65D, exit 0.9D. getBoundingClientRect must be taken relative to el, and the from() tweens need immediateRender:false.

records.name: The Prompt: Generate Button
records.description: An animated generate button template with loading and completion states. Great for AI product demos where the button press is the key moment.

Press at 2.3s (33%): the pill scales 0.94 then elastic.out(1,0.45); the 'Generate' label rolls up out (yPercent -110, expo.out) as a black 'Generating' label with a spinner rolls in, and an oversized conic-gradient border layer fades in and rotates 720deg linearly over 2.4s while the spinner turns 1080. records.name: The Prompt: Voice Search
records.description: An animated voice search interface template with waveform visualization. Good for AI product demos and voice UI showcases where the moment of speaking is the feature.
records.move: mic tap turns blue and breathes, rings radiate, waveform dances, transcript types, results stagger
records.how: A dark 760px search pill with a placeholder and a white mic button, a hint line and three hidden result rows. The pill rises in with expo.out over the first 6% of the 10s loop and a cursor glides to the mic. Tap at 1.5s (15%): the mic dips 0.85 then springs to 1.1 with elastic.out(1,0.45) as it turns blue; the placeholder drops away and a 28-bar waveform fades in whose bars scaleY from a per-bar sum of sines (seeded phases and frequencies) gated by a level proxy tweened 0 to 1; two rings radiate from the mic (scale 1 to 2.6 and 2.2, fading, power2.out) every 0.8s for six cycles; the mic breathes 1.1 to 1.0 on a 0.4s yoyo; the hint rolls to 'Listening…'. At 5.3s the level falls to 0, the waveform fades and TextPlugin types the transcript over 1.2s; the mic returns to white at 6.6s, the hint rolls to '3 results', and three rows rise from y 24 with expo.out staggered 0.12s at 7.0s. At 9.2s rows and the pill exit upward.
records.adapt: Change the placeholder, transcript, hint strings, result rows and the blue accent; bar count N and the sine frequencies set the waveform character. Keep the 0.8s ring cadence and the level-gated waveform envelope.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds glow, search (q with ph/txt/wave bars, mic with two rings), hint and result rows inside el, seeding bar phases with fx.rng; register TextPlugin. animate returns the timeline with tap at 0.15D, rings from 0.17D every 0.08D, transcript 0.56D, results 0.7D, exit 0.92D; the waveform, which here is done by wrapping window.__fx.seek, becomes a D-long no-op tween on the same timeline whose onUpdate sets each bar's scaleY from tl.time() and the level proxy.
caveats: catalog says 20 seconds but the code and render are 10 seconds
waveform is driven by a monkey-patched window.__fx.seek, not by the timeline
cursor fades out at 1.8s and never returns, so the loop does not close on the cursor
needs TextPlugin
from() tweens need immediateRender:false
backgroundColor and svg stroke tweened as colour strings

records.name: Toggle Switch Button
records.description: A single animated toggle template with a smooth satisfying state transition. Good for settings UI demos and on/off interaction presentations.
records.move: knob stretches across, snaps with overshoot, sun becomes moon, world goes dark with stars
records.how: A large 240x130 grey toggle with a white knob holding a sun icon, a label beneath, and 40 hidden seeded stars across the stage. Toggle and label enter with back.out(2) / expo.out in the first 17% of the 3s loop. Flip on at 0.7s (23%): the knob stretches scaleX 1.35 from its left edge with power2.in, slides 110px with back.out(1.8) over 0.45s and relaxes to scaleX 1 from its right edge with elastic.out(1,0.5); the track tweens to purple and pops 1.05 with an elastic settle; the whole stage background tweens to near-black over 0.6s; the sun rotates 90 and shrinks away while a moon spins in from -90 with back.out(2); the label colour goes white and 'Light mode' rolls up to 'Dark mode'; the stars fade in with a random-order 0.01s stagger. At 2.05s (68%) the mirror sequence flips off and the stars fade, ending in the light state.
records.adapt: Change the two labels, the purple/dark palette, the two icons and the star count; TRAVEL = track width - knob - 20. Keep the stretch-slide-relax trio with the alternating transform origins — that is the snap.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds stars (seeded with fx.rng), toggle with knob and two icons, and label pair inside el. animate returns the timeline with flips at 0.233D and 0.683D; the stage backgroundColor tween must target el (or a full-size backdrop inside el) rather than the document stage. The from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: toggle enters from opacity 0 and stays visible, so the loop restarts with an entry pop
tweens backgroundColor on the stage element, which must be scoped to the shot container
from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: YouTube Subscribe Button
records.description: An animated subscribe button template with a satisfying click and bell notification effect. Perfect for YouTube channel intros and outros.

At 31% the cursor lands and the button scales to 0.93 then springs back with elastic.out while a white ripple scales 0 to 22 and fades; the pill turns grey (#272727), widens 190 to 210px, and the label slides up (yPercent -110 / 0) to read Subscribed with a check, the count ticking 128K to 129K the same way. records.name: Animated Arrow

records.name: Animated Progress Bar
records.description: A simple animated progress bar template that fills up with a clean motion. Great for app UI demos and onboarding presentations to show task or step completion.

At 79% the gradient turns green, a Complete pill pops with back.out(2.5), the number scales 1.06 and settles elastic; the panel lifts out at 92%.

records.name: Animated UI Kit
records.description: A template showing a collection of animated UI components moving together. Great for design system showcases and component library presentations.
records.move: six component cards stagger in; toggle, button, slider, checks, pill all cycle
records.how: A 3x2 grid of white cards enters with a grid stagger (y 40, scale .96, expo.out). Each card then loops its own component over 7s: the toggle knob slides x 0/56 with back.out(1.8) and tints blue at 11%, 43%, 71%; the button presses to scale .94 and recovers elastic with a ripple twice; the slider thumb and fill (left %, scaleX) sweep to 72, 30 then 100 with power3.inOut and a counter tooltip; three checkboxes fill with back.out(2.5) and DrawSVG ticks, untick and re-tick; a segmented pill hops xPercent 0/100/200 with back.out; avatars pop and a toast slides in and out twice. At 93% the cards lift out from the end of the grid.
records.adapt: Rename labels and the button/toast copy, swap the four accent colours, and drop cards you do not need; keep the back.out toggle and elastic press timings, they are the tactile feel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the six cards; animate returns one timeline with the per-component helper calls placed at fractions of D (tog at 0.11D, 0.43D, 0.71D etc.). Direct port apart from scoping the .val querySelector and registering DrawSVG.
caveats: many simultaneous tweens; fine for render, dense for editing

records.name: Banking App: Cards
records.description: An animated banking app template focused on card management UI. Good for fintech demos and banking product presentations where the interface needs to feel trustworthy.
records.move: cards deal in, front card swipes off and tucks behind, lock pops
records.how: A phone mockup rises in (y 60, rotateX 8, expo.out) beside a headline while a blue glow drifts x -40 to 40. Three stacked cards deal in from x 340 with rotate 8 and a from-end stagger (expo.out) from 9%; dots, action buttons and transactions follow with power3.out staggers. At 42% the front card flies left (x -360, rotate -10, power3.in), the two behind rise to the front with back.out(1.5), then the flown card returns behind at the back scale (.88) with expo.out and the page dot switches. At 69% the Freeze action presses (scale .85 yoyo) and the middle card desaturates via filter while a white lock badge pops with back.out(2.5). Phone and copy exit at 90%.
records.adapt: Replace card numbers, balances, bank name, transactions and the three card gradients; keep the deal-in stagger and the swipe/tuck sequence timings.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders phone, cards and rows from shot.cards; animate returns the timeline with deal at 0.09D, swipe at 0.42D, freeze at 0.69D. The zIndex set() on the tucked card and the filter tween port directly; scope selectors to el.
caveats: uses filter: saturate/brightness on a card, cheap at this size
from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: Charging [Apple Watch]
records.description: An animated Apple Watch charging screen template with a pulsing battery indicator. Good for wearables UI demos and Apple Watch product presentations.
records.move: watch ring draws to 78% with counter, halo and bolt breathe
records.how: A watch mockup rises in with expo.out. From 5% the green ring arc (DrawSVG 0% to 78%, expo.out, 1.3s) and a blurred glow copy draw around the dial while the big percentage counts 0 to 78 through an onUpdate tween; at 60% it ticks to 79. Throughout, a radial halo scales .7 to 1.15 and brightens, the bolt scales .9 to 1.15, the glow opacity .15 to .45 and the number breathes 0.98 to 1.03, all sine.inOut yoyo with 8 half-beats of 0.5s, and the case gradient slides backgroundPosition over the full 4s.
records.adapt: Change the percentage target, time, green (#30d158) and ring thickness; keep the 0.5s sine yoyo breath and the 1.3s expo.out fill.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the watch and SVG ring; animate returns the timeline with the fill at 0.05D and pulses as repeat counts scaled to D. Ports directly; register DrawSVG and scope the .pct querySelector.
caveats: filter: blur(8px) on the glow circle
the ring keeps its 79% fill at the end, so the loop restart shows the watch fading in with a new empty ring

records.name: Circular Loader
records.description: A circular loading indicator template from Studio Size with smooth steady animation. Good for app loading screens and UI demos.
records.move: material arc head-tail chase while the ring spins, inner comet counter-rotates
records.how: An SVG ring on dark: the outer white arc grows from 8% to 80% of the circle (DrawSVG, power2.inOut) then its tail catches up to a 92-100% sliver, twice per loop, while the whole SVG rotates 720deg linearly over 4s. A thinner purple inner arc does the same 4-45% comet three times per loop while rotating -360deg. Three dots under the label hop y -6 with a 0.12s stagger once a second.
records.adapt: Swap the two stroke colours and the loading label; change the rotation count if the duration changes so it stays whole turns; keep the grow/shrink cycle length.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts the SVG and label; animate returns the timeline with cycles at 0, 0.5D and the inner cycles every D/3. Rotation must be an integer number of turns per D for a clean loop; register DrawSVG.

records.name: Crazy Ellipse
records.description: An animated ellipse template that bounces unpredictably in a looping motion. Good for abstract backgrounds and motion design experiments.
records.move: three balls bounce around the frame, squash on walls, stretch with speed
records.how: A canvas on a sand background: three coloured balls are simulated once at 240Hz with wall bounces and a seeded speed drift on each hit, then every frame is looked up by time. Each ball squashes on impact (a decaying sine, 0.3s) along the hit axis, stretches along its velocity (1 + speed/4000), and leaves four ghost copies fading behind it. It does not return to the start pose, so the loop cuts.
records.adapt: Change ball colours, radii, count and initial velocities; the seed (fx.rng(7)) controls the drift; keep the squash envelope and trail depth.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and precomputes frames for D; animate returns a timeline with a single tween of duration D whose onUpdate draws the frame for tl.time(), replacing the fx.register seek loop. The canvas is 1280x720 fixed so scale it to el.
caveats: loop does not close cleanly; the balls end wherever the sim leaves them
canvas seek loop, becomes an onUpdate tween on the timeline

records.name: Interactive Badges
records.description: An animated badge template where badges light up and react. Works great for achievement systems and gamified UI demonstrations.
records.move: cursor hovers badges: colour floods, ring pulses, sparks; locked one shakes
records.how: Header and four hexagonal badges rise in with expo.out stagger. A cursor moves badge to badge (power3.inOut) and at 17%, 40% and 63% each one lights: hex scales 1.1 and rotates 8deg with back.out(2.5) then settles elastic, a gradient layer fades in, a white ring scales .8 to 1.35 and fades, a diagonal sheen sweeps via backgroundPosition, an Unlocked tag pops with back.out(2), and eight sparks fly out radially 90px (power3.out) and vanish. At 85% the cursor nudges the fourth badge which shakes x -6 six times and flashes a Locked tag; everything fades at 95%.
records.adapt: Rename badges, subtitles and gradients, change the icon SVGs, and choose which ones are locked; keep the light-up sequence timings and the 8-spark burst.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds badges from shot.badges and appends sparks; animate returns the timeline with light(i, k*0.23D). Cursor coordinates are stage-absolute (640 + offset), so compute from the size of el; className tweens and immediateRender:false fromTo calls port as is.
caveats: cursor path assumes a 1280x720 stage
fromTo tweens use immediateRender:false so the rings/sheen stay hidden until their beat

records.name: Interactive Components
records.description: An animated UI components template from Rico showing multiple interactive states. Good for design system showcases and component library presentations.
records.move: cursor tours components: hover, press, load, type, tab, like, dropdown
records.how: Three columns of light UI (buttons, input, tabs, chips, card, dropdown) slide up with a 0.1s expo.out stagger. A cursor then visits them in order over 6s: the primary button lifts y -3 with a shadow, presses to scale .96 and recovers elastic (15-30%); the Submit button presses, its label fades, a spinner rotates 1080deg linearly for 1.3s, then it turns green and Done pops in with back.out(2) (32-63%); the input gets a blue focus ring, the floating label shrinks up (y -38, scale .78, back.out), a caret blinks and TextPlugin types an email over 0.9s before a green tick scales in (42-63%); the tab underline slides x 110 then 200 with power3.inOut; chips fill black one by one with a 0.3s stagger and a small scale pop; the heart presses, springs elastic and fills red (75%); the dropdown chevron flips 180, the menu scales open with back.out(1.8), a row highlights, the label swaps to Pro and it closes (84-93%). The board fades at 96%.
records.adapt: Replace every label, the typed email, tab and chip names, the card image gradient and the accent blue/green/red; drop components you do not need and rebalance the cursor visits; keep the 0.1s press, elastic recovery and 0.35s menu open.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the board and cursor from shot.components; animate returns the timeline with each visit placed at fractions of D (button 0.15D, loader 0.32D, input 0.42D, heart 0.75D, dropdown 0.84D). Cursor x/y are stage-absolute and must be derived from el; scope selectors to el and register TextPlugin.
caveats: cursor coordinates assume a 1280x720 stage
set() calls toggle display on the spinner, so seeking backwards relies on GSAP recording the prior value

records.name: Loading Animation: Bars
records.description: An animated loading bar template where bars pulse in a staggered sequence. Good for app loading states and data processing UI animations.
records.move: seven bars pulse tall then short in a left-to-right wave, twice
records.how: Seven rounded gradient bars sit at scaleY .25 and 55% opacity. Two waves per 3s loop (at 0 and 50%): each bar grows to scaleY 1 and full opacity with power2.out over 0.4s, 0.1s after its neighbour, then falls back over 0.5s with power2.inOut, so a bump travels left to right. The whole set drifts y 4 to -4 and back with sine.inOut and the caption breathes between 60% and 100% opacity four times.
records.adapt: Change bar count, gap, width and the three gradient colours, and the caption; keep the 0.1s per-bar offset and the 0.4/0.5 grow-fall so the wave reads.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates N bars and the caption; animate returns the timeline with wave(0) and wave(0.5D). Ports directly; scope the bar query to el.

records.name: Loading Spinner: Infinite Loop
records.description: A clean infinitely looping loading spinner template. Good for app loading states and UI placeholder animations where the wait should feel designed.
records.move: two dashes chase around an infinity path, dash length breathing
records.how: A grey infinity-shaped track is overlaid by a black and a blue stroke, each given a stroke-dasharray covering 18% of the path length. Two proxy tweens drive strokeDashoffset linearly by minus four path lengths over 8s (the blue one offset half a lap), so each dash makes four laps and the end matches the start. A third tween breathes the dash fraction .18 to .32 with sine.inOut yoyo (8 half-beats of 1s); the caption fades .5 to 1 in the same rhythm and the whole SVG scales .98 to 1.02 with a 2s yoyo.
records.adapt: Swap the track and the two dash colours, the caption and the path (any closed path works since length is measured); keep whole-number laps per D so the loop seals.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts the SVG and measures getTotalLength after layout; animate returns the timeline with the three proxy tweens spanning D. DrawSVG is registered but not used (a lap helper is dead code), so the engine only needs core gsap; scope querySelector to el.
caveats: DrawSVGPlugin is loaded and registered but never used; the lap() helper is dead code
getTotalLength must run after the SVG is in the DOM

records.name: Loading Spinner: Success Animation
records.description: A loading spinner template that transitions into a success animation on completion. Good for form submissions and task completion UI flows.
records.move: spinner morphs into green disc, check draws, particles burst, copy swaps
records.how: A dark card rises in with expo.out. A blue arc chases head-to-tail (DrawSVG 0-10% to 0-75%, power2.inOut, yoyo three times) while its SVG spins 1440deg linearly until 52%, the subtitle pulsing. At 46% the arc closes to 100%, turns green, and at 52% a green disc scales up with back.out(1.8) as the ring fades; a check draws with DrawSVG power2.out, a burst ring scales 1 to 1.5 and fades, the icon pops 1.08 and settles elastic, and twelve dots fly out radially 92-110px and vanish. Title and subtitle cross-fade to the success strings with back.out(1.6), a Done button pops in at 61%, breathes scale 1.04, and the card lifts out at 94%.
records.adapt: Change the two title/subtitle pairs, the button label and the blue/green; the spin length is the wait, shorten it by moving the 4.0s transition earlier; keep the back.out disc and 0.45s check draw.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card, both SVGs and appends 12 particle divs; animate returns the timeline with the spin running to 0.52D and the success beat at 0.52-0.62D. Direct port; scope .ico querySelector to el and register DrawSVG.
caveats: spinner rotation of 1440deg ends abruptly when the disc appears, hidden by the fade

records.name: Pacman
records.description: An animated Pac-Man template with the original dot-chomping motion. Good for retro-themed content and playful branded animations.
records.move: pacman chomps across a dot row, ghosts bob behind, score counts
records.how: A canvas draws a black maze with blue rails and a border. Pac-Man moves left to right at constant speed so he crosses the whole 14-dot row in one 4s loop; his mouth opens and closes at 6Hz (cosine), dots disappear as his centre passes them, the last power pellet blinks, and the score reads 10 per dot. Three ghosts follow at fixed distances, bobbing y +/-6 on a sine and alternating their skirt frill every eighth of a second. He runs off the right edge at the end so the loop restarts with a fresh row.
records.adapt: Change dot count, spacing, colours and the score label; the ghost list is data; keep the 6Hz chomp and the constant-speed crossing tied to duration.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas; animate returns a timeline with one D-long tween whose onUpdate calls the draw(t) function, replacing the fx.register seek loop. Canvas is fixed 1280x720 and uses roundRect, so scale to el and keep the font available.
caveats: canvas seek loop, becomes an onUpdate tween on the timeline
uses ctx.roundRect, needs a recent Chromium

records.name: Pink Loading Spinner
records.description: A loading spinner template in a soft pink tone. Good for consumer-facing apps and pastel-toned UI demos where even the loading state should feel on-brand.
records.move: pink arc breathes while spinning, two satellites orbit, pulse rings, dots bounce
records.how: A white rounded card on a pink stage with two blurred blobs. An SVG arc grows from 8% to 72% of the circumference and back (stroke-dasharray via a proxy tween, power2.inOut, yoyo four half-beats of 0.75s) while its group rotates 720deg linearly over 3s; two small satellite dots orbit at 360deg and -720deg. Two rings scale .85 to 1.3 and fade with power2.out, offset by half a period, and the three ellipsis dots bounce y -7 in sequence. The card floats y -6 and back with sine.inOut.
records.adapt: Swap the pink palette and the label; change arc thickness and satellite sizes; keep whole-turn rotations per D and the 0.75s breath.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and SVG; animate returns the timeline with the dasharray proxy tween, rotations spanning D and pulses at 0 and 0.25D. Direct port; scope the .arc and .label i queries to el.
caveats: two full-stage blobs with filter: blur(60px), slower to render

records.name: Progress Donut
records.description: An animated donut chart template that fills around its ring to show progress. Good for dashboard UI demos and metric visualization content.
records.move: donut ring fills in two segments with counters, unwinds for the loop
records.how: A white dashboard card holds a 300px SVG donut and a three-row legend. From 4% the dark blue segment grows to 58% of the ring (stroke-dasharray driven by an expo.out proxy tween over 1.6s) and from 30% a lighter segment extends behind it to 80%; the centre percentage and the three dollar values are recomputed in the same onUpdate. The donut pops from scale .96 to 1.02 with back.out(3) and settles; legend rows slide in from x 30 with a 0.12s stagger. At 80% the segments unwind (p2 then p1, power3.in / expo.inOut) and the rows slide out reversed, with a set() at the last frame restoring them so frame 0 matches.
records.adapt: Change the two percentages, the money format and total (1.2M), the legend labels, title and the two blues; keep the expo.out 1.6s fill and the unwind timing.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card, SVG and legend from shot.segments; animate returns the timeline with the fills at 0.04D and 0.3D and the unwind at 0.8D. The draw() closure must query its elements inside el; the final set() at D-0.001 is what closes the loop, keep it.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false when composed into a larger timeline

records.name: Progress Pie
records.description: An animated pie chart template that fills to show percentage progress. Good for goal-tracking UI demos and data visualization presentations.
records.move: pie wedge sweeps to 68%, second wedge follows, badge pops, all collapses
records.how: A dark stage with a 340px SVG pie (a 140px-wide stroked circle so the dasharray reads as a solid wedge) and a savings legend. The pie scales in from .7 with back.out(1.6), the text staggers up. From 9% the green wedge sweeps to 68% (proxy tween, expo.out, 1.5s) while the centre tag counts and pops from .8 to 1.08 with back.out(3); at 50% a blue wedge extends to 100% with power3.inOut, updating the dollar figures. At 74% the pie bumps 1.04 and settles elastic while a Goal reached badge pops with back.out(2.2). From 90% the pie shrinks to .7 and fades (power3.in), text lifts out, and set() calls at the last frame reset every value.
records.adapt: Change the goal name, total (4800), the two wedge fractions, colours and the badge text; keep the 1.5s expo.out sweep and the 0.74D badge beat.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the pie SVG and legend from shot; animate returns the timeline with sweeps at 0.09D and 0.5D, badge at 0.74D, exit at 0.9D and the reset set() at D-0.001. Scope draw() querySelectors to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false in a composed timeline

records.name: Push Notifications: List [iOS]
records.description: A template showing a list of iOS push notifications appearing in sequence just as they would on a real device. Great for showcasing a notification system in an app demo.
records.move: lock-screen notifications drop in from above, each pushing the stack down
records.how: A portrait iOS lock screen (aurora wallpaper slowly zooming 1.1 to 1.14 with a 2% vertical drift) with big clock and Dynamic Island. Four frosted notification cards start at y -70, scale .9, invisible; at 8%, 28%, 48% and 67% each one springs into the top slot with back.out(1.6) over 0.6s while every earlier card is pushed down one 196px slot with power3.out. The island squeezes scaleX 1.06 yoyo at the first arrival. At 85% the whole stack lifts 60px and fades with a 0.05s stagger, so the loop begins empty.
records.adapt: Replace the four app names, icons, messages and the wallpaper; change the arrival times via data-t and the slot gap (196px) to match card height; keep the back.out(1.6) 0.6s spring and 0.55s push.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the lock screen and N cards from shot.notifications with data-t fractions; animate returns the timeline placing each arrival at t*D and the clear at 0.85D. Uses backdrop-filter on the cards; scope the .note query to el.
caveats: 1080x1920 portrait stage
backdrop-filter blur on four cards
wallpaper asset assets/backgrounds/aurora.png must exist

records.name: Revenue App [Dribbble]
records.description: An animated revenue app UI template with a polished design aesthetic. Good for fintech app showcases and data dashboard presentations.
records.move: dashboard builds: counters, bars grow, line draws, rows slide; unbuilds
records.how: A light dashboard card rises in (y 40, scale .97, power3.out). Three stat tiles stagger up and their numbers count to $128,430 / $42,910 / 8,412 with expo.out over 1.6s; twelve bars grow from scaleY 0 with a 0.05s expo.out stagger from 9%, a black trend line draws over them with DrawSVG power2.inOut from 18-42%, and a tooltip pops onto the highlighted bar with back.out(2) at 40%. Transaction rows slide in from x 40 (0.09s stagger) and the app floats y -4 and back. From 83% the line undraws to its end, bars collapse right-to-left, rows exit, counters run back to 0 and the card drops out at 92%.
records.adapt: Replace stat values, bar heights (data-h), the SVG line path, months, transactions and the accent blue; keep the 1.6s expo.out count, 0.05s bar stagger and the 1.2s line draw.
records.port: mount(el, shot) renders the app from shot.stats/shot.bars/shot.transactions and sets bar heights and tooltip position; animate returns the timeline with build 0-0.42D, float, and unbuild from 0.83D. Register DrawSVG; scope the counter querySelectors to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false when composed
tooltip position is computed from the highlighted bar index, keep it in sync with the data

records.name: Simple Notification [iOS]
records.description: An iOS notification animation template with a realistic slide-in motion. Perfect for app demos and UI presentations where the notification needs to feel like it came straight from the system.
records.move: banner springs down onto a 3D-tilting phone, dims the home screen, retracts
records.how: A phone mockup under a blue radial glow rotates slowly in 3D (rotationY -14 to 10, rotationX 4 to -3, sine.inOut across the whole 3s, perspective 1600px). At 10% a frosted banner drops from y -130, scale .92 to rest with elastic.out(1,.7) over 0.75s, the Dynamic Island squeezes scaleX 1.2 / scaleY 1.1 yoyo just before, and the app grid and dock dim to brightness .85 via filter. At 77% the banner retracts up with power3.in over 0.4s and the screen brightens again.
records.adapt: Change the app name, icon gradient, message and wallpaper, and the home-screen icon colours; keep the elastic.out(1,.7) drop and the 0.4s power3.in retract, which is the iOS feel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone and banner from shot; animate returns the timeline with the phone tilt spanning D, banner in at 0.1D and out at 0.77D. Needs perspective on el; uses filter brightness and backdrop-filter, both port as is.
caveats: backdrop-filter blur on the banner and dock
wallpaper asset assets/backgrounds/ocean.png must exist
the phone tilt ends at a different angle than it starts, so the loop has a small jump

records.name: Social Media Icons
records.description: An animated social media icon template where icons reveal in a coordinated sequence. Good for end cards and follow CTAs in video content.
records.move: title rises, icon discs pop in spinning, ring ripple, bounce wave, exit
records.how: A cream stage. The title rises from an overflow mask (yPercent 110 to 0, expo.out). From 6% five coloured discs scale from 0 with rotation -60 and a 0.1s back.out(2) stagger, their glyphs following with back.out(3) and the handles rising from masks. At 32% a coloured ring on each disc scales 1 to 1.55 and fades in the same stagger; at 55% the discs lift y -12 and drop with bounce.out in a wave. From 84% handles and discs exit reversed (scale 0, rotation 60, back.in) and the title drops out of its mask.
records.adapt: Replace the five brand colours, glyph SVGs and handles, and the title; add or remove discs; keep the back.out(2) 0.7s pop and the 0.1s stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the title and N discs from shot.accounts; animate returns the timeline with pop at 0.06D, ripple at 0.32D, wave at 0.55D and exit at 0.84D. Direct port; scope selectors to el and use immediateRender:false on the from() tweens if composed.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false when composed

records.name: Splitting Cube: Perfect Loop
records.description: A template where a cube splits apart and reassembles in a seamless loop. Good for abstract motion graphics and geometric animation showcases.
records.move: cube bursts into eight cubelets, spin and twist, snap back seamlessly
records.how: Eight CSS 3D cubelets (six faces each, brightness-shaded) form a 2x2x2 cube inside a group that turns 360deg on Y over the full 5s and nods rotationX 14deg yoyo. A state object drives placement through gsap.set in onUpdate: at 6% spread goes 0 to 1 with back.out(1.8) so each cubelet flies out along its octant to 2.6x the half-size; at 22% spin rotates each cubelet 180deg on Y (sign by position, expo.inOut) and at 30% twist does the same on X; at 58% spread returns with back.in(1.4) as the cubelets snap together; at 74-78% spin and twist run to 360, which is the rest pose, so the last frame equals the first. A soft floor shadow scales 1.35 and thins during the spread.
records.adapt: Change the eight face colours, cube size (H) and the spread factor (1.6); the stage gradient and shadow are the only other visuals; keep the back.out/back.in spread pair and the expo.inOut half-turns so the loop stays seamless.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the world, group and eight cubelets with perspective on el; animate returns the timeline with the proxy-state tweens at 0.06D, 0.22D, 0.3D, 0.58D, 0.74D, 0.78D and the Y turn spanning D. The placement is gsap.set inside onUpdate, which already lives on the timeline, so it ports directly; scope getElementById to el.
caveats: 48 faces with filter: brightness, moderate cost
needs perspective and preserve-3d on ancestors

records.name: The Prompt: AI Chat
records.description: An animated AI chat interface template with message-by-message reveals. Great for conversational AI product demos and chatbot feature presentations.
records.move: prompt types and sends, dots think, reply streams word by word
records.how: A dark chat window with a compose bar. A caret blinks (steps ease, infinite). From 4% TextPlugin types the first prompt over 1.4s, the send button presses, the input clears and the user bubble slides up (y 18 to 0, power3.out); the assistant row appears with three dots bouncing y -5 in a stagger (4 half-beats) and at 35% the dots hide and the reply streams in word by word (opacity 0 to 1, y 6 to 0, 0.055s stagger, power2.out). The second exchange repeats from 54% with a shorter prompt and a 0.07s word stagger. At 94% all messages lift 16px and fade with a 0.06s stagger and set() calls at the last frame restore the hidden state.
records.adapt: Replace the assistant name, the two prompts and the two replies (the word spans are generated from the strings), the avatar gradient and accent purple; keep the 0.055s word stagger and the dots beat, which is what makes the streaming feel live.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the window from shot.exchanges and splits replies into .w spans; animate returns the timeline with exchange one at 0.03-0.5D and two at 0.54-0.85D, clear at 0.94D. The infinite caret tween should become a finite repeat sized to D; scope querySelector calls to el and register TextPlugin.
caveats: caret tween uses repeat:-1, an infinite child; replace with repeat: Math.ceil(D/0.8) so tl.duration() stays finite
display toggles on the dots via set() rely on GSAP reverting when scrubbed backwards

records.name: The Prompt: Image Generation
records.description: An animated UI template showing an AI image generation interface. Great for showcasing AI product features and generative tool demos where showing the experience is more convincing than describing it.
records.move: prompt types, Generate fills, tiles shimmer, four images resolve from blur
records.how: A white app card rises in with four grey tiles staggering in (scale .9, power3.out). A caret blinks and from 9% TextPlugin types the prompt over 1.8s; at 34% the Generate button presses (scale .93 yoyo), its label swaps to Generating and a purple fill grows scaleX 0 to 1 over 2.2s (power1.inOut) while a white shimmer sweeps xPercent -100 to 100 across each tile twice with a 0.12s stagger. From 55% the tile artwork resolves: opacity 0 to 1, filter blur(24px) to 0 and scale 1.1 to 1 with a 0.18s stagger (power2.out), number tags pop, and the colour blobs inside drift for 3s. At 65% the label reads Done and the fill turns green. From 87% the images blur back out, the prompt clears and the button resets with set() calls at the last frame.
records.adapt: Replace the app name, model tag, prompt string and the four gradient/blob compositions (or use real images in .art); keep the 2.2s fill and the 0.18s blur-resolve stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the app, appends grain overlays and the SVG noise filter inside el; animate returns the timeline with typing at 0.09D, generate at 0.34D, resolve at 0.55D and reset at 0.87D. Uses filter: blur on four tiles and an feTurbulence grain filter, both port directly; register TextPlugin and scope selectors to el.
caveats: animates filter: blur(24px) on four tiles plus a feTurbulence grain overlay with mix-blend-mode, the heaviest frames are the resolve

records.name: The Vault: App Icons
records.description: An animated template showing multiple app icons appearing in a grid. Works well for app family presentations and product ecosystem showcases.
records.move: icons flip-pop from centre, light sweep, row wave, hero steps forward
records.how: A dark stage with a 2x6 grid of twelve gradient app icons under a headline that rises from a mask. From 4% each icon scales from 0 with rotationY -90 and back.out(1.8), grid-staggered from the centre outward (0.09s), labels following. At 28% a diagonal sheen sweeps xPercent -110 to 110 across the icons left to right; at 46% a lift wave (y -14, rotationX 12, staggered from the edges) settles with elastic.out(1,.5). At 65% the last icon scales 1.35 and comes forward z 60 with back.out(2) while the other eleven dim to 35% and scale .92, restoring at 82%. From 90% the icons flip out (scale 0, rotationY 90, back.in) from the edges and the headline drops.
records.adapt: Replace the twelve gradients, glyph SVGs and names, the headline and eyebrow, and choose which index is the hero; the grid shape is in the stagger config ([2,6]); keep the back.out(1.8) flip-in and the elastic wave.

caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false when composed
the grid stagger assumes exactly 12 items in a 2x6 layout

records.name: The Vault: Contactless Payment
records.description: An animated template showing a contactless payment tap interaction. Perfect for fintech product demos and banking app showcases where you want the experience to feel smooth.
records.move: phone glides to reader, NFC rings ripple, tick draws, pulls away
records.how: A dark payment terminal rises in showing a $24.00 total. A phone starts off-screen right at rotationY -35; from 6% it glides to x 150 with power3.inOut over 1.4s, then closes to the reader (x 40, y -40) by 28%. At 28% a small nudge marks the tap: the NFC glyph turns green, three rings scale .3 to 2.2 and fade with a 0.28s stagger (twice), the card on the phone bobs. At 45% the Approved screen fades in, its green disc scales from 0 with back.out(2.2), the tick draws with DrawSVG power2.out and the text rises; the phone shows Done. At 66% the phone pulls away with power3.in, at 84% the reader resets and at 94% the terminal drops out, with set() calls at the last frame restoring the tick and hint.
records.adapt: Change the merchant, amount, card brand and holder, the green (#22c55e) and the phone card gradient; keep the 1.4s glide, the 0.28s ring stagger and the back.out(2.2) approval.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the terminal and phone from shot; animate returns the timeline with glide at 0.06D, tap at 0.28D, approval at 0.45D, exit at 0.66D. The phone offsets (x 720) assume a 1280 stage, derive from el width; needs perspective on el and DrawSVG registered.
caveats: catalog lists 14s but the file runs 10s
phone start offset x 720 assumes a 1280x720 stage
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when composed

records.name: The Vault: Digital Wallet

At 29%, 53% and 76% the front card flies left (x -700, rotate -8, power3.in), is sent to the back by zIndex and returns with power3.out while the other two restack with power3.inOut and the page dots switch; each swipe re-counts the balance to that card's value. records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the screen from shot.cards and shot.transactions; animate returns the timeline with the build in the first 0.2D, swipes at 0.29D, 0.53D, 0.76D and exit from 0.91D. from() tweens need immediateRender:false when composed

At 27% the card dips to scale .98 and a hidden detail panel expands from height 0 to its measured height with expo.out over 0.8s while the amount counts to $4,200.00 (expo.out, 1.3s) and the meta grid and buttons stagger up. records.name: The Vault: Payment Notifications
records.description: An animated template showing multiple payment notifications arriving in a stacked sequence. Good for fintech app UI demos and payment system showcases.

records.name: Yosemite: Animated Widget

Inside the screen, sidebar nav items slide from x:-30 with 0.06s stagger, stat cards rise from y:30 with back.out(1.7), three counters tween (onUpdate text) with power3.out, an SVG line chart draws with drawSVG 0->100% (power2.inOut) around 20-40%, and list rows stagger in from x:20. records.name: Animated Mobile Gallery
records.description: A gallery template showing mobile screenshots transitioning smoothly in sequence. Great for app store assets and product page videos.

Every 0.76s (19% of the 4s duration) the track tweens x by one 300px step with expo.inOut over 0.65s while the outgoing card shrinks to 0.86/0.55 (power2.inOut) and the incoming card grows to 1/1 starting 0.12s later; a pagination dot widens 8->24px in step. records.name: Animated Photo Gallery

records.description: An iOS Instagram story template with animated UI elements and accurate framing. Ideal for social media content that needs to look like it was made by someone who cares about the details.
records.move: story chrome slides in, sticker pops elastic, poll fills, swipe-up exit
records.how: A 1080x1920 portrait frame: the background photo scales 1.0 -> 1.12 linearly over the 5s and the current story progress bar scaleX 0 -> 1 linearly in step. The header drops in from y -30 and the footer rises from y 40 (power3.out) in the first 10%. At 10% a white sticker pops from scale 0 / rotate -12 with elastic.out(1,0.5) then wobbles rotate -4 <-> 3 with sine.inOut yoyo. At 20% a poll card rises from y 80 / scale 0.9 with back.out(1.6); at 42% one option squashes to 0.92 as a tap and both fill bars scaleX 0 -> 1 with expo.out from their outer edges, percentages fade in; a location mention slides in from x -40 at 32%. At 88% sticker, poll and mention slide up y -80 and fade with power2.in (0.06s stagger) and the chrome fades.
records.adapt: Replace the photo, account name, sticker text, poll question, options and percentages (fill widths 60%/40%), the mention text and the progress-bar segment count. Keep the elastic pop, the expo.out fills at 0.46 of the duration and the linear progress bar.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the story UI from shot strings; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with header/footer at 0.02D-0.04D, sticker pop at 0.1D, poll at 0.2D, vote at 0.42D-0.5D and exit at 0.88D. The from() tweens should become fromTo with immediateRender:false; the frame is portrait 1080x1920 so the shot must declare that size.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920 frame, not 16:9
backdrop-filter blur on the mention chip
loop does not close: elements swipe up and out

records.name: Mobile App Showcase
records.description: A mobile app showcase template with clean framing and smooth motion. Great for app store previews and product pitch decks where you want to walk through the experience clearly.
records.move: phone turns in, tap ripples swipe pages, side copy swaps, snaps back
records.how: A 280x580 phone inside a perspective stage fromTo's rotateY -30 -> -12, y 40 -> 0, opacity 0 -> 1 with 1.0s expo.out, then drifts rotateY -12 -> 12 over 3.6s sine.inOut, returning to -12 at 92%. A left copy block (step label, headline, paragraph) slides in from x -30 and a vertical step indicator fades in. At 28% and 60% a pink tap ripple expands scale 0 -> 1.6 with opacity to 0 (power2.out) on a tab, the .pages strip slides xPercent -33.3 then -66.6 with 0.6s expo.inOut, tab dots recolour, and the copy exits y -14 / fades (power2.in), swaps text via tl.call and re-enters from y 14 (power3.out) while the step indicator grows. Page 2 has a timer counting down 25:00 -> 24:13 linearly; page 3 bars grow scaleY from the bottom with back.out(1.5). At 90% a third tap snaps the strip back to xPercent 0 and copy to step 1.
records.adapt: Replace the three copy entries, page headings, hero gradient and accent (#ff3d81), timer start value and bar heights; the tapAt x positions correspond to the tab bar slots. Keep the 0.6s expo.inOut swipes at 0.31 and 0.63 of the duration and the 1.0s expo.out phone entry.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone, page strip, copy block and step dots from shot data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entry 0-0.2D, taps at 0.28D, 0.6D and 0.9D. setCopy and the timer onUpdate use document.querySelector and must be scoped to el; the tl.call at 0.01 that resets copy is required for seek-back.
caveats: copy is swapped by tl.call so scrubbing backwards shows the wrong step text between calls
from() tweens on .step, .steps and .bar have default immediateRender
near-loop: pages and copy return to step 1 at the end but the phone and copy start from opacity 0 so frame 0 differs from the last frame
two 700px blur(90px) blobs in the background are slow to render

records.name: Mobile App: Subscribe Field
records.description: An animated subscription input field template designed for mobile UI. Works great for app onboarding demos and email capture feature showcases.
records.move: input focuses, typewriter fills email, button squashes, tick draws, sparks burst, resets
records.how: A 300x620 phone drifts rotateY -18 -> -8 with sine.inOut across the whole 4s over a slowly scaling ocean background; a headline and paragraph rise on the left (expo.out / power3.out) in the first 20%. At 12% the email field lifts scale 1.03 with a blue border and 4px box-shadow ring (power2.out), the placeholder slides up yPercent -160 and fades, a caret blinks (opacity yoyo repeat 7) and TextPlugin types 'ada@northwind.io' linearly over 1.1s (21-49%). At 54% the button squashes scale 0.94 (power2.in) and rebounds with elastic.out(1,0.45), its label rolls up yPercent -100 while a green 'You're in' panel rolls in from yPercent 100 (expo.inOut), an SVG tick draws drawSVG 0 -> 100% and six spark dots fly out radially (x cos*70, y sin*40, opacity to 0, power3.out); the field border turns green. At 87% the panel and label roll back, the typed text clears, the placeholder returns and the border resets, ready to repeat.
records.adapt: Change the typed email string, headline and paragraph, the art card gradient, accent blue (#3d5aff) and success green (#1fa86c), and the background image. Keep the 1.1s linear typing, the 0.12s squash into elastic.out and the 0.35s expo.inOut label roll.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone form and the copy block and applies the initial gsap.set on .ok and .caret; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with focus at 0.125D, typing 0.21-0.49D, tap at 0.54D, reset at 0.875D. The spark loop uses document.querySelectorAll and must be scoped to el; TextPlugin and DrawSVGPlugin must be registered by the engine.
caveats: from() tweens on .tag b and .tag p have default immediateRender
near-loop: the form state resets but the phone rotateY and background scale end at different values from frame 0
full-frame background image with brightness/saturate filter

records.name: Mobile Gallery: Grid
records.description: A template showing mobile screenshots animating into a grid layout. Good for app portfolio presentations and multi-screen showcases.
records.move: screenshots spring from a centre pile into a grid, tilt, pile back
records.how: Eight 200x300 phone screenshots in a 4-column grid all start collapsed on the frame centre (x/y offsets computed from getBoundingClientRect toward 640,360), fanned rotate (i-3.5)*4deg, scale 0.7, opacity 0, 40px low. Each springs to its grid cell with 0.9s back.out(1.4), staggered 0.07s from 3% of the 3s duration; a caption fades in at 30%. The whole grid tilts rotateX -6 / rotateY 6 with sine.inOut from 33% to 73% then returns. From 83% the shots fly back to the centre in reverse order (0.04s stagger), scale 0.7, opacity 0, 40px high, with power3.in, and the caption fades, so the frame ends empty as it began.
records.adapt: Replace the eight screen names and hero gradients (or use real screenshots), the caption and the dark-index rule; change grid columns for a different count. Keep the 0.9s back.out(1.4) spring with 0.07s stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid from shot.screens; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entries at (0.033 + i*0.023)*D, tilt at 0.33D and gather at 0.83D. The centre-offset maths uses getBoundingClientRect against a hard-coded 640,360 viewport centre, so replace it with offsets relative to el's own rect (or rely on the grid's translate(-50%,-50%) and compute from cell index).
caveats: centre offsets assume a 1280x720 viewport via getBoundingClientRect; must be measured relative to the container when ported
the .lbl from() has default immediateRender
loop closes visually: both end frames are empty, though the final pile sits 40px above the initial one

records.name: Mobile Screens Reveal
records.description: A template where mobile screens reveal dramatically from off-screen with a cinematic entrance. Perfect for app launch announcements and product teasers.
records.move: glow swells, three phones slam in with motion blur, flash, pull back
records.how: On black, a purple radial glow scales 0.3 -> 1 and fades in over the first 33% of the 3s (power2.out). The centre phone slams up from y 900 with rotateX -40, scale 1.1 and filter blur(14px) to rest (expo.out, 0.7s) at 12%; the left phone comes from x -1000 with rotateY 60 / rotateZ -12 to x -300, rotateY 22, rotateZ -6 at 17%; the right mirrors it at 20%; the side phones sit at z -120. At 21% a white full-frame flash drops from opacity 0.85 to 0 (power2.out) while the group shakes x 0 <-> 8 six times. The title rises from yPercent 120 (expo.out) at 30%, the group drifts rotateY 8 with sine.inOut, and at 82% the phones recede to z -900 with opacity 0 and blur(10px) (power3.in, 0.04s stagger); glow and title fade so the frame returns to black.
records.adapt: Swap the three screen designs, the title text, the glow colour and the rest poses (x +-300, rotateY +-22). Keep the 0.7s expo.out slams staggered 0.15s, the 0.35s flash and the 0.05s x6 shake.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .glow, .grp with three phones, .flash and .title; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with slams at 0.12D/0.17D/0.2D, flash at 0.21D, drift at 0.37D and exit at 0.82D. The from() tweens on the title should become fromTo with immediateRender:false; el needs perspective:1400px.
caveats: animates CSS filter blur(14px) on three phones with box-shadows, slow while in motion
the 900px radial glow is a large translucent layer
loop closes only because both end frames are black

records.name: Mobile Screens: Grid
records.description: A template showing multiple mobile screens arranged and animated in a grid layout. Useful for showcasing several UI designs or app features at the same time.
records.move: isometric wall of phone screens pops in, lists scroll, camera pans, folds
records.how: A 5x3 grid of 190x400 screens (random rows, themes and dark flags from a seeded rng) is pre-rotated rotateX 32 / rotateZ -16 inside a camera wrapper. The camera pans x 260 -> 60, y -150 -> -10 and scales 1.02 -> 1.14 linearly across the full 7s. Screens pop from scale 0.6, opacity 0, z -300 with 0.9s expo.out using a grid stagger from the centre (0.06s each) starting at 1.5%; every .list scrolls y to -(120 + (i%4)*60) with power1.inOut over 6.4s. A two-line headline rises from yPercent 110 (expo.out) at 7% with a subline; at 89% the headline lifts and fades and screens fold away scale 0.6 / z -300 with expo.in staggered from the grid edges (0.04s).
records.adapt: Change COLS/ROWS, the theme colour pairs, screen titles, headline copy and the glow colour; seed the rng differently for other layouts. Keep the linear camera pan across the whole duration and the centre-out / edges-in grid staggers.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .cam > .grid with COLS*ROWS screens from a seeded rng; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the pan over D, pops at 0.015D, list scrolls from 0.07D for 0.91D and exit at 0.886D. The grid stagger needs grid:[ROWS,COLS]; from() tweens should be fromTo with immediateRender:false; el must supply perspective:2200px.
caveats: a 1200x900 glow with filter blur(30px) sits behind the wall
15 screens with triple box-shadows animate in 3D at once, heavy per frame
loop does not close: camera pan does not return

records.name: Mobile Screens: Slider
records.description: A horizontal slider template that moves through mobile screens with smooth swipeable motion. Good for app feature tours and product demos built for mobile audiences.
records.move: endless coverflow phone carousel: hold, expo swipe one step, focus scales
records.how: Five 260x540 phones sit on a horizontal track 320px apart with wraparound distance d per slot. A fx.register seek loop of N*SEG = 10s splits each 2s segment into a 1.05s hold and a 0.95s move eased with expo.inOut; each frame sets x = d*320, y = 22*|d|, scale 1.12 - 0.28*|d|, opacity 1 - 0.55*min(1,|d|/2), zIndex by distance and filter blur growing 2px per step beyond the neighbour, while the active screen's content settles y 14 -> 0. Pagination dots swap opacity 0.2 -> 1 and scale 1.35 on the rounded position. After five steps the positions repeat exactly, so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Replace the five theme pairs and screen names (or real screenshots), N, STEP spacing and the HOLD/SEG ratio; the title text. Keep the expo.inOut move and the scale/opacity falloff by distance.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the track slots and dots from shot.screens; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with a single tween of duration D and onUpdate that runs the seek(t) function (t = progress*D) applying gsap.set to each slot, since the source is a fx.register seek loop rather than a timeline. SEG becomes D/N; the +-STEP positions assume a 1280-wide frame.
caveats: catalog lists 13s but the file renders 10s
per-frame filter blur on off-centre phones
uses fx.register seek loop, not a GSAP timeline

records.name: Mobile Showreel
records.description: A full mobile showreel template that moves through app screens and UI moments in sequence. Great for app portfolio presentations and mobile product showcases where you want to show the whole product not just highlights.
records.move: phone screen cuts vertically through pages, captions and counter roll each cut
records.how: A 300x620 phone hangs rotateY -14 / rotateX 5 and breathes to -8 / 3 and back with sine.inOut yoyo across the 4s; the aurora background slowly scales. A vertical strip of four full-height pages plus a copy of the first sits in the screen; at cuts 0.65, 1.65, 2.65, 3.55s (16%, 41%, 66%, 89%) the strip moves y by -596px with 0.45s expo.inOut while the phone dips scale 0.965 and back (power2.inOut yoyo). On each cut the caption line rolls yPercent 0 -> -100 out and the next rolls in from 100 inside an overflow-hidden box, as does a large faint 01-04 counter on the left. Each page's children stagger up from y 24 / opacity 0 (power3.out, 0.06s) 0.25s after its cut; the fifth page is the first again so the strip seam is invisible.
records.adapt: Replace the four page templates, caption names and the 'Acme · Showreel' kicker; the cuts array sets when each page arrives and page height (596) must match the strip. Keep the 0.45s expo.inOut cut and the 0.22s scale dip.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone, the strip with pages.concat(pages[0]), the caption and counter spans and applies the initial yPercent gsap.set; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with cuts at 0.1625D, 0.4125D, 0.6625D and 0.8875D. The page from() staggers should become fromTo with immediateRender:false and the nth-child selectors must be scoped to el.
caveats: near-loop: strip, captions and counter return to page 1 but the background scale and the page-1 stagger-in state differ from frame 0
full-frame background image with brightness/saturate filter

records.name: New Message Notification [iOS]
records.description: An iOS message notification template with system-accurate animation. Great for messaging app demos and iOS UI presentations where authenticity matters.
records.move: iOS banner springs down, clock nudges, banner dismisses upward
records.how: On a 1080x1920 lock screen the wallpaper slowly scales 1.04 -> 1.1 with yPercent -0.6 -> 0.6 linearly over the 3s. At 8% a frosted banner (backdrop-filter blur 40px) drops from y -300, scale 0.9, opacity 0 to rest over 0.85s with a CustomEase iOS spring (fast out, one soft overshoot) while the big clock nudges down y 28 with the same spring; the banner's name and message lines fade up y 10 with 0.06s stagger (power2.out). At 82% the banner slides back to y -300, scale 0.92, opacity 0 with power3.in and the clock returns with power3.inOut.
records.adapt: Replace the sender, message, app icon colours, date/time strings and wallpaper. Keep the spring CustomEase path and the 0.85s entry / 0.42s power3.in dismiss timings.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the lock screen and banner from shot strings; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the drop at 0.083D, text at 0.15D and dismiss at 0.817D. CustomEase must be registered once by the engine; the .txt from() should be fromTo with immediateRender:false; the frame is portrait 1080x1920.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920 frame, not 16:9
backdrop-filter blur(40px) on the banner plus blur(30px) on two bottom buttons, slow to render
loop closes only in the sense that the banner is off-screen at both ends; the wallpaper scale differs

records.name: Orbit: Cards
records.description: A template where cards animate in an orbiting motion around a central point. Good for showcasing multiple features or product highlights without cramming them all on screen at once.
records.move: feature cards orbit an ellipse around a core, depth-scaled and back-blurred
records.how: Six white feature cards revolve once around a 440x150 ellipse in the 5s loop, computed each frame by a fx.register seek function: x = cos(a)*440, y = sin(a)*150, with depth = (sin(a)+1)/2 driving scale 0.8 -> 1.3, opacity 0.45 -> 1, zIndex and filter blur 2.2px -> 0 so cards at the back are small, dim and soft and cards passing the front are large and sharp. Eight small dots counter-rotate twice on an inner 230x78 ellipse with the same depth scaling; the core gradient disc pulses scale +-4% at twice the orbit rate and rotates 18deg/s; two dashed SVG ellipses crawl their stroke-dashoffset in opposite directions. Because everything is a function of t/D with whole-number cycles, the last frame equals the first.
records.adapt: Replace the six feature names and icon colours, the core gradient and label, the ellipse radii RX/RY and the dot count. Keep the one-orbit-per-loop rule and the depth formulas so the loop stays seamless.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the ring SVG, core, cards and dots from shot.features; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one tween of duration D whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) body (t = progress*D) applying gsap.set to every card and dot, since the source is a fx.register seek loop rather than a timeline. Scope document.querySelector('.core') and the orb ids to el.
caveats: per-frame filter blur on six cards
uses fx.register seek loop, not a GSAP timeline

records.name: Push Notification [Android]
records.description: An Android push notification template with a realistic slide-in animation. Good for Android app demos and cross-platform UI presentations.
records.move: heads-up card decelerates in, actions unfold, ripple tap, swipes away
records.how: A 310x640 Android phone drifts rotateY -18 -> -10 with sine.inOut over the 4s beside a rising three-line headline (yPercent 110, expo.out) and kicker/paragraph fade-ups. At 12.5% the notification card comes from y -190, opacity 0, scaleY 0.85 to rest in 0.55s with power4.out while the lock-screen clock pushes down y 118 in step; the card's header and body fade up with 0.06s stagger. At 37.5% the action row unfolds height 0 -> 18px and opacity 1 (power3.out) and the clock drops a further 30px. At 62.5% a blue ripple expands scale 0 -> 22 and fades (power2.out); at 77.5% the card swipes off to x 320 with opacity 0 (power3.in), the clock returns and the copy slides left and fades.
records.adapt: Replace the app name, sender, title and message, action labels, the accent blue (#3d6dff), headline words and background image. Keep the 0.55s power4.out arrival, the 0.4s unfold and the 0.45s power3.in swipe.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone, lock-screen and notification card from shot strings; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with arrival at 0.125D, expand at 0.375D, ripple at 0.625D and dismiss at 0.775D. The from() tweens on copy and card text should be fromTo with immediateRender:false; el needs perspective:1800px.
caveats: full-frame background image with brightness/saturate filter
loop does not close: card swipes away, copy fades, phone angle differs from frame 0

records.name: Push Notification [iOS]
records.description: A single iOS push notification template that slides in from the top of the screen with realistic timing. Good for app demos and mobile UI presentations.
records.move: iOS banner springs onto lock screen with haptic shake, dismisses up
records.how: A 300x620 phone with an aurora lock screen drifts rotateY 16 -> 9 with sine.inOut over the 3s while a right-aligned three-line headline rises from yPercent 110 (0.08s stagger, expo.out) and kicker/paragraph fade up. At 15% a frosted banner (backdrop-filter blur 30px) drops from y -170, scale 0.9, opacity 0 to rest in 0.8s on a CustomEase iOS spring while the clock nudges y 10; the banner text fades up with 0.06s stagger and the phone body shakes x 0 <-> 3 six times as a haptic. At 78% the banner retreats to y -170, scale 0.92, opacity 0 with power3.in, the clock returns and the copy slides right and fades.
records.adapt: Replace the app name, message, headline words, the lock-screen image and outer background. Keep the spring CustomEase, the 0.8s drop and the 0.05s x6 haptic.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone and copy; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the drop at 0.15D, haptic at 0.167D and dismiss at 0.783D. CustomEase must be registered by the engine; from() tweens should be fromTo with immediateRender:false; el needs perspective:1800px.
caveats: backdrop-filter blur(30px) on the banner over a cover image
full-frame background image with brightness/saturate filter
loop does not close: copy fades and phone angle differs from frame 0

records.name: Rotating Mobile Screens: Black & White
records.description: A template showing mobile screens rotating in a black and white palette. Good for editorial-style app showcases and design portfolio reels where you want stronger visual contrast.
records.move: three mono phones flip 180 in a ripple, rest, flip again
records.how: Three 250x520 two-faced cards (white front / black back, backface-visibility hidden) sit in a row with a screen-blend SVG grain overlay. At 6% of the 5s each card flips rotateY 0 -> 180 over 1.1s with expo.inOut, staggered 0.18s so the row ripples; at 56% they flip 180 -> 360 the same way, so after two half-turns every card is back at its front. Meanwhile the whole row leans rotateX 6 -> -4 and rotateY -8 -> 8 with sine.inOut over 2.5s and yoyos back, and each card bobs y 0 -> -14 with a staggered yoyo, both mirrored so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Replace the six screen templates (three fronts, three backs), the caption and index text; the palette is deliberately black and white so change the grain opacity rather than adding colour. Keep the 1.1s expo.inOut flips at 0.06 and 0.56 of the duration with 0.18s stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the .row with three .flip cards from shot.screens plus the grain SVG; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with flips at 0.06D and 0.56D and the yoyo lean/bob of duration D/2 repeat 1. The second flip already uses immediateRender:false; el needs perspective:1600px and the grain feTurbulence filter covers the full frame.
caveats: full-frame feTurbulence grain with mix-blend-mode screen adds per-frame cost
catalog has no jitter source; the design is original

records.name: Rotating Smartphones
records.description: A template showing smartphones rotating in 3D space to reveal different screens and angles. Good for mobile product launches where you want to show more than one side of the product.
records.move: three phones spin a full 3D turn, phase-offset, with a bob
records.how: Three 230x470 phones built as front face, back face (camera bump and logo) and two side edges with backface-visibility hidden stand on a blurred floor glow. A fx.register seek loop drives everything from u = t/D: each phone's rotateY = u*360 + i*120 so they are a third of a turn apart, y bobs sin*14px, rotateX tilts sin*5 and rotateZ sits at -4 + 4i; the whole row sways rotateY sin*10 and the caption bobs 3px. All motion uses whole cycles of u so the 5s loop is seamless.
records.adapt: Replace the three theme pairs and screen names (or real screenshots), the back-face finish colours and the caption; change the 120deg phase offset for a different count. Keep one full turn per loop and the sine bob.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the floor, row and three phones from shot.screens; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one tween of duration D whose onUpdate runs the seek body (u = progress) applying gsap.set to each phone, the row and the caption, since the source is a fx.register seek loop. The row and caption selectors must be scoped to el; el needs perspective:2000px.
caveats: uses fx.register seek loop, not a GSAP timeline
the 1400x700 floor uses filter blur(10px) and rotateX 78deg

records.name: Sliding Smartphones
records.description: A template showing multiple smartphones sliding into frame from different directions. A solid format for mobile product launches where you want to show several screens at once.
records.move: phones slide in from left, bottom, right, straighten, float, slide out
records.how: Three 240x490 phones in a row over two blurred pastel blobs. The left phone from()s x -900 with rotate -14 and rotateY 30, the middle from y 800 with rotate 6, the right from x 900 with rotate 14 / rotateY -30, each 1.0s expo.out staggered 0.15s from 3% of the 5s; a two-line headline rises from yPercent 110 (expo.out) and a tag fades in from x 20. Once settled each phone floats y -14 / 12 / -10 with 1.4s sine.inOut yoyo out of phase, and the blobs breathe scale 1 -> 1.15 yoyo over 2.5s. At 86% each phone leaves the way it came with 0.5s expo.in (0.08s stagger), the headline lines exit upward to yPercent -110 and the tag fades.
records.adapt: Replace the three theme pairs and screen names (or real screenshots), the headline words, the tag and the blob colours. Keep the 1.0s expo.out entries with 0.15s stagger and the mirrored 0.5s expo.in exits.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the blobs, caption and the row of three phones from shot.screens; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entries at 0.03D/0.06D/0.09D, floats from 0.24D and exits at 0.86D-0.89D. All the from() tweens should become fromTo with immediateRender:false so seeking is deterministic; el needs perspective:1800px.
caveats: two 600-700px blobs with filter blur(70px) are slow to render
from() tweens have default immediateRender
loop closes only in that the frame is empty at both ends (phones off-screen, headline hidden)

records.name: Sliding Smartphones: Stories
records.description: An animated template showing smartphones sliding into frame with vertical story content already playing. Good for social media campaign previews and app story feature demos.
records.move: phones slide in playing story video, bars fill, sticker pops, slide out
records.how: A 1080x1920 portrait frame with a blurred, dimmed background video. Two smaller side phones slide in from x -700 / +700 with rotate -12 / 12 (0.9s expo.out) at 3% and 7% of the 3s, and the large centre phone rises from y 1200 with rotate 4 (1.0s expo.out) at 8%; a caption drops in from y -30. Every phone plays a story clip whose currentTime is driven each frame from the timeline (offset 1.3s per phone), and the first progress segment fills scaleX 0 -> 1 linearly across the loop. Story text lines rise from yPercent 110 (0.08s stagger, expo.out) around 27-30%, a yellow sticker pops from scale 0 / rotate 30 with back.out(2) at 40% then rocks rotate -14 yoyo. At 85% the side phones slide back out, the centre phone drops to y 1200 (expo.in) and the caption fades.
records.adapt: Replace the three story video clips, account names, story text lines, sticker text and caption. Keep the 0.9-1.0s expo.out entries and the linear progress fill; the per-phone 1.3s video offset can be tuned per clip.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the background video, caption and three phones from shot.videos and awaits loadeddata on each (the source uses fx.wait for this); animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline whose first tween is a linear object tween of duration D with onUpdate setting each video's currentTime, plus the entries at 0.03D-0.08D and exits at 0.85D. document.querySelectorAll('video') must be scoped to el; from() tweens should be fromTo with immediateRender:false; frame is portrait.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920 frame, not 16:9
four <video> elements seeked by currentTime every frame plus a full-frame blur(30px) video, heavy and depends on the clips being preloaded
loop does not close: video times differ at each end and the phones are off-screen at both ends

records.name: Sliding Web Screens
records.description: A template showing multiple web screens sliding into view in sequence. Great for website and SaaS product showcases where you want to show the product in context.
records.move: browser windows slide in from the right, each pushes the stack back
records.how: Four 760x480 browser mockups (landing, dashboard, pricing, docs) share one centre position inside a stack tilted rotateY -12 -> -6, rotateX 6 -> 4 and x 60 -> 90 with sine.inOut over the whole 7s. Every 1.5s (3%, 24%, 46%, 67%) the next window from()s x 1100 with rotateY -20 over 0.9s expo.out, and every window already in place is pushed y -34, z -140, x -40 and opacity -0.12 per step behind (also 0.9s expo.out) so the earlier pages recede as a fanned stack; each page's children fade up y 18 with 0.05s stagger 0.15s after arrival. A caption fades up at 6%. At 90% all windows fly to x -1300 with rotateY 15 and opacity 0 (expo.in, 0.07s stagger) and the caption fades.
records.adapt: Replace the four page templates (colours from the C array, URLs, copy) and the caption; add pages by extending the array, keeping the 1.5s cadence. Keep the 0.9s expo.out arrival and the per-step push-back of 34/140/40px.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the stack with N windows from shot.pages; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with arrivals at (0.03 + i*0.214)*D, push-backs at the same instants and the exit at 0.9D. from() tweens on windows and page children should be fromTo with immediateRender:false; el needs perspective:2000px.
caveats: from() tweens on windows and page children have default immediateRender
loop does not close: windows fly out left

records.name: Text Message [iOS]
records.description: An iOS text message template where chat bubbles appear in a realistic conversation sequence. Good for messaging UI mockups and narrative social content.
records.move: iMessage thread: typing dots, bubbles pop in, reply typed and sent
records.how: A 1080x1920 iOS Messages screen with nav, thread, input bar and keyboard. The thread is bottom-anchored and pre-offset by the height of every hidden item, measured at mount; as each item appears the thread tweens y up by that item's height (0.5s power3.out). Incoming bubbles pop from scale 0.4, opacity 0, x -30, y 20 with 0.55s back.out(1.6) (outgoing from x +30); typing bubbles bounce three dots y -8 in a staggered yoyo and are hidden (opacity 0, scale 0.8, then display none) when the real message replaces them; timestamp labels just fade in. Twice, TextPlugin types the reply into the input field over 0.9s (linear), the blue send button springs in with back.out(2), squashes 0.85 on send and the typed text clears as the outgoing bubble pops. Beats land at 2%, 5%, 15%, 20%, 32%, 40%, 51%, 57%, 62%, 74%, 83%; at 94% the whole thread drifts up 120px and fades so the next pass starts clean.
records.adapt: Replace the contact name, avatar initial, message strings and timestamps; add or remove items in the thread and re-time the show()/hide()/typeIn()/sendIt() calls. Keep the 0.55s back.out(1.6) pops, the 0.9s linear typing and the 0.5s power3.out thread scroll.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the thread from shot.messages and must measure each item's offsetHeight after layout (so the element has to be in the document with real fonts) to compute the bottom-anchored offsets; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the beats scaled by D/10. TextPlugin must be registered; the .ph/.typed/.send selectors and the thread lookup must be scoped to el; the display:none set() calls are seek-safe because set() reverses.
caveats: catalog lists 16s but the file renders 10s
portrait 1080x1920 frame, not 16:9
layout is measured with offsetHeight at mount, so fonts and widths must be final before animate
backdrop-filter blur(30px) on the nav bar
loop closes only in that the thread is empty/faded at both ends; the input bar resets

records.name: The Route: Boarding Pass
records.description: An animated digital boarding pass template with a travel-themed UI. Great for travel app demos and aviation product showcases.
records.move: boarding pass flips in, route draws with plane, gate flips, stub tears
records.how: Over a drifting ocean background a 760x400 white boarding pass fromTo's rotateY -75, x -120, opacity 0 to rotateY -6 with 1.1s expo.out at 1% of the 9s, then rocks rotateY 4 / rotateX 3 with a 3.6s sine.inOut yoyo. Its contents fade up y 20 with 0.07s stagger (power3.out) from 5%, and 44 barcode bars print in with scaleY from the bottom (0.012s stagger) at 11%. From 17% to 52% the blue route path draws drawSVG 0 -> 100% with power2.inOut while a plane icon follows the same bezier with MotionPathPlugin (autoRotate) in sync. At 33% the gate value rolls out yPercent -100, changes text in onComplete, and rolls back from yPercent 100 with back.out(1.6); the status pill pulses scale 1.08 yoyo eight times then turns amber and reads 'Final call' at 58%. At 84% the stub slides x 60, rotate 3 and fades (power3.in); at 91% the pass flips rotateY 70, x 160 and fades (expo.in).
records.adapt: Replace the airline, flight number, airports, times, passenger, gate/seat values and the accent blue (#2f6bff); reshape the route path d attribute (both #p and #p2). Keep the 1.1s expo.out flip-in, the 3.2s power2.inOut draw and the 0.6s expo.in flip-out.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the pass, the SVG arc and 44 seeded barcode bars; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with flip-in at 0.011D, draw 0.167D-0.52D, gate flip at 0.333D, status change at 0.578D, tear at 0.844D and exit at 0.911D.
