DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin must be registered; the motionPath path/align ids must be unique per instance or replaced with element references scoped to el; the onComplete/onReverseComplete text swaps stay as they are.
caveats: text changes use onComplete/onReverseComplete, so a seek that jumps over those tweens without playing them shows stale text
from() tweens on contents and bars have default immediateRender
full-frame background image with brightness/saturate filter
loop does not close: pass flips away

records.name: The Route: iOS Flight Tracker
records.description: An animated iOS flight tracker template with route visualization and real-time-style data. Good for travel and aviation app demos.
records.move: phone turns in, route draws with plane, island expands, sheet rises
records.how: Over a drifting ocean background a 300x620 phone fromTo's rotateY 40 -> 12, x -200 -> 0, opacity 0 -> 1 with 1.1s expo.out, then rocks rotateY 6 / rotateX 3 with a 4s sine.inOut yoyo; a right-side headline rises from yPercent 110 (expo.out) with a kicker and altitude stat. Inside, a generated abstract map (seeded land polygons, grid, roads) settles from scale 1.15 / opacity 0 (power3.out) while a bottom sheet is parked at y 150. From 14% to 66% the cyan route path draws drawSVG 0 -> 100% with power1.inOut as a plane icon (autoRotate) and a white tooltip follow the same bezier with MotionPathPlugin and the sheet's progress bar fills scaleX 0 -> 1; altitude and speed counters climb to 34,000 ft / 512 mph (power2.out) in the tooltip, sheet and side stat; a destination ping ring grows r 6 -> 26 and fades eight times. At 50% the Dynamic Island widens to 170px with back.out(1.5) and shows an ETA; at 66% the sheet rises to y 0 (expo.out) and the status pill turns blue and reads 'Landing'. At 93% the phone turns out rotateY -30, x -220 and fades (expo.in) and the copy slides right.
records.adapt: Replace the flight number, airports, times, altitude/speed targets, ETA strings, headline and background image; reshape the route path d (both #route and #flown) and reseed the map rng. Keep the 5.2s power1.inOut draw/flight and the 1.1s expo.out entry.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone, generates the map SVG from a seeded rng and builds the copy block; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entry 0-0.11D, draw 0.14D-0.66D, island at 0.5D, sheet at 0.66D and exit at 0.93D. The counter onUpdate uses five document.querySelector calls that must be scoped to el; the motionPath path/align ids must be unique per instance; DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin must be registered.
caveats: catalog lists 17s but the file renders 10s
text changes use onComplete/onReverseComplete, so seeks that jump those tweens show stale text
from() tweens on copy and tooltip have default immediateRender
full-frame background image with brightness/saturate filter; drop-shadow filter on the plane
loop does not close: phone turns out

records.name: Web Gallery: Grid
records.description: A template presenting website designs in an animated grid. Great for web design portfolios and agency case studies.
records.move: site tiles pop into a grid, camera pushes into centre, pulls back
records.how: Nine 370x230 browser tiles (seeded dark/light, gradient hero art) sit in a 3-column grid inside a camera wrapper. The camera eases scale 0.9 -> 1.0, y 40 -> 0 with power3.out over the first 30% of the 4s while tiles from() scale 0.7, opacity 0, y 60 with 0.8s expo.out in a row-by-row grid stagger (0.07s); a caption fades up. Each tile's hero art drifts y -8 / rotate -3 with a 1.8s sine.inOut yoyo. At 40% the camera pushes to scale 1.7, y 40 with 1.3s expo.inOut, the other eight tiles dim to opacity 0.35 and the centre tile's page scrolls y -40 (power2.inOut). At 85% the camera snaps back to scale 0.9, y 40 with expo.in, all tiles fade (power2.in) and the caption fades, matching the empty first frame.
records.adapt: Replace the nine site names, headlines and colour pairs (or real screenshots) and the caption; change which tile the camera targets via the nth-child(5) selectors. Keep the 0.8s expo.out pops with 0.07s grid stagger and the 1.3s expo.inOut push.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .cam > .grid with nine tiles from shot.sites via a seeded rng; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with pops from 0.0125D, push at 0.4D, scroll at 0.55D and pull-back at 0.85D. The from() tweens should become fromTo with immediateRender:false; the nth-child selectors must be scoped to el; the 3x370px grid assumes a 1280-wide frame.
caveats: from() tweens on tiles and caption have default immediateRender
loop closes visually: the frame is empty at both ends and the camera returns to scale 0.9 / y 40

records.name: Web Screens: Grid
records.description: A template presenting website screenshots in an animated grid. Good for showing multiple web designs or product features side by side.
records.move: windows pop into a grid, pages scroll, camera dives in, tips away
records.how: Six 340px-tall browser mockups fill a 1680px-wide 3-column grid pre-set to scale 0.62, rotate -3, y 20. Windows from() scale 0.6, y 120, opacity 0 with 0.9s expo.out in a centre-out grid stagger (0.09s) from 0.5% of the 9s; headline lines rise from yPercent 110 and colour cards rise with back.out(1.6); the grid settles to scale 0.74, rotate 0, y 0 with 1.4s expo.out at 3%. At 19% every page scrolls y -130 with power3.inOut in a start-to-end grid wave. At 36% the grid pushes to scale 1.5, y 282 with 1.6s expo.inOut so window two fills the frame and its page scrolls a further y -260; at 60% the grid pulls back to 0.74 and the pages return to y 0 in an end-first wave. At 89% windows fall y 140, scale 0.7, opacity 0 with expo.in staggered from the edges while the grid tips to scale 0.62, rotate 3 (power2.in) and the title fades.
records.adapt: Replace the six site records (url, name, accent, two-line headline, three card colours, dark flag) and the title; change which window the camera dives into by adjusting the y 282 target and the .w1 selector. Keep the 0.9s expo.out pops, the 1.6s expo.inOut push/pull and the grid waves.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid from shot.sites and applies the initial gsap.set; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with pops at 0.005D, settle at 0.033D, scroll wave at 0.19D, push at 0.356D, pull at 0.6D and exit at 0.89D. The grid stagger needs grid:[2,3]; from() tweens should be fromTo with immediateRender:false; the 1680px grid and y 282 push target assume a 1280x720 frame.
caveats: from() tweens on windows, headlines, cards and title have default immediateRender
the grid is wider than the frame (1680px at scale 0.74) so edges are cropped by design
loop closes visually: windows are hidden at both ends, though the grid rotate ends at +3 instead of -3

records.name: WhatsApp Messages
records.description: An animated messaging template where chat bubbles appear in a conversation sequence. Perfect for messaging app UI mockups and social storytelling.
records.move: phone rises, chat bubbles pop in with typing dots, phone drops away
records.how: On a 1080x1920 dark-green frame a 560x1160 phone rises from y 260, rotate -4, scale 0.92 with 1.1s expo.out while a two-line headline lifts from yPercent 110 (expo.out, 0.08s stagger) and a subline fades. All chat items start autoAlpha 0, scale 0.6, y 20. From 9% each bubble pops to autoAlpha 1, scale 1, y 0 with 0.45s back.out(1.8); before every incoming bubble a typing indicator is positioned at that bubble's offsetTop, pops in with back.out(2), its three dots bounce y -6 in a staggered yoyo for 0.7s, then it shrinks away; before every outgoing bubble the send button pulses scale 1.25 yoyo. Cadence is 0.6s after incoming and 0.8s after outgoing, and the header status flips to 'typing…' then 'online'. The phone leans rotate 2, y -20 over 6s sine.inOut; at 92% it drops to y 700 with rotate -6 (expo.in) and the headline lines exit upward.
records.adapt: Replace the contact name, message strings, times and the headline; add or remove .msg elements and the cadence follows automatically from the in/out classes. Keep the 0.45s back.out(1.8) pops and the 0.7s typing pause.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone and chat from shot.messages, applies the initial autoAlpha/scale set and must read each bubble's offsetTop after layout for the typing indicator; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the phone entry at 0, bubble cadence starting at 0.09D and exit at 0.92D. document.querySelector('.typing') and '.status' must be scoped to el; the textContent tweens are set-like and reverse correctly; from() tweens should be fromTo with immediateRender:false.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920 frame, not 16:9
typing indicator position depends on offsetTop measured at mount, so layout must be final first
loop does not close: phone drops off and headline exits

records.name: Animated Square Images
records.description: A template where square images animate into view in a coordinated grid sequence. Great for photo galleries and product image showcases.
records.move: squares clip-wipe open in a diagonal wave with push-in, wipe closed
records.how: Eight square cells in a 4x2 grid start clipped to nothing with clip-path inset(100% 0 0 0 round 14px) and y 40; each wipes open to inset(0) and y 0 with 0.8s expo.out in a start-to-end grid stagger (0.07s) from 1.7% of the 3s, while the image inside settles scale 1.3 -> 1 and yPercent 8 -> 0 with 1.1s expo.out on the same stagger; small captions fade up after and a serif title rises from yPercent 110 (expo.out) with a footer fade. From 40% the images drift yPercent -4 with 1.4s sine.inOut. At 75% the cells wipe closed from the top to inset(0 0 100% 0) with y -30 and 0.5s expo.in in the opposite diagonal (0.05s stagger from end); the title exits upward and the footer fades, leaving the empty frame it started with.
records.adapt: Replace the eight images and their background-position crops, the captions, title and footer; change the grid columns and the grid:[2,4] stagger shape together. Keep the 0.8s expo.out open with 0.07s diagonal stagger and the 0.5s expo.in close.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid of cells from shot.images and preloads them (the source awaits Image.decode via fx.wait); animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with opens at 0.017D, captions at 0.17D, drift at 0.4D and closes at 0.75D. The clip-path inset strings must keep the 'round 14px' suffix on both ends so GSAP interpolates; from() tweens on captions, title and footer should be fromTo with immediateRender:false.
caveats: clip-path animates on eight cover-image cells at once, moderately heavy
from() tweens on captions, title and footer have default immediateRender
loop closes visually: all cells are fully clipped and text hidden at both ends

records.name: Blog Post
records.description: An animated blog post layout template where text and images reveal as if being scrolled through for the first time. Perfect for editorial content demos and publication showcases.
records.move: browser window rises, page scrolls, each block lifts in as it enters
records.how: A 900px browser window with an editorial article (serif headline, hero image, paragraphs, two-up images, pull quote) sits on a warm grey stage. The window enters with from y:120/opacity:0 over the first 18% (expo.out), the nav fades and the two headline lines rise via yPercent:110 line-masks (expo.out, stagger 0.1) at 7%. From 26% to 90% the .doc translates y to -(scrollHeight - viewport) with power1.inOut while a thin scrollbar thumb tracks it; each .r block gets a from y:44/opacity:0 expo.out reveal timed by numerically inverting the scroll ease so it fires when the block crosses the lower third of the viewport, and images settle from scale 1.2 to 1 while their .im layers drift yPercent:-6 for parallax. At 91% the window drops out with y:140/opacity:0 expo.in.
records.adapt: Replace the URL bar text, masthead, headline lines, byline, body copy and the three background images (sunset/ocean/aurora); keep the 0.9s window entrance, the 3.2s power1.inOut scroll and the 0.7s expo.out block reveals. Article length changes the scroll distance automatically since it is measured from scrollHeight.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the window/doc markup inside el from shot strings and image URLs; animate(el, shot, D) measures doc.scrollHeight - view.clientHeight after mount, builds the same timeline with times as fractions of D (window in 0-0.18, scroll 0.26-0.9, exit at 0.91) and returns it. All selectors must be scoped with el.querySelector; the ease-inversion loop for reveal timing works unchanged; images are preloaded with fx.wait so the engine needs an equivalent decode wait.
caveats: reveal timing depends on layout measurement (offsetTop/scrollHeight), so fonts must be loaded before building
three full-bleed cover images with scale tweens
exit drops the window but the last frame is not the first (window enters from below, exits below)

records.name: Gradient Website [Dribbble]
records.description: A gradient website animation template with flowing sections inspired by Dribbble-quality design. Good for web design portfolios and colorful UI presentations.
records.move: canvas gradient blobs flow, hero type rises, glass card floats in
records.how: A 640x360 canvas paints four additive radial-gradient blobs whose centres orbit on sine/cos of time (one full cycle per 5s) over a deep purple base, under an SVG-noise grain overlay. On the GSAP timeline the nav drops in (y:-30, expo.out) at 2%, the two headline lines rise through overflow masks (yPercent:110, expo.out, stagger 0.1) at 6%, paragraph and pill CTAs follow (back.out(1.6)), and a frosted stat card enters from y:120/rotate:6 (expo.out) at 10% with its bars growing scaleY from 0 (stagger 0.06) and a number counting up via textContent snap. Two glossy spheres pop in with elastic.out(1,0.5) and drift on sine.inOut while the card floats up 14px. From 87% everything exits: headline lines shoot up (yPercent:-110 expo.in), card drops y:200, spheres scale to 0.
records.adapt: Change brand name, nav labels, headline words, paragraph, CTA labels, the card metric/bars and the four blob colours in paint(); keep the 5s blob orbit period, expo.out entrances and the 0.45s expo.in exit. Bar heights are inline styles.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends the canvas, grain, nav, hero, card and blobs into el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with entrance times scaled to D and adds a dummy tween with onUpdate calling paint(tl.time()) since the original drives the canvas from the timeline's onUpdate callback. Blob phase should use t/D rather than t/5. Selectors must be scoped to el.
caveats: canvas painted via tl.eventCallback('onUpdate'), must become an onUpdate tween when ported
backdrop-filter blur on the card and grain overlay with mix-blend-mode are costly per frame
gradient orbit completes one cycle but DOM elements exit, so the loop does not close

records.name: Happy Faces: Landing Page
records.description: An animated landing page template with illustrated faces that give the product an approachable personality. Good for playful SaaS brands and consumer apps.
records.move: smiley faces bounce in elastic, blink, bob, wink, then pop out
records.how: A cream landing page: nav, three masked headline lines rising yPercent:110 (expo.out, stagger 0.1) from 3%, paragraph and CTA following with back.out(1.6). On the right five coloured circle faces (inline SVG eyes/brows/mouths) enter from scale:0/y:80 with elastic.out(1,0.55) staggered 0.12 from 7%, then two testimonial pills scale in with back.out(2). During the hold (25%-80%) the faces bob y:-14 and rotate 5deg on sine.inOut yoyo, all eyes blink via scaleY:0.1 flashes at three moments, two mouths morph their SVG path d attribute (back.out(2) and sine.inOut yoyo), one face winks and another tilts 12deg, and the CTA pulses scale 1.06. Exit at 87%: faces shrink back with back.in(1.8) stagger 0.06, headline lines shoot up, nav slides off.
records.adapt: Swap brand name, headline, paragraph, CTA and pill text; recolour the five face circles and change their expressions (SVG path d for brows/mouths) or count; keep the elastic.out(1,0.55) entrance, the sine bob rhythm and the back.in exit. The face bob/blink schedule is absolute seconds and must scale with duration.
records.port: mount(el, shot) writes the nav/hero/faces/pills into el; animate(el, shot, D) builds the same timeline with all absolute times divided by 6 then multiplied by D and returns it. The mouth morphs are attr:{d} tweens on inline SVG, which port directly; every gsap.utils.toArray call must be scoped to el.
caveats: blink and wink timings are hard-coded seconds tuned to D=6
eye blinks use transformOrigin on SVG circles, which needs svgOrigin-safe handling in some browsers
emoji glyphs in the pills depend on system fonts

records.name: Image Mask: Parallax Effect
records.description: An image template with a parallax mask effect that adds depth as the content moves. Good for editorial websites and video presentations.
records.move: ellipse mask opens from a slit, layers parallax, widens to full frame
records.how: Two full-bleed image layers: a dimmed aurora far layer and a sunset near layer that is clipped by an SVG clipPath ellipse (objectBoundingBox units). The ellipse rx tweens from 0 to 0.2 over 2.5%-27% (expo.out) so a slit opens into a tall oval, then rx/ry widen to 0.62/0.72 at 57%-87% (expo.inOut) filling the frame, and collapse rx to 0 with expo.in in the last 11%. Across the full duration the far layer drifts xPercent 2 to -3 and scales 1.05 to 1.12 (linear) while the near layer moves the opposite way xPercent -6 to 4 and scales 1.15 to 1, and the mask wrapper itself slides x -40 to 40 (sine.inOut), giving depth. A thin ring scales in with expo.out then blows out to 1.9 and fades; serif headline lines rise through line masks at 15% and shoot up at 87%.
records.adapt: Replace the two background images, the masthead/issue labels, headline lines and the page counter; keep the three-phase ellipse rx/ry keyframes and the opposing linear drift rates, which are what sell the parallax. The ellipse can be swapped for a rect or path in the same clipPath.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts the hidden svg defs (with a unique clipPath id per instance) plus far/mask/near layers and text into el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with attr tweens on the ellipse and the fromTo drifts spread over D. The clipPath id must be unique per shot to avoid collisions across mounted shots; images need a decode wait like fx.wait.
caveats: clip-path: url(#id) referencing a document-level SVG, id must be scoped per instance
two full-frame cover images continuously scaled, heavy on paint
starts with slit closed and ends closed but layer positions differ, so loop is not seamless

records.name: Landing Page: Blocks
records.description: An animated landing page template where content blocks reveal in sequence. Great for SaaS demos and website design presentations where you want to walk a viewer through the product clearly.
records.move: page blocks stack in top to bottom as it scrolls, cursor clicks
records.how: A 1060px browser window lifts in from y:90/opacity:0 (expo.out) over the first 16%. Inside, the nav drops in, three masked headline lines rise yPercent:110 (expo.out, stagger 0.09) at 7%, paragraph and CTA slide up (power3.out), and a dark product screenshot card enters from y:60/scale:0.92 with its placeholder bars growing scaleX from 0 (transformOrigin 0 50%, expo.out, stagger 0.07). From 34% to 78% the .doc translates y to -(scrollHeight - viewport) with power2.inOut, and as sections enter the viewport the logo strip, h2, three feature cards (y:50, expo.out, stagger 0.12, icons scale in with back.out(2)) and a dark CTA band (y:60/scale:0.96) reveal in sequence. A white SVG arrow cursor flies in with power3.inOut from 68%, lands on the band button at 87% and both squash (scale 0.85/0.94 yoyo) as a click; the window then drops out with expo.in at 92%.
records.adapt: Change the URL, brand, headline lines, copy, CTA labels, the three feature titles/blurbs/icon colours and the band text; keep the 2.2s power2.inOut scroll, the expo.out block reveals and the cursor click beat. Cursor landing coordinates are absolute pixels and must be re-measured if the band moves.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the window/doc/cursor into el; animate(el, shot, D) measures scrollHeight - clientHeight, builds the same timeline with times as fractions of D (scroll 0.34-0.78, click at 0.87, exit 0.92) and returns it. Selectors must be scoped to el; reveal times are hand-placed rather than derived from layout, so keep them proportional.
caveats: cursor path uses hard-coded stage pixel coordinates (1100,700 -> 760,410 -> 900,590)
scroll distance measured at build time, fonts must be ready
window enters from below and exits below, so no loop

records.name: Minimalist Website
records.description: A minimal animated website template with refined transitions and careful use of space. Good for portfolio sites and design-forward product presentations.
records.move: rule draws, type rises line by line, image curtain unveils, reverses out
records.how: On an off-white stage a 1px horizontal rule scales scaleX 0 to 1 (expo.inOut, transform-origin left) over the first 22%. Nav items, three oversized headline lines (one word in italic serif), a three-line meta paragraph and an underlined link all rise through overflow masks with yPercent:110 expo.out and small staggers between 6% and 30%. A portrait image on the right unveils from clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) to inset(0 0 0% 0) over 10%-36% (expo.inOut) while the image inside settles from scale 1.25/yPercent:-6 to 1/0 (expo.out); during the hold it breathes yPercent:4 on sine.inOut and a small dot nudges x:6 yoyo. From 84% the image curtain closes upward (expo.in), every text line shoots up yPercent:-110 with expo.in, and the rule collapses to the right (transformOrigin 100% 50%).
records.adapt: Replace studio name, nav words, the three headline lines (keep one italic em), meta lines, link label, caption, index and the image; keep the 1.1s expo.inOut rule draw, the 1.3s clip-path unveil and the symmetric expo.in exit that make it feel restrained.
records.port: mount(el, shot) writes the nav/rule/h1/meta/img/idx/cap markup into el using shot strings; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with entrances at 0-0.36 of D, hold to 0.84, exit after. clipPath tweens and yPercent line masks port directly; scope selectors to el and preload the image.
caveats: clip-path inset tween on an element whose child is also scaled, two composited layers
borderColor from() tween relies on rgba string interpolation

records.name: Mountains: Animated Website [Dribbble]
records.description: A Dribbble-inspired animated website template with a dramatic mountain landscape. Good for travel brand presentations and editorial web design showcases.
records.move: mountain layers rise with parallax, sun lifts, title lands, layers sink
records.how: A sunset gradient sky with 60 seeded stars, a blurred radial sun and three SVG mountain silhouettes (front darker). The layers enter from y:160/240/320 (far to near) with expo.out over the first 32%, staggered 0.1s so the nearest arrives last; the sun rises from y:160/scale:0.6/opacity:0 (power3.out) and haze fades in, stars flicker in with a random-order stagger. Nav, two big uppercase headline lines (yPercent:110 line masks, expo.out, stagger 0.12), subtitle, pill CTA (back.out(1.6)) and three glass stat cards (y:60, expo.out, stagger 0.1, underline scaleX draws) land between 6% and 32%. From 20% to 100% the three layers drift x -20/25/-35 on sine.inOut for parallax, the sun keeps climbing y:-30, a small SVG bird flock crosses linearly from x:1000 to 640 and fades, cards bob y:-8 yoyo. Exit at 86%: headline shoots up, cards drop, the layers sink back into fog with expo.in (near first) and the sun sets with opacity 0.
records.adapt: Change brand, nav, the two headline words, subtitle, CTA labels and the three stat cards; recolour the sky gradient and the three mountain path fills, or replace the paths with your own silhouettes; keep the 1.6s expo.out layer rise with 0.1s stagger and the opposing sine drifts.
records.port: mount(el, shot) appends sky/stars (generated with fx.rng(7) or the engine's seeded rng)/sun/three SVG layers/birds/text/cards into el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with entrances in 0-0.32 of D, drifts spanning 0.2-1.0, exit from 0.86. All querySelector calls scoped to el.
caveats: stars are generated with fx.rng(7); port must use a seeded rng for determinism
backdrop-filter blur on three cards
layers enter from below and exit below but cards and stars fade differently, no clean loop

records.name: Website Promo
records.description: A website promo template with scroll reveals and layered screen motion. Works well for agency reels and client presentations where you want to bring a web design to life.
records.move: screen rises into 3D pose, stat cards fly in, scrolls, flies off
records.how: Four beats on a dark stage with perspective:1600px. 1) A masked title line rises (yPercent:110, expo.out) and a .cam wrapper carrying an 820x520 browser window comes up from y:520/rotateX:30/rotateY:-14/scale:0.9 to y:70/rotateX:14/rotateY:-12/scale:0.84 (expo.out) over 5%-21%, then nav, headline lines, copy and a gradient art block reveal inside. 2) At 29% the camera swings to rotateY:10/rotateX:8 (power3.inOut, 2s) while the title fades up and three white stat cards fly in from x:-300/rotateY:40, x:300/rotateY:-40 and y:200 (expo.out), their progress bars scaleX from 0 and avatars pop with back.out(2). 3) At 49%-73% the inner .doc scrolls y to -(scrollHeight - viewport) (power2.inOut) as feature cards and a CTA band rise into place; the floats drift opposite ways on sine.inOut and the camera counter-rotates gently. 4) At 78% the screen tilts to rotateX:40 and flies to y:-700 with expo.in, floats lift away, and an end card with a logo dot (scale 0/rotate -90, back.out(2)) fades in, then fades out at 96%.
records.adapt: Replace the promo title/subtitle, the site content inside the window (brand, headline, feature cards, band), the three stat cards and the end-card name/tagline; keep the four-beat structure and camera poses (rotateX/rotateY values), the 2.2s scroll and the expo.in fly-off. Colours live in .cta/.band/.art gradients.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the .cam wrapper, window, floats and end card inside el (el must have perspective and transform-style set); animate(el, shot, D) measures scrollHeight, builds the same timeline with beats at 0.05, 0.29, 0.49 and 0.78 of D and returns it. autoAlpha on .end and gsap.set must be scoped to el; the 3D transforms need the parent to keep perspective.
caveats: 9s effect with four distinct beats, longer than most
relies on parent perspective:1600px and transform-style:preserve-3d
scroll distance measured at build time from layout
multiple large box-shadows on 3D-rotated cards are paint heavy

records.name: Animated Bar Chart
records.description: An animated bar chart template where bars grow from the baseline with clean purposeful timing. Perfect for performance data presentations and metric showcases.
records.move: gridlines draw, bars grow staggered, values count up, bars collapse out
records.how: A white dashboard card on a grey stage with a title, a KPI counter and seven vertical bars (six indigo gradient, the last orange as highlight) built from data. The card rises from y:30/opacity:0 (power3.out) in the first 15%; four horizontal gridlines and the baseline draw with scaleX 0 to 1 from the left (expo.out, stagger 0.05) at 4-20%. Bars grow with scaleY 0 to 1 from transform-origin bottom (expo.out, 0.9s, stagger 0.09) starting at 10%, while each value label counts from 0 to its number in sync and the KPI counts to $459k (power2.out). At 50% the highlight bar breathes scaleY 1.04 yoyo. Exit from 78%: bars collapse scaleY to 0 with expo.in staggered from the end, labels fade, the card lifts out with y:-20.
records.adapt: Edit the data array (label, value, hi flag) and the card title/subtitle/KPI target; change bar gradients in .fill and .bar.hi .fill; keep the 0.9s expo.out grow with 0.09 stagger and the from-end expo.in collapse.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the card and generates .bar elements from shot.data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with entrances at 0-0.3 of D, breath at 0.5, exit at 0.78-0.9; counters are plain object tweens with onUpdate writing textContent, which port directly. All getElementById calls must become el.querySelector.
caveats: from() tweens with stagger on generated elements need the DOM built before animate
uses getElementById for kpi and bars, must be scoped

records.name: Animated Donut Chart
records.description: A standard animated donut chart template that fills its ring with smooth motion. Good for progress indicators and data visualization UI.
records.move: donut track draws, arc fills to 72% with counter, pulses, unwinds
records.how: A white card holds a 300px SVG donut (grey track circle plus a blue round-capped arc, rotated -90deg) with a big percentage in the centre and a text panel with two legend rows on the right. The card scales in from 0.92/opacity:0 (power3.out) in the first 15%; the track draws around with DrawSVG 0% to 100% (expo.out) at 2-22%; the arc fills drawSVG 0% to 72% over 9-46% with expo.inOut while a tween on a plain object drives the centre percent and the Used/Available GB numbers in lockstep. Heading, paragraph and rows slide up y:14 with stagger 0.08. At 52% the arc stroke-width pulses 26 to 30 yoyo (sine.inOut). At 78% the arc unwinds to 0% and the numbers count back down with expo.in, then the card fades out with a slight scale 0.96.
records.adapt: Set TARGET (percent), the centre caption, heading/paragraph and the legend labels and the 512 GB capacity math; change the arc colour in .arc and .dot; keep the 1.5s expo.inOut fill and the symmetric expo.in unwind.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts the card with the SVG circles (r=130, stroke-width 26) and the text panel; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with fill at 0.09-0.46 of D, pulse at 0.52, unwind at 0.78. Needs DrawSVGPlugin registered; the second counter tween reuses the first tween's onUpdate via tl.getTweensOf(o)[0].vars.onUpdate, which is simpler as a named function. Scope getElementById to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
arc unwinds and card fades so the last frame differs from the first (card exits, then would pop back)

records.name: Animated Donut Chart: Black
records.description: A black-themed animated donut chart template. Ideal for dark mode dashboards and analytics UI where aesthetic restraint is important.
records.move: ticks flicker in, white arc draws on black, ticks rotate, arc unwinds
records.how: On a pure black stage a 360px SVG ring: 60 thin tick marks (every fifth longer) generated in a circle, a dark grey track and a flat-capped white arc, rotated -90deg, with an 84pt percentage in the centre and a side panel of label, heading, a rule and three metric rows. Ticks flicker in one by one (opacity from 0, stagger 0.012) over the first 18%; the track draws with DrawSVG expo.out at 2-25%; the arc fills drawSVG 0% to 84% over 10-50% with expo.inOut while a counter drives the percent and the 'x / 128 services' rows. Side text rises y:16 (power3.out, stagger 0.1), the rule scales scaleX from 0, rows slide in. Hold at 50-85%: the tick group rotates 6deg on sine.inOut. From 78% the arc unwinds to 0% and the counter returns to 0 with expo.in, side text fades up, track and ticks fade.
records.adapt: Set T (percent) and the 128-item total in upd(), the label/heading/rows; recolour the arc and track for a non-black theme; change the 60 tick count or lengths in the generator loop; keep the 1.6s expo.inOut fill and the slow 6deg tick rotation.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the SVG, generates the 60 tick lines into the ticks group and the side panel; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with fill at 0.1-0.5 of D, rotation at 0.5-0.85, unwind at 0.78. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; the #ticks id and getElementById calls must be scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
60 individual tick from() tweens with tiny stagger
everything fades to black at the end, which is close to but not identical to the first frame

records.name: Animated Line Chart: Blue
records.description: A blue-themed animated line chart template that draws itself across the frame. Good for growth metric presentations and analytics dashboards.
records.move: line draws left to right with tracking dot, tooltip and area fill
records.how: A white card with title, KPI and a 884x356 SVG plot whose 12 monthly values are turned into a smooth cubic bezier path, an area path with a vertical blue gradient, five gridlines and month/value labels. The card rises y:30 (power3.out); gridlines scale in scaleX from the left (expo.out, stagger 0.05) at 4-22%; axis labels fade with stagger 0.02. From 12% to 57% the line draws with DrawSVG 0% to 100% (power2.inOut) while a synced object tween moves a white dot with a translucent halo along line.getPointAtLength, widens a clipPath rect so the area fill reveals under the line, and positions an HTML tooltip and the KPI text from the current y value. At 59% the halo expands r 10 to 22 and fades twice as a ping. Exit from 82%: tooltip and dot fade, the line retracts to its end (drawSVG '100% 100%', expo.in) and the clip rect shrinks to 0, then the card lifts out.
records.adapt: Replace the vals array, max, month letters and title/subtitle/KPI badge; change #2563eb in .line, .dot, .halo and the gradient stops; keep the 1.8s power2.inOut draw and the synced dot tween, which must share the same ease so the dot stays on the line tip.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and SVG, computes the bezier path and area from shot.values, and generates grid/labels; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with draw at 0.12-0.57 of D and retract at 0.82. The upd() function reads plot.clientWidth/clientHeight to position the HTML tooltip, so it must be called after layout; ids (#line, #clip, #ga, #cr) must be unique per instance and getElementById scoped to el. Requires DrawSVGPlugin.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
getPointAtLength and clientWidth measured on every update, layout dependent
SVG ids (clip, ga) collide if two instances mount on one page
line retracts and card fades out, no seamless loop

records.name: Animated Line Chart: Purple
records.description: A purple-themed animated line chart template. Good for analytics presentations and data visualization content where the standard blue feels too expected.
records.move: two lines draw on dark glass, scan line follows, markers pop, retract
records.how: A dark purple stage with a huge blurred radial glow behind a frosted glass card (backdrop-filter, 1px border). Inside a 904x374 SVG: dashed gridlines, week labels, a dashed muted 'last year' line, a glowing lavender 'this year' line (drop-shadow filter) with a gradient area under it and 12 circle markers. Card and glow enter in the first 15% (card y:30 power3.out, glow scale 0.6 to 1 power2.out); gridlines draw with DrawSVG expo.out (stagger 0.05) at 4-25%; labels fade in. The dashed line draws 0 to 100% from 12% (power2.inOut, 1.6s) and the glowing line from 15% over 1.8s, with a synced object tween that widens a clipPath rect to reveal the area and drags a vertical scan line along line.getPointAtLength; markers pop scale 0 to 1 with back.out(3) staggered 0.14 as the line passes. During the hold the glow drifts x:60 yoyo on sine.inOut and the scan line fades. Exit at 80%: markers shrink from the end, both lines retract to '100% 100%' (expo.in), the clip rect closes, the card lifts out.
records.adapt: Replace arrays a and b, max, week labels, title/subtitle/legend text; change #c084fc and #5b3a86 in .l1/.l2/.mk/.legend and the gradient; keep the two staggered draw starts (dashed line 0.1s ahead) and the synced scan tween with the same power2.inOut ease as the line.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the glow, card and SVG, computes both bezier paths and the area from shot.series, generates grid/labels/markers; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with draws at 0.12-0.6 of D and retract at 0.8. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; SVG ids (gp, clip, cr, scan, l1, l2) must be unique per instance; getElementById scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
900px filter: blur(40px) glow plus backdrop-filter and an SVG drop-shadow filter on the line, expensive per frame
SVG ids collide if two instances mount
lines retract and card fades, no seamless loop

records.name: Bar Chart: Skyline
records.description: A chart with bars that rise and settle. Great for animated data stories, dashboards, and stat reveals.
records.move: city bars rise centre-out with overshoot under a sun, drop away
records.how: A night-gradient stage with a blurred orange sun and ten tall bars (alternating blue gradients, a dotted window pattern via ::after) standing on a thin ground line like a skyline. Title, subtitle and total counter slide up y:20 (power3.out, stagger 0.1) and the sun rises from y:180/opacity:0 (power2.out, 1.4s) from frame 0; the ground line scales scaleX from 0 (expo.out). From 9% the bars rise with scaleY 0 to 1 using back.out(1.6) so they overshoot and settle, staggered 0.07 outward from the centre; city labels and value counters follow with the same centre-out stagger, each value counting to its number with power3.out, while the total counts to 6,980 (power2.out) over 12-52%. Hold: the sun keeps drifting y:-30 on sine.inOut. Exit at 79%: bars collapse scaleY to 0 with expo.in staggered from the edges inward, labels fade, then title/stat/ground/sun fade out.
records.adapt: Edit the data array of [label, height%] pairs (any count) and the title/subtitle/total; change the bar gradients in .b and .bar:nth-child(odd) .b and the sun colours; keep back.out(1.6) with the from:'center' stagger for the rise and from:'edges' for the collapse.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds sun/title/stat/ground and generates .bar elements from shot.data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the rise at 0.09-0.5 of D and collapse at 0.79. Counter tweens are object tweens with onUpdate; getElementById for #tot and #bars must be scoped to el.
caveats: value counters are timed by distance from centre (Math.abs(i-4.5)) which assumes ten bars
sun and title fade to nothing at the end, close to the first frame but the sun starts lower

records.name: Bar Chart: Sleep Tracker
records.description: An animated bar chart template built around sleep tracking data. Good for health app UI demos and wellness product showcases.
records.move: phone rises, sleep stacks build bottom to top, counters tick, collapse
records.how: Portrait 1080x1920: a dark phone frame with notch rises from y:80/opacity:0 (power3.out) over the first 16%; the header, hero time readout and delta slide up y:24 with stagger 0.1. Two gridlines scale in scaleX from the left (expo.out), day letters fade in. From 16% each of seven days builds its stack: the deep segment grows scaleY from 0 at the baseline (expo.out, 0.6s), then core 0.1s later and REM 0.2s later, each starting translated down by the height of the segments beneath it (y from a function reading offsetHeight) so the stack appears to extrude upward; days are staggered 0.12. An object tween from 18% to 50% counts hours/minutes, deep-sleep percent and score (power2.out); legend chips and two stat cards slide in. At 56% today's bar breathes scaleY 1.03 yoyo. Exit at 83%: all segments collapse scaleY to 0 with expo.in staggered from the end, then the phone lifts out y:-60.
records.adapt: Edit the days array (letter, deep, core, rem hours) and the three segment colours in .seg.deep/.core/.rem and the legend --c values; set the hero numbers in the counter tween (h, m, p, s); keep the 0.1s segment cascade and 0.12 day stagger. Layout is portrait, change the phone size for 16:9.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the phone and generates .day stacks from shot.days; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with stack builds at 0.16-0.4 of D and collapse at 0.83. The y function values read offsetHeight and must be evaluated after layout (GSAP function-based values do this at tween creation, so build the timeline after mount is laid out). getElementById calls scoped to el.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920, not 1280x720
segment offsets are function-based values read from offsetHeight at build time, so fonts and layout must be settled
phone enters from below and exits upward, no loop

records.name: Donut Chart: 3 Parts
records.description: An animated donut chart template with three segments that fill in sequence. Good for percentage breakdowns and category comparisons.
records.move: three donut segments draw end to end, ring rotates, slice pops, unwinds
records.how: A 380px SVG donut of three stroked circles (orange, blue, black, stroke-width 44, rotated -90deg) with a percent counter in the centre and a legend of three rows on the right. The ring scales in from 0.8/opacity:0 (power3.out) in the first 15%. Segment one draws with DrawSVG '0% 0%' to '0% 46%' at 10-30% (power3.inOut), segment two continues from 46% to 78% at 29-46%, segment three from 78% to 100% at 45-60%, each with its legend row sliding in x:20 and the centre counter and row percentages filling in lockstep via an object tween with the same ease. Hold at 60-90%: the whole SVG rotates from -90 to -80deg (power2.inOut) while the largest segment pops outward (attr r 150 to 158, strokeWidth 44 to 52, back.out(2)) then returns. From 82% all segments unwind to '0% 0%' with expo.in (stagger 0.05), the counter returns to 0, legend and centre fade, the SVG rotates back to -90.
records.adapt: Set V (three values summing to 100) and mirror them in the drawSVG ranges and data-v attributes; change stroke colours in .s1/.s2/.s3 and the legend swatches; set the heading and row labels; keep the sequential power3.inOut segment timing and the back.out(2) pop on the largest slice.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the ring with three circles and the legend from shot.segments; animate(el, shot, D) computes cumulative drawSVG ranges from the values, returns the same timeline with segments at 0.1-0.6 of D, pop at 0.62, unwind at 0.82. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; the 'svg' selector and getElementById must be scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
drawSVG ranges are hard-coded to match V and must be regenerated if values change
rotate tween on the svg element overrides the CSS rotate(-90deg) transform, so start values must be -90

records.name: Grid Chart: Split
records.description: A multi-panel layout that splits and populates with content. Great for comparisons, category breakdowns, and before/after quadrant views.
records.move: one panel splits into a 2x2 grid, quadrants populate, folds back
records.how: Four dark KPI panels in a 2x2 CSS grid on a near-black stage; at start panels 2-4 are pre-set with gsap.set to x:-527/y:-307 and scaleX/scaleY 0 (transform-origin top-left) so they hide under panel 1, which is scaled 2.03x2.02 to cover the whole grid. Panel 1 fades in (power3.out) and the grid scales from 0.92 in the first 13%; at 12-35% panel 1 scales to 1 while the other three tween to x:0/y:0/scale 1 with expo.inOut so the block visibly splits along both seams. From 25% each quadrant populates: labels and values slide up (stagger 0.03), mini bars grow scaleY from 0 (expo.out, stagger 0.04), a sparkline draws with DrawSVG (power2.inOut), two progress fills scale scaleX from 0, and an object tween counts four numbers with power3.out. Exit at 82%: the three panels collapse back to their hidden positions and panel 1 re-scales to 2.03 with expo.in, then the grid fades with a 0.96 scale.
records.adapt: Change the four panel labels, values (targets in the counter tween), deltas, mini bar heights, sparkline path and progress widths; recolour the accent panel (.p:nth-child(1)) and series colours; keep the 0.7s expo.inOut split and the symmetric expo.in fold. The -527/-307 offsets equal panel width/height plus gap and must be recomputed if the grid resizes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the .grid with four .p panels; animate(el, shot, D) measures panel width/height and gap to compute the hide offsets, applies gsap.set, returns the same timeline with split at 0.12-0.35 of D and fold at 0.82. The counter writes to bare ids v1-v4 via window globals, which must become el.querySelector references; requires DrawSVGPlugin.
caveats: offsets -527/-307 and scale 2.03/2.02 are hard-coded to a 1040x600 grid with 14px gap
counter onUpdate uses implicit window.v1..v4 globals from element ids
requires DrawSVGPlugin for the sparkline
3s duration, tighter than the family

records.name: Horizontal Bar Chart: Metrics
records.description: Horizontal bars that slide in and expand to show off your metrics. A great animated chart for leaderboards, rankings, and side-by-side stat comparisons.
records.move: ranked rows slide in, bars expand with counters, sheen sweeps, retract
records.how: A white leaderboard card with six rows built from data: rank, coloured initial avatar, name, a grey track with a coloured fill sized to the value, and a number. The card rises y:30 (power3.out) and the heading slides up. From 7% rows slide in from x:-80/opacity:0 with expo.out staggered 0.09; the grey tracks scale scaleX from 0 (left origin) 0.1s later, then each fill expands scaleX 0 to 1 over 1s with expo.out (stagger 0.09) starting at 15% while a per-row counter ticks to its value with the same ease. Hold at 50%: a CSS sheen (a translucent white gradient ::after positioned by a --sheen custom property) sweeps left to right across each bar via an object tween from -100% to 300% (power2.inOut, stagger 0.06). Exit at 79%: fills collapse scaleX to 0 with expo.in staggered from the last row, numbers fade, rows slide back out x:-60 from the bottom up, card fades.
records.adapt: Edit the data array of [name, initials, value, colour] (any row count) and the heading; the max value (128) normalises widths and must match the top row; keep the expo.out row-then-bar cascade and the sheen sweep in the hold.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and generates .row elements from shot.rows; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with rows at 0.07-0.4 of D, sheen at 0.5, collapse at 0.79. The sheen is driven by setting a CSS custom property in onUpdate, which ports directly; getElementById and querySelectorAll must be scoped to el.
caveats: sheen relies on a ::after pseudo-element reading a --sheen custom property
from() tweens on generated rows need the DOM built before the timeline

records.name: Line Chart: User Acquisition
records.description: An animated line chart template showing user acquisition growth over time. Good for growth metric showcases and investor pitch content.
records.move: growth line draws with a glowing head, milestone flags pop, area fills
records.how: A dark full-bleed stage with eyebrow, title and a big total counter top-right, over a 1120x460 SVG plot: five gridlines, month labels, a smooth green bezier line built from 18 values, an area under it with a vertical green gradient revealed by a clipPath rect, three milestone groups (rounded label box, text, circle) and a green head circle. Text slides up y:20 (power3.out, stagger 0.1) from frame 0; gridlines draw with DrawSVG expo.out (stagger 0.05) at 4-20%. From 12% to 60% the line draws 0 to 100% with power1.inOut while a synced object tween moves the head along line.getPointAtLength, widens the clip rect so the area fills behind, and counts the total to 72,400. Each milestone pops scale 0 to 1 with back.out(2.5) at the moment the line reaches its x. At 60% the head swells r 8 to 14 and fades; milestones bob y:-4 yoyo. Exit at 84%: milestones shrink, the line retracts to its end (drawSVG '100% 100%', expo.in), the clip closes, everything fades.
records.adapt: Replace vals (any length), max, the month labels, the miles array of [index, label] and the title/eyebrow/total; change #34d399 in .line/.head/.ms and the gradient; keep the 2.4s power1.inOut draw and the milestone timing derived from index/17.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the header, SVG, path, area, grid, labels and milestone groups from shot data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with draw at 0.12-0.6 of D and milestone times computed from their index fraction, retract at 0.84. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; SVG ids (g, c, cr, line, head, ms) must be unique per instance; getElementById scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
milestone timing uses index/17 and a 0.92 fudge, assumes 18 points
SVG gradient/clipPath ids collide across instances
line retracts and stage fades, no loop

records.name: Multiple Bar Chart
records.description: A template with multiple animated bar chart series building simultaneously. Good for comparative data presentations and dashboard UI demos.
records.move: grouped bars of three series grow together, groups cascade, wave, collapse
records.how: A white card with title, subtitle, a three-swatch legend and a plot of six quarter groups, each holding three bars (dark, blue, lavender) sized by data. The card rises y:30 (power3.out); title/legend slide up (stagger 0.07); three gridlines and the baseline scale scaleX from the left (expo.out, stagger 0.05) at 5-22%; quarter labels fade. From 12% the bars grow scaleY 0 to 1 with expo.out over 1s: series 0 across all groups with stagger 0.08, series 1 starting 0.08s later and series 2 another 0.08s later, so each group builds left to right while the groups cascade, all three series rising at once. Hold at 52%: a wave lifts each group y:-8 yoyo (sine.inOut, stagger 0.08). Exit at 79%: all bars collapse scaleY to 0 with expo.in staggered 0.02 from the end, labels fade, card lifts out.
records.adapt: Edit the data array of [label, [v0, v1, v2]] groups and the C colour array (mirrored in the legend --c values), title and gridline labels; keep the 1s expo.out grow with the 0.08 group and series offsets and the from-end collapse.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and generates .g groups with .b.sN bars from shot.data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with grows at 0.12-0.5 of D, wave at 0.52, collapse at 0.79. Series selectors (.b.s0 etc.) must be scoped to el.
caveats: bar heights are inline percentages, values above 100 overflow
card exits upward, no loop

records.name: Multiple Line Chart: Green
records.description: A template with multiple green line chart series drawn simultaneously. Works great for comparative data trends and financial performance showcases.
records.move: three green lines draw at different speeds, end markers pop, lead pulses
records.how: A dark green full-bleed stage with title, subtitle and a three-line legend above a 1120x480 SVG. Three series are generated as seeded random walks (fx.rng(7)) and turned into smooth bezier paths: a bright glowing 'Growth' line (drop-shadow filter), a darker 'Balanced' line and a pale 'Income' line, plus a circle-and-value end marker per line. Header text slides up y:16 (power3.out, stagger 0.08) from 0; six gridlines draw with DrawSVG expo.out (stagger 0.04) at 4-25%; labels fade. From 12% all three lines draw 0 to 100% with power2.inOut, durations 2.0/1.9/1.8s so the lead line finishes first. End markers pop scale 0 to 1 with back.out(2.5) (stagger 0.06) at 56%. Hold: the lead line pulses stroke-width 3.5 to 5 yoyo (sine.inOut) at 65%. Exit at 80%: markers shrink, lines retract to their end (drawSVG '100% 100%', expo.in, stagger 0.04), everything fades.
records.adapt: Replace the walk() calls with real series arrays (13 points) and set min/max, the month letters, title/subtitle/legend and the three greens in .ln.a/.b/.c and legend --c; keep the simultaneous power2.inOut draws with the 0.1s speed difference and the back.out end-marker pop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the header and SVG, computes the three paths and end markers from shot.series, generates grid/labels; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with draws at 0.12-0.62 of D and retract at 0.8. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; ids (pa, pb, pc, grid, ends) must be scoped to el or made unique; the seeded rng only matters if series are generated rather than supplied.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
series values come from fx.rng(7) random walks, not real data
SVG drop-shadow filter on the lead line, moderate cost
lines retract and stage fades, no loop

records.name: Stacked Bar Chart
records.description: An animated stacked bar chart template showing multiple data series building together. Good for comparative analytics and business intelligence presentations.
records.move: stacked bars build segment on segment, totals count, stacks collapse
records.how: A white card with title, subtitle, three-swatch legend, four gridlines, baseline and eight monthly stacks of three segments (dark subscriptions at the bottom, light orange services, orange hardware on top) with a total label above each. The card rises y:30 (power3.out); header slides up; gridlines and baseline scale scaleX from the left (expo.out, stagger 0.05) at 5-22%; month labels fade. From 12% each bar builds in turn (stagger 0.09): the bottom segment grows scaleY 0 to 1 with expo.out over 0.8s, the middle segment 0.12s later starting translated down by the bottom's offsetHeight, the top segment 0.24s later offset by both, so the stack visibly extrudes upward; the total fades up y:10 and counts to its sum with expo.out. Hold at 57%: the middle segments dim to opacity 0.7 yoyo (sine.inOut, stagger 0.05). Exit at 79%: all segments collapse scaleY to 0 with expo.in staggered 0.015 from the end, labels fade, card lifts.
records.adapt: Edit the data array of [label, [bottom, middle, top]] and the C colour array mirrored in the legend --c values, plus the gridline labels (heights are value/2 percent, so max is 200); keep the 0.12s segment cascade and 0.09 bar stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and generates .bar stacks from shot.data; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with builds at 0.12-0.5 of D, dim at 0.57, collapse at 0.79. The function-based y offsets read offsetHeight at tween creation, so the timeline must be built after layout; getElementById scoped to el.
caveats: segment offsets are function-based values read from offsetHeight at build time, so fonts and layout must be settled
heights assume a max of 200 (value/2 percent)
card exits upward, no loop

records.name: Stacked Chart: Cascade
records.description: Chart layers that cascade into place one after another. Great for building anticipation around data reveals and layered metrics.
records.move: stacked area layers rise one after another with overshoot, sink back
records.how: A dark stage with title and subtitle, a right-aligned legend column and a 1120x440 SVG holding six gridlines, week labels and four stacked area paths (orange organic, pink paid, purple referral, green direct) built by stacking smooth bezier curves on top of each other, each stroked with the background colour to separate layers. Header slides up y:20 (power3.out); gridlines scale scaleX from the left (expo.out, stagger 0.04) at 4-25%; labels fade. From 12% the layers rise with scaleY 0 to 1 about the baseline (transform-origin at base y) using back.out(1.2) over 0.9s with a 0.28s stagger so each layer lands with a slight overshoot before the next begins; legend rows slide in x:24 in step. Hold at 55%: the stack breathes scaleY 1.02 yoyo (sine.inOut, stagger 0.05). Exit at 80%: layers sink scaleY to 0 with expo.in staggered 0.08 from the top layer down, legend rows slide out, all fades.
records.adapt: Edit the series array of [name, colour, 12 values] (any count of layers) and max, title/subtitle; keep the 0.9s back.out(1.2) rise with 0.28 stagger, which is the cascade feel, and the from-end expo.in sink.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds header, legend and SVG, stacks the series into area paths with transformOrigin at the baseline; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with layer rises at 0.12-0.55 of D, breath at 0.55, sink at 0.8. getElementById calls scoped to el; no plugins needed.
caveats: scaleY about a pixel transform-origin set via inline style on SVG paths
fx.rng(11) is declared but unused
stage fades to black at the end, no loop

records.name: Stacked Donut Chart
records.description: A template with multiple donut chart rings stacked and animated in sequence. Good for multi-category data visualization and analytics UI presentations.
records.move: concentric donut rings fill outer to inner, rotate together, unwind
records.how: On a near-black stage a 420px SVG holds three concentric faint track circles (r 190/152/114) and three round-capped coloured arcs (red, amber, blue, stroke-width 26) rotated -90deg, with an average-completion percent in the centre and a side legend of three rows. The ring scales in from 0.85/opacity:0 (power3.out) in the first 15%; tracks draw with DrawSVG expo.out staggered 0.1 at 2-25%. The outer arc fills drawSVG 0% to 88% at 12-40% (power3.inOut, 1.1s), the middle to 64% at 24-49%, the inner to 42% at 35-57%, each overlapping the previous slightly; an object tween drives the row percentages and the centre average in lockstep, and each legend row slides in x:20 as its ring starts. Hold at 57%: the whole SVG rotates from -90 to -70deg on sine.inOut. Exit at 80%: arcs unwind to 0% with expo.in (stagger 0.06), counters return to 0, side and centre fade, the SVG rotates back to -90, tracks fade.
records.adapt: Set V (three percentages) and mirror in data-v attributes, the row labels, heading and centre caption; change the three stroke colours on the arc circles and the row --c values; keep the outer-to-inner power3.inOut sequence with 0.45s offsets and the 20deg hold rotation.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the ring with track and arc circles and the legend rows from shot.rings; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with fills at 0.12-0.57 of D, rotation at 0.57, unwind at 0.8. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; the 'svg' selector, querySelectorAll('.it') and getElementById must be scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
rotate tween on the svg element overrides the CSS rotate(-90deg), start value must be -90
tracks fade out at the end, not identical to the first frame

records.name: 5 Stars: Move Up
records.description: An animated five-star rating template where stars rise into frame. Good for rating reveals and customer feedback showcases.
records.move: stars rise through a mask with overshoot, fills pop, exit upward
records.how: On a dark stage with a soft gold radial glow, five outlined SVG stars sit in a 120px-tall overflow-hidden row above a score line. The glow scales in from 0.6/opacity:0 (power2.out) over the first 40%. Each star rises from y:150 and rotation:-12 with back.out(1.6) over 0.8s, staggered 0.1 from frame 0, so they emerge one by one from behind the bottom edge; 14% in, each fill pops from scale:0 with back.out(2.2) (stagger 0.1) while the outline stroke colour cross-fades from gold to dull brown. The '4.9' score and review count rise through their own masks with y:80 expo.out at 25% and 28%. Exit at 78%: stars continue upward y:-160 with power3.in (stagger 0.06), then score and count lift out and the glow fades.
records.adapt: Change the score, review count, star fill (#ffc83d) and outline colours and the glow tint; the star count is the loop limit; keep the 0.8s back.out(1.6) rise with 0.1 stagger and the through-the-top exit.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the glow, generates five star SVGs into a masked row and adds the score line; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with rises at 0-0.27 of D, fills at 0.14, exit at 0.78. The star path P is a constant; selectors must be scoped to el. No plugins needed.
caveats: overflow:hidden rows with fixed heights act as the masks, so row heights must match the font sizes
stars exit upward and never return, no loop

records.name: 5 Stars: Pop
records.description: An animated five-star rating template where stars pop into view with a burst effect. Good for testimonial highlights and customer feedback content.
records.move: stars pop in elastic with ray bursts, quote rises, stars shrink out
records.how: On a cream stage five 110px star cells each hold a burst SVG (eight rays and eight dots arranged radially) beneath an orange star path. From 5% each star, staggered 0.18s, scales from 0 and rotation -40 to full with elastic.out(1,0.45) over 0.6s; at the same instant its rays scale from 0 to 1.6 about the centre and fade (power3.out, 0.5s) and its dots scale 0.3 to 2.2 and fade (power2.out), reading as a firework burst around the landing star. A quote line rises y:30/opacity:0 with expo.out at 38%. Exit at 80%: fills shrink to 0 with back.in(2) staggered 0.06 from the last star, the quote lifts out.
records.adapt: Change the quote text, star fill (#ff9f1c), ray (#ff6b35) and dot (#ffd166) colours and the ray count in the inner loop; keep the 0.18 stagger with elastic.out(1,0.45) and the simultaneous burst.
records.port: mount(el, shot) generates the five star cells with burst SVGs and the label into el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with pops at 0.05-0.4 of D, label at 0.38, exit at 0.8. Per-star querySelector calls are already element-scoped; only the initial toArray('.star') must be scoped to el.
caveats: rays and dots use transformOrigin '0 0' inside a centred viewBox, so the SVG viewBox must stay centred on 0,0
stars shrink to nothing at the end; start and end frames match apart from the label

records.name: Adobe After Effects Logo
records.description: An animated After Effects logo template. Good for motion design tutorials and animation content where the logo should reflect the craft.
records.move: tile outline draws and fills, letters slide in, keyframe rides ease curve
records.how: A dark stage with three faint horizontal grid lines and a 820x380 SVG bezier ease curve behind a 300px rounded tile in After Effects navy with lavender 'Ae' letters. Grid lines scale in scaleX from centre (expo.out, stagger 0.08) from frame 0; the tile's rounded-rect outline draws itself with DrawSVG 0 to 100% over 2-27% (power2.inOut), then the tile background and box-shadow fade in from transparent at 22%. The 'A' drops in from yPercent:-230 and the 'e' rises from yPercent:230 (expo.out) at 27% and 30%, then the pair settles from scaleY 0.8/scaleX 1.1 with elastic.out(1,0.5). From 32% to 72% the ease curve draws with DrawSVG (power1.inOut) while a white diamond keyframe rides it via MotionPath with the same ease, scaling in at the start and out at the end. Exit at 82%: letters shoot up, the tile shrinks to 0.6 and fades, curve and grid fade.
records.adapt: Change the two letters, the tile background (#00005b), accent colour (#9999ff) and the ease-curve path; keep the outline-draw-then-fill sequence and the synced curve draw and keyframe ride with matching power1.inOut eases.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts the curve SVG and the tile with frame SVG and letter spans; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the draw at 0.02-0.27 of D, letters at 0.27, curve ride at 0.32-0.72, exit at 0.82. Requires DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin; the motionPath path selector '.ease' must be an element reference scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin
stylised Ae tile in Atlas Grotesk, not the official Adobe mark
from() tweens on backgroundColor and boxShadow interpolate rgba strings

records.name: Adobe Illustrator Logo
records.description: An animated Adobe Illustrator logo template. Good for design process videos and Adobe tool presentations.
records.move: pen tool traces letter outlines dropping anchors, fill floods in
records.how: A 300px dark-red rounded tile scales in from 0.7 (expo.out) in the first 17%. Two stacked SVGs hold an orange 'Ai' as fills (hidden) and as strokes. From 7% to 40% the 'A' outer outline draws with DrawSVG (power1.inOut, 1.3s) while a small white pen-tool cursor follows the same path via MotionPath; six white anchor circles pop in scale 0 with back.out(3) staggered 0.14 as the pen passes, and two bezier handles draw outward from their midpoints ('50% 50%' to full). The inner triangle then draws at 40-51%, the 'i' stem at 51-64% (pen following each), the pen hides and the dot draws at 60%. At 69% the fills fade in and settle from scale 0.94 with elastic.out(1,0.5) while anchors and strokes fade out, reading as a flood fill. Exit at 89%: the tile shrinks to 0.7 and fades.
records.adapt: Replace the letter paths (fills and strokes must be the same geometry) and anchor/handle coordinates, the tile background (#330000) and accent (#ff9a00); keep the pen-follows-stroke pairing with identical durations and eases and the flood at the end.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the tile with fills, strokes, anchors and pen SVGs; animate(el, shot, D) applies gsap.set for hidden fills/pen and returns the same timeline with traces at 0.07-0.64 of D, flood at 0.69, exit at 0.89. Requires DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin; motionPath path selectors ('.pA', '.pA2', '.pI') must be element references scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin
stylised Ai letterforms drawn as paths, not the official Adobe mark
anchor stagger timing is hand-matched to the pen speed and drifts if the path changes

records.name: Adobe Photoshop Logo
records.description: An animated Photoshop logo template. Good for creative software showcases and Adobe-themed content.
records.move: layer frames fly in and collapse into tile, brush stroke paints letters
records.how: Three translucent bordered rounded squares (layers) fly in from top-left (x:-420, rotation -18), top-right (x:420, rotation 14) and below (y:300) with expo.out over the first 26%, staggered 0.12, then each scales down from 1.35/1.22/1.1 to 1 with expo.inOut at 22-37% so they stack into one. The solid Photoshop-blue tile fades and scales in from 0.9 at 30% while the layer frames fade out. Inside the tile a 'Ps' text is masked by a zig-zag path with a 90px-wide round-capped white stroke; the stroke draws with DrawSVG 0 to 100% (power2.inOut, 1.1s) from 36% so the letters appear painted on by three horizontal brush passes. Three colour swatches pop in scale 0/rotation 90 with back.out(2) (stagger 0.12) at 42% and bob y:-14 yoyo on sine.inOut. Exit at 87%: swatches shrink with back.in(2), the tile scales to 0.7 and fades.
records.adapt: Change the letters in the masked text, tile colour (#001e36), accent (#31a8ff) and swatch colours/positions; keep the three-direction layer arrival with its scale collapse and the 1.1s brush reveal. The zig-zag mask path must cover the text bounds.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts the layer frames, the tile with mask-defs SVG and the swatches; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with layers at 0-0.37 of D, brush at 0.36-0.64, exit at 0.87. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; the mask id must be unique per instance; swatch positions are absolute stage pixels and should be relative to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
SVG mask id 'm' collides across instances
swatch positions are hard-coded stage pixel coordinates
stylised Ps tile, not the official Adobe mark

records.name: Adobe Premiere Pro Logo
records.description: An animated Adobe Premiere Pro logo template with a smooth reveal. Good for video editing content and Adobe workflow presentations.
records.move: playhead scrubs across timeline, wipes tile in behind it, scrubs back
records.how: A dark stage with a 300px purple 'Pr' tile above an 820px timeline track holding three coloured clips and a time ruler, plus a white glowing playhead line with a triangle head. The track scales in scaleX from the left (expo.out) over the first 17%, ruler labels fade up. From 9% to 59% the playhead moves x -410 to 410 (power2.inOut, 2s) while the tile's clip-path tweens from inset(0 100% 0 0 round 56px) to inset(0 0% 0 0 round 56px) with the same ease so its revealed edge stays locked to the playhead; the three clips slide in xPercent:-120 with expo.out staggered 0.5 as the head passes. At 57% the tile settles from scale 0.96 with elastic.out(1,0.5). Exit at 80%: playhead scrubs back to -410 with power3.in while the clip-path closes again, clips slide out, track and ruler fade.
records.adapt: Change the tile letters and colours (#2a0038, #ea77ff), the clip widths/colours and ruler labels; keep the playhead and clip-path sharing the same 2s power2.inOut so the reveal edge tracks the head. The x range of +/-410 equals half the track width.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds tile, track with clips, ruler and playhead; animate(el, shot, D) applies gsap.set(head, {x:-half}) using the measured track width, returns the same timeline with scrub at 0.09-0.59 of D and scrub-back at 0.8. Selectors scoped to el; no plugins.
caveats: clip-path inset with 'round 56px' interpolates as a string, both ends must have identical shape
playhead x range hard-coded to a 820px track
ends with the tile hidden again so first and last frames roughly match apart from the faded track

records.name: Adobe XD Logo
records.description: An animated Adobe XD logo template with clean motion. Good for design tool content and Adobe-related tutorials and presentations.
records.move: tile Y-swings in, X draws, wires connect artboards, swings out
records.how: A dark magenta stage with perspective:1200px; a 300px XD-purple tile turns in from rotationY:-95/x:-80/opacity:0 (expo.out) over the first 25%. Inside, the two diagonal strokes of the 'X' draw with DrawSVG: the first 0 to 100% at 14%, the second from its far end ('100% 100%' to '0% 100%') at 17%, then the 'd' slides in from x:60 (expo.out) at 24%. Two wireframe artboards scale in from 0.6 with back.out(1.8) (stagger 0.15) at 30%, a start node pops with back.out(3), a dashed wire draws from the left artboard into the tile (power2.inOut) at 40% and a second wire from the tile to the right artboard at 54%, ending with a second node pop. Meanwhile the tile eases to rotationY:14/rotationX:-6 on sine.inOut over 35-75%. Exit at 81%: wires retract to their ends, nodes and artboards shrink and fade, the tile swings out to rotationY:95/x:80.
records.adapt: Change the tile letters/strokes and colours (#470137, #ff61f6), the artboard positions and the two wire paths (which must start and end at the artboards); keep the rotationY swing-in/out and the sequential wire draws.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts artboards, the full-frame wire SVG and the tile inside el (el needs perspective); animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with swing-in 0-0.25, wires 0.4-0.68, exit 0.81 of D. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; wire coordinates are in a 1280x720 viewBox and must be recomputed if el is a different size.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
wire SVG uses a fixed 1280x720 viewBox with hard-coded artboard coordinates
relies on parent perspective for the Y rotation
stylised Xd tile, not the official Adobe mark

records.name: Apple Logo
records.description: An animated Apple logo template with minimal motion. Good for Apple-themed content and tech product presentations.
records.move: apple fades up, bite taken, leaf unfurls, slow breath, fades out
records.how: A single 320x360 SVG on a light grey stage: a hand-drawn dark apple body path, a background-coloured circle acting as the bite, a highlight stroke and a leaf path with its transform origin at the stem. The fruit fades in from opacity 0 and scale 0.92 (expo.out) over the first 30%; at 15% the bite circle slides in from x:90 (expo.out) so it appears to be bitten; at 23% the leaf unfurls from scale 0/rotation -60 with back.out(2); at 33% the highlight draws with DrawSVG (power2.out). Hold: the whole logo breathes scale 1.03 yoyo on sine.inOut (37-73%) while the leaf sways rotation 4 yoyo. Exit at 88%: the logo fades to 0 with scale 0.95 (power2.in).
records.adapt: Swap the body/leaf paths for any silhouette logo, change #1d1d1f and the stage colour (the bite circle must match the stage); keep the fade-bite-leaf order and the sine breath.
records.port: mount(el, shot) inserts the SVG into el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with entrances at 0-0.4 of D, breath 0.37-0.73, exit 0.88. Requires DrawSVGPlugin only for the highlight stroke; the leaf's transform-origin is set in CSS with transform-box:view-box.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin for one small stroke
the apple is a hand-drawn approximation of the mark, not the official path
bite is a stage-coloured circle, breaks on non-flat backgrounds
fades to nothing at the end, close to the first frame

records.name: Behance Logo
records.description: An animated Behance logo template. Good for portfolio launch announcements and creative community content.
records.move: ring bursts, letters rise through masks, bar wipes across, lift out
records.how: On a Behance-blue stage a thin ring scales in from 0.2/opacity:0 (expo.out) over the first 40% then expands to 1.6 and fades (power2.out) from 30%. The 240px 'B' and 190px 'e' rise from yPercent:110 through overflow-hidden rows with expo.out at 3% and 7%; a white rounded bar above the e wipes in scaleX from the left (expo.out) at 23%; the whole mark settles from scale 0.96 with elastic.out(1,0.5) at 33% while a caption rises through its own mask (yPercent:120, expo.out) at 32%. Exit from 78%: caption shoots up, bar collapses, letters lift out yPercent:-110 with power3.in staggered 0.07.
records.adapt: Change the two letters, sizes, the caption, stage colour (#1769ff) and bar position; keep the staggered expo.out rise, the elastic settle and the ring burst.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the ring, masked letter rows, bar and caption in el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with entrances 0-0.4 of D and exit from 0.78. No plugins; scope selectors to el.
caveats: overflow:hidden rows with fixed heights act as masks, must match the font sizes
stylised 'Be' in Sharp Grotesk with a bar, an approximation of the Behance mark
letters exit upward, no loop

records.name: Bouncy Icons
records.description: An animated icon template where icons bounce into view with springy motion. Perfect for app icon showcases and onboarding screen animations.
records.move: icons drop from above, bounce and squash on impact, wiggle, spring out
records.how: A 4x2 grid of 140px rounded app icons (each with a white line icon and a blurred ellipse shadow beneath) on a light stage. CustomBounce.create('drop', {strength:0.55, squash:3}) builds a bounce ease and its paired 'drop-squash' ease. Each icon, staggered 0.13 from 2%, drops from y:-520 over 1.1s with the 'drop' bounce ease while scaleX 1.25 / scaleY 0.75 is applied with the 'drop-squash' ease so it flattens on each impact (transform-origin bottom); its shadow grows from scaleX 0.2/opacity 0 with the same bounce. At 54% all icons wiggle rotation 6 yoyo (sine.inOut, stagger 0.05). Exit at 79%: icons anticipate with y:-40, scaleY 1.1/scaleX 0.9 (power2.out) then launch to y:-600 with power3.in staggered 0.05 while shadows shrink and fade.
records.adapt: Change icon count, colours and the inline SVG glyphs; tune strength/squash in CustomBounce.create; keep the 1.1s drop with 0.13 stagger and the anticipate-then-launch exit.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid of .cell/.shadow/.app from shot.icons; animate(el, shot, D) registers the CustomBounce eases once (names are global), returns the same timeline with drops at 0.02-0.5 of D, wiggle at 0.54, exit at 0.79. Requires CustomEase and CustomBounce; toArray('.app') must be scoped to el.
caveats: requires CustomEase and CustomBounce plugins
CustomBounce ease names ('drop', 'drop-squash') are global registrations
filter: blur(4px) on eight shadows
icons exit upward, no loop

records.name: Check Icon
records.description: An animated checkmark template that draws itself with a clean stroke. Good for task completion UI and success state presentations.
records.move: ring draws around, checkmark strokes itself, disc pops in behind, pulse rings out
records.how: A green ring circle, a green disc (scale 0), a green tick path and a white tick path over it, a thin pulse circle, and a message line clipped in a 56px-high box. 0-27%: the ring draws with drawSVG 0->100% from -90deg (power3.inOut); at 17% the green tick draws itself (power3.out, 0.55s). At 35% the disc scales 0->1 with back.out(1.8), the white tick redraws over it and the pulse ring scales 1->1.45 while fading (power2.out); the whole badge does a 1.06 yoyo bump. At 43% 'Payment complete' slides up from yPercent 120 (expo.out). Exit at 83%: text slides up out (power3.in), badge scales to 0 with back.in(1.8), so the frame ends empty; the ring stays drawn under the disc.
records.adapt: Change the message string, the green (#22c55e) for the brand success colour, the tick path for another icon, and the background. Keep the 0.8s ring draw, the back.out(1.8) disc pop and the 0.25 yoyo bump.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the badge SVG and the .msg span inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with each position expressed as a fraction of D (ring 0-0.27D, disc at 0.35D, text at 0.43D, exit at 0.83D). Selectors must be scoped to el; needs DrawSVGPlugin registered; the .from() on .msg span needs immediateRender:false if built inside a paused parent.
caveats: from() tween on .msg span; use immediateRender:false when composing into a larger timeline
frame ends empty (ring remains but under a scale-0 disc, effectively invisible) rather than returning to the drawn state

records.name: Close Icon
records.description: An animated close icon template with a clean reveal. Good for modal UI demos and component presentations.
records.move: modal rises, X disc pops, strokes draw and rotate in, hover spin, press, dismiss
records.how: A dark modal card with placeholder bars, a button, and a circular X button in its corner made of two SVG strokes. 0-23%: the modal rises 60px with scale .94->1 and fades in (expo.out); at 12% the X disc scales 0->1 with back.out(2) while its SVG rotates -90->0 (expo.out) and the two diagonal strokes drawSVG in from opposite ends (power3.out, 0.35s each, offset 0.12s). At 43% a hover state: the disc rotates 90deg, scales 1.12 and turns red (#ff4d5e) with back.out(2). At 68% a press: scale .9 then 1.1 in 0.27s; at 78% the modal drops 40px, shrinks to .94 and fades out with power3.in so the frame ends empty.
records.adapt: Swap the modal contents for a real screenshot or product card, the accent blue and the hover red for brand colours, and the X for any icon. Keep the 0.7s expo.out entrance, the back.out(2) pop and the 0.12/0.15 press beat.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the modal and X markup inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with positions as fractions of D (modal 0, X at 0.12D, hover at 0.43D, press at 0.68D, dismiss at 0.78D). Scope all selectors to el; register DrawSVGPlugin; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false when nested
ends with the modal gone; does not return to the first frame

records.name: Cursor
records.description: An animated cursor template from Luc Chaissac with custom click states and movement trails. Good for web UI demos and interactive design presentations where the cursor itself is part of the story.
