records.move: arrow cursor glides between targets, clicks with ring bursts, comet trail of dots lags behind
records.how: A dark card with a Continue button and a toggle, an SVG of 10 shrinking, fading circles as a trail, a click ring, and a white arrow cursor. The cursor tweens x/y through six waypoints (power2.inOut between targets, sine.inOut for the short click hops) over the full 2s; each trail dot runs the same path on its own sub-timeline offset by (i+1)*0.035s so they trail behind like a comet. Clicks at 37% (button) and 75% (toggle): the cursor scales .8 then back.out(3) to 1, a ring scales .3->1.6 while fading (power2.out), and the target squashes to .93 then elastic.out(1,.5) back; the toggle knob slides x:32 and its track turns green. The waypoints are absolute pixel coordinates for a 1280x720 frame and the trail svg viewBox assumes that size, so both must be derived from el's size; scope '.cur', '.trail circle', '.click' to el.

records.name: Smile
records.description: An abstract animated composition from Luc Chaissac with expressive fluid motion. Good for experimental motion design and artistic brand content.
records.move: liquid orange blob face wobbles, eyes squash-blink, mouth stretches wide, ring swells out
records.how: A pure canvas drawing on a yellow field: 26 dark specks orbit the centre on seeded radii; a big orange metaball-style blob (90-point polygon whose radius wobbles with sine lobes driven by t) with a lighter inner blob, both squashing scaleX 1+.07sin(2p) and rotating +-0.08rad on a slow breath; two dark blob eyes with yellow highlights that drift and blink (scaleY collapsing to .1) around 45% of the loop; a bezier mouth whose corner width swings 150-250px and whose drop swells with a 12px wobble, a pink tongue blob clipped inside it; and a dark outline ring that expands from r 380 to 640 while its line thins and fades once per loop. The draw assumes a 1080x1080 canvas with centre 540,540; scale the context by el size.
caveats: canvas seek loop: port as a proxy tween with onUpdate
draw code assumes a 1080x1080 canvas
the ring swell uses (p*1.0)%1 so it snaps at the loop point, by design

records.name: The Edit: Nested Images
records.description: An edit template where images nest inside each other in a layered collage-like layout. Good for editorial and fashion content with a high-design aesthetic.
records.move: nested frames wipe in with parallax settle, collapse inward
records.how: Four image frames are nested in the DOM, each inset within its parent. Every image pushes from scale 1.0 to 1.12 linearly across D. Each frame reveals left-to-right via clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0)→inset(0 0% 0 0) with expo.out over 0.7s while sliding from x:60+20i to 0 with expo.out, staggered 0.16s from the outermost at 0.025D, so the nest reads as layers settling with parallax. A title rises from a mask, two caption rows rise staggered 0.08, a rule draws scaleX and an issue number fades in. From 0.72D the frames wipe out to inset(0 0 0 100%) innermost first with expo.in 0.32s, 0.07s apart, and the type shoves up.
records.adapt: Replace the four images (and per-frame filters), the title, caption rows and issue number; the nesting depth and inset offsets are CSS so change frame count by editing the frames array and DOM. Keep the 0.16s stagger and the expo.out wipes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the nested .frame tree from shot.images plus .num, .title, .cap and .rule; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with per-frame t = (0.05 + i*0.16)/2 * D and exit at 1.45/2 * D. Scope selectors to el.
caveats: clip-path inset animated on four nested layers each with a scaling background image
very short (2s) so the type barely holds
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when rebuilt

records.name: The Route: Destinations Carousel
records.description: An animated carousel template showing travel destinations along a route. Good for travel app showcases and destination discovery features.
records.move: plane rides route, carousel snaps stop to stop, headline swaps
records.how: A dim background drifts xPercent -2→2 across D. A plane icon follows a dashed route path with MotionPath (autoRotate) linearly for the full loop while a yellow path draws under it with DrawSVG 0→100%. Every D/4 the card track snaps x by one card width with expo.inOut 0.9s; the previous card dims to scale 0.92 opacity 0.55 and the next pops to full with back.out(1.6), the matching stop marker toggles an 'on' class, and the big headline swaps (old word up with expo.in, new word up from yPercent 110 with expo.out). The active card breathes y:-10 with sine.inOut between snaps. At D-0.95 the track slides to a duplicate fifth card (a copy of the first), so the hard cut back to t=0 reads as continuous.
records.adapt: Replace the destination cards (photo, tag, name, meta), the headline words, stop codes and route path; N cards sets STEP = D/N and CW must match card width plus gap. Keep the 0.9s expo.inOut snap and the back.out card pop.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds .bg, .hd, .big spans, a .track of cards with a duplicated first card at the end, the route SVG with two path ids, stops and the plane; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with DrawSVG and MotionPath registered, t = i*D/N snaps and the wrap snap at D-0.95/10*D. Path ids must be unique per instance and nth-child selectors scoped to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin and MotionPathPlugin
loop relies on a duplicate first card and a hard cut; the drawn route and dimmed stops do not reset
uses className sets on the timeline
backdrop-filter blur on card tags
catalog says 12s but the file renders 10s

records.name: The Route: Destinations Map
records.description: An animated map template where routes draw themselves between locations. Great for travel app showcases and content where the geography itself is part of the story.
records.move: routes draw leg by leg between pins, distance counts, drains out
records.how: A stylised SVG map with a generated grid and land shapes drifts from scale 1.06 to 1.12 with a slow x/y pan across D. The first pin pops with back.out(3) and its label with back.out(2). Every 1.9s from 0.07D a leg draws: a blurred glow path and the sharp route path DrawSVG 0→100% with power2.inOut over 1.2s, the HUD text swaps (old up with expo.in, new up from yPercent 110 with expo.out), the destination pin pops at leg end and its label follows, while a distance counter tweens to the cumulative total with power2.out. From 0.22D the pin outer rings pulse (r 14→26, opacity 1→0, repeat 6, stagger 0.1). At 0.9D the routes drain out (drawSVG '100% 100%', expo.in), labels and pins shrink with stagger, the HUD exits and the counter runs back to 0 to close the loop.
records.adapt: Replace the land shapes, route path d's (glow and sharp paths must match), pin positions, label names/distances, HUD leg strings and the dists array; leg count sets the 0.7 + i*1.9 cadence. Keep the 1.2s power2.inOut draw and the back.out pin pops.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the map SVG (grid generated in code, land, paired route paths, pins), labels, brand, HUD and distance readout; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with DrawSVGPlugin registered, leg t = (0.7 + i*1.9)/10 * D, the counter proxy tween with onUpdate, and the drain at 9.0/10 * D. Path ids and the blur filter id must be unique per instance; scope selectors to el.
caveats: requires DrawSVGPlugin
feGaussianBlur filter on the glow paths
uses id selectors (#r1..#r4, #grid, #blur) that collide if instanced twice
pin pulse uses attr r tweens with repeat

records.name: The Route: New Destination
records.description: A template where a route path extends to reveal a new destination. Good for travel app feature launches and destination reveals.
records.move: route line draws on, dot rides the extension, new pin pops elastic
records.how: A cream map (SVG land/water paths) sits inside a .map wrapper that the camera drives: it holds at scale 1.25 with a slow linear pan for the first 35% of the duration, then eases (power2.inOut) out to scale 1.05 and pans down-right to follow the extension. Pins scale in with back.out(3), labels with back.out(2), and the existing route #p1 draws with DrawSVG 0%→100% over ~14% of D (power2.inOut). At 38% a black dot appears and rides #p2 with MotionPath while #p2 draws behind it (both 1.8s, power2.inOut); the dot fades, the orange pin pops with elastic.out(1,0.5), its halo circle pulses r 24→50 with fading opacity repeat 3, then the label, a pill badge (back.out(2.5)) and two masked title lines (yPercent 110→0, expo.out, stagger 0.1) arrive. The last 8% reverses everything with expo.in: title lines exit upward, badge/labels/pins scale to 0, and the routes un-draw to '100% 100%'.
records.adapt: Replace the three land paths and two route paths with the product's geography, rename the three city labels and title lines, and swap the accent #ff5a36 and map palette; keep the draw/dot/pin/label ordering and the 3.5s camera hold before the pan.
records.port: mount(el, shot) injects the map SVG, labels, badge and title into el and runs the gsap.set initial states; animate(el, shot, D) builds the same timeline with positions as fractions of D (route 1 draw at 0.06D, extension at 0.38D, reveal at 0.55-0.61D, exit at 0.92D) and returns it. Selectors like '#p1', '.map', '.dot' must be scoped via el.querySelector; MotionPath align expects the SVG in the DOM before the tween is created.
caveats: camera does not return: map ends at scale 1.02 / x-30 / y-70 but starts at scale 1.25 / x120 / y160, so the loop jumps
render.json duration is 10s while the catalog lists 12s
SVG ids #p1/#p2 collide if two instances are mounted

records.name: The Stack: Livestream
records.description: An animated livestream announcement template with bold motion. Good for live event promotions and streaming content that needs to feel immediate.
records.move: card slams up from below in 3D, live badge pulses, counter ticks
records.how: A dark card with a thumbnail, red LIVE pill, viewer count and two masked headline lines sits over a looping mp4 background (the timeline's onUpdate and a patched __fx.seek set video.currentTime). Both card and a back card start at y 900 / rotateX 18 / scale 0.9 and slam to place with expo.out over 0.9s (back card lags 0.1s and settles to y -22, scale 0.94); the front card gets an elastic.out(1,0.5) scaleY 1.06→1 overshoot. The LIVE pill pops with back.out(3), viewers slide in from x 60, headline lines rise yPercent 110→0 with expo.out stagger 0.08, the button pops back.out(2.5), and a red progress bar scaleX 0→1 runs linearly for D-1.5s. The LIVE dot yoyos scale 1→0.4 nine times, the viewer number counts 2,418→3,106 over 4s (power1.inOut) via a tweened object, and the headline gets a scale 1.03 hit at 50% with an elastic settle. Final 15%: text lines expo.in upward, then both cards fly to y -1100 with rotateX -12.
records.adapt: Swap the mp4 and thumbnail image, the show title lines, host names, date kicker and viewer numbers, and the red #ff2d2d accent; keep the 0.9s expo.out slam, the lagging back card and the 4s counter.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card DOM plus the <video> and awaits loadeddata; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the entrance at 0-0.2D, counter at 0.2-0.87D and exit at 0.85D. The video seek hack (patching window.__fx.seek) does not port: drive video.currentTime from a tween onUpdate on the returned timeline instead, and scope '.card', '.row span', '.n' to el.
caveats: background <video> is seeked by patching window.__fx.seek and via tl onUpdate; video seeking per frame is slow and may not be frame-exact
video.currentTime is wrapped modulo the clip length, so the background may cut mid-loop
backdrop-filter: blur(8px) on the viewers pill

records.name: The Stack: Partnership
records.description: An animated partnership announcement template with a polished card reveal. Ideal for collaboration announcements and co-brand social content.
records.move: three cards land stacked, two logos collide with sparks, deck floats
records.how: Three cards (black, yellow, white) start at y 760 / rotateX 22 / scale 0.85 and land back-to-front with expo.out over 1s at 0.14s offsets, each settling a step higher (y -44/-22/0, scale 0.9/0.95/1) so they read as a stack. On the front card two rounded logo tiles fly in from x ±320 with ±25 rotation (expo.out, 0.7s) and collide at the centre; on impact they get an elastic.out(1,0.4) squash from scaleX 1.1/scaleY 0.9, the × pops with back.out(3), and six spark dots burst outward (power3.out, seeded by fx.rng) to radius 120-200. Headline, subline and pill then rise (masked yPercent 110→0, expo.out). From 34% to 91% the whole deck idles on rotateY ±6 / rotateX ±4 with sine.inOut. Exit at 87%: text drops, logos scale 0, cards fly to y -1000 front-to-back with expo.in.
records.adapt: Replace the two logo SVGs and their tile colours, the headline 'Acme × Northwind', subline and CTA pill text, and the card colours; keep the back-to-front landing offsets and the 1.0s collision beat.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the deck DOM and applies the gsap.set start states; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with cards landing at 0-0.18D, collision at 0.14-0.3D, float 0.34-0.91D, exit from 0.87D. records.name: The Stack: Release Notes
records.description: An animated release notes template that presents product updates as a stack of cards. A more visual alternative to a static changelog post.
records.move: card stack rises, front card peels off right, next steps forward
records.how: Four dark release cards share one position; a pose(depth) helper gives each y -22*depth, scale 1-0.06*depth and opacity fading to 0 past depth 2, so they read as a stack. They start 1000px below at rotateX 25 and rise back-to-front (expo.out, 1s, 0.1s offsets) while two masked header lines rise. Every 2.1s (from 1.0s) the front card peels away to x 260 / y -140 / rotate 10 / opacity 0 with power3.in over 0.55s, and every card behind it re-poses one step forward with back.out(1.4) over 0.8s; a pagination dot swaps class and pops from scale 1.8, and a counter label updates via call(). uses className tweens and call() for the dots and counter; scrubbing backwards can leave stale state

records.name: The Stack: Sale
records.description: An animated sale announcement template with stacked card reveals and animated pricing. Good for e-commerce promotions and retail social content.
records.move: tilted cards land, percent counts up and squashes, price strikes
records.how: On a red field with diagonal stripes drifting x 0→92 linearly, three cards (black, yellow, white) start at y 900 / rotate 8 and land with expo.out over 0.9s at 0.12s offsets, the back two settling to rotate -4 and 2.5 with elastic.out(1,0.5). The big number fades/rises in and a tweened object counts 0→40 over 1.1s (power3.out) into the .n span, then the whole figure gets an elastic scaleY 1.15/scaleX 0.92→1 squash; 'off everything' rises masked; a red strike line scaleX 0→1 crosses the old price (expo.out) and the new price counts $120→$72 while its colour tweens to red. records.description: An animated testimonial template that reveals quotes as a stack of cards one at a time. A more engaging alternative to a static quote graphic for social media or marketing videos.

records.how: Three quote cards (white, yellow, orange) share a position with a pose(depth) of y -26*depth, scale 1-0.06*depth and alternating ±2.5 rotate. Three job cards start stacked 14px apart at y +600 / rotateX 30 / opacity 0 with scale 1-0.05*i; they rise as one with expo.out over 1s (0.08s offsets), then at 19% fan down into a list (y i*172, scale 1) with back.out(1.5) over 0.9s at 0.1s offsets. records.name: Blast: Social Media Showcase
records.description: A high-energy social media showcase template with fast motion and strong pacing. Good for bold creative portfolios and brand content that needs to make a quick impression.
records.move: hard-cut panels slam, letters punch, wipes, grid explodes, marquee stripes rip
records.how: Five full-frame colour panels and three images are toggled with autoAlpha sets at hard cut points. 0-17%: a red panel scales up from scaleY 0 (expo.out 0.35s), BLAST letters snap in from scale 3 with stagger 0.06 and the word slowly scales to 1.08. 17%: a sunset image punches in from scale 1.6 with clip-path inset 40%→0 then creeps to 1.12. 32%: a yellow panel wipes xPercent -100→0 (expo.inOut 0.4s), MAKE/NOISE rise masked from yPercent 110 and drift apart ±6%. 52%: an aurora image slams up from yPercent 100, a 3x2 grid of cells pops from scale 0 with back.out(2.5) from centre (each 0.05) and scales to 1.06. 72%: a blue panel drops from yPercent -100 and two rotated marquee stripes rip across (xPercent 45→-15 and -45→15, power2.out 1.2s). 87%: a black panel blooms via clip-path circle 0→80%, logo spins in from rotation -90, name and tagline rise, then the CTA scales to 1.6 and fades, and the black panel is hidden at the last frame.
records.adapt: Replace the three images, the BLAST / MAKE NOISE / stripe words, the grid cell labels, the panel colours and the closing logo/name; keep the cut points (1.4, 2.6, 4.2, 5.8, 7.0 of 8s) and the sub-0.5s slam durations.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the panels, images, grid and CTA and sets the initial autoAlpha 0 on everything but the first panel; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the cut points as fractions (0.175, 0.325, 0.525, 0.725, 0.875 of D). All #id selectors become el.querySelector; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
relies on many .set autoAlpha cuts; scrubbing backwards across cuts can show stale layers
three full-frame images with scale and clip-path tweens

records.name: Design Preview
records.description: A design preview template from Vendredi Society that presents work inside an animated frame. Good for design handoff presentations and client-facing showcases.
records.move: selection frame draws, mockup drops in, cursor drags it to mobile width
records.how: A dotted canvas fades in, a blue SVG selection rect draws around the artboard with DrawSVG 0%→100% (power3.inOut, 1s), four corner handles pop with back.out(3) and two dimension labels fade in. The mockup (browser chrome plus a two-column hero) reveals with clip-path inset bottom 100%→0 (expo.inOut 0.9s), hero children rise and the stat card scales from 0.8 with back.out(1.6). At 34% an SVG cursor flies in from bottom-right, nudges onto the right handle, and from 42% a tweened object shrinks the artboard width 760→420 (expo.inOut 1.1s) via an onUpdate that sets style.width/left, the rect width and the label text, while the cursor moves with the handle; the grid collapses to one column (gridTemplateColumns tween), the stat card fades and the heading font-size tweens 42→34; the side label text swaps to 'Mobile / Home' via call(). From 60% the artboard sways rotationY 6 / rotationX -3 and back with sine.inOut, then at 92% lifts y -60 and fades, note and dots fade.
records.adapt: Replace the mockup contents (heading, body, buttons, stat card), the artboard name labels, the start/end widths and the accent blue; keep the 1s draw, the 1.1s expo.inOut resize and the cursor lead-in.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the artboard, frame SVG, cursor and note; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with draw at 0.01D, drop at 0.12D, cursor at 0.34D, resize at 0.42D, sway 0.6-0.9D, exit at 0.92D. The resize onUpdate must write to el-scoped nodes; from() tweens need immediateRender:false; gridTemplateColumns and fontSize tweens are layout tweens, not transforms.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
side label text is changed by call() and never reset, so it reads 'Mobile / Home' on the second loop
render.json duration is 10s while the catalog lists 11s
resize tweens width/left/gridTemplateColumns/fontSize, forcing layout each frame

records.name: Drop It Like It's Hot: Mask
records.description: A mask-based animation template from Savee with bold kinetic motion. Perfect for creative agency showreels and high-impact brand content.
records.move: knockout word drops, blows up to reveal image, circle, slice, stripe wipes
records.how: An SVG mask knocks the word DROP out of a cream rect over a sunset image scaling 1.25→1.05; the <text> drops from y -700 with expo.out, squashes scaleY 0.82 yoyo on landing, then at 19% scales to 14 with expo.in so the letter interiors swallow the frame and the image is full-bleed. 28%: a black layer blooms via clip-path circle 0→75% (expo.inOut) and IT lands from y -500 with bounce.out and a scaleX 1.15/scaleY 0.85 squash. 44%: an ocean image slices open from clip-path inset 50% top/bottom to 0 (expo.inOut 0.6s) while LIKE drops through from yPercent -250 and exits to +250. 62%: four bars scale x 0→1 with stagger 0.07 (expo.inOut), then an aurora image wipes diagonally via a polygon clip-path and HOT snaps in from scale 4 / opacity 0, its letter-spacing easing out to .05em. 92%: the cream rect (mask temporarily removed) wipes down over everything and the mask is restored at the last frame.
records.adapt: Replace the four words, the three images and the cream/black/red/yellow palette; keep the beat spacing (0, 2.8, 4.4, 6.2, 9.2 of 10s) and the mask blow-up at 1.9s with expo.in.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the SVG mask, word layers, circle, bars and images with the initial autoAlpha/clip-path sets; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the beats at 0.28, 0.44, 0.62, 0.72 and 0.92 of D. The SVG mask id must be unique per instance; attr mask toggles and #id selectors must be el-scoped; from() on #tx needs immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
SVG mask id #m1 collides if two instances mount
render.json duration is 10s while the catalog lists 16s
the #bars .bar background-attachment: fixed rule is overridden and unused

records.name: Drop It Like It's Hot: Sizzle Reel
records.description: A fast-paced sizzle reel template made by Savee with energetic cuts and strong transitions. Great for agency showreels and creative portfolio content.
records.move: fast push-ins, whip pan with blur, hard cuts, strobe invert, red endcard
records.how: Four full-frame shots are cut with autoAlpha sets plus a white flash (opacity 0.9→0, 0.25s) at each cut, and a REEL counter updates via call(). Shot 1 pushes in scale 1→1.25 (power1.in 1.3s) while 'Drop' rises masked from yPercent 120 and leaves upward; four corner brackets pop in. At 22% a whip pan: shot 1 slides xPercent -60 with filter blur 0→20px (power3.in) and shot 2 arrives from xPercent 60 blurring back to 0 (power3.out), then settles scale 1.1→1; 'It like' skews in from xPercent -80 / skewX 20 and skews out the other way. At 48% a hard cut zooms shot 3 from scale 1.4 / rotation 3 to 1.05 (expo.out) with 'It's hot' snapping from scale 2.2 and strobing with filter invert 0→1 repeat 3 yoyo. At 75% shot 4 slams up from yPercent 100, then a red endcard wipes in via clip-path inset right 100%→0 with the title rising and scaling to 1.1; at 97% everything cuts back to shot 1 reset for the loop.
records.adapt: Replace the four shots, the three word cards and the endcard title/credit, and the red; keep the cut points (1.3, 2.9, 4.5, 5.1 of 6s), the 0.25s flash and the 0.3s whip blur.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the shot layers, flash, corners, counter and endcard with initial autoAlpha sets; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with cuts at 0.22, 0.48, 0.75, 0.85 and reset at 0.975 of D. Move the cut()/flash() helpers inside animate with el-scoped selectors; the counter call()s become el-scoped; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
filter: blur(20px) on two full-frame images during the whip pan, slow to render
counter text is set via call() and can go stale when scrubbing backwards

records.name: Folio: Social Media Showcase
records.description: A portfolio-format social media showcase template with elegant animated transitions. Good for creative professionals who want their social content to feel as considered as their work.
records.move: two images wipe open with counter-move, serif title rises, wipe away
records.how: Two image frames on a warm paper ground reveal by clip-path: the large one inset right 100%→0 over 1s (expo.inOut) while its inner image counter-moves xPercent -8→0 from scale 1.08 (expo.out 1.4s); the small one inset top 100%→0 at 0.25s with a yPercent 8→0 counter-move. An index line fades up, two serif title lines rise masked from yPercent 110 (expo.out, stagger 0.1), a horizontal rule scales x 0→1 and two footer captions fade in. From 30% both inner images drift to scale 1.05. At 65% the transition: the large frame wipes closed from the left (inset left 100%) with its image sliding xPercent 10, the small frame wipes closed from the bottom, title lines exit upward with expo.in, the rule shrinks from the right and captions fade.

caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
the description promises a transition between works but the code only wipes out; no second work is shown

records.name: Frames: Mobile Showreel
records.description: A mobile showreel template that presents app screens inside device frames with animated transitions. Great for portfolio presentations and app store assets.
records.move: three phones rise, fan in 3D, screens scroll, centre phone comes forward
records.how: Three CSS phone frames rise from y 700 / rotationX -20 with expo.out over 1.1s (stagger 0.12) and the outer two turn to rotationY ±18 with a 30px inward shift, while the title and caption fade in and the first screen's children rise (stagger 0.04). From 27% each phone's .screens column scrolls yPercent 0→-100 with expo.inOut over 0.8s, 0.25s apart, revealing the second screen, and the caption highlight swaps via call(). At 47% the middle phone scales to 1.12 with z 80 while the outer phones turn further to rotationY ±32 and shrink to 0.92 (expo.inOut 1s); the whole row sways rotationY -10 then +10 with sine.inOut. At 80% the screens scroll back to 0 (stagger 0.08), then the phones drop back to y 700 / rotationX 15 with expo.in and the text fades.
records.adapt: Replace each phone's two screen mockups (heading, subline, hero gradient, list rows, CTA), the title and caption; keep the 0.12s rise stagger, the 0.8s scroll and the 1s forward move.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the row of N phones with two screens each and the caption; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with rise 0-0.15D, scroll at 0.27D, forward at 0.47D, sway 0.6-0.9D, scroll-back at 0.8D, exit at 0.92D. The perspective on .stage must move to el; the caption innerHTML call()s must be el-scoped; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
caption highlight is set by call() and can go stale when scrubbing backwards
perspective is on the stage container

records.name: Image Carousel: Parallax
records.description: A carousel template where images move at slightly different speeds to create a parallax depth effect. Good for editorial slideshows and photo presentations that would feel flat with a standard transition.
records.move: card track slides, inner images and blurred backdrop lag at different speeds
records.how: Four wide image cards (the fourth a copy of the first) sit on a horizontal track; behind them a blurred, saturated copy of each image fades in as its own backdrop. Three moves at 20%, 51% and 83% of the duration slide the track x by -760px per step with expo.inOut over 1.2s while every inner image (130% wide) tweens x in the opposite direction at 40% speed and the backdrop layer at 12%, so three planes move at three speeds; the matching backdrop crossfades opacity to 0.45 and the others to 0, and a call() updates the '01 / 03' counter and the pill dot halfway through each move. All cards breathe scale 1→1.02 and back with sine.inOut over the full duration. The dots are hidden on the last frame; no explicit exit because the fourth card equals the first.
records.adapt: Replace the three images, captions and headings (the fourth card must duplicate the first), the step width if the card width changes; keep the 1.2s expo.inOut move and the 0.4 / 0.12 speed ratios.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the backdrops, track with N+1 cards and dots; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with moves at 0.2D, 0.51D and 0.83D via the move() helper written against el-scoped nodes. The counter/dot call()s should become el-scoped; the 8s breathe tween should be sized to D.
caveats: inner image x offset grows to 304/608/912px per step, far beyond the 15% bleed, so the left of each card goes empty after the first move
the final frame does not match the first: inner images sit at x 912 and the backdrop layer at x -273, so the loop jumps
filter: blur(30px) on three full-frame backdrops, slow to render
counter and dots are updated via call()

records.name: Instagram Stories: Collage
records.description: A collage story template with multiple images animated in an overlapping layout. Works for mood boards and creative posts that want to feel assembled rather than designed.
records.move: polaroid tiles thrown in from all sides, wobble, float, scatter out
records.how: Five white-bordered photo tiles with tape strips sit on a dotted paper ground at fixed rotations (-6, 5, -3, 7, -9). The top serif word drops in from y -160, then each tile flies in from off-frame (x ±900 and/or y ±300..1200, rotation ±25..40) with expo.out over 0.7s at 0.15s offsets; a round red sticker spins in from scale 0 / rotation 180 with back.out(2.5) and the bottom word rises from y 160; tape strips scale x from 0 with stagger 0.1. On landing each tile over-rotates ±2 then settles with elastic.out(1,0.5); from 42% they float y ±12-14 with sine.inOut and back, while the sticker rocks -12→-2→-12. Exit at 86%: tiles scatter to x ±1100 with ±40 rotation and expo.in (stagger 0.05), sticker shrinks with back.in(2), words leave the way they came.
records.adapt: Replace the five images and their tile boxes, the two serif words and the sticker text/colour; keep the rot[] array, the 0.15s throw cadence and the elastic settle.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the paper, tiles with tape and the words; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with throws at 0.02-0.18D, settles 0.15-0.4D, float 0.42-0.72D, scatter at 0.86D. Use el.querySelectorAll('.tile'); from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: Instagram Story: 2 Images
records.description: A story template with two images and clean animated transitions between them. Good for before/after content and dual product showcases.
records.move: image one breathes in, image two wipes down over it, labels swap
records.how: Two full-bleed images stack; the second starts clipped to inset bottom 100%. Image one's inner layer eases from scale 1.15 / yPercent 4 to 1 / 0 over 2s (power2.out) while a pill drops from y -30, the '01 / 02' small label slides from x -20 and two headline words rise masked from yPercent 110 (expo.out, stagger 0.1); the first story progress segment fills scaleX 0→1 linearly. At 40% the headline exits upward (expo.in), the second image wipes down (clip-path inset 0 0 100% 0 → 0, expo.inOut 0.9s) with its inner layer moving yPercent -10→0 from scale 1.12, while image one pushes down yPercent 10 and scales 1.1; the second label set rises and the second progress segment fills. At 86% the second headline exits, image one's inner layer is reset by a set, image two wipes back up to inset top 100% with expo.inOut, and the progress bars are zeroed on the last frame.
records.adapt: Replace the two images, the two two-word headlines and their counters, and the pill text; keep the 2s breathe, the 0.9s expo.inOut wipe at 1.9s and the counter-push on the outgoing image.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the two image layers, shade, progress bar, pill and two labels with the initial sets; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with wipe at 0.475D, second label at 0.6D, exit at 0.86D. #a/#b/#l1/#l2 become el-scoped; from() tweens need immediateRender:false (the fromTo on '#b i' already sets it).
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
backdrop-filter: blur(12px) on the pill

records.name: Instagram Story: 2 Images With Captions
records.description: A story template with two images and animated text captions for each. Good for product descriptions and storytelling posts where the image and the words need to work together.
records.move: two image blocks wipe down, serif titles rise, word captions cascade
records.how: Two stacked blocks each hold an image and a caption. An enter() helper reveals each image with clip-path inset bottom 100%→0 (expo.inOut 0.9s) while its inner layer eases from scale 1.15 / yPercent -6 to rest (expo.out 1.6s); the index number slides from x -14, the serif heading rises masked from yPercent 110 (expo.out) and the description words (split into spans) cascade y 14→0 with opacity, stagger 0.03 (power3.out). Block one enters at 2.5%, a dividing line scales x 0→1 at 17% (expo.inOut), block two enters at 22%; header and footer fade in. From 42% both images Ken Burns to scale 1.06 linearly. exit() at 75% and 81%: headings exit upward with expo.in, words fade with a 0.01 stagger, images wipe closed to inset top 100% (expo.in 0.5s), the line shrinks from the right and header/footer fade.
records.adapt: Replace the two images, product names and descriptions, the header/footer strings and the paper colour; keep enter()'s 0.9s wipe with 1.6s settle and the 0.8s spacing between blocks.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the two blocks, splits '.cap p' into .w spans and adds header/line/footer; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with enter at 0.025D and 0.225D, hold 0.42-0.75D, exits at 0.75D/0.81D. Move enter()/exit() inside animate with el-scoped selectors; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: Instagram Story: 2 Square Images
records.description: A story template with two square images side by side and animated transitions. Good for comparison posts and paired product showcases.
records.move: two squares slide in from opposite sides, VS pops, vote bars fill
records.how: A two-line title rises masked (yPercent 110→0, expo.out, stagger 0.1). Two square images slide in from x ∓700 with ∓8 rotation (expo.out 0.8s) and meet at the centre while their inner layers settle from scale 1.2; a round VS badge spins in from scale 0 / rotation -120 with back.out(2.5), corner labels drop in, a 'Tap to vote' line and two result bars rise (power3.out, stagger 0.1). At 42% the vote lands: bar fills scaleX 0→0.62 and 0→0.38 (expo.out 1s) while a tweened object writes the percentages, the winning square lifts y -20 / scale 1.04 with back.out(2) and the loser shrinks to 0.96 with filter brightness 0.6; both inner images drift to scale 1.06. Exit at 84%: squares slide back out the way they came with expo.in, VS shrinks with back.in(2), title lines exit upward, bars and subline fade down.
records.adapt: Replace the two images and A/B labels, the title, bar names and the 62/38 split (both bars and the counter targets); keep the 0.8s opposing slide and the 1s expo.out fill at 1.7s.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the title, pair, VS, subline and bars; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with slide at 0.04D, vote at 0.42D, exit at 0.84D. The percentage object and its onUpdate must target el-scoped spans; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
backdrop-filter: blur(8px) on the corner labels
filter: brightness tween on the losing square

records.name: Instagram Story: 2 Vertical Images
records.description: A story template with two vertical images and smooth animated transitions. Perfect for portrait photography and fashion editorial posts.
records.move: two portrait columns wipe in from opposite ends, drift apart, names glide
records.how: Two tall image columns reveal by clip-path in opposite directions: the left from inset top 100%→0 and the right from inset bottom 100%→0 (expo.inOut 1.1s, 0.15s apart) while their inner layers counter-move yPercent ∓10→0 from scale 1.1 (expo.out 1.8s). Small uppercase captions fade up (stagger 0.08) and two large serif name words slide in from x -200 and x +200 with opacity (expo.out 0.9s). From 37% to 92% the hold is a vertical parallax: the left image drifts yPercent 0→5, the right 0→-5, and the name words glide x ±30 the other way, all sine.inOut over 2.2s. Exit at 85%: each column wipes closed the way it opened (expo.in 0.6s), names slide back out with expo.in and captions fade.
records.adapt: Replace the two portrait images, the two name words and four caption strings, and the paper colour; keep the 1.1s opposing wipes with the 10% counter-move and the 2.2s drift.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the two columns, names and captions; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with wipes at 0-0.3D, drift 0.37-0.92D, exit at 0.85D. '.ca'/'.cb'/'.n1'/'.n2' become el-scoped; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.

records.name: Instagram Story: 3 Horizontal Images
records.description: A story template with three horizontal images and animated reveals. Good for photo dumps and lifestyle content that wants a bit of structure.
records.move: three strips wipe in alternating directions, images slide against the wipe
records.how: Three landscape strips stacked vertically reveal with clip-path insets in alternating directions (right, left, right) using expo.inOut over 0.9s at 0.3s offsets; inside each, the image (124% wide) counter-slides xPercent ∓8→0 from scale 1.1 (expo.out 1.5s) and a time-stamp tag rises with back.out(2). Exit at 81%: each strip wipes closed in the opposite direction (expo.in 0.5s, 0.12s offsets), tags fade, footer words exit upward, hairlines shrink from the right and the header fades.

The forEach over strip selectors must use el.querySelectorAll; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.

records.name: Instagram Story: 3 Square Images
records.description: A story template with three square images in an animated layout. Good for product showcases and photo collages.
records.move: square deck fans in, top card flicks off to reveal next
records.how: Three square product cards stack at one spot with depth poses (y -40 / scale 0.92 / rotationZ 3 and y -80 / 0.84 / -3). A title rises masked (expo.out), then the cards fly up from y 1400 with ±12-20 rotationZ back-first (expo.out 0.8s, 0.12s apart) and the dots, price and CTA fade up; inner images settle from scale 1.12. At 37% and 62% a flick() beat throws the top card to x -900 with rotationZ -18 / rotationY -30 (power3.in 0.55s), the next card steps to the front with back.out(1.4) and the one behind re-poses, while a call() moves the active dot and rewrites the price. At 85% the last card flicks off, title lines exit upward and the dots/price/CTA fade down; the first dot and price are restored by call() on the last frame.

The flick() helper's call() must update el-scoped dots/price; from() tweens need immediateRender:false; perspective on .stage moves to el.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
dots and price are set via call() and can go stale when scrubbing backwards

records.name: Instagram Story: 3D Hand
records.description: A story template featuring an animated 3D hand element. Good for product interaction demos and social content that wants a tactile feel.
records.move: 3D hand enters, taps a swatch, presses button, button squashes, ring ripples
records.how: A three.js scene (procedural capsule hand: palm, four curled fingers, extended index, thumb, wrist, MeshStandardMaterial skin) renders on a transparent canvas over a DOM product card. A title rises masked and the card rises from y 300 / scale 0.9 (expo.out). A pose object (x, y, z, press, rz) is tweened: the hand glides from bottom-right to the blue swatch (expo.out 1.1s), dips z 3→0.6 with the index curling (press 1) for a 0.18s tap, and a call() switches the active swatch and price while the swatch scales 0.85 yoyo. It then moves to the button (expo.inOut 0.9s) and presses; the button scales 0.94 then elastic.out(1,0.4) back, the label reads 'Added ✓', a ring ripples scale 0.5→6 fading, and the card dips y -12 with an elastic settle. At 73% the hand retreats off-frame with power3.in; the title and card leave at 88-92% and swatch/price reset. The seek() callback seeks the GSAP timeline, applies the pose to the hand, adds a sin/cos idle sway from t, and renders.
records.adapt: Replace the card copy, swatch colours, prices and button label, and the yellow ground; the world-space targets are computed from DOM pixel positions via toWorld(), so move the swatch/button and update those two coordinates; keep the 0.18s tap dip and the 0.9s travel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card and a canvas sized to el, creates the renderer/scene/hand and the pose object; animate(el, shot, D) returns the GSAP timeline plus a tween with onUpdate that sets the hand from pose, applies the idle sway from the timeline's time, and calls renderer.render (replacing the fx.register seek loop). toWorld() assumes a 1080x1920 canvas and fov 35 at z 30, so recompute vh/vw from el's size; the call()s for swatch/price/label must be el-scoped.
caveats: fx.register seek loop must become a tween with onUpdate on the returned timeline
assumes a 1080x1920 viewport for the DOM-to-world mapping
WebGL canvas with preserveDrawingBuffer overlays the DOM
swatch, price and button label are changed via call() and can go stale when scrubbing backwards
the hand is a stylised procedural mesh, not a modelled hand

records.name: Instagram Story: 4 Images
records.description: A story template with four images in a dynamic animated layout. Good for collections and multi-product features where editing down to one image isn't an option.
records.move: four tiles fly in from four edges, layout reshuffles twice, snap out
records.how: Four rounded image tiles in a 2x2 grid fly in from four edges (x ∓700 or y ∓900 with ±6-8 rotation, expo.out 0.8s, 0.1s apart) while a masked headline rises, a footer line slides from x -30 and a pill pops with back.out(2). Four story-progress segments fill scaleX 0→1 linearly, one per second. Inside every tile the image drifts scale 1→1.08 and xPercent -2→2 linearly for the whole duration. At 37% the layout shifts by tweening left/top/width/height with expo.inOut over 0.9s: tile 1 grows to a 940x900 feature and tiles 2-4 line up as 296x370 thumbnails below (0.05s offsets); at 65% tile 2 takes the feature and tile 1 drops to the row. Exit at 86%: tiles snap to y -1400 with expo.in (stagger 0.05), headline exits upward, footer fades down.
records.adapt: Replace the four images and numbers, the headline, footer line and pill text, and the two feature layouts' pixel boxes; keep the 0.1s fly-in cadence and the 0.9s expo.inOut reflows at 1.5s and 2.6s.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the dots, header, four tiles and footer; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with fly-in 0.01-0.3D, reflows at 0.375D and 0.65D, exit at 0.86D. The reflow tweens left/top/width/height in px, so they assume the 1080-wide stage and must be scaled to el; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
layout is tweened via left/top/width/height, forcing layout each frame and assuming a 1080x1920 stage

records.name: Instagram Story: 5 Images
records.description: A story template that moves through five images in a flowing animated sequence. Good for event recaps and collection launches.
records.move: card stack peels upward one by one, digit rolls, fresh stack returns
records.how: Five portrait image cards share a slot with depth(k) poses of y -40k / scale 1-0.06k and a black dim overlay at 0.22k opacity. A headline rises from y 60, a footer fades, a thin bar fills scaleX 0→1 linearly over the whole duration and every inner image drifts xPercent -3→3 with scale to 1.06. Every 0.72s from 0.35s the front card peels to y -1800 with rotation -7 (power3.in 0.55s), the remaining cards re-pose one step forward with expo.out and their dims lighten, and a counter digit rolls out yPercent -100 with opacity, is replaced via set(textContent), and rolls in from +100 (expo.out). At 84% the fifth card peels off, the digit resets to 1, and the first four cards return from y 1700 / rotation 5 with expo.out at 0.05s offsets, dims restored by set, so the stack is fresh for the loop.
records.adapt: Replace the five images and captions, the headline and footer, and the card count (STEP is 0.72s for five in 4s); keep depth()'s 40px / 6% pitch and the 0.55s power3.in peel.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the stack of N cards with dims and the counter, applying the depth() sets; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with T0 = 0.09D, STEP = 0.18D and the return at 0.86D. The digit set(textContent) and card selectors must be el-scoped; the fromTo returns already carry immediateRender:false.
caveats: digit text is swapped with set(textContent) and can go stale when scrubbing backwards

records.name: Instagram Story: Blog Post
records.description: A story template designed for sharing blog post highlights with animated text reveals. Good for content creators and media brands driving traffic to written articles.
records.move: veil slides off hero, serif lines rise, words cascade, veil closes
records.how: A paper-coloured veil over the hero image scales x 1→0 from the right (expo.inOut 0.9s) while the hero rises from y 60 and its image Ken Burns from scale 1.12 / yPercent -3 to 1 / +3 linearly over the whole duration. A black pill tag grows scaleX from 0 at its left edge (expo.out) and its orange dot pops with back.out(3). Three serif headline lines rise masked from yPercent 110 with a 3° rotation from the top-left corner (expo.out, stagger 0.12); the excerpt's words (split into spans) cascade y 18→0 with opacity, stagger 0.035; a short rule scales x from 0, meta text slides in, a CTA rises with back.out(1.6) and a brand line fades. The CTA arrow nudges x 10 yoyo ×3 from 60%. Exit at 84%: headline lines exit upward with expo.in (stagger 0.06), the other blocks fade up, and the veil scales back to 1 from the left with expo.in.
records.adapt: Replace the hero image, tag text, three headline lines, excerpt, meta, CTA label and brand, and the paper/orange colours; keep the 0.9s veil wipe and the 0.12s line stagger with the 3° rotation.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the hero with veil, tag, title rows, splits the excerpt into .w spans, and adds meta/CTA/brand; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with veil at 0.01D, lines at 0.175D, words at 0.31D, nudge 0.6-0.8D, exit at 0.84D. All from() tweens need immediateRender:false; selectors el-scoped.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: Instagram Story: Browse More
records.description: A story template with an animated swipe-up prompt. Great to use for driving content discovery and directing traffic from stories.
records.move: chevrons ripple upward, finger swipes card deck up, deck steps forward
records.how: Over a slowly panning aurora background, two masked headline lines rise (expo.out, stagger 0.1), a subline fades up and three stacked cards (y -44i, scale 1-0.06i, filter brightness 1-0.25i) rise from +900 with expo.out (negative stagger so the back arrives first); a 'Swipe up' label fades in. Three chevrons ripple continuously: y 14→-14 with opacity 0.15→1 (power2.out, stagger -0.12) then to y -30 fading, every 0.8s for four cycles. A swipe() beat at 32% and 62%: a translucent finger ring fades in at the bottom, drags y 0→-420 with power3.inOut over 0.45s and fades out enlarged, while the front card flies to y -2000 with rotation -4 (power3.in 0.55s) and the cards behind step forward (y, scale, brightness with expo.out 0.6s). At 86% the last card flies off and all three return from y 1000 with expo.out at 0.05s offsets, restoring the fresh deck.
records.adapt: Replace the background image, headline, subline, the three card thumbnails/titles and the label; keep the 0.8s chevron cycle, the 0.45s finger drag and the 0.55s card throw.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the background, header, prompt with chevrons, deck and finger with the initial pose sets; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with swipes at 0.325D and 0.625D and the deck reset at 0.86D. Move swipe() inside animate with el-scoped selectors; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
filter: brightness tweens on the back cards

records.name: Instagram Story: Fashion
records.description: An editorial story template with strong visual hierarchy and a fashion-forward feel. Good for clothing brands and style-focused social media posts.
records.move: paper panel lifts off photo, small type then giant serif lines, closes
records.how: A photo occupies the lower 1400px with a slow push scale 1→1.1 / yPercent 2→-2 across the whole duration; a paper panel over it scales y 1→0 from the top (expo.inOut 1s) like a page lifting. Hierarchy builds small-to-large: season and issue number slide in from x ∓30, a vertical rule scales y from 0 (expo.out), a side block drops from y -30, then three giant serif lines in mix-blend-mode difference rise masked from yPercent 120 (expo.out, stagger 0.14). A swatch image slides in from x 200, its veil scales y to 0 from the bottom, and its image settles from scale 1.15; a credit rule scales x from 0 with captions sliding in. At 57% the italic middle line slides x 120 (expo.inOut) as a flourish. Exit at 82%: lines exit upward with expo.in, small elements fade, the rule shrinks to the bottom and the panel scales back to 1 from the bottom (expo.inOut 0.5s).
records.adapt: Replace the main photo and swatch image, the three headline words, season/number/side/credit strings and the paper colour; keep the 1s panel lift, the 0.14s line stagger and the italic slide at 2.3s.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the photo, panel, type blocks, swatch and credit; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with panel at 0.025D, lines at 0.2D, flourish at 0.575D, exit at 0.82D. All from() tweens need immediateRender:false; selectors el-scoped; mix-blend-mode difference on the headline needs the photo in the same stacking context.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
headline uses mix-blend-mode: difference over the photo

records.name: Instagram Story: Pastel
records.description: A pastel-toned story template with gentle animations that don't compete with the content. Ideal for lifestyle brands and aesthetic-forward social media content.
records.move: pastel blobs breathe, petals drift, card and serif lines ease in softly
records.how: Three large radial-gradient blobs move x/y ±60-90 with scale to 1.1 and back on a sine.inOut yoyo across the full duration, and four petal shapes drift y ±30-50 with ±20-40 rotation on the same yoyo. Entrances are slow and soft: a kicker fades up over 0.9s, two serif title lines rise masked from yPercent 105 with power3.out over 1.1s (stagger 0.15), a white photo card rises from y 80 / scale 0.96 with opacity over 1.2s while its image eases from scale 1.08 to 1 linearly for 4.4s, a pink round sticker pops from scale 0 / rotation -30 with back.out(1.4) and rocks to rotation 8 and back, the italic quote's words fade up with stagger 0.06 and a footer fades. Exit at 84%: quote/footer/kicker fade with power2.in, sticker shrinks with back.in(1.4), title lines exit upward with power3.in and the card lifts y -60 fading.
records.adapt: Replace the card image, kicker, two title words, quote, sticker text and footer, and the three pastel blob colours; keep the slow 0.9-1.2s power3.out entrances and the 2.5s yoyo breathe.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the blobs, petals, type, card and sticker and splits the quote into .w spans; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with the yoyo tweens sized to D/2, entrances 0.02-0.44D, exit at 0.84D. from() tweens need immediateRender:false; selectors el-scoped.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false

records.name: Mirror: Social Media Showcase
records.description: A showcase template where content is reflected symmetrically across a mirrored layout. Works for portfolio reels and brand content with a bold visual structure.
records.move: axis draws, pictures slide to centre from both halves, words swap, fold
records.how: The frame is two 540px halves, the right one CSS-mirrored with scaleX(-1) (its text is flipped back), so every move on the left is reflected on the right. A centre axis line scales y from 0 (expo.inOut 0.8s), a logo drops from y -100 with back.out(2) and a label fades. The first picture slides toward the axis from xPercent -110 (expo.out 0.9s) and the first word rises masked from yPercent 110; all inner images drift xPercent -3→3 linearly for the whole duration. At 37% and 65% a swap: the current picture pushes on to xPercent 20 while the next slides in to 0 (both expo.inOut 0.7s), the current word exits upward with expo.in and the next rises with expo.out. Exit at 87%: all pictures slide back out to xPercent -110 with expo.in, the last word exits, tag/label/logo fade and the axis scales back to 0.
records.adapt: Replace the three pictures and three words (both halves carry the same markup), the tag, label and logo; keep the 0.9s slide, the swaps at 1.5s and 2.6s and the 0.7s expo.inOut push.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds both halves with identical children, the axis and centre block, and applies the sets (absolute word spans, flipped right tag); animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entrance 0-0.25D, swaps at 0.375D and 0.65D, exit at 0.875D. The half widths assume a 1080px stage, so size them from el; selectors el-scoped; from() tweens need immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens need immediateRender:false
half widths and the axis position are hard-coded to a 1080px stage

records.name: Orbit: Social Media Showreel
records.description: A showreel template from Rico where content pieces orbit around a central point in a continuous loop. Great for portfolio presentations and social media showcases.
records.move: eight cards spring from a core, orbit a tilted ring, fold back
records.how: A white circular core sits at centre with two faint concentric rings; eight 250px square cards (six photo, two flat colour) are positioned each frame on a tilted elliptical orbit (x = cos*330, y = sin*330*0.42), the front of the orbit larger (scale up to 1.27) and brighter, the back smaller (0.72) and dimmer, z-index swapped by depth. One full revolution takes the whole duration. A spread factor drives the intro and outro: over the first 10% the cards fly out from the core (expo.out) while unrotating from -90deg and fading in; over the last 6% they collapse back to the core (expo.in). Meanwhile the core pops in with back.out(1.8) and pulses scale 1.06 yoyo, the rings expo.out from scale 0.2, and the title/year/footer fade in at 6% and out at 94%; the last frame matches the first.
records.adapt: Swap the eight card images and captions, the core name and footer strings, the palette of the two flat cards and the stage colour; card count can change (N is derived). Keep the orbit radius:tilt ratio, the one-turn-per-loop rate and the 1s/0.6s spread envelope.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the core, rings and card nodes inside el and reads images/captions from shot. animate(el, shot, D) returns the wrap timeline plus one added tween on a proxy object ({t:0}->{t:D}, ease none, duration D) whose onUpdate runs the orbit placement with gsap.set, so the fx.register seek loop becomes an onUpdate tween on the same timeline. All selectors must be scoped to el; the 540px centre must become el.clientWidth/2 and clientHeight/2.
caveats: orbit is computed per frame via gsap.set in a seek callback, not a tween; port as an onUpdate proxy tween
stacked hue-rotate filters on three cards each frame are mildly costly

records.name: Product Of The Week [Product Hunt]
records.description: An animated Product Hunt badge template for product launch announcements. Great for launch day social posts and milestone content.
records.move: badge pops in, laurels draw, confetti bursts, upvote counter runs up
records.how: On a pale peach stage a pill badge with a round P mark and the text #1 Product of the Week bounces in from scale 0.2 and -12deg rotation with back.out(2.2) over the first 25%; the P spins in from -180deg. Two laurel branches are drawn as SVG stems via drawSVG over 30% and their leaves scale in from the stem with back.out(3) at 35ms stagger. A black vote chip and a product name slide up (expo.out) at 20-25%; the vote number counts 0 to 1,284 (power3.out, 47%) while the triangle bobs six times. Forty-six confetti rectangles fire ballistically from centre (positions computed from velocity and gravity in an onUpdate) between 10% and 63%, fading out at the end of their flight. The badge wiggles +/-2deg at 63%, then the whole composition scales to 0.85 and fades with expo.in at 88%.
records.adapt: Change the rank text, product name and tagline, the upvote target, the brand red (#ff6154) and confetti colours; leaf count and laurel radius are parameters. Keep the 0.7s back.out pop, the counter length and the confetti window.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the SVG laurel (branch() builds paths), badge, votes, name and the confetti divs inside el, seeded with fx.rng-style deterministic randomness. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the counter tween and the ballistic confetti proxy tween (onUpdate gsap.set) placed at the same fractions of D; the querySelector for .num must be scoped to el. DrawSVGPlugin must be registered.
caveats: needs DrawSVGPlugin registered
confetti uses a proxy tween with onUpdate calling gsap.set on 46 elements
exits to blank rather than returning to the first frame; the loop restarts from the pop

records.name: Project Reveal
records.description: A reveal template from Vendredi Society that builds gradually before showing the work. Good for portfolio drops and project announcements where you want to create a sense of anticipation.
records.move: frame lines draw, counter loads, flash, work wipes down, title snaps in
records.how: A dark grid stage: four thin frame lines scale in one after another (scaleX/scaleY, expo.inOut, 0-28%), four client/year/scope/studio meta lines rise out of overflow masks (yPercent 110 to 0, expo.out) at 8, 17, 26 and 35%, an italic serif centre sentence rises at 22-25%, and a big tabular percentage counter climbs 00 to 100 with a matching loading bar (scaleX, power2.inOut) from 6% to 68% while the grid background slowly pans. At 65% the meta, sentence, counter and bar pull up and fade (power2.in). At 69% a white flash hits (0.08s in, 0.6s out), the work panel clip-path insets from 100% bottom to 0 (expo.inOut 0.9s) with the photo settling from scale 1.15, a mock UI card slides up 240px (expo.out) and the title line rises from its mask; the frame lines fade. At 94% the work clips away upward (expo.in) and the title drops out so the stage is dark again.
records.adapt: Replace the meta labels, the centre sentence, the project title and case-study tag, the loader caption, the work image and the mock UI; recolour the grid and flash. Keep the long 6.2s counter build, the 0.4s pull-out, the 0.08s flash and the 0.9s clip wipe.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid, frame lines, meta rows, counter, loadbar, work panel and title inside el, with initial gsap.set for clipPath and yPercent. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with positions as fractions of D (build 0-0.65, reveal 0.69, exit 0.94); the counter onUpdate must query .pct .n within el.
caveats: from() tweens for the frame lines and meta rows; if the timeline is built after the first render use immediateRender:false or fromTo
the frame lines fade at 70% and are not restored, so frame 0 shows lines that the final frame lacks

records.name: Project Teaser
records.description: A cinematic project teaser template from Vendredi Society with a slow build and dramatic reveal. Great for portfolio drops and project announcements where you want to create anticipation.
records.move: letterboxed image rises from black, letters blur in, light sweep, flash reveal
records.how: A full-frame photo sits under a vignette and two 90px letterbox bars. For the first 61% the image barely lifts from brightness 0.05 to 0.32 while scaling 1.3 to 1.12 (power2.inOut) and the bars settle from scaleY 3 (power3.out); corner labels fade in staggered. A kicker line rises from its overflow mask at 16% (power3.out), then the nine letters of the serif wordmark drift in one by one from y 30 with blur(14px) to 0, 140ms apart from 22%; a rule scales open and the date fades in while its letter-spacing tightens from .9em (47-49%). At 62% a skewed light streak sweeps across (x 0 to 1700, power2.inOut), a white flash hits at 69%, the image jumps to full brightness and saturation 1.2 with an expo.out push to scale 1, the word scales to 1.12 and glows, the bars shrink to scaleY 0.4. From 90% everything fades to black and the bars grow back for the loop.
records.adapt: Swap the wordmark letters (one .l span each), kicker, date, corner labels and background image; the glow colour and bar height are tunable. Keep the 5.5s slow build, the 140ms letter stagger and the 0.06s flash at ~70%.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the film image, vignette, light streak, corners, kicker, letter spans, date and bars inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with all labels scaled from the 9s base to fractions of D; the light sweep distance (1700px) should be derived from el width.
caveats: animates CSS filter (brightness/saturate/blur) on a full-frame image and on nine letters, heavy at render time
from() tweens on letters need immediateRender:false if built after first paint
final frame is black with bars at scaleY 3, not exactly the first frame's dim image

records.name: Revolve: Social Media Showcase
records.description: A showcase template where content rotates into view with a smooth spinning motion. Works well for social media reels and portfolio presentations in portrait format.
records.move: slides revolve in on a far pivot as the previous swings out
records.how: Portrait 1080x1920: four tall photo slides hang on arms whose pivot sits 2300px below the top so a rotation of 80deg swings a slide fully off frame; slides wait at rotation 80 (off right) and each revolves to 0 with expo.out over ~14% of the loop while the previous one revolves to -80 (off left, expo.inOut). Handoffs occur at 27, 50 and 72% of the 8s loop; at each, a tabular index counter rolls up one line (yPercent -100*i, expo.inOut) and the dial dot swaps colour. A headline rises from an overflow mask at 0 (expo.out), the first slide arrives at 1%, and all slide images slowly drift (scale 1 to 1.06, xPercent -2 to 2, linear) over the full duration. At 87% the last slide swings out with expo.in and the headline drops up out of its mask; the hint, index and dial fade.
records.adapt: Replace the four slide images, captions and subtitles, the headline word and studio hint; slide count changes the interval (1.8s per slide). Keep the far-pivot geometry (pivot ~1.2x stage height below top), the 80deg swing and the expo.out/inOut pairing.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the pivot, arms and slides inside el, positioning the pivot relative to el size. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with handoffs at 0.05+i*0.225 of D and the loop exit at 0.875 of D; initial arm rotations set with gsap.set in mount.
caveats: portrait 1080x1920 layout, pivot and offsets are absolute px
exit leaves the stage empty, the loop restarts with the headline rise

records.name: Slideshow: Social Media Showreel
records.description: A slideshow template with smooth transitions between frames sized for social media. Great for portfolio content on Instagram and similar platforms.
records.move: full-bleed slides, white wipe with push, captions rise, progress fills
records.how: Square stage with five full-frame photo slides stacked, only one visible at a time. Each slide lasts 20% of the loop: its image drifts in a different direction (xPercent/yPercent +/-3, scale up to 1.1, linear), its caption rises from an overflow mask (yPercent 110 to 0, expo.out 0.8s) 0.3s in and its subtitle fades in from x -20, then both leave (caption yPercent -110 expo.in) 0.5s before the segment ends. Five thin progress bars fill left to right (scaleX, linear) one per segment. The transition at each segment boundary is a white wipe: a full-frame white plane scales from left over 0.4s (expo.inOut), the next slide is set visible and the old one hidden under it, the new slide pushes in from x 120 (expo.out 0.7s) while the wipe collapses toward the right. The fifth segment wipes back to slide one, and the progress bars reset 20ms before the end so the loop closes.
records.adapt: Swap the five images, captions, subtitles and the HUD strings; N slides derives the segment length automatically. Keep the 0.4s expo.inOut wipe, the 0.7s push and the drift amplitude.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the deck slides, wipe plane, HUD and progress bars inside el and sets slide 1 visible. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with SEG = D/N; the fromTo calls already carry immediateRender:false so the build order is safe.
caveats: catalog says 13s but render.json duration is 10s
transitions rely on .set() opacity swaps, which are seek-safe but not reversible mid-wipe if you scrub backwards across several

records.name: Spiral: Social Media Showcase
records.description: A showcase template where content enters the frame with a spiral motion. Good for social reels and portfolio content that needs a bit more visual energy.
records.move: cards spiral in along a drawn path, fan-stack, unwind out
records.how: A dashed spiral path (2.25 turns from 1100px radius to centre) is drawn with drawSVG over the first 20% (power2.out) as the title rises from a mask. Four portrait photo cards each ride the path with motionPath from start to end over 1.2s (power3.out), spinning from rotation -540 to 0 and scaling 0.4 to 1 while fading in, launched at 3, 24, 45 and 66% of the 6s loop. As each new card lands, the earlier cards step back into a fanned stack (x/y offsets, +/-7deg, scale minus 4% per depth, expo.out). At 83% the stack bobs up 10px and back (sine.inOut yoyo), then at 89% all cards fling out to the upper right with rotation 540, scale 0.2 and fade (power3.in, 40ms stagger) while the path undraws and the title drops out.
records.adapt: Replace the four card images and captions, the title, subtitle and footer strings, and the stage/ink colours; card count changes the 1.25s launch cadence. Keep the 2.25-turn spiral, 1.2s power3.out ride and the -540deg spin.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the SVG spiral path (points computed from el size), title and cards inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with MotionPathPlugin and DrawSVGPlugin registered; the path id must be unique per instance (use a generated id or pass the path element) so the motionPath selector does not hit another shot.
caveats: needs MotionPathPlugin and DrawSVGPlugin
motionPath references #sp by document id; must be unique when scoped to el
final frame is empty stage rather than the initial frame

records.name: Animated Cards
records.description: An animated card template from Rico where cards reveal with smooth expressive motion. Great for feature showcases and content feed presentations.
records.move: feature cards rise with tilt and overshoot, shine sweeps, float, lift out
records.how: On a warm stage with two slowly rotating colour blobs, a headline rises from a mask (expo.out) and a subline follows. Three feature cards in a grid rise from y 260 with rotateX -28 and individual z-rotations, scale 0.86 and opacity 0, landing with back.out(1.6) over 1s at 140ms stagger from 5% of the 5s loop. Inside each, the icon spins in from scale 0 (back.out(2.5)), the two-line heading rises from masks (60ms stagger), the paragraph fades up and the tag pill pops with back.out(3). From 32% a diagonal shine gradient sweeps across each card (xPercent -80 to 80, power2.inOut, 150ms stagger). During the hold the cards float up 10px and back (sine.inOut yoyo). At 87% the cards lift up 60px, shrink to 0.94 and fade with power3.in at 80ms stagger, and the header fades.
records.adapt: Replace the three headings, paragraphs, tags and icon shapes, the card colours and blob gradients; card count works with the grid. Keep the back.out(1.6) 1s rise at 140ms stagger and the shine timing.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds blobs, header and the card grid inside el (perspective on el). animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with labels at fractions of D; the per-card rotate array should be sized to shot.cards.length.
caveats: from() tweens throughout; set immediateRender:false if the timeline is built after first paint
last frame is empty stage, not the first frame

records.name: Bento Grid
records.description: A bento grid template where animated cells reveal content in a structured sequence. Great for product showcases and portfolio presentations where you have a lot to show in one composition.
records.move: dashboard cells pop in staggered, stats count, bars grow, fold out
records.how: A dark 4x2 bento of five cells (overview text, completion ring, team list, active-user stat, velocity bars) scales in from 0.7 with y 60 and opacity 0, expo.out over 0.9s at 120ms stagger from the start. Labels then lift in, the overview lines rise (power3.out), twelve bar-chart bars grow from scaleY 0 (expo.out, 50ms stagger) at 11%, four avatar rows slide in from x 40, an SVG ring stroke-dashoffset runs 100 to 14 (expo.out 1.6s) and two counters run 0 to 86% and 0 to 12,480 with expo.out over 1.8s from 12%. During the hold a timeline dot travels 550px along its line (power1.inOut, 25-62%) and the bars breathe to new heights and back (sine.inOut yoyo). At 89% the cells shrink to 0.8, lift and fade with power3.in in reverse order.
records.adapt: Replace the five cell contents, counter targets (data-to), bar heights array, avatar names and accent colours; the grid areas can be rearranged in CSS. Keep the 0.9s expo.out entry at 120ms stagger and the 1.8s expo.out counters.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid and cells inside el and sets bar heights from shot data. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline; the counter tweens iterate el.querySelectorAll('.n') and the dot travel distance should be measured from the cell width instead of the fixed 550px.
caveats: from() tweens; use immediateRender:false if built after first paint
ends on an empty stage, restarts with the pop-in

records.name: Bento: 16:9
records.description: A 16:9 widescreen bento grid template from Clint. Good for YouTube thumbnails and landscape video content showcases.
records.move: bento cells pop in, wipes uncover photos, counters run, wipes close
records.how: A 16:9 four-column by two-row bento grid (c7 ticker cell hidden) of white, black, yellow and blue cells plus three photo cells. All cells scale in from 0.85 and opacity 0 (expo.out 0.9s, 100ms stagger) at 0; a stage-coloured wipe plane over each photo cell collapses to scaleX 0 from the left (expo.inOut 0.9s, 150ms stagger) from 5%, revealing photos that slowly settle from scale 1.25 to 1.05 over 90% of the loop. Category chips drop in from y -30 with back.out(2), headings, labels, logo and dots lift in from y 26 (power3.out, 60ms stagger), a big stat counts 0 to 48 with expo.out over 1.6s from 10%, and three dots blink in sequence (opacity yoyo repeats). Mid-loop at 45% the photo cells lift 12px and scale 1.02 yoyo while their images drift (xPercent -6 / yPercent 5, sine.inOut 4s) and the stat cell rocks -2deg. At 81% the wipes close back over the photos from the right (expo.inOut) and at 89% the cells collapse to 0.85 and fade in reverse order.
records.adapt: Replace the studio name, tagline, chip labels, stat target (data-to), the three photos and the four brand colours; grid-area assignments give the layout. Keep the 0.9s expo.out pop at 100ms stagger, the 0.9s expo.inOut wipe and the 45% mid-loop lift.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid, cells, wipe planes and ticker inside el (hide unused cells). animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with labels scaled from the 10s base to fractions of D; counter tweens must select .n inside el.
caveats: catalog says 20s but render.json duration is 10s
from() tweens throughout; use immediateRender:false when built late
ends on an empty stage, not the first frame

records.how: A 4:5 two-column by four-row bento grid (identity photo cell hidden, a years-stat cell with a horizontal ticker shown instead; the ticker scrolls x 0 to -520 linearly over the whole loop and the years counter runs 0 to 12) of white, black, yellow and blue cells plus three photo cells. Category chips drop in from y -30 with back.out(2), headings, labels, logo and dots lift in from y 26 (power3.out, 60ms stagger), a big stat counts 0 to 48 with expo.out over 1.6s from 10%, and three dots blink in sequence (opacity yoyo repeats).
