records.name: Bento: Modular Showreel
records.description: A bento grid showreel template from Rico that presents multiple pieces of work in a dynamic modular layout. Great for creative studios and agencies with a range of projects to show.
records.move: six tiles pop in, reflow through three bento layouts, return to start
records.how: Six tiles (three photos, a yellow word tile, a blue gradient tile, a striped studio tile) live in a 6x4 grid. At load the script measures each tile's rect under three CSS layouts (L0, L1, L2), then takes the tiles absolute. Tiles pop in from scale 0.6, y 80 and opacity 0 (expo.out 0.9s, 80ms stagger) with captions lifting after; photo images settle from scale 1.2 to 1 linearly over the loop. At 27%, 57% and 82% every tile tweens left/top/width/height to the next layout's rect over 1.1s with expo.inOut at a 40ms per-tile stagger, while all tiles dip to scale 0.96 and back (power2.inOut yoyo). The third reflow returns to L0 so the final frame matches the settled first layout.
records.adapt: Replace the tile images, captions, word tiles and colours, and define the layouts as grid-area rules (any number of layouts). Keep the 1.1s expo.inOut reflow with 40ms stagger and the 0.96 dip.
records.port: mount(el, shot) must build the grid inside el, measure the layouts relative to the grid rect (requires el to be attached and sized), then switch to absolute positioning. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with swaps at 0.275, 0.575 and 0.825 of D; measurement is a layout read, so run it in mount before animate.
caveats: FLIP-style measurement of grid rects at mount; el must be laid out at its final size before measuring
loop frame 0 has tiles at scale 0.6 (from tween), so it only closes after the intro

records.name: Cascading Squares: Grid
records.description: A template from Hervé Studio where squares drop into a grid in a staggered sequence. Good for pattern-based intros and structured reveal sequences.
records.move: squares drop column by column with squash bounce, ripple, fall through
records.how: Thirty-two 72px rounded squares in an 8x4 grid, randomly black, yellow, blue, red or green (seeded rng). Each drops from y -900 over 1.2s with a CustomBounce 'drop' ease (strength .5, squash 2) while a matching scaleY .6 / scaleX 1.35 squash tween runs on the 'drop-squash' ease, staggered 50ms across the grid on the x axis so columns land left to right. A title line rises from its mask at 20%. At 40% a ripple from the grid centre shrinks each square to 0.72 and rotates 90deg and back (power2.inOut yoyo, 40ms grid stagger); at 62% a second ripple from the far corner rotates 45deg and back. At 82% the squares fall through the floor (y 520, opacity 0, power3.in, 30ms stagger) and the title drops out.
records.adapt: Change the grid dimensions, square size and radius, palette and the title; the rng seed changes the colour scatter. Keep the CustomBounce strength/squash pairing and the 50ms x-axis stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the grid of squares inside el with seeded colours. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with grid:[rows,cols] staggers and CustomBounce.create called once (guard against re-creating the ease name).
caveats: needs CustomEase and CustomBounce; drop-squash ease is created alongside drop
from() drop tween needs immediateRender:false if built late
ends on an empty stage, loop restarts with the drop

records.name: Interactive Gallery
records.description: An animated gallery template where images or cards reveal in an exploratory layout. Works for portfolio sites and creative project showcases.
records.move: scattered cards pop in, cursor wanders and lifts cards, field drags
records.how: Eight cards of mixed sizes are placed at fixed positions in a draggable field on a warm grey stage. They pop in from scale 0.4, y 40 and opacity 0 with expo.out over 1s, staggered 80ms in random order, while a hint text slides in from the left. A drawn SVG arrow cursor starts at the bottom centre and travels (power2.inOut 0.9s) to three cards at 17, 45 and 70% of the 8s loop; on arrival each card lifts to scale 1.12 with a deeper shadow (power3.out), its caption fades up and its image zooms to 1.08, holding 1.3s before settling back. Between visits the whole field drifts as if dragged (x -60/y 20 then x 40/y -30, power2.inOut 2.2s) and returns to origin at 84%. At 92% the cards shrink away in random order and the hint fades.
records.adapt: Replace the card spec array (position, size, image, caption), the hint copy and the visit order; card count is free. Keep the 0.9s cursor travel, the 1.3s hover hold and the drag drift amplitude.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the field, cards from shot.cards and the cursor SVG inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with visit times at 0.175, 0.45 and 0.7 of D; card positions are absolute px for a 1280x720 stage and should scale with el.
caveats: fixed pixel layout for 1280x720
boxShadow tween is string-interpolated, mildly costly
ends on an empty stage, not the first frame

records.name: Linear Cards
records.description: An animated card template with minimal motion and a clean aesthetic inspired by Linear. A natural fit for SaaS and developer tool showcases.
records.move: dark cards fade up quietly, border sheen travels, rows check off
records.how: On a near-black stage with a soft indigo glow, the headline blurs in (filter blur 8px to 0, y 18, power3.out 0.9s), a subline follows, a hairline scales open (expo.out 1.2s) and three bordered cards rise 28px into place (power3.out 1s, 120ms stagger) from 6% of the 8s loop; icon, heading, paragraph and mock task rows lift in with small staggers. At 27% a masked gradient border sheen (a ::before pseudo element driven by CSS variable --sx from -100% to 100%, power2.inOut 1.2s) travels each card in turn, 0.5s apart. Task checkboxes fill at 45% and 52%, the command-menu rows highlight one after another (background yoyo at 60%), and the glow breathes over the whole loop. At 89% the cards lift 20px and fade (power2.in, 80ms stagger) with the header and line following.
records.adapt: Replace the headline, subline, three card titles/copy and the mock task rows; recolour the indigo accent (#5e6ad2) and glow. Keep the restrained 1s power3.out rises and the 0.5s sheen cadence.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds glow, header, line and cards inside el, including the ::before sheen styles. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline; the sheen tweens CSS custom properties (--sx, --so) on each card, which GSAP supports, and the nth-child selectors must be scoped to el.
caveats: animates filter: blur on the headline
sheen relies on a ::before with mask-composite and CSS variables set via GSAP
ends on an empty stage, not the first frame

records.name: Photo Gallery
records.description: A photo gallery template with smooth elegant transitions between images. Great for photography portfolios and visual storytelling projects.
records.move: veil wipes open, photos ken-burns then drift-fade, italic captions swap
records.how: Three full-frame photos are stacked inside a letterboxed frame on black. A black veil scales from 1 to 0 toward the right (expo.inOut 1.1s) to open the first photo; each photo then slowly settles from scale 1.12 to 1 while sliding xPercent -2 to 2 (alternating direction, linear) across its 3.33s slot. At each slot boundary the outgoing photo fades and drifts left (opacity 0, xPercent -6, scale 1.04, power2.inOut 1s) to uncover the next; the italic serif caption drops up out of its mask (yPercent -120, power3.in) and the next caption rises in (expo.out 0.7s), and a counter call updates 01/02/03. Three thin progress lines fill linearly, one per slot. At 92% the last photo drifts away, photos 1-2 are reset, the first caption returns and the veil closes from the left so the loop restarts on the veil wipe.
records.adapt: Replace the three photos and captions and the frame inset; N photos changes the slot length (D/N). Keep the 1.1s expo.inOut veil, the 1s drift-fade transition and the opposing xPercent drift per slot.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the frame, stacked photos (last first), veil, captions and progress lines inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with slot = D/N; the tl.call counter updates must reference el.querySelector('.num') and the final resets keep immediateRender:false.
caveats: uses tl.call for the counter text, which fires only when the playhead crosses it; scrubbing backwards may leave a stale number
final frame is the closed veil, first frame is the veil at scaleX 1, so the loop closes

records.name: Project Showcase
records.description: A project showcase template from Vendredi Society with elegant animated reveals and a pace that gives the work room to breathe. Great for agency portfolios and creative case studies.
records.move: image unmasks upward, serif lines rise, rule draws, re-cover and lift
records.how: A cream stage split into copy on the left and a tall photo on the right. A stage-coloured mask over the photo scales to scaleY 0 from the bottom edge (expo.inOut 1.2s) while the photo settles from scale 1.25 to 1.05 linearly over the whole 4s. The case-study index lifts in at 8%, three serif title lines rise out of overflow masks (yPercent 110 to 0, expo.out 0.9s, 100ms stagger) from 11%, the description lifts (power3.out), a hairline rule draws from the left (scaleX, expo.out 0.9s) at 26%, tag pills lift in at 80ms stagger and the studio credit fades in. At 80% the mask re-covers the photo from the top (expo.inOut 0.7s), the title lines drop up out of their masks (power3.in, 50ms stagger) and the remaining copy fades up and away.
records.adapt: Replace the index, three title lines, description, tags, credit and the photo; recolour the cream and ink. Keep the 1.2s expo.inOut unmask and the 0.9s expo.out line rises at 100ms stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the copy column and the masked picture inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the exit at 0.8 of D; from() tweens should become fromTo with immediateRender:false.
caveats: from() tweens; use immediateRender:false if built after first paint
ends on an empty stage, restarts with the unmask

records.name: Rewind
records.description: A rewind effect animation template with a retro VHS-style aesthetic. Works as a creative transition for nostalgic or retro-themed content.
records.move: VHS rewind: footage scrubs backwards with tears and flicker, snaps to PLAY
records.how: A full-frame video is seeked backwards at 3x (currentTime set per frame from a seek callback) for the first 80% of the 7s loop, with two horizontal tear strips (clipped duplicate videos offset 24px) sliding down and up on linear repeats, a blurred tracking band sweeping bottom to top four times, an RGB-split gradient flickering (opacity 0.6 to 0.2, 0.12s yoyo x40), scanlines, a seeded canvas noise field cycling six frames, a 2px horizontal stage jitter, and a monospace REW OSD blinking while the timecode counts down. At 80% the tears, band and RGB overlay cut out, the OSD switches to PLAY, which blinks five times, the video plays forward and the timecode counts up.
records.adapt: Replace the video source, the OSD strings, timecode start value and rewind speed; the noise seed and overlay colours are tunable. Keep the 80% snap point, the 3x reverse rate and the 0.12s RGB flicker.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the three video elements, overlays, noise canvas and OSD inside el and waits for loadeddata. animate(el, shot, D) returns the GSAP timeline plus a proxy tween (0 to D, ease none) whose onUpdate sets video currentTime, timecode text, noise frame and stage jitter, replacing the fx.register seek loop; the stage transform jitter must target el, and the tl.seek inside the seek callback is unnecessary once everything is on one timeline.
caveats: drives three video elements by currentTime every frame; needs loadeddata before first frame and is slow to seek
uses fx.register seek loop plus a separate paused GSAP timeline, not fx.timeline
canvas putImageData per frame
does not return to the first frame; the loop restarts at full-speed rewind

records.name: Rotating Cards
records.description: A card animation template where cards flip into view one by one. Great for presenting features or pricing tiers where a reveal adds something to the experience.
records.move: pricing cards rise, flip one by one with overshoot, flip back, drop
records.how: On a dark stage with perspective 1600px, a headline and subline fade up, then three preserve-3d card wrappers rise from y 80 with rotateX -20 and opacity 0 (expo.out 0.9s, 120ms stagger) showing their blank backs. From 17% each card flips rotationY 0 to 180 over 1.1s with back.out(1.4) at 550ms stagger while lifting 18px and settling (power2.out yoyo); the front-face contents (tier, price, list rows, button) fade up 10px at 40ms stagger. At 57% the middle card scales to 1.04 and back. At 77% the cards flip on to 360 in reverse order (power3.inOut 0.9s, 180ms stagger), then drop away (y 80, opacity 0, power3.in) and the header fades.
records.adapt: Replace the headline, three tiers with prices, feature rows and button labels, and the front colours; card count just needs the grid. Keep the 1.1s back.out(1.4) flip with 550ms stagger and the reverse-order flip-back.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the header and the flip cards (back and front faces) inside el with perspective on the row. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with labels at fractions of D; nth-child selectors scoped to el.
caveats: backface-visibility and preserve-3d required on the faces
from() tweens; use immediateRender:false if built after first paint
ends on an empty stage, restarts with the rise

records.name: Share Your Work
records.description: A social media template made by Fons Mans for sharing creative work. Clean layout and simple motion that lets the work speak for itself.
records.move: browser mockup rises with overshoot, captions rise from masks, quick lift out
records.how: A square cream stage with a browser-window mockup holding a photo hero. In one second the mockup rises 120px from scale 0.94 and opacity 0 (expo.out 0.55s) while its page body slides up within it (yPercent 20, expo.out 0.8s) for a parallax feel; a small label and the two-part caption rise out of overflow masks (yPercent 120 to 0, expo.out, 60ms stagger) between 5% and 18%. At 78% the mockup lifts 40px and fades (power3.in 0.25s) and the text lines drop up out of their masks (yPercent -120, 30ms stagger).
records.adapt: Replace the URL, hero text, screenshot image, label and caption strings; the mockup size and radius are CSS. Keep the 0.55s expo.out rise and the 0.25s exit, scaled with D.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the label, mockup and caption inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with entry at 0-0.2 of D and exit at 0.78 of D; the 1s base is very short, so D should stay near 1-1.5s.
caveats: very short 1s loop
from() tweens; use immediateRender:false if built after first paint
ends on an empty stage

records.name: Slideshow Loop
records.description: A looping slideshow template that cycles through frames without a visible cut. Great for continuous display screens and social carousels where the content should keep moving.
records.move: endless strip holds then expo-slides one frame, centre scaled up
records.how: A track of six frames (three photos, three gradients) is tripled so the strip is endless; each frame is 640px wide with a 40px gap. The whole loop is divided into six slots; within a slot the strip holds for 55% then slides one frame left over the remaining 45% with expo.inOut, computed each frame as a fractional index and applied as translate3d on the track. Frames scale from 1 at centre down to 0.88 and dim to 0.5 opacity one frame away, and each frame's image counter-translates 30px per frame of distance for parallax. A dot row highlights the current index (scale 1.5, white). Because six slots move six frames and the strip repeats every six, the last frame matches the first exactly.
records.adapt: Replace the items array (class, title, number), frame width and gap, and the hold fraction (0.55). Keep the expo.inOut slide, the 0.12 scale falloff and N slots == N frames so the loop closes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the tripled track and dots inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one proxy tween ({t:0}->{t:D}, ease none) whose onUpdate runs the per-frame placement (track translate, frame scale/opacity, dot state), replacing the fx.register seek loop; the centre offset must be derived from el width.
caveats: no GSAP timeline in the source; motion is an fx.register seek function writing inline transforms (gsap.parseEase only)
centre assumes a 1280px stage

records.name: Sliding Squares
records.description: A template where colorful squares slide into position in a staggered sequence. Works for abstract intros and dynamic brand content.
records.move: coloured squares slide in from alternating sides, shuffle columns, slide out
records.how: Eighteen 150px squares in a 6x3 grid on a warm stage, coloured from a six-colour palette. Rows slide in from alternating sides (x +/-1400, expo.out 1.1s) staggered 60ms along the x axis; a large ACME word pops in at 17% with back.out(1.8) blended multiply over the squares. At 32% every square slides one column right (x step 160, expo.inOut 0.7s, 30ms grid stagger) while the last column wraps to the front. At 50% columns alternately shift up and down half a step (stagger from edges) and at 65% return to y 0 (stagger from centre). At 81% the word shrinks away and the squares slide out the opposite way they came (expo.in 0.8s, stagger from end).
records.adapt: Change the palette, cols/rows/step, square radius and the centre word; the alternating row directions derive from row index. Keep the expo.out 1.1s entry, the 0.7s expo.inOut shuffles and the mirrored expo.in exit.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid of squares and the word inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with labels at fractions of D; the 1400px slide distance should come from el width.
caveats: mix-blend-mode multiply on the word
from() slide-in needs immediateRender:false if built late
ends on an empty stage

records.name: Stacked Cards
records.description: A card animation template from Anagram where cards fan out and reveal in sequence. Works great for testimonials and any content that benefits from a one-at-a-time reveal format.
records.move: testimonial stack fans out, each card lifts front then tucks, collapses
records.how: Four white testimonial cards sit in a tight offset stack (y -6 and scale -0.03 per depth) over a blurred photo. At 2.5% they fan out to rotations of -21, -7, 7 and 21deg around a low pivot (transform-origin 50% 150%, expo.out 0.7s, 40ms stagger). From 21% each card in turn lifts to the front (rotation 0, y -26, scale 1.06, expo.out 0.42s, zIndex 10), holds, then tucks back to its fan angle +4deg at scale 0.98 (power2.inOut 0.36s) and settles; the dot row tracks the active card. Cards are 0.72s apart. At 91% the fan collapses back into the stack (expo.inOut 0.5s, 30ms stagger) and z-indexes are restored.
records.adapt: Replace the four quotes, names, roles and avatar gradients and the label; card count drives the fan angles (14deg per card). Keep the 0.42s expo.out lift, 0.36s tuck and 0.72s cadence.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the blurred bg, label, deck of cards and dots inside el and applies the initial stack with gsap.set. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with step = 0.18*D and start = 0.21*D; zIndex swaps are .set() calls on the timeline.
caveats: the collapse (starting at 3.63s + 0.5s) overruns the 4s register duration slightly, so the final frame is not quite the tight stack
the last dot stays active at the end while frame 0 highlights the first
filter: blur(10px) on a full-frame background image

records.name: Config: Photo Gallery 01
records.description: The first animated photo gallery template from the Config series. Good for design conference content and visual work presentations.
records.move: three photo columns scroll endlessly in opposite directions under a difference-blend title
records.how: Three vertical columns of photo tiles (five per column, duplicated so the strip is seamless) scroll linearly over the whole 8s loop, the outer columns upward and the middle one downward, each wrapping exactly one strip length so frame 8s equals frame 0. A top and bottom vignette gradient fades the tiles into the dark stage. A huge two-line title (Config / 2026) in mix-blend-mode difference and a subline rise out of overflow masks (yPercent 110 to 0, expo.out 0.9s, 100ms stagger) at 5% and drop up out of them (expo.in) at 86%. The whole column group breathes from scale 1.02 to 1.08 and back (sine.inOut yoyo over the loop).
records.adapt: Replace the tile images, hue-filter skins, captions and the per-column height arrays, and the title lines. Keep the linear one-wrap-per-loop scroll, opposite middle direction and the 0.9s expo.out title rise.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the three columns with doubled tiles and the title inside el and computes each column's total height. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the scroll tweens lasting D and the title exit at D-1.1; column heights are absolute px for 720px tall stages.
caveats: several tiles carry hue-rotate/sepia/grayscale filters, mildly costly
title uses mix-blend-mode difference
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when built late

records.name: Config: Photo Gallery 02
records.description: A second animated photo gallery template from the Config series. Perfect for design conference content and visual work presentations.
records.move: accordion strip: wide slide narrows as the next expands, strip slides
records.how: A horizontal strip of seven slots (six slides plus a copy of the first) on a cream stage; one slot is wide (720px) and the rest thin (200px). Every second (D/N) at 0.62s offset, the wide slot's width tweens to 200 while the next slot's width tweens to 720 and the strip x shifts so the new wide slot is centred, all with expo.inOut over 0.7s; the outgoing caption fades down (power2.in 0.25s) and the incoming title and subtitle fade up (expo.out 0.4s). The wide image drifts scale 1.08 to 1 and xPercent -2 to 2 while it holds. A progress bar width fills linearly over the loop and a 01/06 counter is computed from time in a patched seek. The seventh slot is identical to the first so the final frame matches the start.
records.adapt: Replace the six skins and titles, the location string, the wide/thin widths and gap. Keep the 0.7s expo.inOut width and strip move and the 0.62s offset within each step.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the strip of N+1 slots inside el and sets initial widths and offset from el width. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline; the patched __fx.seek counter becomes a proxy tween with onUpdate (or a set() per step) on the returned timeline.
caveats: animates width, which triggers layout each frame
counter is written by overriding window.__fx.seek, not on the timeline
the last expo.inOut step ends at 5.32s and frame 6s equals frame 0 only because slot 7 duplicates slot 1

records.name: Config: Photo Gallery 03
records.description: A third animated photo gallery template from the Config series with a different compositional feel. Good for design community content and visual storytelling.
records.move: giant word settles letter by letter, polaroids drop with spin, sweep out
records.how: A dark stage with a 330px CONFIG word in dim grey rising letter by letter (yPercent 40, opacity 0, expo.out 0.8s, 50ms stagger). Five white-bordered polaroid photos at fixed positions drop in every 0.5s from 8%: each comes from scale 1.6, y -80 and +25deg over its seeded rest rotation, landing with back.out(1.4) over 0.75s, then drifts slightly (y and +/-2deg, sine.inOut 1.6s) while holding. A tag line rises from a mask at 20%. At 77% the photos sweep up out of frame (y -800, -20deg, expo.in 0.55s, 120ms stagger), the tag drops out and the letters lift away.
records.adapt: Replace the word letters, the five photo images, captions and positions/sizes, and the rng seed for tilt. Keep the 0.75s back.out(1.4) landing, 0.5s cadence and the 120ms sweep stagger.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the big word spans and the polaroids inside el with seeded rotations. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with drops at 0.083+i*0.083 of D and the exit at 0.77 of D.
caveats: fixed pixel positions for 1280x720
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when built late
ends on an empty stage

records.name: Feature Sneak Peek
records.description: A teaser template from Vendredi Society that partially reveals an upcoming feature. Good for pre-launch social content where you want to build anticipation without giving everything away.
records.move: circular lens wanders a blurred UI, opening sharp windows, then closes
records.how: Two identical copies of a settings UI card sit on a dark stage with a purple glow: the lower copy is blurred (filter blur 18px) under a frosted panel, the upper copy is sharp but clipped by clip-path circle(r at x y). Header lines and a footer rise out of masks (expo.out) and the blurred panel lifts in from y 60 over the first 14%. From 14% a lens object visits five stops: it travels (x/y, expo.inOut 0.9s), opens (r from 0 to 130-210px, back.out(1.6) 0.6s) while a ring element scales with it, holds 0.5s (0.9s on the last centred stop), then closes (r to 0, expo.in 0.45s), each stop taking ~2.1s. The UI copies drift up 14px and back over the loop, and two switches flip on at 52%. At 92% the header, footer and blurred panel push out.
records.adapt: Replace the UI markup (rendered into both copies), the header/footer copy, the stop coordinates and radii, and the accent gradient. Keep the 0.9s expo.inOut travel, 0.6s back.out opening and 0.45s expo.in close.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the glow, header, both UI copies, frost, lens ring and footer inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline; the lens proxy tweens with onUpdate apply must write clip-path on the sharp layer inside el, with stop coordinates relative to el.
caveats: filter: blur(18px) on a full card plus blur(30px) on the glow, slow to render
clip-path circle updated every frame via onUpdate
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when built late
ends on an empty stage

records.name: Holo
records.description: A holographic shimmer animation template from Luc Chaissac with iridescent color shifts. Good for premium product showcases and brand content that wants a distinctive futuristic quality.
records.move: card tilts on a figure-eight, rainbow foil slides and hue-cycles, sheen wipes
records.how: A single portrait card sits in 3D perspective over a blurred conic-gradient halo. Every frame the card rotates rotateY sin(p)*22deg and rotateX cos(p)*10-2deg for one figure-eight per loop; an oversized rainbow gradient foil layer (mix-blend screen) translates opposite the tilt (-ry*6px, rx*8px) with a slight rotate and its hue-rotate filter runs 0 to 360deg across the loop, over a diagonal grating and an SVG feTurbulence grain. A hard white sheen band wipes across the card once per loop (translateX -60% to 60%). The halo spins a full turn and pulses scale +/-8% twice per loop. Every parameter is periodic in the loop so the last frame equals the first.
records.adapt: Replace the card title, chip, subtitle, logo and the foil gradient stops; tilt amplitudes (22/10deg) and foil travel factors are tunable. Keep the one-cycle-per-loop periodicity so it loops.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the halo, card (foil, grate, sheen, noise, ink) and caption inside el, including the inline SVG filter with a unique id. animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline holding one proxy tween ({t:0}->{t:D}, ease none) whose onUpdate writes the card, foil, sheen and halo transforms and filter, replacing the fx.register seek loop; gsap is loaded but only fx.register is used.
caveats: animates filter hue-rotate on a large foil layer plus a feTurbulence grain and blur(28px) halo every frame, render-heavy
several mix-blend-mode layers (screen, overlay, soft-light)
no GSAP timeline in source; motion is a seek function writing inline styles

records.name: Instruction Card
records.description: An animated instruction card template that presents steps one at a time in a clear layout. Great for onboarding flows and how-to content.
records.move: card rises, steps slide in, ring draws, number becomes tick, bar advances
records.how: A white card rises 60px from scale 0.96 and opacity 0 (expo.out 0.8s) on a light stage; a kicker and heading rise out of masks. Three step rows are then presented 1.5s apart from 14%: each slides in from x -30 with opacity 0 (expo.out 0.6s), its circular ring stroke draws with drawSVG 0 to 100% (power2.inOut 0.6s), the number badge turns blue and the digit scales to 0 while a checkmark path draws in (power2.out 0.35s), and the progress bar width jumps to the next third (expo.out 0.5s); the previous step dims to 0.55 opacity. A patched seek writes the 'n of 3 done' counter from time. At 92% the card lifts 60px and fades (expo.in 0.5s).
records.adapt: Replace the kicker, heading and three step titles/descriptions, the accent blue (#3a5bff) and card size; step count changes the bar fractions and cadence. Keep the 0.6s expo.out slide, 0.6s ring draw and 1.5s cadence.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the card, rows with SVG ring and tick paths, counter and bar inside el, and sets drawSVG 0% on rings and ticks. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with steps at (1.0+i*1.5)/7 of D; the counter override of window.__fx.seek becomes .call() or a proxy tween on the timeline; DrawSVGPlugin must be registered.
caveats: needs DrawSVGPlugin
counter is written by overriding window.__fx.seek, not on the timeline
animates width on the progress bar
ends on an empty stage

records.name: NFT Cards: 3D
records.description: A 3D animated card template from Rico showing digital artwork rotating in space. Perfect for digital collectibles showcases and product presentations.
records.move: three textured 3D cards orbit a ring, spinning and bobbing, camera drifts
records.how: A three.js scene on a near-black stage: three box-geometry cards (2.2 x 3.1 x 0.06) with generative canvas-texture artwork (seeded shapes, baked frame and label) and metallic edges are placed on a ring of radius 3.1 inside a group. Each frame the group rotates a full turn per loop (rotation.y = p*2pi); each card counter-rotates the group and adds its own full spin plus a sine wobble of 0.55rad, bobs in y by 0.22 twice per loop and rocks in z by 0.06rad. A 300-point purple dust field rotates half a turn the other way, and the camera bobs 0.35 in y while looking at the origin, lit by a key directional light and pink and violet rim point lights. HTML title and edition labels sit static over the canvas. All motion is periodic so the loop closes except the dust (half turn), which is nearly uniform.
records.adapt: Replace the art() generator (or map real artwork textures), the seeds/hues, card count, ring radius, light colours and the HTML title/edition strings. Keep the one-orbit-per-loop rate and the bob/wobble amplitudes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) creates the renderer on a canvas inside el sized to el, builds the scene, textures and dust, and appends the HTML labels. animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with a proxy tween ({t:0}->{t:D}, ease none) whose onUpdate runs the per-frame scene update and renderer.render, replacing the fx.register seek loop; the module importmap for three must be available to shots.custom.js.
caveats: WebGL renderer with preserveDrawingBuffer; needs three loaded via importmap as an ES module
seek callback renders the scene every frame
dust field rotates only half a turn per loop so it does not close exactly, but the points are uniform enough that the seam is invisible
W/H fixed at 1280x720

records.name: Ready For Config
records.description: An animated template celebrating Figma Config. Good for Figma community posts and design conference content.
records.move: brand shapes bounce in from corners, words push up, dot pops, confetti
records.how: Four 220px shapes in Figma brand colours (circle, half-circles, arch) bounce in from the four corners (x/y +/-400/300, +/-90deg rotation, back.out(1.5) 1s, 100ms apart) on a dark grey stage. A kicker, three big word lines (Ready / for / Config) and a date line rise out of overflow masks (yPercent 115-120 to 0, expo.out 0.7-0.9s, 120ms stagger) from 9% to 17%. At 24% a green centre dot pops in with back.out(3) and shrinks away at 32% as sixty confetti bits fire outward in seeded directions (260-640px, rotation 360-900deg, power3.out 1.4-2s) with gravity offset and fade. The shapes then slowly rotate +/-90deg (sine.inOut 4.6s) and hop 30px four times in staggered sync. From 86% the words push up out of their masks and the shapes fly back out to their corners with back.in(1.5).
records.adapt: Replace the kicker, three word lines, date and the shape colours/radii; confetti count and palette are arrays. Keep the 1s back.out(1.5) corner entries, the 120ms word stagger and the confetti burst at 31%.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the shapes, confetti bits (seeded rng) and copy lines inside el. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with labels at fractions of D and exits at D-1.3 onward; the 400/300px throws should scale with el size.
caveats: sixty confetti elements each with their own fromTo tween
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when built late
ends on an empty stage

records.name: Thank You Config
records.description: An animated thank you card template for Figma Config. Good for post-conference community posts and event recap content.
records.move: thank-you with heartbeat dot, stat cards count up, dark wipe to sign-off
records.how: Scene 1 (0-35%): a kicker and two big lines rise from overflow masks (expo.out, 120ms stagger) on a cream stage, a red dot pops in with back.out(2.5) and beats four times (scale 1.18 yoyo, 0.18s), then the lines drop up out of their masks and the dot shrinks with back.in(2). Scene 2 (36-68%): three white stat cards drop in from y 120 with slight rotations and back.out(1.4) at 100ms stagger, three counters run to 3, 86 and 12k with power3.out over 1.2s, then the cards lift away with expo.in. Scene 3 (67-100%): a dark plane wipes up from the bottom (scaleY, expo.inOut 0.6s), a sunset photo fades to 0.85 behind and drifts, the plane wipes away from the top, the sign-off lines rise from masks, and at 92% they push up while the photo fades so the loop returns to the cream stage.
records.adapt: Replace the kicker, thank-you lines, three stat labels and data-to targets, the sign-off lines, the background photo and the brand colours. Keep the scene split (35/32/33%), the four-beat pulse and the 0.6s expo.inOut wipes.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds the bg, three scene containers and the wipe plane inside el with z-index sets. animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with scene boundaries at 0.36 and 0.67 of D; counter tweens select .n inside el.
caveats: catalog says 14s but render.json duration is 10s
from() tweens need immediateRender:false when built late
stats scene opacity relies on a .set() at 3.6s

records.name: Zero Gravity: Floating Cards
records.description: Cards drift weightlessly in space, slowly rotating and bobbing as if in zero gravity. Good for product card showcases and floating UI hero shots.
records.move: glass cards bob, tilt and drift weightlessly, shadows shrink as they rise
records.how: Three frosted-glass product cards (backdrop-filter blur) float over a blurred aurora background in a perspective stage. Each frame a phase w = t/D*2pi drives every card: translateY sin(w+phase)*26*amp, translateX cos*10, rotateY cos*14*amp, rotateX sin(2w)*7 and rotateZ sin*4*amp, with per-card phase offsets (0, 2.1, 4.2) and amplitudes (1, 0.8, 1.15). Each card's elliptical shadow follows x at 0.6x, scaling from 1.05 down to 0.75 and fading from 0.55 to 0.2 as the card rises. The header bobs 6px. Everything is a sine of one cycle per loop, so the final frame equals the first.
records.adapt: Replace the three product names, prices, image gradients and positions, and the header copy; amplitudes and phases are per-card parameters. Keep the one-cycle-per-loop sines so it loops.
records.port: mount(el, shot) builds bg, header, shadows and cards inside el at positions relative to el. animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one proxy tween ({t:0}->{t:D}, ease none) whose onUpdate writes the card and shadow transforms, replacing the fx.register seek loop; gsap is loaded but unused in the source.
caveats: backdrop-filter blur(20px) on three cards plus blur(30px) on the background and blur(18px) shadows, render-heavy
no GSAP timeline in source; motion is a seek function writing inline transforms
